What this period added. The earlier published version of this report (last revised 2026-10-16T21:02Z, from a first research period of about 21.6 hours, 2026-10-15T23:24Z to 2026-10-16T21:03Z) had the same status label and contained Theorems 1 to 5, 7, 9 and 13 and Propositions 6, 8, 10 to 12 and 14 to 26. This period added Propositions 27 to 40, repaired and sharpened earlier statements, and had the new material and the summaries checked by independent referees (Reviews and consultations 1 to 120 in sec. 5). The main additions are the following. (a) Proposition 29 identifies the sub-case of branch (I) in which D/M^2 is bounded below at all late times with historical swirl domination, whose exclusion is the regularity criterion (SD), which is not established. (b) Proposition 33 splits Case 1 by the near-axis strain into a Type I swirl branch and a branch on which limsup (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity, and Proposition 35 shows that every Type I swirl constant is at least 3^{-1/2}. (c) On the Type I swirl branch, Proposition 34 gives the structure of the limit, Proposition 38 is a Liouville theorem in similarity variables, Proposition 39 represents the potential vorticity along backward five-dimensional diffusions and gives conditional exclusions, and Proposition 40 excludes the limit under the source bound (39.19_H) on Euler boxes of a slope H > K with a small dyadic budget. Proposition 40 also excludes it under bounds on the actual strain along the backward circulation paths: an averaged compression bound with a coefficient c <= 1/2, the endpoint c = 1/2 included; for c < 1/2 its localization to circulation superlevel sets, with a conditional endpoint c = 1/2 and an abstract example showing that the extra condition of that endpoint cannot be dropped in the abstract setting; a pathwise profile bound; and a one-sided axial stretching bound. None of these hypotheses was derived for the limits. (d) Propositions 27, 28, 30 to 32, 36 and 37 add a conditional finite-window realization, a shape bound for axisymmetric fields with swirl, lower bounds for the inward radial speed near the axis, and necessary conditions on the strain branches. (e) Proposition 11(v) now gives the sharp lower bound C_* >= sqrt10/12 = 0.26352... obtainable from the three suprema for all bounded C^{1,1} fields, and it closes the range left undecided in the earlier version for the inviscid branch: the unconditional bounds inherited by its limits exclude them by themselves exactly when C_* < sqrt7/8. (f) The profile exclusion of Proposition 25(f) is now proved. The first missing implication is unchanged in kind and is now stated relative to the dichotomy of Proposition 33.

Overview. This guide summarizes the report; the precise statements, with all hypotheses, are the numbered results of sec. 1.2, and the open steps are stated in full below, in sec. 1.3 and in sec. 4.
(The problem.) A smooth finite-energy axisymmetric Navier-Stokes solution with bounded circulation Gamma = r u^theta first becomes singular at T_*. Case 1 adds the historical shape condition (A) on the suprema of u, grad u and grad^2 u, and two witnesses at the swirl first-crossing records (r_n, z_n, t_n): the rescaled solutions are bounded on compact normalized sets (K), and their weighted far field is uniformly small (TAIL). The case would be closed by a proof that the normalized limit at the records cannot exist, or by a fixed-datum counterexample. Neither was obtained.
(Reduction.) A limit exists along a subsequence (Theorems 1 and 2, after fixing the sign of the record swirl, reflecting if necessary and extracting further): it is a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution U with viscosity in [1/G, (K^2 - 1)^{1/2}] (G is the circulation bound ||r u_0^theta||_infty of the datum, K the bound in (K), and gamma_* in [(K^2 - 1)^{-1/2}, G] a limit of the record circulations gamma_n = r_n S_n, sec. 1.1), bounded circulation, |U^theta| <= 1 = U^theta(e_1, 0) and inflow -gamma_* U^R(e_1, 0) >= 1. After rescaling to unit viscosity it lies in the class LL of bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solutions with bounded circulation and nonzero swirl. Conversely (Theorem 3), for every W in LL some member of the closure of its axial and past-time translates, parabolic rescalings and reflections x_2 -> -x_2 has, after a change of viscosity, every property of U listed in Theorem 2, with some admissible constants in place of K, G and gamma_*. An exclusion that uses only those properties, for all admissible constants, would therefore prove that LL is empty, which is the bounded-circulation case of the Liouville conjecture of Koch, Nadirashvili, Seregin and Sverak, open to our knowledge; the report therefore seeks further information inherited from the fixed solution.
(Information inherited from the fixed solution.) Under (A) the gradient is not of Type I: limsup (T_* - t) D(t) = infinity for the historical gradient maximum D(t) = sup_{s <= t} ||grad u(s)||_infty (Theorem 9), and every sequence of gradient records tending to T_* has a subsequence in one of two branches (Theorem 13): a viscous single-scale branch, whose limits lie in LL after viscosity normalization and alignment of the axis, and an inviscid branch, whose limits are ancient swirl-free Euler flows (weak limits with C^1 spatial convergence). Independently of (A), the near-axis strain k(t) = ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty absorbs the circulation (Proposition 33), so that either the swirl is of Type I, (T_* - t) ||u^theta(t)||_infty^2 bounded near T_*, or it is not, and then limsup (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity. In the setting of the report limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) ||u^theta(t)||_infty^2 >= 3^{-1/2}, so every Type I swirl constant is at least 3^{-1/2} (Proposition 35, which uses a continuation lemma of Chen, Fang and Zhang and no circulation bound). On the Type I swirl branch ||U^theta(tau)||_infty = O(|tau|^{-1/2}) as tau -> -infinity, grad U tends to 0 uniformly on each cylinder of fixed radius around the axis, and every local limit of the translates U(. + z_k e_3, . + s_k), s_k -> -infinity, is a constant axial field (the constant may depend on the sequence); the meridional field is not asserted to decay.
(Results aimed at the Type I swirl branch.) Proposition 38 is a Liouville theorem in similarity variables: a bounded smooth ancient axisymmetric solution with viscosity nu > 0 and |Gamma| <= G satisfies |Gamma| <= lambda everywhere if U^R >= -C (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} - theta R/(tau_* - tau) on {|Gamma| > lambda}, for some tau_* > 0, C >= 0, theta in [0, 1/2) and lambda in [0, G); in particular a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with bounded circulation and |U| <= C (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} vanishes, without spatial decay hypotheses or bounds on scale-invariant local energy, dissipation or pressure quantities. Consequently, for every Case-1 limit, in either alternative, every lambda in [0, 1), C >= 0, theta in [0, 1/2) and p > 1 + (G/gamma_* - lambda)/((1 - 2 theta)(1 - lambda)), every sufficiently late window [T_0, T_0^p] contains a time s and a point with max{R, |Z|} < 2 (||U||_infty + nu_*) s, |Gamma_U| > lambda and U^R < -C s^{-1/2} - theta R/s at time -s (Proposition 38(c), (e) and (38.6)). The potential vorticity eta = omega^theta/R of the limit solves a drift-diffusion equation in five dimensions with source d_Z(q^2), q = U^theta/R, and no stretching term; on the Type I swirl branch Proposition 39 represents eta through this source along backward five-dimensional diffusions (Feynman-Kac representation) and, with the localized Biot-Savart law, reduces the missing inflow bound to bounds for the source. On the Type I swirl branch the limit is excluded under each of the following hypotheses, none of which was derived: the axial regularity bound (39.21) for the near-axis strain on an Euler cone, with no compression hypothesis; or the cone-local window bound (CW_loc) on the time integral of the compression in the parabolic cylinders inside an Euler cone, together with any one of a vorticity decay bound outside the parabolic cylinders (39.14), the related bound (39.15), or a logarithmic bound for the time-integrated critical source mass, globally (39.16) or on Euler boxes (39.19). Under the Type I compression bound of Proposition 37(d), which holds on the Type I strain branch, or under its global time-integrated form (CW), an outflow bound U^R <= kappa R/|tau| with kappa < 1 outside the parabolic cylinders also suffices. With no compression hypothesis, the source bound (39.19) on Euler boxes of a slope H > K with a small dyadic budget B also suffices: 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + C_abs B/nu < 1/2, with C_abs = 0.735 (Proposition 40; next paragraph).
(What remains open.) It suffices to exclude the swirl-record limit in each alternative of Proposition 33. (1) If the swirl is not of Type I, the properties derived for this alternative (the strain records and their limits, Proposition 37(a), (b) and Remark (2)) do not exclude the swirl-record limit; a Liouville theorem for LL would exclude it (it would not by itself exclude inviscid strain-record or gradient-record limits, which this route does not need to exclude). (2) On the Type I swirl branch the bound (39.21) would suffice by itself; on the route through (CW_loc) the first missing step is (CW_loc) itself, a control of the compression of the parabolic cylinders inside an Euler cone, after which a source bound such as (39.19) is still needed. With no compression hypothesis, the source bound (39.19), taken on the boxes of a slope H > K, bounds the dyadic window integrals of the compression on the parabolic cylinders inside every Euler cone of slope A < H by C_A (1 + log t); if H > A_c (A_3 is an explicit constant depending on K and nu fixed in Proposition 39(f)(ix), and A_c > A_3 is the cone slope of (x)) and the pointwise rate |d_Z(q^2)| <= F |tau|^{-5/2} also holds on the cone of the same slope H, it gives (CW_loc), hence the exclusion (Proposition 39(f)(xiv)). The logarithm is permitted by the unsigned estimate used there, and the logarithmic window growth is attained in the enlarged linear problem with a prescribed bounded smooth divergence-free drift V having R V^R = 2 nu on the relevant annular regions (or R V^R < 2 nu everywhere with a deficit tending to zero there), both for the unsigned majorant and for the reconstructed strain generated by a source d_Z phi with phi >= 0; under a global dyadic L^1 source budget, drifts without radial velocity give a uniform window bound (Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(5)(d), (e)). These examples do not satisfy the velocity-vorticity coupling or the Type I and circulation envelopes of the swirl field; sharpness for Navier-Stokes limits remains open. Under the same source budget the coupling Delta_5 a_U = d_Z eta excludes, for the limits, the long critical and near-critical annular plateaux of that construction: the vorticity mass of every parabolic cylinder in a smaller cone is bounded, the signed averages of the strain over a diffusive height are O(1/|tau|), and so an outflow R U^R >= c nu cannot persist across a diffusive height at any radius o(|tau|^{1/2}); this does not exclude every mechanism for logarithmic growth and does not remove the logarithm, and an explicit kinematic field with exact coupling, bounded velocity, bounded vorticity mass and logarithmic window growth (which violates the source budget only through its evolution) shows that exact coupling, bounded velocity and bounded vorticity mass do not imply (CW_loc); transport, occupation or signed-cancellation estimates derived from the coupled evolution are possible sufficient routes, none of which is proved or shown to be necessary (Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(6)). If the source vanishes on the boxes C_H(-beta) of a slope H > A_c, with A_c > A_3 as in (xiii) (zero budget), the window bound holds and (xiii) excludes the limit; for a positive budget the multiscale counting, the averaged radial flux and the survival decay under a pointwise outflow gap leave the transport step open, and an exact forced expanding pair with nonnegative potential shows that logarithmic compression windows cost a logarithmic source (Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(7)). The budget also bounds int_I sup_{C_{E'}(-v)} |a_U(., -v)| dv by C_1 + kappa log(1 + |I|), where a_U = U^R/R, K < E' < H, I is an interval contained in [s, 4s] and s is sufficiently large, with constants as in (39.29) and kappa proportional to B/nu, which gives a survival bound for packets stopped at their exit from the cone on which the strain bound holds (an unconditional survival bound must add the exit probability) and a bound for a radial occupation functional that is not shown to be comparable with the potential a packet produces at an axis point, but not a uniform packet estimate: prescribed bounded drifts obeying that bound, even with additive constant zero, give radial occupations not bounded uniformly in the drift and the starting point, and packet windows growing like log log T, and these drifts violate the vorticity mass bound for their own vorticity (Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(8)). For a small budget the window bound is not needed: if 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + C_abs B/nu < 1/2, with K = ||U||_infty, B the dyadic source budget on the boxes of slope H and an explicit absolute constant C_abs < 7.64 (2.80 suffices after optimizing a splitting radius and using a duality form of the kernel bound, 0.81 with the sharp Nash constant, and 0.735 with the heat value (4 pi)^{-3/2} of the kernel constant, which is the least value valid uniformly over the smooth bounded divergence-free axisymmetric drifts with bounded derivatives, Proposition 40, Remarks (3) to (5); (39.19_H) and the smallness of B are hypotheses), the backward circulation paths are killed at the axis almost surely, because the compression averaged over their surviving law at the age s is at most c P(survival to s/2)/s with some c < 1/2, up to an integrable error, while eternal survival forces a time-integrated compression of at least (1/2) log t; this contradicts the survival probability bound 1/A from the record, so such a limit does not exist (Proposition 40). For larger budgets, and without (39.19_H), this is open. Without (39.19_H) the same contradiction follows from a bound on the actual strain a = U^R/R along the backward circulation paths: the averaged compression bound with a coefficient c <= 1/2 and an integrable error (Proposition 40, Remark (2); for c < 1/2 the bound is needed only on a positive circulation superlevel set {Gamma_U > ell}, 0 <= ell < 1, normalized by the probability of that set along the paths, at a level ell at which the terminal killed circulation has no atom, Remark (9)(f)), or the pathwise bound (40.6) with a fixed nonnegative nonincreasing profile f_pr, integrable near 0, whose limit at infinity is below 1/2, and a fixed deterministic nonnegative integrable error e_path, needed either along all paths only at the ages where the circulation exceeds a level ell < 1, or eventually, for almost every age, on an event of positive probability inside eternal survival (Remarks (9)(d), (f)); the one-sided axial stretching bound (d_Z U^Z)^+ <= D_+/|tau| with D_+ < 1, on the radial segments below the paths, gives the pathwise bound, and on an Euler cone of slope larger than K gives it eventually on almost every eternally surviving path, which suffices by the restarted comparison of Remark (9)(f); the endpoint D_+ = 1 is excluded as well (Remarks (9)(g), (h)); for a limit, the global stretching bound follows from C_ax + d_ZZ P >= -alpha/tau^2 on R^3 x (-infinity, -1] with alpha in [0, 2], where C_ax := d_Z U^R d_R U^Z and P is the pressure (Remark (9)(h)). None of these bounds has been derived for the limits. The bounded kinematic example of Remark (9)(h)(i) shows that the compression and axial stretching bounds do not follow, for prescribed fields, from the velocity, gradient and circulation bounds and the circulation equation, even with a Type I swirl bound; the construction does not impose the momentum equation, so the example does not test the pressure condition for limits. The dyadic barrier argument of Proposition 37(e) does not turn the logarithmic window bound into the rate q = O(1/|tau|). A failure of (CW_loc) forces unbounded dyadic window integrals of (K E'(s))^{1/2} + s^{1/2} E'(s), where E'(s) is the supremum of |eta| on any larger Euler cone at time -s (Proposition 37, Remark (5)(c)). The inequalities collected in Proposition 37, Remark (5)(c), item (9) (the two-cone inequality, the axis envelope, the time-integrated swirl barrier, q_U = o(s^{-1/2}), and a cone-local Lagrangian inequality for the potential vorticity that is stated there and not proved) are all satisfied by scalar power profiles with sup q^2 of order s^{-2}, E' of order s^{-3/2} and compression of order s^{-3/4} on the cone, whose window integrals are unbounded; so these inequalities do not imply (CW_loc). The axis envelope bounds the compression by C (K E')^{1/2} + C K/(delta s), and the square root has the sharp spatial scaling among bounded smooth divergence-free axisymmetric fields; neither this scaling nor the scalar profiles show such behavior for a Navier-Stokes solution. The rate E'(s) = O(s^{-2}) on a suitable larger cone implies (CW_loc) (proved there); it is not proved for the limit. Along the backward paths from a point where the potential vorticity of such a configuration is at least c' s^{-3/2}, an expected absolute source of at least (c'/2) s^{-3/2} must be collected while the paths are inside a fixed parabolic cylinder (with no profile hypothesis); under the scalar profiles taken as global bounds (||q_U(-beta)||_infty^2 <= c_q beta^{-2} and ||a_U^-(-beta)||_infty <= c_m beta^{-3/4}), either an upper bound o(s^{7/8}), uniform over the set carrying the envelope, for the expected time that the backward paths spend up to a finite horizon in the cylinder of radius lambda_0 s^{1/8} beta^{1/2}, or a bound o(s^{-3/2}), uniform over that set, for the weighted axial swirl dissipation beta^{1/2} |d_Z q_U|^2 collected inside the fixed parabolic cylinder, would exclude it; neither is proved (Proposition 37, Remark (5)(c), item (10)(c), (f), (g)). Under (CW_loc), (39.19) is one sufficient source condition; for the fixed-amplitude axially periodic profiles q = s^{-1} Q(R/s^{1/2}, Z/l(s)) of Proposition 39(f)(ix) it holds exactly when int_s^{2s} dbeta/l(beta) is bounded, so cells of Euler length satisfy it and cells of parabolic length persisting over the dyadic windows violate it; this calculation does not classify general sources, and no argument excludes such persistent cells in a Case-1 limit. (3) The branches of Theorem 13 give a second, independent splitting: on the inviscid branch a backward-decay estimate for the ancient swirl-free Euler limits (Proposition 12) would exclude it, and none was derived.

First missing implication. No argument yet derives a contradiction from the fixed physical solution, (A) and the Case-1 witnesses (K) and (TAIL), and no fixed-datum counterexample was found. The missing implication is an exclusion of the swirl-record limit in each alternative of Proposition 33 or, alternatively, an exclusion of both branches of Theorem 13 below. Within branch (I), the sub-case in which D/M^2 is bounded below at all late times is equivalent to historical swirl domination, sup_{s <= t} ||u(s)||_infty <= C_S sup_{s <= t} ||u^theta(s)||_infty near T_*, and its exclusion is exactly the regularity criterion (SD) of Proposition 29, which is not established in the sources checked.
(I) Viscous, single-scale branch. At the swirl records the normalized global numbers m_n, d_n, h_n (sec. 1.2, Proposition 8) are bounded, and, after viscosity normalization, the limits taken at the swirl records and at the gradient records belong to the class LL defined in sec. 1.1, with global W^{2,infinity} bounds and, at the gradient records, the shape bound Q <= C_* (Q is the shape ratio of Proposition 8(b)). Proposition 15 selects (existentially, not within a prescribed branch or subsequence) gradient-record limits that are eternal, with the gradient maximum over all space and time attained; their whole-time shape bound is Q <= 18 C_*^2. Every member of LL has finite Q. Consequently, an exclusion using only the ancient limit properties of Theorem 2 and finiteness of Q, uniformly over all finite shape constants, would settle the bounded-circulation case of the Liouville conjecture of Koch, Nadirashvili, Seregin and Sverak (Theorem 3); this reduction gives no such conclusion for one fixed C_*. This reduction does not apply to an argument using the additional eternal selection or information from the fixed physical trajectory. For the eternal swirl-record limits available when all late gradient records are uniformly viscous, the attained swirl maximum adds nothing to a Liouville theorem uniform over the constants: such a theorem is equivalent to one for all eternal bounded mild axisymmetric solutions with bounded circulation and nonzero swirl, steady ones included (sec. 3.7). (A) and the vector Landau inequality D^2 <= 6 M H (Theorem 13(e)) already exclude C_* < 1/6 (C_* is the constant of (A), M H <= C_* D^2, for the historical suprema M, D, H of |u|, |grad u|, |grad^2 u|) (the sharp form of this inequality in Frobenius norms, sup|grad U|^2 <= (12/sqrt10) M H for every bounded C^{1,1} field on R^3, improves this to C_* < sqrt10/12 = 0.26352..., the best bound obtainable from the three suprema for all bounded fields, and for divergence-free fields, such as the velocity, sup|grad U|^2 <= B_div'' M H with B_div'' = 3.70253... gives C_* < 1/B_div'' = 0.27008..., Proposition 11(v); an explicit divergence-free field, axisymmetric with swirl, shows that no inequality between the three suprema valid for all such fields can exclude C_* > 0.313019...); no exclusion was obtained for the remaining admissible parameter regime. Proposition 29 shows that the condition inf D/M^2 > 0 over all late times is equivalent to (A) with D/M^2 bounded below at all late gradient records, and to historical swirl domination M <= C_S S; under it (A), (K) and (TAIL) hold on every sufficiently late first-crossing swirl-record sequence, so an exclusion of Case 1 would prove the regularity criterion (SD) that historical swirl domination prevents a finite-time singularity. Under historical swirl domination a singularity must be of Type II in the swirl itself, limsup (T_* - t)^{1/2} S(t) = infinity, since a Type I velocity bound excludes it [CSTY2]. Sufficient conditions proved here are a large-radius compression envelope with divergent scale integral (Theorem 5) and sup R^3 |eta| < infinity (Theorem 4); neither was derived for the Case-1 limit.
(II) Inviscid branch. At the gradient records the rescaled viscosity kappa = D/M^2 tends to 0, the swirl ratio S/M tends to 0, and the gradient-scale limits are ancient swirl-free Euler flows (axisymmetric about a fixed line, or planar). Backward decay ||grad V(-sigma_k)||_infty = o(sigma_k^{-1/2}) along some sequence sigma_k -> infinity, in particular backward gradient windows, would exclude them (Proposition 12); no such estimate was derived, and Proposition 11 shows that it does not follow from the scalar information used so far. The unconditional bounds of Proposition 8(c) that these limits inherit do not exclude them by themselves when C_* >= sqrt7/8 (= 0.3307...): steady planar radial vortices satisfy all of them (Proposition 11(v)), and steady columnar jets do when C_* > 1/2 (Proposition 11(iv)); for C_* < sqrt7/8 there is no such field, planar or axisymmetric without swirl (the inviscid limits have no swirl; Proposition 11(v), by the sharp planar and swirl-free inequalities). If the energy at the gradient scale, M^5/D^3, is bounded below along the records defining a limit, that limit has finite energy and is not planar, and along these records a fixed amount of energy concentrates in balls of radius comparable to M/D (Proposition 11(vi)); planar limits and limits with infinite energy, which include all the examples above, therefore require M^5/D^3 -> 0 along the records. The first alternative forces an atom of the terminal energy measure (the weak-* limit of |u(t)|^2 dx as t -> T_*) at a point of the axis, and hence a failure of energy equality at T_* (Proposition 11(vii)); this is excluded if ||u(t)||_infty = o((T_* - t)^{-3/5}) or ||u||_infty^{5/3} is integrable up to T_*, but neither bound is available, and neither alternative is excluded. In Case 1, (K) and (TAIL) force the gradient records attached to the swirl records in this branch to be separated from them in time (in swirl time units) or in space (on the scale (M^5 D^{-3} r_n^3)^{1/4} when the maximizer is at bounded rescaled distance from the axis), and the gradient maximizers converge to the axis in physical variables (Proposition 11(viii)); no estimate derived here excludes the separation. Alternatively, by Proposition 14 this branch forces the critical potential-vorticity mass N(t) = ||omega^theta/r(t)||_{L^1(dx)} to satisfy N(s_n) >= c_1(C_*)/kappa_n -> infinity at the gradient records, with the constant c_1(C_*) of Proposition 14, so a strict deficit liminf_n kappa_n N(s_n) < c_1(C_*) would exclude it; the available physical balance gives only N(t) = o(S(t)), with S the historical swirl amplitude (when N is finite at some time; Proposition 18(e)), which is too weak: it only forces kappa_n S(s_n) -> infinity, and a truncated form of the balance gives this without the finiteness of N (Proposition 18(f)). When moreover M(s_n)^5/D(s_n)^3 >= epsilon_0 > 0, the truncated balance localizes the deficit: the swirl source d_z(q^2) on the superlevel set {|omega^theta/r| > c_eta D(s_n)^2/(2 M(s_n))}, with c_eta > 0 depending only on C_*, the initial energy E_0 = ||u_0||_2^2 and epsilon_0, at distance r >= c' M(s_n)/D(s_n) from the axis contributes o(1/kappa_n) for every fixed c' > 0, so the required mass of order 1/kappa_n must be produced at distance o(M(s_n)/D(s_n)) from the axis (Proposition 18(f)); no bound on that inner source has been derived. Averaging the truncated balance over a band of levels removes the sign problem of the source at the price of a positive term: in all of branch (II), int int q^4 over the band of levels comparable to D(s_n)^2/(M(s_n) B_n) up to time s_n must be at least c D(s_n) M(s_n)/B_n, B_n being the distance of the gradient maximizer from the axis in units M(s_n)/D(s_n) plus a constant (Proposition 18(h)); no upper bound small enough to contradict this lower bound has been derived.
(Critical functionals.) The Y_p family of critical weighted swirl energies (Proposition 16) has one unsigned term, an inflow term. Other functionals leave additional unsigned terms; the coupled meridional energy has cubic, pressure and axis-flux terms after cancellation of the swirl transfer. The conditional absorption criteria stated in Proposition 16 (a global inflow bound or a smallness of the stream function) were not derived from the Case-1 assumptions, and their global weighted-integral justification is not fully supplied here. In Case 1 the critical inflow integral is necessarily infinite (Proposition 18). No compatible bound on the total has been obtained; spatial or temporal localization is another possible approach.
(Unified sufficient condition.) In both branches it would suffice that, for some constant c_0, the meridional vector potential of the swirl-record limit U satisfies sup_{tau <= 0} ||(psi_U(R, Z, tau) - c_0 R/2) e_theta||_{BMO(R^3)} < infinity (Proposition 19(b), via the Hoelder estimate of Lei and Zhang). This was not derived. Proposition 19 also shows that in Case 1, for every C, some normalized phase tau_C carries liminf_n N(t_n + T_n tau_C) >= C, so the bound sup_tau liminf_n N(t_n + T_n tau) < infinity, which would give the BMO bound, cannot hold.
(Localized physical form.) At every singular point (0, z_*, T_*) the solution is of Type II in the sense of Seregin, and for every rho > 0 the local critical mass int_{C_rho(z_*)} |omega^theta/r| dx is unbounded as t -> T_* (Proposition 20). A contradiction along this line needs an upper bound, uniform as t -> T_*, for that local mass or for the local BMO norm of the meridional vector potential B = psi^theta e_theta (defined in Proposition 19) on one cylinder around the singular point; either bound would give a contradiction by the argument of Proposition 20(c), which uses [Se20, sec. 3] qualitatively, and no estimate derived here gives one. (A) does not enter the available local inequalities; this does not show that it cannot help in combination with other estimates.
(Far-field one-sided form.) The circulation of every Case-1 limit U saturates at large normalized radius, and saturation forces strong inflow there (Proposition 23): for every R_0 >= 1 there are L and n_0 such that, for every index n >= n_0 of the subsequence defining U, the physical solution has a point of the window W_n(R_0, L) := {R_0 r_n < r <= L r_n, |z - z_n| <= L r_n, t_n - L^2 T_n <= t <= t_n} with Gamma > gamma_n (A - m) and -r u^r > 2, where A = sup Gamma_U and m = m(R_0) > 0 is the deficit of Proposition 23(b). Hence the following would exclude Case 1: for some fixed R_0 >= 1 and every finite L, the bound -r u^r <= 2 holds, for all sufficiently large indices of that subsequence (the first index may depend on L), on W_n(R_0, L) intersected with {Gamma > gamma_n (A - m)}. This is a localized sufficient form of critical meridional control. By Proposition 25 the bound is needed only at such points where moreover d_r Gamma > 0, and it would follow from the weighted critical vorticity bound calQ <= 4 there (calQ is the weighted integral of |omega^theta| of Proposition 25(c), which bounds 2 r |u^r| by the Biot-Savart law); an explicit bounded drift model indicates that the scalar circulation equation, incompressibility and the record conditions are consistent with strong far-field inflow (its circulation is obtained by a monotone exhaustion whose elliptic estimates are not reproduced here, and the model fails the vorticity equation); posed for the whole class LL, the same bound is equivalent to the Liouville problem for LL (this is not automatic for the subclass of physical limits); and an exact exterior solution, the Landau meridional flow with a potential swirl, shows that bounded velocity, potential swirl, bounded signed flux and the exterior equations alone allow -r u^r > 2 on a cone reaching infinity (Proposition 25(f)). Averaging the circulation equation over cylinders and long boxes expresses the averaged circulation through the correlation of inflow and circulation at larger radii (Proposition 26); at each fixed radius rho the mean circulation deficit in all sufficiently long boxes is at least 2 nu A/(K rho + 3 nu) minus any prescribed epsilon, averaged saturation forbids a critical one-sided outflow bound, and averaged saturation was not derived. An averaged exclusion would follow if one fixed family of long boxes and one common normalized positive averaging functional MM (a Banach limit of the box means) satisfied MM[Gamma_U(r_*)^2] > 0 at some radius r_*, together with MM[(Phi_rho - c_rho)^2] <= nu^2 rho^2 C(rho)^2 for every sufficiently large rho, where Phi_rho is the axial flux of U through the disk of radius rho, nu = 1/gamma_* is the viscosity of U, each c_rho is bounded in time and int^infinity d rho/[rho(1 + C(rho)^2)] = infinity (Proposition 26(i)). Neither positive mass nor the required flux bound has been derived for the same family. By Proposition 26(l), positive mass in some family is equivalent to the existence of a shift-invariant measure on the hull of axial-temporal translates of U that charges nonconstant fields; limits without such a measure (density-trivial limits) have zero long-box means for the circulation-weighted quantities and derivative-energy terms considered here, and this includes structures uniformly localized in the axial direction throughout their past; velocity moments need not vanish, and excluding these limits needs information beyond those vanishing averages, for example an unaveraged or Z-integrated argument. The averaged energy budgets (Proposition 26(k)) do not supply the flux bound, and by Proposition 26(j) it would follow from critical averaged decay of the axial velocity fluctuation, which was not derived either. The available flux bound is one power of the radius weaker, and the first construction of Proposition 26(i), an exact scalar solution with bounded drift and slowly increasing axial wavelength, saturates, which shows that the scalar circulation equation alone cannot supply the critical bound (the corrector error bounds of that construction are not reproduced here, and the solution fails the meridional vorticity equation). For axially localized limits, Proposition 26(g) instead requires positive axial-integrated weighted mass, explicit trace integrability, a radial growth bound O(rho^alpha) with alpha < 2, and a weighted mean inflow at most kappa times the weighted mass, for one constant kappa < (2 - alpha) nu at all large radii (a ratio below the threshold with a gap tending to zero does not suffice). For a physical finite-box argument, the adverse earlier-time inventory and axial boundary errors must be controlled relative to the actual Dirichlet contribution throughout the radial range used. On the near-maximal set {R > R_0, Gamma_U > A - m} of Proposition 23(b), where m = (A/2) e^{-lambda_{R_0}}, the circulation is almost flat, and Proposition 23(e) bounds the instantaneous local swirl source of the meridional vorticity by 2 A (4 m (R h + 2 d))^{1/2}/R^3, with d and h bounds for the first and second derivatives of U on the meridional ball of radius R/2; this is exponentially small in lambda_{R_0}. It does not locate the vorticity producing the inflow, because existing local vorticity can reflect earlier creation and transport, and the bound -r u^r <= 2 on these windows was not derived.
(Near-axis strain.) The circulation is absorbed by the radial strain k(t) := ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty <= ||grad u(t)||_infty: |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G (1 - exp(-r^2 w)) with w^{-1} = 4 int_0^h exp(-2 int_{sigma - v}^{sigma} k) dv, for 0 < h <= sigma < T_* (viscosity one, as in sec. 1.1), a Burgers-type comparison that uses the circulation bound G and no finer information on earlier data (Proposition 33(a)). Consequently either limsup (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity (Type II near-axis strain), or (T_* - t) S(t)^2 is bounded near T_* (Type I swirl); these alternatives are not exclusive. Type I swirl already follows when only the integrals of k over the dyadic windows [T_* - 2h, T_* - h] are bounded, and then the time-integrated compression condition (CW) of Proposition 37(e) holds for every limit (Proposition 39(f)(xii)). In the second alternative every Case-1 limit U satisfies ||U^theta(tau)||_infty = O(|tau|^{-1/2}) as tau -> -infinity, the swirl records t_n satisfy (T_* - t_n)/T_n <= C_I/gamma_n (T_n = r_n/S_n is the record time scale, and C_I the Type I swirl constant, (T_* - t) S(t)^2 <= C_I, Proposition 33), every local limit of translates U(. + z_k e_3, . + s_k) with z_k in R and s_k -> -infinity is a constant axial field, and grad U tends to 0 uniformly on each cylinder around the axis as tau -> -infinity. In both alternatives the cumulative backward strain of U over [-v, 0] exceeds (1/2) log v by an amount that tends to infinity as v -> infinity, whereas a cumulative strain of at most (1/2) log v + C along some sequence v_j -> infinity would force U to be constant (Proposition 33(f)(iii), (iv)). Neither alternative is excluded: the Type I swirl limits would be excluded by a one-sided Type I bound for their inflow on the circulation superlevel sets (Proposition 38), which was not derived, and no iterated-logarithm strengthening of limsup (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity is obtained in the Type II alternative without the historical swirl domination of Proposition 33(d).
(Strain from vorticity and the Type I swirl branch.) The near-axis strain is controlled by the potential vorticity: ||u^r/r||_infty <= (2 ||u^r||_infty ||omega^theta/r||_infty)^{1/2} (Proposition 34(a)), and the circulation absorption of Proposition 33 needs the strain only where |Gamma| exceeds a given level (Proposition 34(b)). For a Case-1 limit U this gives: for every lambda in [0, 1) the compression (U^R/R)^- must exceed 1/(2|tau|) on the superlevel set {|Gamma_U| > lambda} in a time-integrated sense, and ||eta_U(-s)||_infty <= 1/(8 K_U s^2) (K_U := ||U^R||_infty) cannot hold for all large s. On the Type I swirl branch, for lambda in (0, 1), the superlevel set lies beyond the radius rho_lambda(tau) = lambda (gamma_* (tau_* + |tau|)/C_I)^{1/2} (here tau_* in [0, C_I/gamma_*] is the limit of (T_* - t_n)/T_n along a further subsequence, Proposition 33(e)(i), not the time parameter of Proposition 38), a positive multiple of the parabolic radius |tau|^{1/2}, so U needs, in the same time-integrated sense, inflow -U^R > R/(2|tau|) at points of that region, and ||eta_U(-s)||_infty tends to 0 at least like 1/log s; no intermediate decay rate is established here from Type I swirl alone; under the additional hypothesis (CW), or under the self-similar core source bound (H3) of Proposition 39, Proposition 39 gives the conditional rate O(s^{-3/2}), which does not reach the excluded bound either. A swirl Type I bound ||u^theta(t)||_infty <= C (T - t)^{-1/2} with C < 3^{-1/4} excludes a singularity at time T of an axisymmetric H^2 solution with viscosity 1, without any circulation hypothesis (Proposition 35, from estimates of Chen, Fang and Zhang and of Wei), so every solution as in sec. 1.1 has limsup (T_* - t) ||u^theta(t)||_infty^2 >= 3^{-1/2}; this does not exclude the Type I swirl branch. Combined with the pointwise circulation bound and the strain comparison of Proposition 33(a), (b), (35.2) gives limsup (T_* - t) ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty >= 1/2 + 2/(3^{1/2} mu_0 G^2), with mu_0 = max_{x > 0} (1 - e^{-x})^2/x = 0.4072..., for every singular solution, and a weighted energy in which the circulation bound controls ||u^theta/r||_infty replaces the term 2/(3^{1/2} mu_0 G^2) by the larger term (3/2) mu_0^{-1/3} G^{-4/3} when G >= 1.659 (35.3); this sharpens the constraint C_a > 1/2 of Proposition 33(e)(ii) on the Type I strain branch and excludes neither branch. Proposition 36 caps the drift of the comparison diffusion for the circulation both by the near-axis strain and by the inflow: if ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty <= alpha/(T_* - t) and ||(u^r)^-(t)||_infty <= C(T_* - t) (T_* - t)^{-1/2} with a continuous nonincreasing envelope C >= 2 that grows so slowly that a spectral integral satisfies Lambda(v)/C(v)^2 -> infinity as v -> 0 (alpha > 1/2 fixed), then the circulation decays at the axis, uniformly in time, like exp(-c Lambda(r)), faster than every power of 1/|log r|. On the Type I strain branch of a Case-1 trajectory this gives limsup (T_* - t) ||(u^r)^-(t)||_infty^2/log log(1/(T_* - t)) >= 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1), which raises the coefficient 1 of Proposition 31(d) to 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1) (at most 1 + min{3^{1/2} mu_0 G^2/4, mu_0^{1/3} G^{4/3}/3} by (35.3)); this is a necessary growth condition for the inflow and excludes neither branch.
(Strain records and a swirl barrier.) On the Type II strain branch the near-axis strain has records: times sigma_j -> T_* at which k = ||(u^r/r)^-||_infty equals its running maximum K_j, with (T_* - sigma_j) K_j -> infinity. At a minimum point of u^r/r at such a time the pressure satisfies p_r/r >= (u^theta/r)^2 - K_j^2, and p_zz <= -4 K_j^2 if that point lies on the axis; the infinite-energy Burgers vortex with z-independent swirl attains equality in both, as a local model that does not realize the Type II history, and the circulation bound gives S(sigma_j)^2 <= (mu_0 G^2/2 + o(1)) K_j (Proposition 37(a), (b)). The limits normalized at these records are either viscous, with nonzero swirl by the swirl-free Liouville theorem of Koch, Nadirashvili, Seregin and Sverak, or, under (A) and a gradient bound D <= C K_j, along subsequences swirl-free ancient Euler flows whose bounded-gradient and compression normalizations are shared by steady vortex rings in their comoving frame; neither is excluded. Under the Type I swirl bound a positive limiting viscosity is impossible at these records, which have S(sigma_j) = o(M(sigma_j)) and K_j = o(M(sigma_j)^2), while the inviscid regime remains, with the additional hypotheses needed for its compactness (Proposition 37, Remark (2)). On the Type I swirl branch a barrier for the equation of U^theta/R on cylinders around the axis gives ||U^theta/R(tau)||_infty = o(|tau|^{-1/2}) as tau -> -infinity for every Case-1 limit, and O(1/|tau|) unless |tau| sup{(U^R/R)^-(y, tau) : R < |tau|^{1/2}} is unbounded as tau -> -infinity (Proposition 37(c), (d)), and O(1/|tau|) also when only the integrals of that supremum over the dyadic windows t <= |tau| <= 2 t stay bounded, the condition (CW) of Proposition 37(e); a smooth bounded test field, which with an added swirl has bounded circulation and Type I swirl, fails (CW) with zero potential vorticity in the parabolic cylinders at large times; it violates the evolution equations and the normalization of the limits, and whether the failure of (CW) is compatible with all properties of Case-1 limits is not known (Proposition 37, Remark (5)); (CW) on the parabolic cylinders implies the same bound on every fixed multiple of them (Remark (5)(c)); neither rate reaches the decay of the potential vorticity that Proposition 34(d)(ii) excludes. A compression bound (U^R/R)^- <= A/L(tau)^2 on cylinders {R < L(tau)} for all sufficiently negative tau, with radii L(tau) nondecreasing backward in time and growing faster than |tau|^{3/4}, would exclude the branch (Proposition 37, Remark (3)); it is not known. Albritton and Barker relate non-trivial bounded mild ancient solutions with a finite scale-invariant quantity I (a supremum over all parabolic balls) to suitable weak solutions with Type I singular points; combined with Seregin's exclusion of axisymmetric Type I singular points (Proposition 37, Remark (4)) this excludes non-trivial bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solutions with I < infinity, and I < infinity is not known for these limits.
(Type I inflow.) The circulation equation in similarity variables has a supersolution that grows logarithmically at large normalized radius, so a bounded smooth ancient axisymmetric solution with positive viscosity and circulation |Gamma| <= G whose inflow satisfies U^R >= -C (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} - theta R (tau_* - tau)^{-1} at the points where |Gamma| > lambda, with tau_* > 0, C >= 0, 0 <= theta < 1/2 and 0 <= lambda < G, has |Gamma| <= lambda everywhere; with lambda = 0 and mildness it is a constant axial field (Proposition 38). In particular bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solutions with bounded circulation and a Type I bound on the velocity vanish, without spatial decay or scale-invariant bounds. For every Case-1 limit, on either branch, the inflow therefore exceeds C s^{-1/2} + theta R/s, for every C >= 0, every theta in [0, 1/2) and every lambda in [0, 1), at points of the superlevel sets {|Gamma_U| > lambda} at arbitrarily late backward times s; on the Type I swirl branch these points lie beyond rho_lambda. In the time-integrated form, the spatial supremum over these sets of the positive part of the normalized excess of the compression over C R^{-1} s^{-1/2} + theta/s has a positive lower average in logarithmic time. The kinematic family of Proposition 37, Remark (3), satisfies both conditions (the second asymptotically), so an exclusion using Proposition 38(a) would require establishing its inflow hypothesis, which was not derived. Through a Feynman-Kac representation of the potential vorticity, Proposition 39 derives the inflow bound, and so excludes the Type I swirl branch, under two further hypotheses on the limit: exterior inflow outside the parabolic cylinders {R < M |tau|^{1/2}} (or the weaker U^R <= C/R there, if M^2 >= (1 + 2^{1/2}) C) and a self-similar bound for the source d_Z(q_U^2) inside them; a circulation-energy identity along the backward paths controls the exterior source. Under Type I compression on the parabolic cylinders (A_* < infinity, Proposition 37(d)), in particular on the Type I strain branch (k(t) <= C_a/(T_* - t)), and more generally under its time-integrated form (CW) (Proposition 39(f)(xi)), an energy along the backward paths joining q inside the cylinders and the circulation outside them replaces the hypothesis on the core source, and the exclusion holds under the exterior hypothesis alone, even in the weaker form U^R <= kappa R/|tau| with kappa < 1 outside the cylinders: every limit on the Type I swirl branch violates (CW) (in particular has A_* = infinity) or, for every M >= 1 and every kappa in [0, 1), has points with R >= M |tau|^{1/2} and U^R > kappa R/|tau| at arbitrarily late backward times; the same holds with the cone-local window bound (CW_loc) of Proposition 39(f)(xiii) in place of (CW), with such points in the Euler cone max{R, |Z|} < A_c |tau|. For the physical solution: a trajectory with (K), (TAIL) and the Type I strain bound, or only bounded integrals of k over the dyadic windows [T_* - 2h, T_* - h] (Proposition 39(f)(xii)), cannot satisfy u^r <= kappa r/(T_* - t) with kappa < 1, or u^r <= C/r, on the regions r >= M_0 (T_* - t)^{1/2} for t near T_*, for any fixed M_0. The required exterior bound has not been derived; (CW) follows under the physical strain hypotheses just stated, but neither those hypotheses nor (CW) has been established from Type I swirl alone. Within the standing Type I swirl setting, under A_* < infinity, under (H3) (the self-similar core source bound), or under bounded dyadic window integrals of the compression on the part of the cylinders inside an Euler cone max{R, |Z|} < A_c |tau| with A_c > A_3 (a hypothesis weaker than (CW), Proposition 39(f)(xiii)), the exterior inflow hypothesis can be replaced by hypotheses on the vorticity or on the source only: a Dini-type decay of |tau| |omega^theta_U| outside the cylinders, or, more weakly, smallness of the masses of |omega^theta_U| (unsigned circulations) in the meridional half-plane near each exterior point and in the dyadic annuli about it, weighted at the scale of the distance (Proposition 39(f)(vi), (vii)), or the scale-invariant bound int_s^T ||d_Z(q_U^2)(-beta)||_{L^1(R^3)} dbeta <= B_0 (1 + log(T/s)) for the total unsigned source (Proposition 39(f)(viii)); none of these was derived. Since the comparison localizes, the inflow required by the survival of the circulation already occurs inside the Euler cone max{R, |Z|} < 2 (K + nu_*) |tau|, at times in every window [T_0, T_0^p] with p > p_* and T_0 large (Proposition 38(e)); accordingly the source bound is needed only in boxes of size proportional to |tau| (Proposition 39(f)(ix)), which allows any number of Euler-scale cells along the axis; for the fixed-amplitude periodic model profiles of Proposition 39(f)(ix), with non-trivial axial variation and axial scale l(|tau|), this form holds when l(|tau|) >= c |tau| and fails when l(|tau|)/|tau| -> 0; wavelength alone does not decide it for general profiles. In terms of the meridional field, with no compression hypothesis, the same contradiction follows from an Euler-scale axial regularity of the strain on a cone max{R, |Z|} < A_c |tau| with A_c > A_3, |d_Z(U^R/R)| <= C |tau|^{-2}, together with the one-sided bound R d_R(U^R/R) <= eps/|tau| with 0 <= eps < 1 (Proposition 39(f)(x)), since this regularity bounds the compression on the cone and that bound replaces A_* < infinity in the estimates localized to the cone; this was not derived, and the Type I bound on the potential vorticity does not give it through the elliptic relation.
Summary. No contradiction or fixed-datum counterexample has been established. Theorem 13 gives two possible subsequential regimes. Proposed sufficient exclusions include an appropriate viscous Liouville theorem, the backward decay of Proposition 12, a strict critical-mass deficit, and suitably quantified BMO or inflow control. None was derived. Proposition 15 selects an eternal limit, but not within an arbitrarily prescribed branch. Propositions 19 to 26 add necessary conditions and local identities; their joint consistency is not established, and no contradiction among them has been derived. Proposition 27 gives (with a proof sketch containing the key estimates), under a uniform bound for the cutoff solutions, finite-energy solutions regular on a prescribed finite interval that approximate a specified normalized ancient solution on a fixed window. They retain bounded circulation and the stated window and tail bounds; an additional boundary-gap hypothesis gives the record inequality at a window maximum. Proposition 28 proves |grad U|^2 <= B_ax M H at axis points, B_ax = 3.860749266..., and |grad U|^2 <= 3.9184 M H at all points, for bounded axisymmetric divergence-free fields with swirl. Under (A) it raises the exclusion C_* < 0.25452... obtained first from Proposition 11(v) to C_* < 0.25520..., and for C_* < 1/B_ax = 0.2590170796... it confines the late gradient records to a shell in the variable r D/M. Both consequences are superseded by the sharp inequality of Proposition 11(v), which gives |grad U|^2 <= (12/sqrt10) M H at every point of every bounded C^{1,1} field on R^3, with 12/sqrt10 = 3.794733... < B_ax, and excludes C_* < sqrt10/12 = 0.263523...; for divergence-free fields Proposition 11(v) also gives |grad U|^2 <= B_div'' M H with B_div'' = 3.702534..., which excludes C_* < 1/B_div'' = 0.270085...; so no admissible C_* lies in the range C_* < 1/B_ax of the shell statement. Proposition 29 shows that a uniform lower bound for D/M^2 at all late times is equivalent to historical swirl domination M <= C_S S, under which (A), (K) and (TAIL) hold automatically; an exclusion of Case 1 would therefore prove the regularity criterion (SD) that historical swirl domination excludes a finite-time singularity, which the sources checked do not establish. Proposition 30 shows, by a comparison for the circulation and the Kolmogorov-Petrovskii integral test, that on every Case-1 trajectory, and under historical swirl domination, no lower-class envelope can bound the cumulative inward radial displacement, the time integral of ||(u^r)^-||_infty, on all sufficiently short terminal windows, or uniformly on all sufficiently late sliding windows; as a consequence, limsup [(T_* - t) ||(u^r)^-(t)||_infty^2 - log log(1/(T_* - t)) - (3/2) log log log(1/(T_* - t))] = +infinity. Proposition 31 keeps the exact radial operator, so that the comparison diffusion is a time-scaled Bessel process of dimension zero with an additional outward drift whose cumulative displacement is bounded by the envelope, and raises the coefficient 3/2 to 5/2; with the circulation criterion [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], it also shows that every singular solution satisfies the same limsup statement with any coefficient below 3/2 in place of 5/2 (the corresponding statement in [Sh, Corollary 5.4] has coefficients below 1/2). Proposition 32 bounds the scale-invariant inflow -r u^r pointwise near the axis instead of its time integral: by a stationary supersolution built from the scale function of a radial comparison diffusion, a bound -r u^r <= 2 - kappa/log(1/r) near the axis at late times, with kappa > 1, forces |Gamma| <= C (log(1/r))^{1 - kappa}. Hence, with Lambda(r, t) := sup_z (-r u^r(r, z, t)), every singular solution satisfies liminf_{(r, t) -> (0, T_*)} log(1/r) (2 - Lambda(r, t)) <= 3, and <= 5/2 conditionally on [Wei], and every Case-1 trajectory satisfies it with 1 in place of 3. These results restrict the inflow and exclude neither branch. Proposition 33 bounds the circulation by the cumulative radial strain ||(u^r/r)^-||_infty and splits Case 1 into Type II near-axis strain and Type I swirl; in the second alternative grad U tends to 0 uniformly on each cylinder of fixed radius around the axis as tau -> -infinity and every local limit of backward translates of a Case-1 limit is a constant axial field (the constant may depend on the sequence; convergence to one common constant is not proved), and no Liouville theorem covering these limits is known to us. Proposition 34 bounds the near-axis strain by the potential vorticity, localizes the absorption to superlevel sets of the circulation, and shows that on the Type I swirl branch the Case-1 limits need inflow of self-similar size beyond a multiple of the parabolic radius and have potential vorticity that decays at least like 1/log s but not below 1/(8 K_U s^2) at all large s; Proposition 35 shows that a Type I swirl bound ||u^theta(t)||_infty <= C (T_* - t)^{-1/2} with C < 3^{-1/4} nu^{1/2} (in the squared form used above, a constant C_I < 3^{-1/2} nu) excludes a singularity and, in the viscosity-one setting of sec. 1.1, combined with the circulation bound, that every singular solution has limsup (T_* - t) ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty >= 1/2 + c_G, where c_G = max{2/(3^{1/2} mu_0 G^2), (3/2) mu_0^{-1/3} G^{-4/3}} and mu_0 = 0.4072.... Proposition 36 shows that, under a Type I bound k(t) <= alpha/(T_* - t) with a fixed alpha > 1/2 for the near-axis strain, an inflow bound ||(u^r)^-(t)||_infty^2 <= kappa (log log(1/(T_* - t)) + B)/(T_* - t) with kappa > 0, kappa (1 - 1/(2 alpha)) < 1 and B large enough for the envelope conditions of Proposition 36(d) forces the circulation to decay at the axis; on a Case-1 trajectory with Type I strain constant C_a this gives limsup (T_* - t) ||(u^r)^-(t)||_infty^2/log log(1/(T_* - t)) >= 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1). Proposition 37 gives strain records on the Type II strain branch and a cylinder barrier for the swirl of the Type I swirl limits, and excludes neither branch. Proposition 38 is a Liouville theorem in similarity variables: a one-sided Type I bound for the inflow on a circulation superlevel set {|Gamma| > lambda} forces |Gamma| <= lambda; this bound was not derived for the limits. Proposition 39 represents the potential vorticity of a Type I swirl limit through its swirl source along backward five-dimensional diffusions and excludes the limit under each of several hypotheses on the strain or on the source, none of which was derived. Proposition 40 shows that the backward circulation paths of such a limit are killed at the axis almost surely, which excludes it, if the source bound (39.19_H) holds on Euler boxes of a slope H > K with a dyadic budget B such that 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + 0.735 B/nu < 1/2; neither this bound nor the smallness of B was derived. Its Remarks reduce the exclusion, without the source bound, to a bound on the actual strain U^R/R along the backward circulation paths (sec. 4, item 1), which was not derived either. The o(r_n) window-dissipation target is false. These observations leave distinct unproved estimates; they do not establish an equivalent reformulation of the original problem.

## 1. Result

### 1.1 Setting

u is a smooth finite-energy axisymmetric solution of the Navier-Stokes equations on R^3 x [0, T_*) with viscosity 1, smooth decaying data u_0, maximal classical solution with first singular time T_* < infinity, E_0 := ||u_0||_{L^2(R^3)}^2, and circulation Gamma = r u^theta with |Gamma| <= G := ||r u_0^theta||_infty (maximum principle), where G < infinity is assumed (finite energy and smoothness do not imply it). Historical quantities are suprema over [0, t]:
  M(t) = sup_{s <= t} ||u(s)||_infty, D(t) = sup_{s <= t} ||grad u(s)||_infty, H(t) = sup_{s <= t} ||grad^2 u(s)||_infty, S(t) = sup_{s <= t} ||u^theta(s)||_infty,
with Cartesian (Frobenius) tensor norms. Hypotheses of the case:
 (A) M(t) H(t) <= C_* D(t)^2 for all t in [t_A, T_*), for some t_A < T_*.
 Swirl first-crossing records (r_n, z_n, t_n): S_n := S(t_n) = |u^theta(r_n, z_n, t_n)| -> infinity, t_n first time at which S reaches S_n. Normalization gamma_n = r_n S_n, T_n = r_n/S_n, U_n(y, tau) = u(r_n y', z_n + r_n y_3, t_n + T_n tau)/S_n, which solves NS with viscosity nu_n = 1/gamma_n.
 (K) limsup_n sup_{|y| <= L, -A <= tau <= 0} |U_n| <= K for all L, A < infinity.
 (TAIL) lim_{L -> infinity} limsup_n sup_{-A <= tau <= 0} int_{|y| > L} |U_n|^2 |y|^{-4} dy = 0 for each A.

LL denotes the class of bounded mild ancient solutions W of NS on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] (viscosity 1), axisymmetric about the x_3 axis, with Gamma_W = r W^theta bounded and W^theta not identically 0.

Further notation. Cylindrical coordinates (r, theta, z) refer to the x_3 axis; normalized limits use (R, Theta, Z) and time tau. The meridional velocity is b = u^r e_r + u^z e_z (V or U^b for limits), omega^theta is the angular vorticity, q := u^theta/r and eta := omega^theta/r (potential vorticity). Delta_5 := d_rr + 3 r^{-1} d_r + d_zz is the Laplacian of R^5 acting on functions of (r, z), and L := d_RR - R^{-1} d_R + d_ZZ is the operator of the circulation equation d_t Gamma + b.grad Gamma = L Gamma (nu L Gamma at viscosity nu). For axisymmetric functions with sufficient decay, int phi Delta_5 F dx = int F L phi dx - 4 pi int F(0, z) phi(0, z) dz. The angular stream function psi^theta, with b = curl(psi^theta e_theta), is written psi^theta = r phi (phi is the 5D stream potential); then u^r = -r phi_z, u^z = 2 phi + r phi_r, -Delta_5 phi = eta, and the 5D divergence of b is div_5 b = d_r u^r + 3 u^r/r + d_z u^z = 2 u^r/r. C_P < infinity and t_P < T_* are constants with D(t) <= C_P M(t)^2 for t in [t_P, T_*) (historical mild smoothing; C_P is absolute). A gradient record is a time s with ||grad u(s)||_infty = D(s); kappa(s) := D(s)/M(s)^2 (Theorem 13), N(t) := ||eta(t)||_{L^1(dx)} (Proposition 14), and C_0, C_2 = 1 + C_0(1 + log_+ C_*) are the constants of Theorem 7. The smoothing estimate for bounded mild ancient solutions is used repeatedly: a bounded mild ancient solution W with ||W||_infty <= K_0 and viscosity nu satisfies ||d_tau^m grad^k W||_infty <= C(k, m, K_0, nu) on its whole past (proved as the extraction of Theorem 2, without the far field).

### 1.2 What was proved

The numbered results 1 to 40 below are stated with all their hypotheses. Their conditional hypotheses and external inputs (cited at the point of use, listed in sec. 4, item 5, and resolved in the References) are part of the statements. Each item is followed by its proof, or by its key estimates together with an explicit statement of the steps not reproduced, and ends with a Status line recording the extent of the argument given here, its source and its verification. Items whose complete argument is not reproduced say so and are not checkable from the report alone; the report does not rely on any other document for the arguments it presents; the verification record (sec. 5) does not certify every argument or subsequent summary sentence.

Theorem 1 (normalization and record identity). S(t) -> infinity as t -> T_*, so first-crossing records exist, and at each record with S_n > S(0) (then t_n > 0; this excludes at most finitely many records of a sequence with S_n -> infinity) -r_n u^r(r_n, z_n, t_n) >= 1. Under (K): K^2 >= 1 + G^{-2} (so K > 1 is a consequence), every limit point gamma_* of gamma_n lies in [(K^2 - 1)^{-1/2}, G], the limit viscosity nu_* = 1/gamma_* lies in [1/G, (K^2 - 1)^{1/2}], r_n -> 0, and the backward depth t_n/T_n tends to infinity.

Proof. Write b = u^r e_r + u^z e_z; the swirl satisfies d_t u^theta + b.grad u^theta + u^r u^theta/r = (Delta - r^{-2}) u^theta with Delta = d_rr + r^{-1} d_r + d_zz. (a) S(t) -> infinity. If S(t) <= S_0 for all t < T_*, then |Gamma| = r |u^theta| <= S_0 r <= C |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= 1/4 and all t < T_* (r (log r)^2 is bounded on (0, 1/4]). By [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] (for the strong axisymmetric solution with data in H^{1/2} and Gamma_0 in L^infty, a bound sup_{0 <= t < T} |Gamma(t, r, z)| <= C_1 |log r|^{-2} for r <= delta_0, with any delta_0 in (0, 1/2) and any C_1 > 1, implies global regularity), applied with the smooth decaying data u_0, or after restarting at a positive time t_0 < T_* with data u(t_0), the solution would not break down at T_*, a contradiction. Since S is nondecreasing, S(t) -> infinity. (b) Records. s -> ||u^theta(s)||_infty is continuous on [0, T_*), so for every level lambda > ||u_0^theta||_infty there is a first time t(lambda) with ||u^theta(t(lambda))||_infty = lambda = S(t(lambda)); since u^theta(t(lambda)) is continuous, tends to 0 at spatial infinity and vanishes on the axis, the value lambda is attained at a point with r > 0. Levels S_n -> infinity give records with t_n -> T_*, because S is finite on [0, t] for every t < T_*. (c) Record identity. After the reflection x_2 -> -x_2 if necessary (it maps u^theta to -u^theta and preserves u^r, u^z and the equations), u^theta(r_n, z_n, t_n) = S_n > 0. For S_n > S(0), so that t_n > 0, d_t u^theta >= 0 at the point (one-sided derivative; t -> u^theta(r_n, z_n, t) is maximal at t_n on [0, t_n]), and d_r u^theta = d_z u^theta = 0, (d_rr + d_zz) u^theta <= 0 there (global spatial maximum). The equation at this point gives u^r S_n/r_n = -d_t u^theta + (d_rr + d_zz) u^theta - S_n/r_n^2 <= -S_n/r_n^2, i.e. -r_n u^r(r_n, z_n, t_n) >= 1. Only the classical equation at one point is used. (d) Constants. In normalized variables U_n^theta(e_1, 0) = 1, |U_n^theta| <= 1 on R^3 x [-t_n/T_n, 0] (|u^theta(x, t)| <= S(t) <= S_n for t <= t_n), and -gamma_n U_n^R(e_1, 0) = -r_n u^r(r_n, z_n, t_n) >= 1. Hence |U_n(e_1, 0)|^2 >= (U_n^theta)^2 + (U_n^R)^2 >= 1 + gamma_n^{-2} >= 1 + G^{-2}, since gamma_n = |Gamma(r_n, z_n, t_n)| <= G. By (K) with L = 2, A = 1, for every eps > 0 and n large |U_n(e_1, 0)| <= K + eps; so K^2 >= 1 + G^{-2} (in particular K > 1), and gamma_n^{-2} <= (K + eps)^2 - 1, whence liminf gamma_n >= (K^2 - 1)^{-1/2}, while gamma_n <= G. Every limit point gamma_* therefore lies in [(K^2 - 1)^{-1/2}, G], and nu_* = 1/gamma_* in [1/G, (K^2 - 1)^{1/2}]. Finally r_n = gamma_n/S_n <= G/S_n -> 0, and t_n/T_n = t_n S_n/r_n = t_n S_n^2/gamma_n >= t_n S_n^2/G -> infinity, because t_n -> T_* > 0.

Status: proved here; source: own derivation (using [LZ2, Corollary 1.3]); verification: adversarial audit rounds 1, 21, 22.

Theorem 2 (extraction through the terminal time). Pass to a subsequence with a fixed sign of the record swirl and, if necessary, reflect the angular coordinate so that u^theta(r_n, z_n, t_n) = S_n > 0. Under (K) and (TAIL), a further subsequence of U_n converges in C^{2,1}_loc(R^3 x (-infinity, 0]), including tau = 0, to a bounded ancient mild axisymmetric solution U of NS with viscosity nu_* and canonical pressure gradient, satisfying |U| <= K, |U^theta| <= 1 = U^theta(e_1, 0), -gamma_* U^R(e_1, 0) >= 1, |Gamma_U| <= G/gamma_*.

Key estimates. Mild with viscosity nu means U(tau) = e^{nu(tau - sigma) Delta} U(sigma) - int_sigma^tau e^{nu(tau - s) Delta} Pi div(U (x) U)(s) ds for sigma < tau <= 0 (Pi the Leray projector); the canonical pressure gradient of a bounded field is grad P = grad R_iR_j(chi U^i U^j) + int grad d_i d_j N(. - z) (1 - chi(z)) U^i U^j(z) dz (N the Newtonian potential, R_i the Riesz transforms, chi a compactly supported cutoff equal to 1 near the point; the result does not depend on chi). By Duhamel's formula for the physical solution (p = R_iR_j(u_i u_j)), U_n is mild with viscosity nu_n on [-t_n/T_n, 0]. (1) Kernels. The kernel O^h of e^{h Delta} Pi div satisfies |d^alpha O^h(x)| <= C_alpha (|x| + sqrt h)^{-4-|alpha|}, int |O^h| = c h^{-1/2}, int |O^h(x + e) - O^h(x)| dx <= C min(h^{-1/2}, |e| h^{-1}), int grad O^h = 0 and int |grad O^h(x)| |x|^a dx = c_a h^{-1+a/2} (0 < a < 1); the far pressure kernel satisfies |grad^m d_j d_k N(x)| <= C |x|^{-3-m}. (2) Tail. J_n(L, A) := sup_{-A <= s <= 0} int_{|z| > L} |U_n(z, s)|^2 |z|^{-4} dz. (TAIL) gives lim_L limsup_n J_n(L, A) = 0, and with (K), limsup_n J_n(L, A) < infinity for fixed L, A (the shell L < |z| < L_1 contributes at most 4 pi (K + 1)^2/L). (3) Local bounds. Fix L, A >= 1, k >= 0 and n_0 with nu_n in [nu_*/2, 2 nu_*] and |U_n| <= K + 1 on B_{64L} x [-A - 3, 0] for n >= n_0. Take radii 16L = rho_0 > rho_1 > ... > rho_{k+4} = 2L, restart times sigma_j = -A - 2 - 2^{-j} and delays delta_j = 2^{-j-2}, so that sigma_j - sigma_{j-1} = 2^{-j} >= delta_{j-1} and sigma_j + delta_j < -A - 2. Step j uses the mild formula from sigma_j, only for tau in [sigma_j + delta_j, 0] (never beyond tau = 0), and splits U_n (x) U_n by a cutoff chi_j equal to 1 on B_{(rho_j + rho_{j-1})/2} with support in B_{rho_{j-1}} (step 0: 1 on B_{32L}, support in B_{64L}); for |y| <= rho_j and z outside {chi_j = 1}, |y - z| >= c_j |z| with c_j > 0. With h = nu_n(tau - sigma_j) in [nu_* delta_j/2, 2 nu_*(A + 3)], the heat part has spatial derivatives of order alpha on B_{rho_j} at most C_alpha (K + 1) + C'_alpha J_n(64L, A + 3)^{1/2} (Cauchy-Schwarz on |z| > 64L); the far part satisfies |d^alpha N^far_n(y, tau)| <= C_{alpha,j} (A + 3) rho_j^{-|alpha|} J_n(rho_j, A + 3); by the kernel bounds of (1), the near part is uniformly C^a in space (a < 1) after step 0 and, inductively, uniformly C^{j, a_j} on B_{rho_j} x [sigma_j + delta_j, 0] for some a_j in (0, 1). After k + 4 steps all spatial derivatives up to order k + 3 are bounded on B_{2L} x [-A - 2, 0], uniformly in n >= n_0. Then d_tau U_n = nu_n Delta U_n - U_n.grad U_n - grad P_n is bounded on B_L x [-A, 0] with its spatial derivatives: the near pressure (cutoff 1 on B_{3L/2}, support in B_{2L}) by the Riesz transform bounds, and |grad^k grad P^far_n| <= C_k J_n(3L/2, A) (kernel of degree -4-k, |y - z| >= |z|/3). (4) Limit, in this order. Arzela-Ascoli for the grad^m U_n (bounded, uniformly Lipschitz in tau) and a diagonal argument give convergence in C_tau C^m_y on every B_L x [-A, 0], through tau = 0. Then the pressure gradients converge locally uniformly: for L > 2l the near parts with cutoff radius L converge on B_l, and the far parts are at most C J_n(L, A) for U_n and C K^2/L for the limit; let n -> infinity, then L -> infinity, using (TAIL). Then d_tau U_n converges locally uniformly, which gives C^{2,1}_loc convergence. In the mild formula the contributions of |z| > L_1 are at most C(tau - sigma, nu_*) J_n(L_1, |sigma|)^{1/2} (heat part) and C (tau - sigma) J_n(L_1, |sigma|) (nonlinear part) for U_n, and C K L_1^{-1/2}, C K^2/L_1 for U; the rest converges by dominated convergence (nu_n -> nu_*). The listed properties are pointwise limits of (K), of the normalized record in the proof of Theorem 1 and of Gamma_{U_n} = Gamma/gamma_n (Gamma_U = R U^theta). For U itself (TAIL) is automatic: sup_tau int_{|y| > L} |U|^2 |y|^{-4} dy <= 4 pi K^2/L.

The Hoelder bootstrap in (3) uses only the kernel bounds of (1), and the passage to the limit in the mild formula in (4) uses only the displayed tail bounds and dominated convergence; these routine steps are indicated rather than written out in full.

Status: proof with key estimates (routine steps indicated, not written out in full); source: own derivation; verification: adversarial audit rounds 1, 5, 21, 22.

Theorem 3 (reduction). W(y, s) = gamma_* U(y, gamma_* s) belongs to LL. Conversely, for every W in LL some member W' of its C^infinity_loc(R^3 x (-infinity, 0]) orbit closure under axial translations, time translations into the past, parabolic scalings and the reflection x_2 -> -x_2 has, after rescaling to viscosity 1/gamma', every stated property of the limit field in Theorem 2 with (K, G, gamma_*) replaced by some admissible (K', ||Gamma_W||_infty, gamma'). Consequently: LL empty implies the exclusion of Case 1, and any exclusion argument using only the properties in Theorem 2 (for all admissible K, G) proves that LL is empty, which is the bounded-circulation case of the Liouville conjecture of Koch, Nadirashvili, Seregin and Sverak, open on R^3 to our knowledge.

Proof. We use the smoothing estimate for bounded mild ancient solutions: a bounded mild ancient solution W with ||W||_infty <= K_0 and viscosity nu satisfies ||d_tau^m grad^k W||_infty <= C(k, m, K_0, nu) ([KNSS, sec. 4]; also proved as in Theorem 2, with no far field). With Arzela-Ascoli and dominated convergence in the mild formula (no tail term, the bound being global), every sequence of such solutions with a common bound has a subsequence converging in C^infty_loc(R^3 x (-infinity, 0]) to a bounded mild ancient solution. LL is invariant under Z-translations, time translations into the past, the reflection x_2 -> -x_2 and the parabolic scalings W -> lambda W(lambda ., lambda^2 .), and Gamma is invariant under the last. (a) W(y, s) = gamma_* U(y, gamma_* s) turns viscosity nu_* = 1/gamma_* into 1 and is a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with ||W||_infty <= gamma_* K, ||Gamma_W||_infty <= G, sup |W^theta| = W^theta(e_1, 0) = gamma_* > 0 and -W^R(e_1, 0) >= 1; so W is in LL. (b) Let W be in LL, K_0 = ||W||_infty, G_0 = ||Gamma_W||_infty, s_0 = sup |W^theta| > 0 over R^3 x (-infinity, 0], and C_1 := ||grad W||_infty, finite by the smoothing estimate. Since W^theta/R is, up to sign, an entry of grad W in the frame (e_R, e_theta, e_Z), |W^theta| <= C_1 R; also |W^theta| <= G_0/R. Take (R_k, Z_k, tau_k) with |W^theta| -> s_0; eventually |W^theta| > s_0/2 there, so R_k lies in [s_0/(2 C_1), 2 G_0/s_0]. Pass to a subsequence with R_k -> R_* > 0 and a fixed sign (+ after the reflection). The translates W(. + Z_k e_3, . + tau_k) converge to some W'' in LL with |W''^theta| <= s_0 everywhere and W''^theta(R_* e_1, 0) = s_0. Put W'(y, tau) = R_* W''(R_* y, R_*^2 tau) and gamma' := R_* s_0. Then sup |W'^theta| = W'^theta(e_1, 0) = gamma' = Gamma_{W'}(e_1, 0) <= G_0, and the record calculation in the proof of Theorem 1 at this space-time maximum (viscosity 1, R = 1) gives -W'^R(e_1, 0) >= 1. U'(y, tau) := W'(y, tau/gamma')/gamma' is a smooth bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with viscosity 1/gamma' and canonical pressure gradient, with |U'| <= R_* K_0/gamma' = K_0/s_0 =: K', |U'^theta| <= 1 = U'^theta(e_1, 0), -gamma' U'^R(e_1, 0) >= 1 and |Gamma_{U'}| <= G_0/gamma'; moreover K'^2 >= |U'(e_1, 0)|^2 >= (U'^theta)^2 + (U'^R)^2 >= 1 + gamma'^{-2}. Thus (K', G_0, gamma') is admissible, meaning gamma' in (0, G_0] and K'^2 >= 1 + gamma'^{-2}. (c) Consequences. In Case 1, Theorem 2 and (a) produce a member of LL, so LL empty excludes Case 1. Conversely, an argument that derives a contradiction from the properties in Theorem 2 alone, for all admissible parameters, applies to U' for every W in LL and hence proves LL empty. W' is in general a different member of the closure of W, and nothing here realizes W as a limit of a fixed finite-energy datum.

Status: proved here; source: own derivation; verification: adversarial audit rounds 1, 21, 22.

Theorem 4 (Route A, the critical R^3 eta mechanism). Let W be a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with viscosity nu and bounded circulation, K := ||W||_infty, V the meridional part of W and eta_W = omega_W^theta/R. If sup R^3 |eta_W| < infinity, then the meridional velocity V is c(tau) e_3 + b_0 with |b_0| <= C min(1, 1/R) (5D Newton potential plus a bounded harmonic remainder), c is constant, and W = c_0 e_3 (Galilean change of frame and [KNSS, Theorem 5.3]). Hence every member of LL has sup R^3 |eta| = infinity. The weighted equation for R^3 eta has zero-order coefficient 3(nu + R V^R)/R^2. The elementary maximum-principle argument requiring a nonpositive zero-order coefficient would require -R V^R >= nu throughout the relevant region, and the vertical-flux identity (Proposition 25(b)) rules out that condition on vertical segments longer than K R^2/nu. This does not exclude every weighted maximum-principle argument; the source term also requires control. The global physical bound sup r^3 |eta| <= C is itself a known regularity criterion ([LP, Corollary 1.1]), so it is a valid but strong target.

Proof. The scaling W(y, tau) -> nu^{-1} W(y, tau/nu) makes the viscosity 1 and multiplies eta by 1/nu, so in (a) to (c) nu = 1. Let K_0 = ||W||_infty, G_0 = ||Gamma_W||_infty and A_eta := sup_{R, Z, tau} R^3 |eta_W| < infinity. By the smoothing estimate for bounded mild ancient solutions (stated in Theorem 3) all derivatives of W are bounded. omega^theta extends oddly in R, so eta is even and smooth in R and lifts to a smooth bounded function on R^5 = R^4_{y'} x R, with |eta| <= C_eta := ||grad omega||_infty; thus |eta(y)| <= m(|y'|) := min(C_eta, A_eta |y'|^{-3}). (a) Newton potential. Fix tau and let phi_0 = N_5 * eta, N_5(x) = c_5 |x|^{-3}, c_5 = 1/(8 pi^2), so -Delta_5 phi_0 = eta. Integrating the kernels first in the axial variable, int_R (d^2 + s^2)^{-3/2} ds = 2/d^2 and int_R (d^2 + s^2)^{-2} ds = pi/(2 d^3), so |phi_0(x)| <= C int_{R^4} m(|y'|) |x' - y'|^{-2} dy' and |grad phi_0(x)| <= C int_{R^4} m(|y'|) |x' - y'|^{-3} dy', both finite. For R = |x'| >= 2 split R^4 into I = {|y'| < R/2}, where |x' - y'| >= R/2 and int_I m <= C(1 + R); II = {|y' - x'| < R/2}, where m <= 8 A_eta R^{-3}, int |w|^{-2} dw = C R^2 and int |w|^{-3} dw = C R over |w| < R/2; and III, the rest, where |x' - y'| >= |y'|/3 and the integrands are at most C A_eta |y'|^{-5} and C A_eta |y'|^{-6}. Hence |phi_0| <= C/R and |grad phi_0| <= C/R^2 for R >= 2, with C = C(A_eta, C_eta); phi_0 is invariant under rotations of y', so phi_0 = phi_0(R, Z). (b) Harmonic remainder. b_0 := curl(R phi_0 e_theta) = -R d_Z phi_0 e_R + (2 phi_0 + R d_R phi_0) e_Z is smooth and divergence free, |b_0| <= C_1 min(1, 1/R) with C_1 = C(A_eta, C_eta), and curl b_0 = R(-Delta_5 phi_0) e_theta = omega^theta e_theta. V is smooth, div V = 0 and curl V = omega^theta e_theta. So h := V - b_0 is bounded, divergence free and curl free; its Cartesian components are bounded harmonic functions on R^3, hence constant in space, and rotation invariance gives h = c(tau) e_3. (c) c is constant and W = c_0 e_3. Translates W(. + R_k e_1, .), R_k -> infinity, converge along a subsequence (compactness, stated in Theorem 3) to a bounded mild ancient solution which equals c(tau) e_3, since |W^R| = |b_0^R| <= C_1/R, |W^theta| <= G_0/R and W^Z = c(tau) + O(1/R). For a spatially constant mild solution the nonlinear Duhamel term vanishes (the kernel of e^{h Delta} Pi div is integrable with integral 0) and the heat semigroup fixes constants, so c(tau) = c_0. The Galilean transformation W'(x, tau) := W(x + c_0 tau e_3, tau) - c_0 e_3 is a smooth bounded axisymmetric NS solution with bounded derivatives, whose meridional part is b_0 and whose swirl is W^theta, both evaluated at (x + c_0 tau e_3, tau); hence |W'| <= (C_1 + G_0)/R for R >= 1 and |W'| <= (K_0 + |c_0|)/R for R <= 1. By [KNSS, Theorem 5.3] (a bounded weak axisymmetric ancient solution with |u| <= C (x_1^2 + x_2^2)^{-1/2} vanishes identically) W' = 0, i.e. W = c_0 e_3; so W^theta = 0 and no member of LL satisfies sup R^3 |eta| < infinity. (d) Weighted equation (viscosity nu). From (d_tau + V.grad) eta = nu Delta_5 eta + d_Z(q^2), q = W^theta/R, direct differentiation gives for f = R^3 eta: (d_tau + V.grad) f = nu(f_RR - 3 R^{-1} f_R + f_ZZ) + 3 R^{-2}(nu + R V^R) f + R^{-1} d_Z(Gamma^2). The zero-order coefficient is nonpositive exactly where -R V^R >= nu. Vertical flux: the flux of the divergence-free field V (|V| <= K) out of the cylinder {R < rho, |Z - Z_0| < h} vanishes, so 2 pi rho int_{Z_0-h}^{Z_0+h} V^R(rho, Z) dZ = -2 pi int_0^rho [V^Z(R, Z_0 + h) - V^Z(R, Z_0 - h)] R dR, whence |int_{Z_0-h}^{Z_0+h} rho V^R(rho, Z) dZ| <= K rho^2. If -rho V^R >= nu on that segment, then 2 h nu <= K rho^2, which fails when the length 2h exceeds K rho^2/nu. (e) Physical bound. r^3 |eta| = r^2 |omega^theta|, and [LP, Corollary 1.1] states that |omega^theta| <= C r^{-2} gives a bounded angular stream function and regularity; a bound uniform on [t_0, T_*) suffices after restarting at t_0.

Status: proved here; source: own derivation (using [KNSS, Theorem 5.3] and [LP, Corollary 1.1]); verification: adversarial audit rounds 2, 21, 22; checked by a computer calculation

Theorem 5 (Route B, radial-compression comparison principle). Let W be a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with viscosity nu and bounded circulation. If, for some R_0 > 0, -W^R(R, Z, tau) <= b(R) for every R >= R_0, Z in R and tau <= 0, with b locally integrable on [R_0, infinity) and int_{R_0}^infinity R exp(-(1/nu) int_{R_0}^R b) dR = infinity, then Gamma_W = 0 and W is constant. The threshold b = 2 nu/R is sharp for the scalar exterior problem (the line sink -(c/R) e_R with c > 2 nu admits the bounded nonconstant steady solution Gamma = C_0 - R^{-(c/nu - 2)}).

Proof. Let V be the meridional part of W. Gamma = R W^theta solves d_tau Gamma + V.grad Gamma = nu L Gamma on {R > 0} x (-infinity, 0]. By the smoothing estimate for bounded mild ancient solutions (stated in Theorem 3) ||grad W||_infty < infinity, so Gamma is uniformly Lipschitz in the spatial variables on each bounded radial strip and |Gamma| <= ||grad W||_infty R^2. Envelope: B(R) := sup_{Z, tau <= 0} (-V^R(R, Z, tau)) satisfies |B| <= ||W||_infty and |B(R) - B(R')| <= ||grad W||_infty |R - R'|, so B is bounded and Lipschitz; B <= b on [R_0, infinity), hence exp(-(1/nu) int_{R_0}^R B) >= exp(-(1/nu) int_{R_0}^R b), and the scale integral with B also diverges. (An upward mollification of b would not do: for b = 2 nu/R the integral diverges, for b + eps it converges.) For R_1 >= R_0 let sigma_{R_1}(R) = int_{R_1}^R rho exp(-(1/nu) int_{R_1}^rho B) d rho, the scale function [Fel] of the radial generator nu d_RR + (B - nu/R) d_R. Then sigma_{R_1} is C^2, sigma_{R_1}(R_1) = 0, sigma_{R_1}' > 0, sigma_{R_1}(R) -> infinity as R -> infinity, and nu(sigma_{R_1}'' - sigma_{R_1}'/R) = -B sigma_{R_1}'. Step 1 (outer comparison). Let m(R_1) = sup_{Z, tau} Gamma(R_1, Z, tau) and, for eps > 0, w = Gamma - m(R_1) - eps sigma_{R_1}(R). Then d_tau w + V.grad w - nu L w = -eps (V^R + B) sigma_{R_1}' <= 0 on {R > R_1}, w <= 0 on {R = R_1}, and w -> -infinity as R -> infinity uniformly in (Z, tau). Suppose sup_{R >= R_1} w = m > 0. Since Gamma - m(R_1) <= C (R - R_1) near R_1 by the gradient bound, near-maximizing points have R in a compact subinterval of (R_1, infinity). Translate them in (Z, tau) to Z = 0, tau = 0 and pass to a limit (compactness, stated in Theorem 3); the limit field satisfies the same envelope (it is preserved under Z, tau translations and locally uniform convergence), so the limit w~ is a subsolution attaining its maximum m at an interior point of {R > R_1} x (-infinity, 0]. The operator d_tau - nu(d_RR + d_ZZ) + (V^R + nu/R) d_R + V^Z d_Z has locally bounded continuous coefficients on {R > 0}, so Nirenberg's strong maximum principle [Nir] gives w~ = m on {R > R_1} x (-infinity, 0], contradicting w~ -> -infinity. Hence Gamma <= m(R_1) + eps sigma_{R_1} on R >= R_1, and letting eps -> 0, sup_{R >= R_1} Gamma = m(R_1). Step 2. Suppose G_+ := sup Gamma > 0. By Step 1 with R_1 = R_0, G_+ = sup_{R <= R_0} Gamma, so near-maximizing points have R in [delta, R_0] for some delta > 0 (|Gamma| <= C R^2). Their translated limits attain G_+ at an interior point and by [Nir] equal G_+ on {R > 0} x (-infinity, 0], contradicting Gamma = 0 on the axis. So Gamma <= 0, and the same argument for -Gamma gives Gamma = 0. W then has no swirl and is constant by [KNSS, Theorem 5.2 and Remark 6.1]. Sharpness: V = -(c/R) e_R is divergence free on R > 0; with p = c/nu - 2 > 0, Gamma = C_0 - R^{-p} satisfies V.grad Gamma = -c p R^{-p-2} = -nu p (p + 2) R^{-p-2} = nu(Gamma_RR - Gamma_R/R), so it is a bounded nonconstant steady solution on R >= 1, while for b = c/R the scale integrand is a multiple of R^{1 - c/nu}, integrable at infinity exactly when c > 2 nu.
