Proposition 25 (the far-field inflow arrow: refinement, flux, Biot-Savart, scalar models). Notation of Proposition 23; Q_R(Z, tau) := -R U^R(R, Z, tau).
(a) (refinement) Under the hypotheses of Proposition 23(b), for every R_0 > 0 and every 0 < eps <= m(R_0), m(R_0) = (A/2) e^{-lambda_{R_0}}, there is a point with R > R_0, Gamma_U > A - eps, d_R Gamma_U > 0 and -R U^R > 2 nu (for larger eps apply this with min{eps, m(R_0)}). The proof is that of 23(b): at a positive interior maximum of the comparison function the radial derivative of Gamma_U equals minus the radial derivative of the barrier, which is nonnegative, and where it vanishes the drift term of the barrier vanishes too. If U is in LL after normalization, the Cartesian translates along such points with R -> infinity converge along a subsequence to a_0 e_1 + c_0 e_3 with a_0 <= 0 (a_0 < 0 is not obtained).
(b) (vertical flux) Assume in addition that U is divergence-free (true for Case-1 limits). For all Z_1 < Z_2 and tau, |int_{Z_1}^{Z_2} Q_R dZ| <= K R^2, because F_R = int_0^R s U^Z(s, Z, tau) ds satisfies |F_R| <= K R^2/2 and d_Z F_R = Q_R. So each connected Z-interval on which Q_R > 2 nu has length less than K R^2/(2 nu). The identity bounds neither the total measure nor the duration of the strong-inflow set (stream function chi(R) sin Z; steady drifts), and it forces every long signed axial average of Q_R at fixed radius to vanish, so smallness of long signed averages at fixed radius cannot replace the pointwise hypothesis of 23(b) (it does not control positive-part averages, and the convergence is not uniform in R).
(c) (Biot-Savart) If the meridional field b is the Biot-Savart integral of omega^theta e_theta (true for the finite-energy physical field at positive classical times), then r |b(r, z)| <= (1/2) calQ_omega(r, z), with calQ_omega(r, z) := int_0^infinity int_R r R (d D)^{-1} |omega^theta(R, Z)| dZ dR, where d^2 = (r - R)^2 + (z - Z)^2 and D^2 = (r + R)^2 + (z - Z)^2 (from |b(x)| <= (4 pi)^{-1} int |omega(y)| |x - y|^{-2} dy and int_0^{2 pi} d theta/(d^2 + 2 r R (1 - cos theta)) = 2 pi/(d D)). calQ is invariant under the Navier-Stokes scaling. Hence calQ_omega <= 4 nu at a point gives -r b^r <= 2 nu there, and in Case 1 the physical bound calQ_{omega^theta(t)} <= 4 (viscosity one) at the points of the windows of Proposition 23(c) that lie in the near-maximal circulation set, and by (a) only where d_r Gamma > 0, would exclude Case 1; this is a stronger sufficient condition, not an equivalent form. The critical (scale-invariant) vorticity Morrey norm sup_{x in R^3, s > 0} s^{-1} int_{B(x, s)} |omega| dy and the unweighted meridional mass int int |omega^theta| dR dZ, used alone, do not control r|b|: a smooth compactly supported stream-function bump of width delta gives a divergence-free field with |b| <= 20 nu, -b^R(1, 0) = 3 nu and vorticity Morrey norm at most 28080 pi nu delta (9360 pi eps for amplitude eps = 3 nu delta) (a kinematic example, not a Navier-Stokes solution; it refutes estimates from these two norms alone, not an implication using all the ancient Navier-Stokes hypotheses).
(d) (scalar models) (i) Exterior: for p > 0 the steady field U^R = -nu(p + 2)/R, U^Z = 0 with Gamma = A - R^{-p}/p, A = (p + 1)/p, on R > (p + 1)^{-1/p}, is an exact steady exterior Navier-Stokes solution with 0 <= U^theta <= 1 = U^theta(1) and -R U^R = nu(p + 2) > 2 nu everywhere; it has no smooth axis extension. (ii) Whole space: the smooth bounded divergence-free drift V with Stokes stream function beta R^2 xi (1 + xi^2)^{-1/2}, xi = Z/(1 + R^2), beta = 64 nu, has vertical flux int Q_R dZ = 2 beta R^2, so the axial scale R^2 allowed by (b) is attained. It carries a steady circulation with max{0, 1 - 1/R - Z^2/R^4} <= Gamma <= 1 - e^{-32 R^2} (monotone exhaustion of Dirichlet problems with boundary data 1 - e^{-32 R^2}; the barrier signs have an analytic proof). The circulation of each axial translation limit vanishes by 23(b) applied to the constant axial drift (Theorem 5 assumes the Navier-Stokes equations and does not apply to a prescribed drift), so Gamma/R attains a positive maximum. After normalization at that maximum it satisfies the scalar record conditions, every far-radial translation limit of V is an axial constant, and, before normalization, for fixed 0 < eps <= 1 the inflow exceeds 2 nu on {Gamma > 1 - eps} in a region of axial extent comparable to R^2 at every large R. It is not a Navier-Stokes field: along Z = R^2, R^4 V.grad eta -> 3 beta^2 and R^4 nu Delta_5 eta -> -(21/sqrt2) nu beta while R^4 d_Z(q^2) -> 0, so R^4 times the residual of the steady equation for eta = omega^theta/r tends to 3 beta^2 + 21 nu beta/sqrt2 > 0 (the source limit uses that bounded entire solutions of a constant-drift heat equation are constant); it also has infinite energy. The model shows that the listed scalar and kinematic properties are insufficient; it does not show which further estimates a successful argument must use.
(e) (limit-level equivalence) Consider the assertion: for every W in LL (viscosity one) with A_W := sup Gamma_W > 0 there is R_0(W) > 0 such that -R W^R <= 2 on {R > R_0(W), Gamma_W > A_W - m_W(R_0(W))}, with m_W the deficit of Proposition 23 computed for W. By 23(b) it rules out every member with A_W > 0; a member with nonzero circulation and sup Gamma_W <= 0 is ruled out by applying it to the reflection W^#(x, t) = P W(P x, t), P = diag(1, -1, 1), which preserves the equations and the meridional components and reverses the swirl; and a member with Gamma_W = 0 is excluded by the definition of LL. So the assertion implies that LL is empty, and conversely LL empty makes it vacuous: posed for the whole class LL, the far-field bound is equivalent to the Liouville problem for LL (Theorem 3). The contradiction is obtained member by member, so no uniformity of m_W is needed. The equivalence is not automatic when the bound is asserted only for a proper subclass, such as the limits of one physical trajectory; information that distinguishes physically obtainable limits from unrestricted members of LL, for example a uniform bound inherited by the physical limits, is one possible route.
(f) (slender asymptotics and an exact exterior solution) For the Stokes stream function Psi = beta R^2 g(Z/R^2) one has exactly eta = R^{-2} E + R^{-4} F, E = -4 beta k^2 g'', F = -beta g'', k = Z/R^2, and the steady swirl-free vorticity residual W.grad eta - nu Delta_5 eta (W the field of Psi) is R^{-4} C_4 + R^{-6} C_6 + R^{-8} C_8 with C_4 = 2 beta (g E)' - 4 nu (k^2 E')', C_6 = 2 beta (2 g' F + g F') - nu (4 k^2 F'' + 16 k F' + 8 F + E'') and C_8 = -nu F'' (primes are d/dk); the reduced equation C_4 = 0 is not uniform in the core |Z| <~ R, and the unsteady leading equation keeps a time derivative on the time scale R^2/nu. No odd reduced profile with bounded axial velocity and nonzero vorticity satisfies the whole-space flux bound (b): for beta != 0, (b) forces g to be bounded (flux identity in the key estimates), and C_4 = 8 nu beta k E_1(g), where E_1 is the long-pattern operator of Proposition 26(i) with beta/nu in place of its parameter (checked by a symbolic computation); by the rigidity statement there, a bounded solution of C_4 = 0 is constant on each half-line (the once-integrated form of C_4 = 0 in the key estimates bootstraps C^3 to C^4 off 0), and an odd profile continuous at 0 is then identically 0. This uses neither the finite slope at k = 0 nor the finer classification in the key estimates, which is not proved here. Oddness is needed, since a constant profile (constant axial velocity) satisfies (b). This excludes only global steady slender similarity profiles of this class. With s = (R^2 + Z^2)^{1/2}, mu = Z/s, a > 1, the field with Stokes stream function 2 nu R^2/(a s - Z) (the Landau jet), swirl A/R and pressure 4 nu^2 (a Z - s)/(s (a s - Z)^2) - A^2/(2 R^2) is an exact steady Navier-Stokes solution off the axis, smooth and bounded on {R > R_1}, with |int_{Z_1}^{Z_2} Q_{R_1} dZ| <= 2 nu R_1 (a^2 - 1)^{-1/2} and Q_R = 2 nu (1 - mu^2)(1 - a mu)/(a - mu)^2, which equals 20 nu/9 > 2 nu on the ray Z = R/sqrt3 for a = 17/16. So an inequality derived only from bounded velocity, potential swirl, bounded signed inner flux and the exterior equations cannot give the far-field bound. The example has Gamma = A and d_R Gamma = 0 everywhere, so it does not satisfy the whole-space conditions A - Gamma > 0 and d_R Gamma > 0 at the witnesses of (a), and it has no smooth extension through the axis.

Key estimates. Conventions: Psi is the Stokes stream function, b^R = -Psi_Z/R, b^Z = Psi_R/R, so Q_R = Psi_Z; w := A - Gamma_U. The comparison behind the deficit of Proposition 23 uses only the circulation equation, |U| <= K and |Gamma_U| <= K R, and gives w >= m(R_0) on {R <= R_0} under the hypotheses of Proposition 23(b).
(a) Suppose -R U^R <= 2 nu on {R > R_0, w < eps, d_R Gamma_U > 0} for some 0 < eps <= m(R_0). Put calL := d_tau + U^R d_R + U^Z d_Z - nu L, so calL w = 0. Let Y(R, t) solve Y_t = Y_RR + Y_R/R on R_0 < R < R_1 with Y = 0 at t = 0 and at R = R_1 and Y = h(t) at R = R_0 (h smooth, nondecreasing from 0 to 1, a smooth switch-on); then 0 <= Y <= 1, Y_R <= 0, and Y_eps := eps Y(R, nu(tau - tau_1)) satisfies calL Y_eps = (U^R + 2 nu/R) Y_eps_R. With c_1 := K + nu + 1 and sigma > 0 let v := Y_eps - w - sigma e^{c_1 (tau - tau_1)} cosh Z on {R_0 < R < R_1, tau_1 < tau <= 0, w < eps}; v < 0 on the parabolic boundary and for large |Z|. At a positive interior maximum d_R v = 0, so d_R Gamma_U = -Y_eps_R >= 0. If d_R Gamma_U > 0 the hypothesis gives calL Y_eps <= 0; if d_R Gamma_U = 0 then Y_eps_R = 0 and calL Y_eps = 0. In both cases calL v <= -sigma e^{c_1 (tau - tau_1)} cosh Z (c_1 + U^Z tanh Z - nu) < 0, whereas calL v >= 0 at a maximum. Hence w >= Y_eps; letting sigma -> 0, tau_1 -> -infinity (Y_eps -> eps log(R_1/R)/log(R_1/R_0)) and R_1 -> infinity gives w >= eps everywhere, contradicting sup Gamma_U = A. For U in LL take R_0 = k and eps = min{m(k), 1/k}: the witnesses have R_k -> infinity, Gamma_U -> A and U^R < -2 nu/R_k, so the translate limits of Proposition 6 have a_0 <= 0.
(b) Incompressibility gives d_s(s U^R) = -s d_Z U^Z, and s U^R -> 0 at the axis, so R U^R = -d_Z F_R, i.e. d_Z F_R = Q_R; |F_R| <= K R^2/2 gives the flux bound, and on an interval I with Q_R > 2 nu, 2 nu |I| < int_I Q_R dZ <= K R^2. For the steady stream function chi(R) sin Z one has Q_R = chi(R) cos Z, so where chi > 2 nu the set {Q_R > 2 nu} has infinite axial measure and persists for all time, while |I|^{-1} |int_I Q_R dZ| <= K R^2/|I|.
(c) With y = (R cos theta, R sin theta, Z), |x - y|^2 = d^2 + 2 r R (1 - cos theta) and int_0^{2 pi} d theta/(a - b cos theta) = 2 pi (a^2 - b^2)^{-1/2} with a = d^2 + 2 r R, b = 2 r R, a^2 - b^2 = d^2 D^2; inserting this into |b(x)| <= (4 pi)^{-1} int |omega| |x - y|^{-2} dy gives |b| <= (1/2) int int R |omega^theta| (d D)^{-1} dR dZ. For omega_lambda(x) = lambda^2 omega(lambda x), calQ_{omega_lambda}(r, z) = calQ_omega(lambda r, lambda z); hence calQ_{omega^theta(t)}(r_n R, z_n + r_n Z) = gamma_n calQ_{omega_{U_n}(tau)}(R, Z), and the physical criterion follows from (a) as Proposition 23(c) follows from 23(b). Bump: zeta(t) = exp(1 - 1/(1 - t^2)) for |t| < 1 (0 otherwise), f(p, q) = q zeta(p) zeta(q), Psi = eps f((R - 1)/delta, Z/delta), 0 < delta <= 1/4. Since f_q(0, 0) = 1, b^R(1, 0) = -eps/delta. From |f_p| <= 3, |f_q| <= 4, |f_pp| <= 84, |f_qq| <= 90 and R >= 3/4 on the support: |b| <= (20/3) eps/delta; omega^theta = -(eps/(R delta^2))(f_pp + f_qq) + (eps/(R^2 delta)) f_p, so |omega^theta| <= 234 eps/delta^2 and int int |omega^theta| dR dZ <= 936 eps. The Morrey quotient is at most 312 pi eps for s <= delta (ball volume) and at most 9360 pi eps for s >= delta (the support meets B(x, s) in volume at most 40 pi delta^2 s). With eps = 3 nu delta: |b| <= 20 nu, -b^R(1, 0) = 3 nu, Morrey norm at most 28080 pi nu delta.
(d) (i) Gamma_R = R^{-p-1} and L Gamma = -(p + 2) R^{-p-2} = U^R Gamma_R/nu; (Gamma/R)_R = ((p + 1)/p) R^{-p-2} (1 - R^p), so U^theta has its maximum 1 at R = 1; the viscous term of -c/R vanishes, (R U^R)_R = 0, and the pressure has P_R = (nu^2 (p + 2)^2 + Gamma^2)/R^3.
(ii) With D_V := (1 + R^2)^2 + Z^2: V^R = -beta R (1 + R^2)^2 D_V^{-3/2}, V^Z = 2 beta Z (1 + R^2 + Z^2) D_V^{-3/2}; V^R/R and V^Z are smooth in (R^2, Z), |V^R| <= beta R/(1 + R^2) <= beta/2, |V^Z| <= 2 beta, -V^R <= beta R, Z V^Z >= 0, and Q_R = beta R^2 (1 + R^2)^{-1} (1 + xi^2)^{-3/2}, whose Z-integral is 2 beta R^2. Put calA := nu L - V.grad, B := 1 - e^{-32 R^2}, l := 1 - R^{-1} - Z^2 R^{-4}. Since nu L B = -beta R B_R, calA B = (-beta R - V^R) B_R <= 0. On {l > 0} (so R > 1, |Z| < R^2): -V^R >= 8 sqrt2 nu/R, -V^Z l_Z >= 0, and calA l >= nu [(8 sqrt2 - 3) R^{-3} - 2 R^{-4} + (32 sqrt2 - 24) Z^2 R^{-6}] > 0. The Dirichlet solutions Gamma_k on (1/k, k) x (-k, k) with data B satisfy max(0, l) <= Gamma_k <= B and decrease in k (Gamma_{k+1} <= B = Gamma_k on the boundary of the k-th domain); the limit keeps both barriers, so sup Gamma = 1. Axis: q = Gamma/R^2 lies in [0, 32] and solves nu Delta_5 q - V.grad q - 2 (V^R/R) q = 0 with coefficients smooth across the axis; the axis has codimension four in R^5, so cutoffs around it have gradient energy O(eps^2) and q extends smoothly; 0 <= Gamma/R <= min(32 R, 1/R) <= sqrt32. Axial translation limits have drift +-2 beta e_z and no inflow, so their circulation vanishes by 23(b); hence Gamma/R attains its maximum S_* at some (R_*, Z_*), where -R_* V^R = nu [1 - (R_*^2/S_*)(d_RR + d_ZZ)(Gamma/R)] >= nu. Normalization: V^(R, Z) := R_* V(R_* R, Z_* + R_* Z), Gamma^ := Gamma(R_* R, Z_* + R_* Z)/(R_* S_*), which preserves the scalar equation. Before normalization, R > 2/eps and |Z| < R^2 (eps/2)^{1/2} give Gamma >= l > 1 - eps and Q_R > 2 nu. Residual: eta = beta Z (11 R^4 + 12 R^2 Z^2 + 22 R^2 + 8 Z^2 + 11) D_V^{-5/2}; in k = Z/R^2, V^R = -beta R^{-1} (1 + k^2)^{-3/2} + O(R^{-3}), V^Z = 2 beta k^3 (1 + k^2)^{-3/2} + O(R^{-2}), eta = R^{-2} E_V(k) + O(R^{-4}) with E_V = 12 beta k^3 (1 + k^2)^{-5/2} and (E_V, E_V', E_V'')(1) = (3 beta/sqrt2, 3 beta/(2 sqrt2), -33 beta/(4 sqrt2)), which gives the two limits along Z = R^2. Far-radial translates of Gamma converge to bounded entire solutions of a constant-drift heat equation, which are constant (|grad| <= C ||.||_infty (nu T)^{-1/2} for every T), so R^4 d_Z(q^2) = 2 Gamma Gamma_Z -> 0; V^Z does not decay, so the energy is infinite.
(e) If A_W > 0, Proposition 23(b) with nu = 1 and K = ||W||_infty gives a point with R > R_0(W), Gamma_W > A_W - m_W(R_0(W)) and -R W^R > 2, contradicting the assertion. P is orthogonal, so W^# is a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with the same meridional components and Gamma_{W^#} = -Gamma_W; if sup Gamma_W <= 0 and Gamma_W is not identically 0, then A_{W^#} > 0 and W^# is in LL.
(f) For Psi = beta R^2 g(k): -R W^R = beta g'(k), W^Z = 2 beta (g - k g'). The residual follows from W.grad(R^{-p} J(k)) = beta R^{-p-2} (p g' J + 2 g J') and Delta_5(R^{-p} J(k)) = R^{-p-2} (4 k^2 J'' + 4 p k J' + p (p - 2) J) + R^{-p-4} J'' (p = 2, 4). Core: (R^{-4} F)/(R^{-2} E) = 1/(4 R^2 k^2) = R^2/(4 Z^2). Unsteady scaling R = L r, Z = L^2 z, t = t_0 + L^2 s/nu, Psi = beta L^2 psi: e := -beta r^{-2} (psi_rr - psi_r/r) solves nu e_s - (beta psi_z/r) e_r + (beta psi_r/r) e_z = nu (e_rr + 3 e_r/r) at leading order. C_4 = 0 integrates to beta g E = 2 nu k^2 E' + c; with g_0 := beta g/(2 nu), alpha := g_0'(0) = Q_0/(2 nu) (Q_0 the inflow at k = 0) and H_0 := k^2 g_0'' it reads k^2 H_0' - g_0 H_0 = c/(16 nu^2), and W^Z = 4 nu (g_0 - k g_0'). Finer classification, a claim from a research consultation that is not proved here and not used above (odd profiles, C^1 at 0, C^3 off 0, globally defined, bounded W^Z): a finite slope at 0 forces c = 0; linear profiles have zero vorticity; nonzero-vorticity profiles exist exactly for alpha > alpha_*, a constant in (1, 2) (the terminal slope l(alpha) is continuous and strictly decreasing, l(alpha) -> 1 as alpha -> 1, l(2) = -1, and l(alpha_*) = 0; the decimal alpha_* = 1.6334... comes from uncertified shooting); for each such alpha there is one family under g(k) -> g(lambda k)/lambda, strictly concave on k > 0, with g_0 = l k + B_infinity + O(k^l), l = l(alpha) < 0, as k -> infinity; smooth nonzero-vorticity profiles exist exactly for alpha in {3, 5, 7, ...}; none has alpha <= 1, i.e. Q_0 <= 2 nu. Only two cases were rechecked: the alpha = 2 profile g_0 = k (2 - a|k|)/(1 + a|k|), a > 0 (C^1 but not C^2 at 0), and the series g_0 = 3k + a_1 k^3 + (3/20) a_1^2 k^5 + (13/560) a_1^3 k^7 + ... for alpha = 3. Flux: int_{Z_1}^{Z_2} Q_R dZ = beta R^2 [g(Z_2/R^2) - g(Z_1/R^2)], so (b) forces g bounded, which excludes linear tails and nonzero linear profiles. Landau jet (h := a s - Z, Psi = 2 nu R^2/h): the swirl is potential (Gamma = A), the centrifugal term is balanced by -A^2/(2 R^2), and the swirl-free jet solves the meridional equations, with eta = 4 nu (a^2 - 1)/h^3. Since h >= (a - 1) s >= (a - 1) R_1, the field is smooth and bounded on {R > R_1}; min_Z h = R (a^2 - 1)^{1/2} (at Z = R (a^2 - 1)^{-1/2}), so 0 < Psi <= 2 nu R (a^2 - 1)^{-1/2}, which is the flux bound. For a = 17/16 and mu = 1/2, Q_R = 20 nu/9. A smooth extension through the axis would require Gamma = O(R^2) there, which is incompatible with Gamma = A != 0 on {R > R_1} by real analyticity of smooth steady Navier-Stokes solutions.

Proposition 26 (averaged circulation flux through cylinders). Let U be as in Proposition 23(b), and in addition divergence-free, with bounded first and second derivatives (D_1, D_2) and G' := sup |Gamma_U| < infinity (Proposition 23(b) does not assume incompressibility, and without it (a) and (d) fail: U^R = -4 nu R/(1 + R^2), U^Z = 0, Gamma_U = A R^2/(1 + R^2) solves the scalar equation, has R U^R <= 0 and d(rho) = A/(1 + rho^2)); for rho > 0 let N_rho(Z, tau) = int_0^rho R Gamma_U dR and Q_rho = -rho U^R(rho, Z, tau).
(a) d_tau N_rho + d_Z int_0^rho R U^Z Gamma_U dR - nu d_ZZ N_rho = Q_rho Gamma_U(rho) + nu rho d_R Gamma_U(rho) - 2 nu Gamma_U(rho) (the axis contributes nothing because Gamma_U = O(R^2)). For the exterior line sink of Proposition 23(b) the same expression is a nonzero constant at every radius; for that singular field only the annulus form (difference of the right sides at two radii) applies.
(b) For a box B of axial half-length Lambda and duration T in the past and every constant c, the box means satisfy |2 nu <Gamma_U(rho)> - nu rho <d_R Gamma_U(rho)> + <Q_rho (c - Gamma_U(rho))>| <= G' rho^2/T + (K G' rho^2/2 + nu D_1 rho^3/3 + |c| K rho^2/2)/Lambda, using the flux bound of Proposition 25(b).
(c) For boxes B_j with Lambda_j, T_j -> infinity and a Banach limit, used at every radius, write MM[X] := lim <X>_{B_j} for the resulting normalized positive linear functional on bounded functions of (Z, tau) (the same MM at every radius; lim <X> and MM[X] denote the same quantity below). The averaged profile a(rho) = MM[Gamma_U(rho)] is differentiable and a(rho) = (rho^2/nu) int_rho^infinity lim <Q_s Gamma_U(s)> s^{-3} ds: the averaged circulation at radius rho is supplied only by the correlation of inflow and circulation at larger radii.
(d) Let A = sup Gamma_U > 0 and d(s) := A - a(s) >= 0. Then d(rho) >= 2 A rho^2 e^{K rho/nu} int_rho^infinity e^{-K s/nu} s^{-3} ds >= 2 nu A/(K rho + 3 nu) for every rho > 0 and every box family; hence for every sequence of boxes with Lambda_j, T_j -> infinity, liminf_j <A - Gamma_U(rho)>_{B_j} >= 2 nu A/(K rho + 3 nu), and d(s) <= eps A/s for all large s forces eps >= 2 nu/K. This averaged rate condition is implied by the uniform rate hypothesis of [LRZ2, Theorem 1.2] and is weaker than it, so (d) is a stronger necessary condition, with an explicit constant whose optimality is not known. If R U^R <= C (C >= 0) on {R >= R_1}, then d(rho) >= 2 nu A/(C + 2 nu) for all rho >= R_1. So if d(s) -> 0 for some box family (averaged saturation), R U^R is unbounded above on {R >= R_1, A - Gamma_U > 0} for every R_1: averaged saturation and a critical one-sided outflow bound at large radii are incompatible for every C.
(e) (convex weights) Let f be convex and C^2 with f(0) = 0 and f >= 0, and put a_f(rho) = lim <f(Gamma_U(rho))>, F_f(rho) = lim <Q_rho f(Gamma_U(rho))>, D_f(rho) = lim <int_0^rho R f''(Gamma_U) |grad Gamma_U|^2 dR> >= 0. Then a_f(rho) = (rho^2/nu) int_rho^infinity (F_f - nu D_f) s^{-3} ds. If F_f(s) <= 2 nu a_f(s) for all s >= rho_0, then a_f = 0 at every radius. If a_f(r_*) > 0 at one radius, then limsup_{s -> infinity} F_f(s)/a_f(s) >= 2 nu + nu D_f(r_*)/sup f(Gamma_U), with D_f(r_*) > 0; for f = (gamma - theta)_+^3, 0 < theta < A, the excess is at least 8 nu a_f(r_*)/(3 (A - theta)^3 log(r_* (D_1/theta)^{1/2})). So nonzero weighted mass at one radius forces the weighted mean inflow strictly above 2 nu at arbitrarily large radii, the critical value of Proposition 23(b) for weighted box means. For the displayed cubic weight, and more generally for an admissible f with f(A) > 0, averaged saturation gives positive weighted mass by Jensen's inequality. The pointwise special case (-R U^R <= 2 nu on {R >= rho_0, Gamma_U > theta}) is already excluded by Proposition 23(b) when theta < A. For f(gamma) = gamma^2 one gets int_0^infinity lim <Q_s Gamma_U(s)^2> s^{-3} ds = nu int_0^infinity lim <|grad Gamma_U(R)|^2> R^{-1} dR, whose left side equals the averaged correlation of the outflow s U^R with the nonnegative quantity (G')^2 - Gamma_U^2. Under averaged saturation the averaged outflow on the deficit set, O(s) = lim <s U^R(s) (A - Gamma_U(s))>, satisfies limsup O(s)/d(s) = infinity, and its log-average over [r_0, L] tends to 2 nu A.
(f) (scalar and kinematic models) If sup_tau int |Q_R| dZ < infinity at every radius, then a = 0 for every box family. A smooth bounded divergence-free drift with Stokes stream function 64 nu R^2 xi/(1 + xi^2), xi = Z/(1 + R^2)^{1/2}, carries a steady solution of the scalar circulation equation with smooth axis and sup Gamma = 1 attained only at infinity, has near-maximal points with d_R Gamma > 0 and -R U^R > 2 nu at arbitrarily large radii and unbounded critical outflow, satisfies the flux bound of Proposition 25(b), and has a = 0 for every box family; it fails the meridional vorticity equation at large radius (a numerical observation at R = 10^3, 10^5, 10^7). A second explicit smooth bounded field, with stream function 8 nu R^2 (1 + R^2)^{-1/2} cos Z, saturates uniformly (A - Gamma comparable to A/R), satisfies the averaged relation of (c), the flux bound, both radial signs and the linear averaged vorticity identities, and fails the unaveraged circulation equation. It also violates the convex identity of (e) for f = gamma^2: there D_f(R) = (A^2/4) log R + O(1), while the identity with a_f -> A^2 and F_f -> 4 nu A^2 would force D_f -> 2 A^2. So it excludes only arguments from the linear averaged identities. Other radial weights, the equation for u^theta/r and the averaged equation for omega^theta/r (which needs the meridional vorticity equation as an additional hypothesis) give either consequences of (c) or identities with unsigned terms. In every sequence of long boxes the set {A - Gamma_U(rho) >= nu A/(K rho + 3 nu)} has lower density at least eps_rho/(2(A + G') - eps_rho), eps_rho = 2 nu A/(K rho + 3 nu).
(g) (axially localized fields) If Gamma_U(rho, Z, tau) -> 0 as |Z| -> infinity uniformly in tau at every radius, all circulation-weighted long-box means in (c)-(e) vanish (the deficit mean is A) and (d), (e) say nothing. Let f be as in (e) and write h_f := f(Gamma_U). Assume, for every rho > 0, sup_tau int_R int_0^rho R (|h_f| + |U^Z h_f| + |d_Z h_f|) dR dZ < infinity and sup_tau int_R int_0^rho R f''(Gamma_U) |grad Gamma_U|^2 dR dZ < infinity, and, for every compact I subset (0, infinity), sup_{tau, rho in I} int_R (|h_f| + |d_R h_f| + |d_RR h_f|)(rho, Z, tau) dZ < infinity (a bulk integrability condition alone does not control these traces). Let MM_tau be a Banach limit of time means over [tau_j - T_j, tau_j], T_j -> infinity, applied after the axial integration (axial cutoffs are removed before the time average), and put abar_f(rho) := MM_tau int_R h_f(rho, Z, tau) dZ, Fbar_f(rho) := MM_tau int_R Q_rho h_f(rho, Z, tau) dZ and Dbar_f(rho) := MM_tau int_R int_0^rho R f''(Gamma_U) |grad Gamma_U|^2 dR dZ >= 0. Then 2 nu abar_f - nu rho abar_f' + nu Dbar_f = Fbar_f. If abar_f(s) <= C s^alpha for s >= rho_0 with 0 <= alpha < 2, and Fbar_f(s) <= kappa abar_f(s) on [rho_0, infinity) for a constant kappa < (2 - alpha) nu (local notation), then abar_f = 0 on [rho_0, infinity). The threshold therefore degrades with the axial extent of the superlevel sets, and no growth bound was derived for Case-1 limits.
(h) (convex hierarchy, momentum balances, positive mass) Write w = A - Gamma_U, W = A + G', and <X>_log for the limit of (log(L/rho_0))^{-1} int_{rho_0}^L X(s) ds/s. Assume averaged saturation. For g in C^2[0, W] convex with g(0) = g'(0) = 0 and f(gamma) = g(A - gamma) - g(A), the following holds. The cylinder identity underlying (e) holds for every C^2 function f with f(0) = 0; its nonnegativity assumption is needed only for the vanishing consequences. Applying that identity to the present f gives <MM[Q_s g(w(s))]>_log = -2 nu g(A) + nu D_g(infinity), where D_g(infinity) = int g'' d mu and mu is the averaged Dirichlet energy carried by the level sets of w, constructed as follows. For r > 0 put mu_{r,j}(E) := <int_0^r R |grad w|^2 1_{w in E} dR>_{B_j} for Borel sets E in [0, W]. The thin-strip bound mu_{r,j}((v - eps, v + eps)) <= C_r eps (integrate the divergence of R T_eps(w - v) grad w, T_eps the truncation of the identity at level eps; the axis term vanishes and the axial boundary average carries a factor 1/Lambda_j) gives mu_{r,j}(E) <= C'_r |E|, so the Banach limit mu_r is a countably additive measure, absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure; mu := lim_{r -> infinity} mu_r is a countably additive extended measure without atoms (possibly infinite), and D_g(r) = int g'' d mu_r (C^1 approximation of g at fixed radius first, radial limit second); together with the linear relation <lim_L <Q_s w(s)>>_log = -2 nu A and the zero mean of Q. These relations are consistent: for 0 < W_2 < A the inflow distribution (2 nu A/W_2)(delta_0 - delta_{W_2}) over deficit levels and the nonnegative measure mu with density 2 v (A - W_2)/W_2 on [0, W_2] and 2 (A - v) on [W_2, A] satisfy all of them, so excluding them needs additional constraints, such as the flux-energy estimate of (i); no field realizing these data is constructed, and the flux ratio 2 nu A/W_2 they give is a logarithmic-mean value, not a pointwise limit. For steady fields of fixed axial period P with |U^R| <= B, the Wirtinger inequality gives D_{gamma^2}(L) >= (32 pi^2 nu^2 A^2/(B^2 P^2)) log L (1 - o(1)), and then the gamma^2 identity forces <rho d(rho)>_log = infinity; the second field of (f) has rho d -> A, which is why it fails. Assume in addition that U solves the momentum equations with a pressure P such that MM P_R and MM P_Z are defined at every radius and the long-box means of d_Z P_R tend to zero, locally uniformly in R (true when P_R is bounded, and when the pressure gradient is Lipschitz and bounded in BMO; sublinear axial growth |P_R| = o(|Z|) suffices when the box centres satisfy |Z_0| = O(Lambda)). Averaging the radial, angular and axial momentum equations with MM gives (1/R)(R MM (U^R)^2)' + MM P_R = MM Gamma_U^2/R^3, the relation of (c) again, MM(U^R U^Z) = nu (MM U^Z)' - R MM P_Z/2 with MM P_Z constant in R (since the box means of d_Z P_R tend to zero), hence MM P_Z = 0 because MM(U^R U^Z) and MM U^Z are bounded, so MM(U^R U^Z) = nu (MM U^Z)', and a vanishing axis value of the averaged meridional vorticity; a steady periodic field (from a research consultation; its pressure bounds were checked only by a computer calculation, and this part was not independently reviewed) satisfies all averaged momentum and vorticity balances, the linear relation of (c), uniform saturation and the full pressure Poisson equation with bounded pressure, with weighted mean inflow ratio 6 nu A/(A - theta) > 2 nu for f = (gamma - theta)_+^3, while failing the unaveraged equations and the convex hierarchy. Nonzero weighted mass at a fixed radius is equivalent to positive upper density of a separated superlevel set {Gamma_U(r_*) > theta + delta} in some long-box family; if it fails for every family and every radius, every limiting law of sampled translates of U is carried by ancient solutions with Gamma <= theta, which says nothing about the record orbit itself. At scale R the effective viscosity is nu/R, and the endpoint hypothesis of (e) becomes a first-order statement in nu/R that weak limits do not see.
(i) (critical axial flux; sharpness) Let Phi_rho(Z, tau) := int_0^rho s U^Z(s, Z, tau) ds, the axial flux through the disk of radius rho, so d_Z Phi_rho = Q_rho and |Phi_rho| <= K rho^2/2. If for one box family and its functional MM there are rho_0, a measurable function C(rho) >= 0 and bounded functions c_rho(tau) with
  (H) MM[(Phi_rho - c_rho)^2] <= C(rho)^2 nu^2 rho^2 for all rho >= rho_0,
and int^infinity d rho/(rho (1 + C(rho)^2)) = infinity (for example C constant), then MM[Gamma_U(rho)^2] = 0 at every radius. Proof. Put a := MM[Gamma_U(rho)^2], delta_R := MM[(d_R Gamma_U(rho))^2], delta_Z := MM[(d_Z Gamma_U(rho))^2], D := 2 int_0^rho R (delta_R + delta_Z) dR (the dissipation D_{gamma^2} of (e)), F_2 := MM[Q_rho Gamma_U(rho)^2] and s = log rho, and write dots for d/ds. Since Q_rho = d_Z (Phi_rho - c_rho), integration by parts in Z (the box boundary term vanishes in the limit) and Cauchy-Schwarz give |F_2| <= 2 G' nu rho C(rho) delta_Z^{1/2}. Also a-dot = rho MM[2 Gamma_U d_R Gamma_U] <= 2 G' rho delta_R^{1/2} and D-dot = 2 rho^2 (delta_R + delta_Z). The gamma^2 identity of (e), 2 a - a-dot + D = F_2/nu, therefore yields D <= 2 a + D = a-dot + F_2/nu <= 2^{1/2} G' (1 + C(rho)^2)^{1/2} (D-dot)^{1/2}, hence D-dot >= D^2/(2 G'^2 (1 + C(e^s)^2)). If D(s_1) > 0, integrating d(1/D)/ds <= -1/(2 G'^2 (1 + C(e^s)^2)) over [s_1, infinity) contradicts the divergence of int^infinity d rho/(rho (1 + C(rho)^2)). Thus D = 0, so F_2 = 0, a = c rho^2 by the identity, and boundedness of a gives a = 0. No monotonicity of C is needed and C = 0 is allowed. So C may grow, for example C(rho) = (log rho)^{1/2}, whereas a bound only along an arbitrary unbounded sequence of radii does not suffice (a scalar counterexample, read but not rechecked; see the Status line). Fixed axial period P with |U^R| <= B gives the hypothesis with C = P B/nu. The hypothesis is one power of rho stronger than the available bound, and the growth condition is sharp at the scalar level: for C(rho) = (log rho)^p with p in (1/2, 1] there are exact steady scalar solutions with bounded drift that saturate uniformly in Z (for p = 1 with root-mean-square flux oscillation exactly nu rho log rho/sqrt2; for each fixed p in (1/2, 1] the construction includes the required corrector estimates, and no uniformity of its constants or starting radius as p down 1/2 is asserted), and 1 + C^2 cannot be replaced by C^2 (an example with narrow dips of C). The first construction of this kind uses a bounded smooth divergence-free drift with Stokes stream function Psi = nu R sum_j (v_j(R)/k_j) sin(k_j Z), fixed frequencies k_j = 2^{-j} and smooth radial partition weights v_j, at most two active at each radius and with active k_j comparable to R^{-1/8}, normalized by sum_j v_j^2/k_j^2 = R^{1/4} (so |b^R| <= 3 nu, |b^Z| < nu, |Psi| <= 2 nu R^{9/8} and MM[Phi_R^2] = (nu^2/2) R^{9/4} in every long-box family), and an exact steady circulation with 0 <= A - Gamma <= 6 A (R_0/R)^{1/8} for R >= R_0 = 10^100 and a smooth axis, so exact scalar solutions saturate uniformly, satisfy every scalar convex identity and have Q > 2 nu at near-maximal points with d_R Gamma > 0 at arbitrarily large radius; its axial flux oscillation is of size nu R^{9/8}. It fails the meridional vorticity equation: at R_n = 2^{8n}, Z_n = pi 2^{n-1} the residual times R_n^{11/8} tends to nu^2. For the physical solution, the energy inequality gives the hypothesis with constant C on boxes of physical axial half-length at least ||u_0||_2^2/(8 pi C^2), but such boxes are not seen by the Case-1 limit, and on them the energy inequality bounds the mean Dirichlet energy only by the same order as the available bound for the time-boundary error, so the box version of the argument does not close. A scaling test (not a proof) detects a quasi-steady imbalance in the meridional vorticity equation for short supercritical flux patterns, which is why the first construction above fails it, and gives no dimensional exclusion of axially long patterns (axial wavelength much larger than R at inflow of order nu). For the maximal long pattern psi = nu beta R^2 f(Z/R^2) (Stokes stream function, x = Z/R^2) the leading-order steady vorticity equation is E_1(f) = 2 (x^3 f'')'' - beta [ (x f f'' + f f')' - f'^2 ] = 0. Every bounded C^4 solution of it on (0, infinity) or on (-infinity, 0) is constant. Proof: I := 2 x^2 (x^2 f'')' - beta f x^2 f'' satisfies I' = x E_1(f), so I is constant, and in t = 1/x the function Y := x^2 f'' solves Y' + (beta/2) f(1/t) Y = -I/2. Writing F(t) = f(1/t) (local notation), boundedness near t = 0 forces both Y(0) = 0 and lim_{t down 0} t^2 F'(t) = 0. If I != 0, the integrating-factor formula gives Y a fixed sign and |Y(t)| >= c > 0 for t >= 1; hence F' has a fixed sign and |F'(t)| >= c/(2t) for t >= 2, contradicting boundedness. With I = 0 one gets Y = 0, so f is affine and, being bounded, constant. So bounded steady leading-order outer patterns of this form are uniform axial flows with zero inflow. For the particular steady inner ansatz Psi = nu R^2 h(y), y = Z/R, the leading equation is (h[(1 + y^2) h'' - y h'])' = 0. Under boundedness of h and y h', this equation forces h to be constant. This does not classify general inner matching. Proof: put A_h := (1 + y^2) h'' - y h', so h A_h = k is constant. If k != 0, h has a fixed sign and (h'/(1 + y^2)^{1/2})' = A_h/(1 + y^2)^{3/2} = k/(h (1 + y^2)^{3/2}); since h'/(1 + y^2)^{1/2} -> 0 as y -> infinity (y h' is bounded) and |h| is bounded, h' has a fixed sign and |h'(y)| >= c/y for large y, contradicting boundedness of h. Hence k = 0; continuity gives A_h = 0 everywhere, so h' = b (1 + y^2)^{1/2} for a constant b, and boundedness forces b = 0. This excludes one quadratic-flux mechanism in a restricted class; it does not prove (H) or any o(R^2) bound on the flux oscillation, since compactness on the outer scale, time dependence, general inner matching and intermediate scales are not treated.
(j) (axial velocity) Let m(tau) be bounded measurable with |m| <= K and e(s) := MM[(U^Z(s, ., .) - m)^2]^{1/2}. Then MM[(Phi_rho - rho^2 m/2)^2]^{1/2} <= int_0^rho s e(s) ds. Hence e(s) <= nu C_1/s for s >= s_0 implies (H) with c_rho = rho^2 m/2, rho_0 = s_0 and C = C_1 + K s_0/nu, and then MM[Gamma_U(rho)^2] = 0 at every radius by (i); a nondecreasing C_1(s) with int^infinity d rho/(rho (1 + C_1(rho)^2)) = infinity also suffices. So in a family with positive circulation-square mass, limsup_{s -> infinity} s e(s)/nu = infinity for every such m. This rephrases the missing bound; it is not a route.
(k) (averaged energy budgets) Assume in addition that U is a bounded ancient mild solution of the full Navier-Stokes equations with canonical pressure P. Write u = U^R, v = U^theta, w = U^Z, E_b = (u^2 + w^2)/2, E_theta = v^2/2, d_b = u_R^2 + u_Z^2 + w_R^2 + w_Z^2 + u^2/R^2 and d_theta = v_R^2 + v_Z^2 + v^2/R^2, and put D_b(R) = int_0^R s MM[d_b] ds, D_theta(R) = int_0^R s MM[d_theta] ds, J_b = R MM[u E_b - nu d_R E_b] + MM[Phi_R P_Z], J_theta = R MM[u E_theta - nu d_R E_theta] (Phi_R the disk flux of (i), not a radial derivative) and W(R) := int_0^R MM[U^R Gamma_U^2] s^{-2} ds (centrifugal work). The pressure is centred at (0, Z_0, tau) in each box; the canonical pressure is BMO with bounded gradient, so it grows at most logarithmically relative to this centre, the axial pressure boundary terms are O_R(log Lambda/Lambda), and axial integration by parts turns the radial pressure work R MM[u P] into MM[Phi_R P_Z] (R u = -d_Z Phi_R). Then J_b + nu D_b = W and J_theta + nu D_theta = -W. Moreover W(R) = nu a(R)/R^2 - nu int_0^R D s^{-3} ds with a = MM[Gamma_U^2] and D as in (i), J_theta = -nu D/(2 R^2), W(infinity) = -nu D_theta(infinity) <= 0 and nu D_theta(infinity) <= 2 K^2 G'. These budgets do not imply (H): the pressure work and the meridional transport are unsigned, and the smooth bounded divergence-free kinematic field psi = (V/2) R^2 tanh y, Gamma = A R^2 (L^2 + R^2)^{-1} sech^2 y, y = L Z/(L^2 + R^2), V L = 8 nu, has, for symmetric axial boxes centred at Z = 0 and with the pressure set to zero in these kinematic budget identities, all averaged dissipations, radial energy fluxes and averaged circulation quantities equal to zero, while oddness in Z gives MM[(psi - c_R(tau))^2] >= V^2 R^4/4 for every bounded time-only gauge c_R, so (H) fails for this family. It fails both the circulation equation (residual A L^2 R^2 (10 nu - V L)/(L^2 + R^2)^3 at Z = 0) and the vorticity equation (d_Z R_eta(L, 0) = (A^2 + 168 nu^2)/(4 L^6) > 0 for R_eta = b.grad eta - nu Delta_5 eta - d_Z(q^2)).
(l) (invariant measures; the density-trivial case) Assume in addition that U is a bounded ancient mild axisymmetric solution with |grad^2 U| <= D_2 (for example a Case-1 limit). Let X be the closure of the translates U(. + zeta e_3, . + s), zeta in R, s <= 0, in the topology of local uniform convergence of the field and its first spatial derivatives on R^3 x (-infinity, 0]. Then X is compact and consists of bounded ancient mild axisymmetric solutions with the same bounds (and W^theta <= 1 for a Case-1 limit). For every box family and Banach limit there is a Borel probability measure mu on X, invariant under the axial-temporal shifts, such that MM of every continuous local functional of U is its mu-expectation; in particular a(rho) = int Gamma_W(rho, 0, 0)^2 d mu(W). The mass a vanishes at every radius if and only if mu is concentrated on the constant fields c e_3, |c| <= K. Every box family has a = 0 at every radius if and only if, for all rho, eps > 0, the set of (Z, tau) at which |grad U| > eps somewhere in {R <= rho, |Z' - Z| <= rho, tau - rho^2 <= tau' <= tau} has zero upper Banach density in R x (-infinity, 0]. Here the upper Banach density of a set E is inf_{L, H > 0} sup |E cap B|/|B| over boxes B = [Z_0 - Lambda, Z_0 + Lambda] x [t_0 - T, t_0] with Lambda >= L, T >= H, t_0 <= 0. The record equality, the record inflow and the value of sup Gamma need not pass to members of X. The support of an invariant measure consists of histories that extend uniquely to bounded eternal mild solutions with the same bounds. Hence either (S1) some invariant measure on X charges nonconstant fields, and then an ergodic one does, or (S2) every invariant measure on X is concentrated on constant fields, equivalently U is density trivial in this sense. In case (S1), with V(R) := E|Phi_R - Pi_Z Phi_R|^2 for a nontrivial ergodic measure, where Pi_Z is the projection onto axially invariant random variables, one has int_{R_*}^infinity dR/(R (1 + V(R)/(nu^2 R^2))) < infinity for some R_* > 0; only V(R) <= K^2 R^4/4 is known, and a bound V(R) <= C nu^2 R^2 log R at all large R, for every nontrivial ergodic measure, would exclude (S1), while no fixed power excess V(R) of order R^{2 + 2 alpha}, alpha > 0, would suffice. By (i), the flux bound (H) puts its family in the trivial case, so the averaged route can only exclude (S1). (S2) contains every pattern uniformly localized in the axial direction throughout its past, in the sense used in (g), for example a structure that stays near one height for all past times. All circulation-weighted and derivative-energy balances of this proposition then reduce to 0 = 0, while velocity moments need not vanish, and an exclusion must use unaveraged or Z-integrated information. For a Case-1 limit, in either case, the backward diffusion of the circulation equation from the record, dR_s = (2 nu)^{1/2} dB_s + ((Q - nu)/R)(R_s, Z_s, -s) ds, dZ_s = (2 nu)^{1/2} dB'_s - U^Z(R_s, Z_s, -s) ds, killed at the axis at time zeta, satisfies 1 = E[Gamma(R_s, Z_s, -s) 1_{zeta > s}], so it survives with probability at least 1/A and sup_x Gamma(x, t) >= 1 for every t <= 0; moreover R_s -> infinity almost surely on survival, and E int_0^zeta 1_{R_s <= rho} ds <= h/p_{rho, h} for every h > 0, where p_{rho, h} := P(N(0, 1) < -(rho + K h)/(2 nu h)^{1/2}). This occupation measure is not axial-temporal measure and order-one circulation at radius R forces only |grad U| >= c/R^2, so no lower bound for the density of the nontrivial set follows. Along almost every surviving path, moreover, int_0^infinity (Q - 2 nu)_+ R^{-2} ds = infinity: by Ito, log R_s = log R_0 + int_0^s (Q - 2 nu) R^{-2} ds' + N_s with a martingale N of quadratic variation int_0^s 2 nu R^{-2} ds', and log R_s -> infinity forces the drift integral to be unbounded above (if the quadratic variation stays finite, N converges; otherwise liminf N_s = -infinity). This is a pathwise form of the inflow threshold 2 nu; the magnitude bound (Q - 2 nu)_+ R^{-2} <= K/R is compatible with it.
For Case-1 limits neither averaged saturation nor its failure was established; Proposition 23 gives saturation only along some points.

Key estimates. Notation: D_1, D_2 bound the first and second derivatives of U; w := A - Gamma_U; B = [Z_0 - Lambda, Z_0 + Lambda] x [tau_0 - T, tau_0] with tau_0 <= 0 is a box and <X>_B the mean over B; J_rho := int_0^rho R U^Z Gamma_U dR. MM is a Banach limit (a positive linear functional on bounded sequences, equal to 1 on constants and to the limit on convergent sequences) of <X>_{B_j}, so |MM[X]| <= sup |X|.
(a) R L Gamma = (R Gamma_R - 2 Gamma)_R + R Gamma_ZZ, so int_0^rho R L Gamma_U dR = rho d_R Gamma_U(rho) - 2 Gamma_U(rho) + d_ZZ N_rho (Gamma_U = O(R^2), d_R Gamma_U = O(R)); incompressibility, d_R(R U^R) = -R d_Z U^Z, gives R U^b.grad Gamma_U = (R U^R Gamma_U)_R + (R U^Z Gamma_U)_Z, whose integral is -Q_rho Gamma_U(rho) + d_Z J_rho. For the line sink, Q Gamma + nu rho Gamma_R - 2 nu Gamma = nu p A with p = beta/nu - 2.

The measure: mu_r(E) := lim mu_{r,j}(E) is finitely additive, and the thin-strip bound, extended from intervals to Borel sets by outer regularity of each mu_{r,j}, gives mu_r(E) <= C'_r |E| (|E| the Lebesgue measure); for disjoint E_k, mu_r(union_{k > n} E_k) <= C'_r |union_{k > n} E_k| -> 0, so mu_r is countably additive and atomless, and int phi d mu_r = MM[int_0^r R |grad w|^2 phi(w) dR] for continuous phi (uniform approximation by step functions). Since mu_r increases with r, mu := lim mu_r is a countably additive extended measure; D_f(r) = int g'' d mu_r, D_g(infinity) = int g'' d mu by monotone convergence, and for g_v(w) := (w - v)_+^2/2, C^1 approximation at fixed r and the absence of atoms give D_{g_v}(r) = mu_r((v, W]). So the level balance reads <MM[Q (w - v)_+^2/2]>_log = nu mu((v, W]) - nu (A - v)_+^2. Periodic momentum field (redefining a_0, eps): t_1 := (1 + R^2)^{1/4}, beta = 16 nu, Psi = beta R^2 t_1^{-3} cos Z, a_0 = A (1 - 1/t_1), eps = A nu (t_1 - 1)(4 t_1^3 + 3 t_1^2 + 2 t_1 + 1)/(beta t_1^2 (t_1 + 1)(t_1^2 + 1)), Gamma = a_0 - eps sin Z; then 3A/(4 t_1) <= A - Gamma <= 5A/(4 t_1), ||P||_infty <= (13/4) beta^2 + 7 A^2, ||grad P||_infty <= (37/2) beta^2 + 90 A^2, MM[Q Gamma] -> 2 nu A, F_f/a_f -> 6 nu A/(A - theta), R^2 times the circulation residual at Z = 0 tends to 2 nu A and R^{3/2} times the vorticity residual at Z = 0 to nu beta. (i) Details of the proof of the main theorem (notation of the statement). (1) In each box Q_rho = d_Z(Phi_rho - c_rho), and integration by parts in Z gives <Q_rho Gamma_U(rho)^2>_B = -<2 (Phi_rho - c_rho) Gamma_U d_Z Gamma_U>_B + e_B with |e_B| <= (K rho^2/2 + sup|c_rho|) G'^2/Lambda. For bounded x_j, y_j >= 0, positivity of the Banach limit and x^{1/2} y^{1/2} <= (t x + y/t)/2, minimized over t > 0, give lim (x_j y_j)^{1/2} <= (lim x_j)^{1/2} (lim y_j)^{1/2}. With Cauchy-Schwarz in each box and (H) this yields |F_2| <= 2 G' (MM[(Phi_rho - c_rho)^2])^{1/2} delta_Z^{1/2} <= 2 G' nu rho C(rho) delta_Z^{1/2} for rho >= rho_0, and a' = MM[2 Gamma_U d_R Gamma_U] (difference quotients converge uniformly by the second-derivative bounds) with |a'| <= 2 G' delta_R^{1/2}. (2) R -> |grad Gamma_U(R, Z, tau)|^2 is Lipschitz on [0, rho] uniformly in (Z, tau), so MM commutes with the Riemann sums of the radial integral: delta_R + delta_Z is continuous, D is C^1 and nondecreasing, D-dot = 2 rho^2 (delta_R + delta_Z), and D(rho) <= rho^2 sup_{R <= rho} |grad Gamma_U|^2. (3) Since a >= 0, the gamma^2 identity gives, for s >= log rho_0, D <= 2a + D = a-dot + F_2/nu <= 2 G' rho (delta_R^{1/2} + C delta_Z^{1/2}) <= 2 G' rho (1 + C^2)^{1/2} (delta_R + delta_Z)^{1/2} = 2^{1/2} G' (1 + C^2)^{1/2} (D-dot)^{1/2}. (4) If D(s_1) > 0 for some s_1 >= log rho_0, then D > 0 on [s_1, infinity) and d(1/D)/ds = -D-dot/D^2 <= -1/(2 G'^2 (1 + C(e^s)^2)), so 0 < 1/D(s) <= 1/D(s_1) - (2 G'^2)^{-1} int_{s_1}^s du/(1 + C(e^u)^2), whose right side tends to -infinity. Hence D = 0 on [rho_0, infinity), and on [0, infinity) by monotonicity; so delta_Z = 0, (1) with c_rho = 0 and |Phi_rho| <= K rho^2/2 gives F_2 = 0 at every radius, the identity gives (a/rho^2)' = 0, and 0 <= a <= G'^2 forces a = 0. For theta >= 0, 0 <= (gamma - theta)_+^2 <= gamma^2, so that weight has zero mass as well. Variants: for one fixed axial period P with |U^R| <= B, the period mean c_rho(tau) of Phi_rho(., tau) gives |Phi_rho - c_rho| <= P sup|Q_rho| <= P B rho, so C = P B/nu; if (H) holds on radii with bounded gaps, |Phi_r - Phi_R| <= K |r^2 - R^2|/2 gives it at all large radii with a larger constant. A bound along an arbitrary unbounded sequence of radii does not suffice: the two-mode construction below with exponent 1/64 in place of 1/8, its weights multiplied on |R - R_j| < R_j^{3/4}, R_j = 2^{64 j}, by a smooth factor equal to R_j^{-1/64} near R_j, has MM[Phi_{R_j}^2] = nu^2 R_j^2/2 and an exact saturating circulation; this example was read, not rechecked. The kinematic model of (f) and the periodic momentum field of (h) satisfy (H) (the latter with C^2 = 256 sqrt3/9) and have MM[Gamma^2] -> A^2 > 0; this is possible only because both violate the gamma^2 identity, through which the circulation equation enters. Physical boxes: Cauchy-Schwarz and the energy inequality give int psi(r, z, t)^2 dz <= r^2 E_0/(4 pi) for psi := int_0^r s u^z ds, hence, in the normalized variables of U_n, <Phi_{n,rho}^2>_B <= nu_n^2 rho^2 E_0/(8 pi Lambda r_n), which is (H) on boxes of physical half-length Lambda r_n >= E_0/(8 pi C^2). The argument on such boxes needs the box errors below D_b/4 up to radius rho_1 exp(c G'^2 (C^2 + 1)/D_b), D_b the box-mean Dirichlet energy at rho_1 (local notation), while |grad Gamma|^2 <= 2 r^2 |grad u|^2 and the energy inequality give only D_b <= 4 C^2 rho_1^2/(gamma_n T), the order of the time-boundary error G'^2 rho^2/T; for the heat example Gamma = r^2 h_t^{-5/2} e^{-(r^2 + z^2)/(4 h_t)}, h_t = 1 + t, Phi = 0 and the initial inventory carries all the dissipation.
Constructions (exact steady solutions of the scalar circulation equation only). Let lambda be the flat step from 0 to 1 obtained by normalizing int_0^t e^{-1/[u(1-u)]} du on [0, 1], and k_j = 2^{-j} (local notation). With H := R^{-1/8}, chi := sum_j (v_j/k_j^2) cos(k_j Z) (so chi_ZZ = -V) and zeta the cosine polynomial whose Z-second derivative is minus the deviation from its period mean of V (chi H'' + chi_R H') - nu^{-1} b^Z chi_Z H' (all its frequencies lie between R^{-1/8}/2 and 4 R^{-1/8}, so there are no small divisors), the function sigma := H + chi H' + zeta (local notation) satisfies exactly nu^{-1} calA sigma = (H/R^2)(17/64 - R^{1/4}/128) + E, the main term being the period-averaged operator (two-mode orthogonality), with |E| <= 10^42 H R^{-5/2}; hence, for R >= R_0, H/2 <= sigma <= 3H/2 and nu^{-1} calA sigma <= -H R^{-7/4}/256. The barriers 1 - e^{-2 R^2} (calA of it is (-4 nu R - b^R) times its R-derivative, hence <= 0) and (1 - c sigma)_+ on R >= R_0, 0 below, with c = 4 R_0^{1/8} (so c sigma >= 2 at R_0), the exhaustion of (f) on (1/j, j) x (-j, j), and the axis argument (q_0 = g/R^2 in [0, 2] is Delta_5-harmonic where b = 0; tube errors O(eps^2), O(eps^3)) give Gamma = A g and the bounds of the statement; at each radius the active modes are commensurable, so MM is the period mean, and Q(R_n, 0) = nu R_n at R_n = 2^{8n}. Logarithmic construction: s = log R >= 4, x = log_2 s, v_n = s k_n cos((pi/2) lambda(t)), v_{n+1} = s k_{n+1} sin((pi/2) lambda(t)) (so 1/(2s) <= k_j <= 2/s, sum_j |v_j| <= 3, sum_j v_j^2/k_j^2 = s^2), and the same correctors with H = H(s); the averaged operator becomes R^{-2} [(1 + d) H_ss + (d_s - 2) H_s] with d := s^2/2 (local notation), equal to (H/R^2)(-1/8 + 1/s + 3/(4 s^2)) <= -H/(16 R^2) for H = s^{-1/2} and s >= 20, and |sigma - H| <= K_1 H s^{29}/R, |E| <= K_1 H s^{35}/R^3 for a fixed constant K_1. The same barriers (c = 4/H(s_0), s_0 = log R_0) and exhaustion give 0 <= A - Gamma <= 6A (log R_0/log R)^{1/2} and MM[Phi_R^2] = nu^2 R^2 (log R)^2/2. At R_n = exp(2^n), Z_n = pi log R_n/2, eta = nu (k^2 R^2 + 1)(log R) sin(kZ)/R^3 with k = 1/log R_n, the transport vanishes and R_n (log R_n)^3 times the vorticity residual tends to nu^2; the residual divided by nu k^2 is comparable to eta, so no perturbative conclusion follows. General p in (1/2, 1]: v_j = s^p k_j times the same weights (bounded drift because p <= 1), d := s^{2p}/2, J := int_4^s dt/(1 + d), w_p := e^{4J}/(1 + d) and H := int_s^infinity w_p = (e^{4J(infinity)} - e^{4J(s)})/4. From w_p' = w_p (4 - d_s)/(1 + d) one gets (1 + d) H_ss + (d_s - 2) H_s = -2 w_p exactly; H is finite and tends to 0 iff int^infinity ds/(1 + d) < infinity, i.e. p > 1/2, and then H ~ (2 e^{4J(infinity)}/(2p - 1)) s^{1 - 2p} and w_p/H ~ (2p - 1)/s. For fixed p, sum_j |d_R^m v_j| <= C_p R^{-m} (m <= 3), |d_R^m H| <= C_p H R^{-m} (m <= 4), |sigma - H| <= C_p H s^{29}/R and |E| <= C_p H s^{35}/R^3, which is dominated by 2 w_p/R^2 for R >= R_0(p); MM[Phi_R^2] = nu^2 R^2 s^{2p}/2, i.e. (H) with C(rho) = (log rho)^p. Dips: with s_j = 2^j, delta_j = s_j^{-2}, a smooth bump vartheta supported in [-1, 1], equal to 1 on [-1/2, 1/2], with values in [0, 1], and beta_d(s) := 1 - sum_{j >= 3} vartheta((s - s_j)/delta_j) (local notation), multiply the v_j of the logarithmic construction by beta_d(s) and take d := beta_d^2 s^2/2 with the same J, w_p, H: the dips have total length 1/24, J(infinity) <= 13/24, 1/s <= H <= 60/s and -2 w_p <= -H/(30 s), and the exact saturating solution has A - Gamma <= 6A H(s)/H(s_0); C(R) := (log R) beta_d(log R) + R^{-1} satisfies MM[Phi_R^2] <= nu^2 R^2 C(R)^2 and int^infinity C^{-2} dR/R = infinity, while int_4^infinity ds/(1 + C(e^s)^2) <= 7/24.
Profiles. For psi = nu beta R^2 f(x), x = Z/R^2, the steady vorticity equation without swirl forcing has residual 8 beta nu^2 x E_1(f) R^{-4} + O(R^{-6}) at fixed x, and the swirl forcing is O(R^{-6}) when Gamma is a function of x to leading order. Rigidity: I' = x E_1(f) by direct differentiation. With t = 1/x and F(t) = f(1/t), t^2 F'(t) = -f'(1/t), Y = (t^2 F')' = x^2 f'', and d/dx = -t^2 d/dt turns I into -2 Y' - beta F Y. On (0, 1] the coefficient of Y' + (beta/2) F Y = -I/2 is bounded, so Y = Y(0) + O(t), t^2 F' = V_0 + Y(0) t + O(t^2) and F = -V_0/t + Y(0) log t + O(1); boundedness gives V_0 = Y(0) = 0, i.e. Y(0) = 0 and lim_{t down 0} t^2 F'(t) = 0. Then Y(t) = -(I/2) int_0^t exp(-(beta/2) int_u^t F) du, and the part u in [t - 1, t] gives |Y(t)| >= c := |I| e^{-B_F}/2 for t >= 1, B_F := |beta| sup|F|/2 (local notation); t^2 F'(t) = int_0^t Y gives |F'(t)| >= c (t - 1)/t^2 >= c/(2t) for t >= 2, with a fixed sign, so |F(t) - F(2)| >= (c/2) log(t/2). If I = 0, uniqueness for the linear equation with Y(0) = 0 gives Y = 0, so f'' = 0 and the bounded affine f is constant. For x < 0 apply this to f(-x), which solves the equation with beta replaced by -beta. Inner ansatz: for Psi = nu R^2 h(y), U^R = -nu h', U^Z = nu (2h - y h') and eta = -nu R^{-2} A_h, and for Gamma a function of y the full steady vorticity equation is -2 nu^2 R^{-3} (h A_h)' + nu^2 R^{-4} [(1 + y^2) A_h'' + 3 y A_h'] - R^{-5} (Gamma^2)' = 0. If h A_h = k is not 0, then h'(y)/(1 + y^2)^{1/2} = -int_y^infinity k h(u)^{-1} (1 + u^2)^{-3/2} du has a fixed sign and modulus at least (|k|/sup|h|) int_y^infinity (1 + u^2)^{-3/2} du, which gives |h'(y)| >= c/y for large y. If k = 0, A_h = 0 on the open set {h != 0} and on the interior of {h = 0}, whose union is dense, hence everywhere by continuity.

(j) Phi_rho - rho^2 m/2 = int_0^rho s f_s ds with f_s := U^Z(s, ., .) - m. Since |d_s U^Z| <= D_1, the Riemann sums sum_i w_i f_{s_i} (w_i = s_i Delta s) converge to it uniformly in (Z, tau), and |x^2 - y^2| <= |x - y| (|x| + |y|) shows that MM of the squares converges. For each finite sum, Cauchy-Schwarz in each box and MM[x^{1/2} y^{1/2}] <= MM[x]^{1/2} MM[y]^{1/2} for box means x, y >= 0 give MM[(sum_i w_i f_{s_i})^2] = sum_{i,k} w_i w_k MM[f_{s_i} f_{s_k}] <= (sum_i w_i e(s_i))^2. The map s -> <f_s^2>_B is Lipschitz uniformly in B (|f_s| <= 2K, |d_s f_s| <= D_1), so e is continuous and the Riemann sums of int_0^rho s e(s) ds converge. With e <= 2K on [0, s_0]: int_0^rho s e ds <= K s_0^2 + nu C_1 rho <= nu (C_1 + K s_0/nu) rho for rho >= s_0.
(k) The two balances are the long-box means of the local energy identities for E_b = ((U^R)^2 + (U^Z)^2)/2 and E_theta = (U^theta)^2/2, integrated over the cylinder of radius R; the exchange term between them is U^R (U^theta)^2/R = U^R Gamma_U^2/R^3, whose cylinder integral per unit axial length is W. With F = MM[Q_rho Gamma_U(rho)^2] and the gamma^2 identity 2 nu a - nu rho a' + nu D = F of (e), W(R) = -int_0^R F s^{-3} ds = nu a(R)/R^2 - nu int_0^R D s^{-3} ds. Expanding |grad(Gamma_U/R)|^2 + Gamma_U^2/R^4 and integrating the cross term gives D_theta(R) = D(R)/(2R^2) + int_0^R D s^{-3} ds - a(R)/R^2. Since |F(s)| <= K G'^2 s, int^infinity D s^{-3} ds < infinity, and int_R^{2R} D s^{-3} ds >= 3 D(R)/(8 R^2) gives D(R)/R^2 -> 0; hence W(infinity) = -nu D_theta(infinity), and |U^R Gamma_U^2| s^{-2} <= K min(K^2, G'^2 s^{-2}) gives nu D_theta(infinity) <= 2 K^2 G'. The kinematic field was checked symbolically (divergence, averages, residuals).
(l) Compactness: the translates are bounded in W^{2,infinity} in space, and the mild formula gives time moduli C h^{1/2} for the field and its gradient on unit intervals (|(e^{nu h Delta} - 1) f| <= C (nu h)^{1/2} ||grad f||_infty, and the kernel of grad e^{nu sigma Delta} P has L^1 norm at most C (nu sigma)^{-1/2}, applied to W.grad W = div(W x W)); Arzela-Ascoli applies, and the mild formulation passes to such limits by the near/far splitting used for Theorem 2. The functional l(f) := MM[f(U(. + zeta e_3, . + s))] on C(X) is positive with l(1) = 1, so Riesz gives mu; invariance follows from |l(f o T) - l(f)| <= 2 ||f||_infty lim |B_j sym. diff. (B_j + (zeta', s'))|/|B_j| = 0. If a = 0 at every radius, invariance gives int Gamma_W(rho, zeta, s)^2 d mu = 0 for all rational rho, zeta and s <= 0, so mu-almost every W has Gamma_W = 0; such W is a bounded ancient mild axisymmetric solution without swirl, hence W = (0, 0, b_3(tau)) by Theorem 5.2 of [KNSS], and a spatially constant mild solution is constant in time (the nonlinear term vanishes). For the density statement use the continuous functional g(W) := min{1, (sup_window |grad W| - eps/2)_+/(eps/2)}, which equals 1 on the set in question and vanishes on constants, in both directions; a nonconstant W in X has grad W != 0 somewhere. The ergodic clause uses Krein-Milman (if all extreme invariant measures were concentrated on the closed set of constants, every invariant measure would be) and, for generic members, the pointwise ergodic theorem along tempered Folner sequences [Lin], used as stated. Mild closedness: drop the last eps of the Duhamel integral (error C K^2 (eps/nu)^{1/2}) and split the convolution into a large ball, where the convergence is local, and its complement, where the Oseen tails are integrable; this excludes a parasitic time-dependent constant. The dichotomy concerns all invariant probabilities: if one gives positive integral to a nonnegative continuous f vanishing on constants, some finite-box average of f at a member of X, and hence at a translate of U, is positive, and expanding boxes give a family with positive mean. The backward shifts are injective on X by forward mild uniqueness, so on the (invariant) support of an invariant measure they are homeomorphisms, which gives the eternal extension and an R^2 action, to which the pointwise ergodic theorem applies along the dyadic boxes [-2^j, 2^j] x [-2^j, 0]. For the necessary condition in (S1): stationarity of p_Z and logarithmic axial growth of the canonical pressure give E p_Z = 0; the axial spectral measures satisfy d sigma_Q = k^2 d sigma_Phi, so V(R) = int_{k != 0} k^{-2} d sigma_{Q, R}(k); axial integration by parts gives E(Q Gamma^2) = -E[(Phi_R - Pi_Z Phi_R) 2 Gamma Gamma_Z], and the Riccati argument of (i) with C(R)^2 = V(R)/(nu^2 R^2) gives the integral condition (positive mass forces positive Dirichlet integral D(R_*)). A stationary axially ergodic kinematic field (annular stream-function bumps with independent phases and incommensurable frequencies k_n = l_n/L_n^2) has bounded variance of Q and flux variance of order R^4, and satisfies the mean axial momentum relation and the mean meridional-vorticity relation (but not every averaged energy budget), so these relations, stationarity and boundedness do not control V; it is not a Navier-Stokes solution. For the radial escape: the radial drift (Q - nu)/R = -U^R - nu/R is at most K, so from R <= rho the comparison R_h <= rho + K h + (2 nu)^{1/2}(B_h - B_0) gives absorption within time h with probability at least p_{rho, h}, uniformly in the starting point; at stopping times of returns to {R <= rho} separated by h the conditional survival probability is at most 1 - p_{rho, h}, so infinitely many returns have probability zero on survival, and the same comparison gives p_{rho, h} P(zeta > s, R_s <= rho) <= P(zeta > s) - P(zeta > s + h), which integrates to the occupation bound. A three-dimensional stationary energy argument (nu E|grad W|^2 = 0) is not available because homogeneity holds only along the axis and the radial energy flux of (k) can feed the dissipation.

Proposition 27 (finite-window realization; conditional). Let nu > 0 and let W be a bounded mild ancient solution of the Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity nu on R^3 x (-infinity, 0], axisymmetric, with bounded circulation and nonzero swirl, normalized by sup |W^theta| = 1 = W^theta(e_1, 0) (Theorem 3(b) supplies this normalization at the viscosity 1/gamma'; the viscosity cannot in general also be set to 1, because the scaling preserves the product of the swirl amplitude and the record radius: the resulting viscosity is 1/gamma', which equals 1 only when gamma' = 1). Put K := ||W||_infty (so K >= 1) and G' := ||Gamma_W||_infty. Fix T > 0. Let Psi(r, z) := int_0^r s W^z(s, z, -T) ds be the Stokes stream function of the meridional part b of W(., -T) and psi := Psi/r, so b(., -T) = curl(psi e_theta), |Psi| <= K r^2/2 and psi e_theta is smooth. Let chi be a smooth radial cutoff with 0 <= chi <= 1, chi = 1 on B_1, supp chi in B_2, |grad chi| <= 2, chi_rho := chi(./rho), and
  v_0^rho := curl(chi_rho psi e_theta) + chi_rho W^theta(., -T) e_theta,   rho >= 1.
Then v_0^rho is smooth, supported in B_{2 rho}, axisymmetric and divergence free, equals W(., -T) on B_rho, and |v_0^rho| <= 10^{1/2} K, |r v_0^{rho,theta}| <= G', |v_0^{rho,theta}| <= 1. Let v^rho be the classical solution with viscosity nu and data v_0^rho, with maximal time T_rho, and w^rho(x, tau) := v^rho(x, tau + T).
(a) (Weighted stability.) Assume K_1 := sup_{rho >= rho_1} ||v^rho||_{L^infty(R^3 x [0, min(T, T_rho)))} < infinity for some rho_1 >= 1. Then T_rho > T for rho >= rho_1, and for every a in (0, 1) and L > 0,
  sup_{|x| <= L, -T <= tau <= 0} |w^rho - W| <= C_1 K (1 + L/(nu T)^{1/2})^a [2^{3/2} e^{-rho^2/(32 nu T)} + (2 (nu T)^{1/2}/rho)^a] (1 + 2 B T^{1/2}) e^{pi B^2 T},
with C_1 = 1 + 10^{1/2}, B = C_4 (K_1 + K) nu^{-1/2} and C_4 = (4 pi/3) C_O + 4 pi C_O B(3 + a, 1 - a), where C_O is the constant of the Oseen kernel bound below and B(., .) is the Beta function. If moreover L >= 2 and T >= L^2 + 1, then w^rho -> W in C^2 of closure(B_L), uniformly for tau in [-L^2, 0], as rho -> infinity.
For parts (b) and (c), fix L >= 2 and T >= L^2 + 1.
(b) (Window bounds.) Under the hypothesis of (a), for every eps > 0 and all large rho: |w^rho| <= K + eps on Q_L := closure(B_L) x [-L^2, 0]; |Gamma_{w^rho}| <= G' on R^3 x [-T, T_rho - T); sup_{-T <= tau <= 0} int_{|y| > L'} |w^rho|^2 |y|^{-4} dy <= 4 pi K_1^2/L' for every L' > 0; v^rho is smooth with finite energy on [0, T].
(c) (Record inequality.) Under the hypothesis of (a), assume the strict-maximum condition: the set {W^theta = 1} cap Q_L does not meet the parabolic boundary of Q_L. Then for all large rho the maximum of w^{rho,theta} over Q_L is attained at a point (x', tau') with |x'| < L, -L^2 < tau' <= 0 and distance r' > 0 from the axis, close to {W^theta = 1} cap Q_L, and there -r' w^{rho,r}(x', tau') >= nu, with no loss. The condition fails for every steady W.
(d) (Dichotomy.) If the hypothesis of (a) fails for every rho_1, then either the data v_0^rho lose regularity at or before time T for arbitrarily large rho, or T_rho > T for all large rho and ||v^{rho_k}||_{L^infty(R^3 x [0, T])} -> infinity along some rho_k -> infinity.
Not claimed: a global first crossing of the swirl of v^rho on R^3 x [0, T] (the bound |v^{rho,theta}| <= 1 holds in the shell rho <= |x| <= 2 rho at time 0 and is not established there later); an energy bound uniform in rho (||v_0^rho||_2^2 is bounded above by (320 pi/3) K^2 rho^3; no bound uniform in rho is established); any quantitative bound on the historical shape ratio of v^rho (under the hypothesis of (a), that ratio is finite on [T/2, T] for all sufficiently large rho); a bound for all later times (under the hypothesis of (a), the local existence theory for bounded data also gives a continuation beyond T, with a bound uniform in rho, on an interval of length c nu/K_1^2 for an absolute constant c > 0).
Consequence (conditional compatibility, not a classification). Under the hypothesis of (a), the stated finite-window bounds, bounded circulation and local C^2 approximation are compatible with finite-energy solutions regular on [0, T]. Under the additional strict-maximum hypothesis, the window maximum also satisfies the exact record inequality. This is a conditional compatibility result, not a theorem classifying all possible exclusion arguments. The proposition does not reproduce a global first-crossing record, several ordered records of one trajectory with common physical constants, or condition (A) across those records. The strict-maximum hypothesis is sufficient; no necessity is asserted. Local C^2 approximation alone does not establish preservation of a global first-crossing record.

Proof sketch with key estimates. Data: curl(chi_rho psi e_theta) = chi_rho b(., -T) + grad chi_rho x (psi e_theta), and on supp grad chi_rho one has r <= 2 rho, so the second term is meridional and at most (2/rho)(K r/2) <= 2K; hence |v_0^rho|^2 <= (3K)^2 + 1 <= 10 K^2, and d_0 := v_0^rho - W(., -T) is supported in {|x| >= rho} with |d_0| <= C_1 K. (a) Both w^rho and W are bounded mild solutions on [-T, 0], and d := w^rho - W satisfies d(tau) = e^{nu(tau + T) Delta} d_0 - int_{-T}^tau e^{nu(tau - s) Delta} P div(d (x) w^rho + W (x) d)(s) ds, the force being at most (K_1 + K)|d|. The kernel O^h of e^{h Delta} P div satisfies |O^h(x)| <= C_O (|x| + h^{1/2})^{-4} [KNSS, sec. 3, (3.7)]. With ell := (nu T)^{1/2}, the weight omega(x) := (1 + |x|/ell)^{-a} satisfies omega(y)/omega(z) <= 1 + (|y - z|/ell)^a, and int |O^h(x)| (1 + (|x|/ell)^a) dx <= C_4 h^{-1/2} for h <= ell^2 (the corresponding moment of the kernel majorant equals 4 pi C_O h^{(a-1)/2} B(3 + a, 1 - a), finite because a < 1). The heat term is at most 2^{3/2} C_1 K e^{-rho^2/(32 nu T)} for |y| <= rho/2 (the Gaussian with doubled variance has mass 2^{3/2}) and at most C_1 K with omega(y) <= (2 ell/rho)^a for |y| > rho/2. So N(tau) := sup_x omega(x)|d(x, tau)| satisfies N(tau) <= N_0 + B int_{-T}^tau (tau - s)^{-1/2} N(s) ds; inserting this once into itself, with int_u^tau (tau - s)^{-1/2}(s - u)^{-1/2} ds = pi, and applying the Gronwall lemma gives N <= N_0 (1 + 2 B T^{1/2}) e^{pi B^2 T}. The C^2 convergence follows from the smoothing bounds ||grad^k u(t)||_infty <= C_k K_1 [min{nu(t - t_0), nu^2 K_1^{-2}}]^{-k/2} for bounded mild solutions ([KNSS, Proposition 4.1], rescaled to viscosity nu), which give bounds uniform in rho for k <= 3 on [-L^2, 0], and the symmetric-difference interpolation |d_ee g(x)| <= 4 ||g||_infty/delta^2 + (delta/3)||grad^3 g||_infty, applied with the C^0 convergence on B_{L+1} (mixed second derivatives by polarization; the margin T - L^2 >= 1 gives the third-derivative bounds up to the terminal time). (b) The circulation bound is the maximum principle for Gamma, and the tail bound is int_{|y| > L'} |y|^{-4} dy = 4 pi/L'. (c) With sup_{Q_L} |w^rho - W| < eps <= (1 - max over the parabolic boundary of W^theta)/3, the maximum of w^{rho,theta} over Q_L exceeds 1 - eps and the values on the parabolic boundary are at most 1 - 2 eps, so the maximum is interior in space, its left time derivative is nonnegative, its spatial gradient vanishes and d_rr + d_zz of w^{rho,theta} is nonpositive (diagonal entries of the nonpositive Hessian); the swirl equation then gives -r' w^r = nu + (r'^2/w^theta)(d_tau w^theta - nu d_rr w^theta - nu d_zz w^theta) >= nu. A steady W attains the value 1 at (e_1, -L^2). (d) is logic: if the first alternative fails, choose for each k a radius rho_k >= k with sup norm at least k on [0, T]. A continuity argument in rho does not replace this choice: a smoothly parametrized family may lose regularity at bounded parameters while the escaping members stay small (the scalar family y' = y^2, y(0) = 2/rho shows the logical point).

Status: the argument above is a proof sketch with the key estimates, for the conditional form stated; the consequence is a conditional compatibility statement, not a classification of exclusion arguments; source: own derivation; verification: checked step by step by the author, and in two independent adversarial reviews; the first confirmed (a)-(c) and found two errors in an earlier version (a continuity argument for (d), and a normalization fixing both the swirl amplitude and the record radius at viscosity 1), both repaired as above; the second confirmed the estimates again and required the window restrictions before (b), the kernel-majorant and interpolation wording, the energy upper bound and the narrowed consequence, all included.

Proposition 28 (shape bound for axisymmetric fields with swirl; location of gradient records). Let U be a bounded, globally C^{1,1}, divergence-free vector field on R^3, axisymmetric about the x_3-axis (swirl allowed), and put M = sup|U| > 0, H = ess sup|grad^2 U| > 0 (Cartesian Frobenius norms, as in (A)). Put p = 2 7^{-1/4}, q = 2^{1/4}, c = 6 10^{-1/4}, let B_2 = 2 + (2p - 2^{1/2})^2 = 3.091897... and B_3 = B_2 + (c - 2p)^2 = 3.928931... be the constants of Proposition 11(v), and put
  B_ax := max{2p^2, q^2, 2p^2 + (c - 2p)^2, (c - q)^2/2 + q^2} = 2p^2 + (c - 2p)^2 = 3.860749266...,
  F(lambda) := lambda + (2p - lambda^{1/2})^2 + (c - 2p)^2.
For a point x let r(x) be its distance from the axis and rho(x) := r(x) (H/M)^{1/2}.
(a) At every point x of the axis, |grad U(x)|^2 <= B_ax M H.
(b) At every point x, |grad U(x)|^2 <= (B_ax + rho(x)^2) M H. If r(x) > 0, then |grad U(x)|^2 <= B_2 M H + |U(x)|^2/r(x)^2 <= (B_2 + rho(x)^{-2}) M H, and for every lambda in [1 + c^2/18, 2) = [1.632456..., 2),
  |grad U(x)|^2 <= max{F(lambda), B_2 + lambda (2 - lambda)/(rho(x)^2 + 2 - lambda)} M H.
(c) Consequently sup|grad U|^2 <= B_axi M H with B_axi := 3.9184 < B_3.
(d) (Historical consequences.) Assume (A). Then C_* >= 1/B_axi = 0.25520.... If C_* < 1/B_ax = 0.2590170796..., every late gradient record (x, s), i.e. |grad u(x, s)| = D(s), satisfies
  r(x) D(s)/M(s) >= (1 - B_ax C_*)^{1/2}/C_* > 0.
If C_* < c_2 = 1/B_2 = 0.3234..., every late gradient record satisfies
  r(x) D(s)/M(s) <= (1 - B_2 C_*)^{-1/2};
in particular the quantity a(s) of Proposition 11(viii) is bounded by (1 - B_2 C_*)^{-1/2} at every late gradient record. Consequently, when C_* < c_2, in the last statement of Proposition 11(viii) the hypothesis epsilon_n >= epsilon_0 is needed only for the stated lower bound on Lambda_n, and the inequality of the L^infty budget of Proposition 14 holds along every branch-(II) sequence without the hypothesis epsilon_n >= epsilon_0, with C_4 = 4 (R_1 + (1 - B_2 C_*)^{-1/2}) max(1, C_5)/c_0 depending only on C_* and G.
(e) (Cylindrical second derivatives.) For U = u e_r + v e_theta + w e_z smooth and axisymmetric, at (r, 0, z) with r > 0, put a = u_r, b = u_z, c_0 = u/r, d = w_r, e = w_z, f = v_r, g = v_z, h = v/r. Then grad U has rows (a, -h, b), (f, c_0, g), (d, 0, e), and
  |grad^2 U|^2 = sum_{F = u, v, w} (F_rr^2 + 2 F_rz^2 + F_zz^2) + [3(a - c_0)^2 + 3(f - h)^2 + 2 b^2 + 2 g^2 + d^2]/r^2;
if div U = 0, then |grad^2 U|^2 >= [(11/3)(a - c_0)^2 + (8/3) b^2 + 3(f - h)^2 + 2 g^2 + d^2]/r^2.
Proposition 11(v) excludes C_* < 1/B_3 = 0.25452... outright at gradient record times; part (d) raises this to 0.25520..., and for 1/B_axi <= C_* < 1/B_ax it confines the late gradient records to the shell (1 - B_ax C_*)^{1/2}/C_* <= r D/M <= (1 - B_2 C_*)^{-1/2}. The divergence-free bound of Proposition 11(v), obtained later, supersedes (a), (c) and these two consequences: it gives |grad U|^2 <= B_div M H at every point with B_div = 3.830187... < B_ax, so (A) forces C_* >= 1/B_div = 0.261083... > 1/B_ax, and no admissible C_* lies in the range of the shell statement; the sharp inequality of Proposition 11(v), obtained after that, gives |grad U|^2 <= (12/sqrt10) M H for every bounded C^{1,1} field, without the divergence condition, and hence C_* >= sqrt10/12 = 0.263523...; the divergence-free inequality of Proposition 11(v), obtained last, gives |grad U|^2 <= B_div'' M H with B_div'' = 3.702534... and hence C_* >= 1/B_div'' = 0.270085...; the upper bound for C_* < c_2 is not affected. With the sharp planar inequality of Proposition 11(v), applied to y -> U(x + Q_2 y) with G := grad U(x) and Q_2 the 3 x 2 matrix of its first two right singular vectors, one obtains sigma_1^2 + sigma_2^2 <= B_2' M H, where B_2' = 8/sqrt7. In the normalization M = H = 1 used in step (1) of the proof of (b), this reads sigma_1^2 + sigma_2^2 <= B_2'; so B_2 may be replaced by B_2' in the second and third bounds of (b) and in the proof of the upper bound of (d), which therefore holds for C_* < sqrt7/8 = 0.3307... in the form r(x) D(s)/M(s) <= (1 - B_2' C_*)^{-1/2}, and the statements of Propositions 11(viii) and 14 that use it hold for C_* < sqrt7/8 with this bound. The route cannot be decisive: by the columnar vortex of Proposition 11(v) (the planar radial vortex with its rotation axis as the symmetry axis) no constant of this kind is smaller than 8/sqrt7 = 3.0237..., and by the example with swirl of Proposition 11(v) none is smaller than 6(2 + 10^{1/2})/94^{1/2} = 3.1946..., so no inequality of this type can exclude C_* > 94^{1/2}/(6(2 + 10^{1/2})) = 0.313019.... In particular the swirl-free constants 1/c_3 = 3.1660..., 1/c_3' = 3.1217... and 1/c_3'' = 3.0476... of Proposition 11(v), and the sharp swirl-free constant 8/sqrt7 = 3.0237... there, do not hold with swirl.
Proof. All statements are trivial when M = 0 or H = 0 and invariant under the scaling U -> U(x (M/H)^{1/2})/M, which preserves the axis and replaces r(x) by rho(x); so assume M = H = 1, hence rho = r. By radial mollification in R^3, which preserves axisymmetry, incompressibility and both bounds and gives locally uniform convergence of U and grad U, assume U smooth: the conclusions of (a)-(c) are closed conditions on (U(x), grad U(x)) and pass to the limit.
(a) At an axis point, invariance of grad U under conjugation by rotations about e_3 forces the horizontal block to be a rotation-dilation [[a, -h], [h, a]] and the mixed entries to vanish, and div U = 0 gives d_3 U_3 = -2a. The singular values are t, t, v with t = (a^2 + h^2)^{1/2}, v = 2|a|, and |grad U|^2 = 2t^2 + v^2. The singular-value inequality of Proposition 11(v) with k = 2 (since 2t <= sigma_1 + sigma_2, regardless of the ordering of t, t, v) and k = 3 gives t <= p and 2t + v <= c. Differentiating div U = 0 in x_3 gives U_{3,33} = -(U_{1,13} + U_{2,23}); the Frobenius norm counts U_{1,13} and U_{2,23} twice, so |grad^2 U|^2 >= U_{3,33}^2 + 2U_{1,13}^2 + 2U_{2,23}^2 >= 2U_{3,33}^2 everywhere, and the scalar inequality |f'(s)|^2 <= 2L(sup|f| - |f(s)|) for |f''| <= L on the axial line through x, with L = 2^{-1/2}, gives v^2 <= 2^{1/2}, i.e. v <= q. This bound on |d_3 U_3| holds at every point of R^3. Thus (t, v) lies in the polygon {0 <= t <= p, 0 <= v <= q, 2t + v <= c}, whose vertices are (0, 0), (p, 0), (p, c - 2p), ((c - q)/2, q), (0, q) because 0 < c - 2p < q and 0 < (c - q)/2 < p. The convex function 2t^2 + v^2 attains its maximum over the polygon at a vertex, and the vertex values are 0, 2p^2 = 3.0237, 2p^2 + (c - 2p)^2 = 3.86075, (c - q)^2/2 + q^2 = 3.80098, q^2 = 1.41421.
(b) By rotation take x = (r, 0, z) with r > 0 (at axis points (a) gives the first bound); let G = grad U(x), V = U(x), sigma_1 >= sigma_2 >= sigma_3 the singular values of G, s := sigma_1^2, m := sigma_3^2. (1) The singular-value inequality of Proposition 11(v) with k = 1, 2, 3 gives sigma_1 <= 2^{1/2}, sigma_1 + sigma_2 <= 2p, sigma_1 + sigma_2 + sigma_3 <= c. By weak majorization as in Proposition 11(v), sigma_1^2 + sigma_2^2 <= B_2; if s <= lambda for some lambda in [p^2, (4p - c)^2] = [1.5118..., 2.3847...], the nonincreasing vector (lambda^{1/2}, 2p - lambda^{1/2}, c - 2p) weakly majorizes (sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3), so |G|^2 <= F(lambda); and 3 sigma_3 <= c gives m <= c^2/9. (2) For a unit vector n, phi = n.U satisfies |phi| <= 1, |grad^2 phi| <= |grad^2 U| <= 1 (Cauchy-Schwarz in the component index) and grad phi(x) = G^T n; the scalar inequality used in (a), on the line through x in the direction of grad phi(x), gives |G^T n|^2 <= 2(1 - |n.V|), that is, n^T G G^T n + 2|n.V| <= 2. (3) If s >= 1 + m/2, then |V|^2 <= (2 - s)(s - m). Indeed, let V != 0, A = G G^T, e_1 a unit eigenvector of A for s, k = s - m, V = alpha e_1 + w with w orthogonal to e_1, beta = |w|; then n^T A n >= m + k (n.e_1)^2 for unit n. (2) with n = V/|V| gives |V| <= 1 - m/2 <= k. Choose epsilon in {-1, 1} with epsilon alpha = |alpha|, taking epsilon = 1 when alpha = 0. Since m <= c^2/9 < 2, k >= 1 - m/2 > 0. For n = epsilon (1 - beta^2/k^2)^{1/2} e_1 + w/k (a unit vector) we get n^T A n >= s - beta^2/k and n.V = |alpha| (1 - beta^2/k^2)^{1/2} + beta^2/k >= |V|^2/k, since (1 - beta^2/k^2)^{1/2} >= |alpha|/k is equivalent to k^2 >= |V|^2; (2) gives s - beta^2/k + 2|V|^2/k <= 2, and beta <= |V| gives s + |V|^2/k <= 2. (4) Axisymmetry: the derivative of U in the direction e_theta at x is G e_theta = (u e_theta - v e_r)/r, so sigma_3 <= |G e_theta| <= |V|/r, i.e. r^2 m <= |V|^2. With (1) this gives |G|^2 <= B_2 + |V|^2/r^2, the second bound. (5) Fix lambda in [1 + c^2/18, 2). If s <= lambda, (1) gives |G|^2 <= F(lambda). If s >= lambda, then s >= 1 + m/2 by (1), and (3), (4) give r^2 m <= (2 - s)(s - m); since the right side is nonincreasing in s for s >= 1 + m/2 (its derivative is 2 + m - 2s), r^2 m <= (2 - lambda)(lambda - m), so m <= lambda (2 - lambda)/(r^2 + 2 - lambda), and (1) gives |G|^2 <= B_2 + m. This is the third bound. (6) Let G_0 be the average of R G R^T over the rotations R about e_3 (Haar measure). Each R G R^T has the singular values of G, and the sums of the k largest singular values are convex functions of the matrix, so G_0 satisfies the inequalities of (1); G_0 commutes with these rotations, so it has the axis form [[alpha_0, -beta_0, 0], [beta_0, alpha_0, 0], [0, 0, e]] with alpha_0 = (a + c_0)/2, beta_0 = (f + h)/2 in the notation of (e), and its (3, 3) entry is that of G, e = d_3 U_3(x) = -(a + c_0) = -2 alpha_0, with e^2 <= 2^{1/2} by the bound on |d_3 U_3| in the proof of (a). The polygon argument of (a) therefore gives |G_0|^2 <= B_ax. Averaging over a group of Frobenius isometries is the orthogonal projection onto the invariant matrices, so |G|^2 = |G_0|^2 + |G - G_0|^2, and G - G_0 = [[(a - c_0)/2, (f - h)/2, b], [(f - h)/2, (c_0 - a)/2, g], [d, 0, 0]] has |G - G_0|^2 = (a - c_0)^2/2 + (f - h)^2/2 + b^2 + g^2 + d^2 <= r^2 |grad^2 U(x)|^2 <= r^2 by the inequality of (e). This is the first bound.
(c) For rho <= 0.24 the first bound of (b) gives |grad U|^2 <= B_ax + 0.0576 = 3.918349.... For rho >= 0.24 the third bound with lambda = 1.958 gives |grad U|^2 <= max{F(1.958), B_2 + 1.958 (0.042)/(0.0576 + 0.042)} = max{3.918351708844..., 3.917560267630...}, since the second term decreases in rho. Hence sup|grad U|^2 <= 3.918352 < 3.9184.
(d) Let (x, s) be a late gradient record and apply (b), (c) to U = u(s), whose sup norms are at most M(s) and H(s); (A) at s gives M(s) H(s) <= C_* D(s)^2. By (c), D(s)^2 <= B_axi C_* D(s)^2, so C_* >= 1/B_axi. By the first bound of (b), D(s)^2 <= B_ax M(s) H(s) + r(x)^2 H(s)^2 <= B_ax C_* D(s)^2 + r(x)^2 C_*^2 D(s)^4/M(s)^2, which is the lower bound on r(x) D(s)/M(s). By the second bound, D(s)^2 <= B_2 C_* D(s)^2 + M(s)^2/r(x)^2, which is the upper bound. In Proposition 11(viii), a(s) = r(x(s)) D(s)/M(s); with a_n bounded, r(x_n) = a_n M(s_n)/D(s_n) = o(Lambda_n) by the statement M(s_n)/D(s_n) = o(Lambda_n) proved there, and |x_n - z_n e_3| <= |z(x_n) - z_n| + r(x_n) gives |z(x_n) - z_n|/Lambda_n -> infinity whenever (t_n - s_n)/T_n stays bounded along a sequence of swirl records in branch (II). In the proof of the L^infty budget of Proposition 14 the hypothesis epsilon_n >= epsilon_0 enters only through the bound on a(s_n) in step (iii); replacing that bound by a(s_n) <= (1 - B_2 C_*)^{-1/2} gives the stated C_4.
(e) The Cartesian second derivatives at (r, 0, z) are d_11 U = (u_rr, v_rr, w_rr), d_12 U = (-(f - h)/r, (a - c_0)/r, 0), d_13 U = (u_rz, v_rz, w_rz), d_22 U = ((a - c_0)/r, (f - h)/r, d/r), d_23 U = (-g/r, b/r, 0), d_33 U = (u_zz, v_zz, w_zz) (components in the frame (e_r, e_theta, e_z)); summing the squares, mixed derivatives twice, gives the identity. Differentiating u_r + u/r + w_z = 0 gives u_rr + w_rz = -(a - c_0)/r and u_rz + w_zz = -b/r, and min{x^2 + 2y^2 : x + y = X} = 2X^2/3 applied to the disjoint groups (u_rr, w_rz) and (w_zz, u_rz) gives the inequality.
Status: proved here; source: (a) and (e) were proposed by an independent referee, (b) and (c) by a second independent referee and written out in full in an independent derivation, (d) is the author's; every step was checked by the author; verification: the identity in (e) was checked symbolically at random points for generic axis-regular profiles; the constants, the polygon maximum and the three comparison values in (c) were checked in 30-digit arithmetic, and a scan over 22000 values of rho and 200000 values of lambda gave numerical evidence for an optimum near 3.91833679 (rho approximately 0.23997400, lambda approximately 1.95793848); the scan does not prove optimality, and optimality is not used.

Proposition 29 (historical swirl domination and a uniform lower bound for the gradient-scale viscosity). In the setting of sec. 1.1, without assuming (A), (K) or (TAIL), put kappa(t) := D(t)/M(t)^2 for every t.
