(a) (Historical smoothing.) There are absolute constants C_D, C_H and a time t_1 < T_*, depending on the solution, such that D(t) <= C_D M(t)^2 and H(t) <= C_H M(t)^3 for t in [t_1, T_*).
(b) The following are equivalent:
 (i) (historical swirl domination) there are C_S < infinity and t_0 < T_* with M(t) <= C_S S(t) for t in [t_0, T_*);
 (ii) (uniform gradient-scale condition) there are c > 0 and t_0 < T_* with kappa(t) >= c for t in [t_0, T_*);
 (iii) (A) holds for some C_*, and there are c > 0 and t_0 < T_* with kappa(s) >= c at every gradient record s >= t_0.
Quantitatively, (i) implies (ii) with c = 1/(G C_S^2); (ii) implies (A) with C_* = C_H/c^2; (iii) implies (i) with C_S = 18 C_* C_c, where C_c is the constant of Theorem 13(b) for this c. In particular (i) implies (A) with C_* = C_H G^2 C_S^4.
(c) Assume (i). Then S(t) -> infinity and first-crossing swirl records exist. For every sufficiently late first-crossing swirl record (equivalently, after discarding finitely many terms of any sequence of such records): |U_n(y, tau)| <= C_S for all y in R^3 and tau in [-t_n/T_n, 0], so (K) holds with K = C_S on the whole normalized past; sup_tau int_{|y| > L} |U_n|^2 |y|^{-4} dy <= 4 pi C_S^2/L, so (TAIL) holds; C_S > (1 + G^{-2})^{1/2}, 1/G < nu_n <= (C_S^2 - 1)^{1/2} and t_n/T_n -> infinity; and kappa(s_n) >= 1/(G C_S^2) for the times s_n of Theorem 13(d), so every such sequence lies in branch (I).
(d) (Consequence.) Consider the regularity criterion
 (SD) if u is a smooth finite-energy axisymmetric solution with ||r u_0^theta||_infty < infinity on [0, T), T < infinity, and limsup_{t -> T} M(t)/S(t) < infinity, then u does not lose regularity at T.
The uniform gradient-scale condition means inf_{t_0 <= t < T_*} D(t)/M(t)^2 > 0 for some t_0 < T_*, equivalently condition (iii). A finite-time singular solution satisfying this condition would be a counterexample to (SD) and would satisfy the Case-1 assumptions on every sufficiently late first-crossing swirl-record sequence. Under condition (i), (A), (K) and (TAIL) follow from the estimates above. No converse is asserted from (A), (K), (TAIL), or the existence of a single branch-(I) subsequence alone. Hence an exclusion of Case 1 valid for every finite C_* (even one restricted to sequences in branch (I)) would prove (SD), and a finite-time singular solution violating (SD) would be a fixed-datum counterexample to the exclusion of Case 1.
Remark (literature). Historical domination M <= C_S S is different from instantaneous domination ||u(t)||_infty <= C ||u^theta(t)||_infty and from pointwise bounds between components, and criteria using those hypotheses cannot be interchanged with it. The sources checked do not establish regularity from bounded historical M/S alone; they establish regularity under additional spatial, integrability or blowup-rate assumptions. A Type I bound ||u(t)||_infty <= C (T_* - t)^{-1/2} excludes a singularity ([CSTY2, Theorem 1.1] together with the far-field argument in the proof of Theorem 9), so under (i) a singular solution must satisfy limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t)^{1/2} S(t) = infinity: the swirl itself must grow at a Type II rate. Propositions 30(d) and 31(d) sharpen this without further assumptions: under (i) a singular solution must satisfy limsup_{t -> T_*} [C_S^2 (T_* - t) S(t)^2 - log log(1/(T_* - t)) - (5/2) log log log(1/(T_* - t))] = +infinity, and the same holds with any finite number of further iterated logarithms subtracted. The sliding Petrovskii criterion of [Sh, Corollary 5.4] (a preprint result that invokes the circulation criterion [Wei, Corollary 1.1]) gives a statement of the same kind for every singular solution in its class, with the inflow ||(u^r(t))^-||_infty in place of C_S S(t) and any coefficient below 1/2 in place of 5/2 (remark after Proposition 30); Proposition 31(f), which uses [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] instead, gives any coefficient below 3/2. By contrast, pointwise domination |u| <= C |u^theta| gives |u| <= C G/r and hence regularity by [CSTY2, Theorem 1.1] with epsilon = 0; historical domination gives no such spatial bound. The near-axis circulation modulus |Gamma| <= C_1 |log r|^{-2} of [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] fails at the records, since |Gamma(r_n, z_n, t_n)| = gamma_n >= (C_S^2 - 1)^{-1/2} while r_n -> 0. The one-sided bound u^r >= -C (T - t)^{-1/2} of [QZ, Theorem 1.1] is not furnished by (i). The record results of [Sh4, sec. 10] concern local kinetic energy and time occupation, not historical L^infinity records. The first paper of [SeII] assumes scaled energy, dissipation and pressure bounds and a scaled bound on second derivatives, and passes to limits with vanishing viscosity. Proposition 29 supplies a conditional reduction to (SD), not a proof of (SD) or a verified novelty claim.
Proof. (a) Choose eps_0 > 0 no larger than the bounded-data existence constant and the constants of [KNSS, Proposition 4.1] for (k, l) = (1, 0) and (2, 0). For k = 1, 2, uniqueness of bounded mild solutions and that proposition give constants c_k such that every bounded mild solution v on [t', t' + eps_0 N^{-2}] with ||v(t')||_infty <= N satisfies ||grad^k v(t)||_infty <= c_k N (t - t')^{-k/2} for t in (t', t' + eps_0 N^{-2}]. Put s_0 := eps_0/(2 ||u_0||_infty^2), which is positive and smaller than T_*, since the existence time from u_0 is at least eps_0 ||u_0||_infty^{-2}. For s >= s_0 we have M(s) >= ||u_0||_infty, so t' := s - eps_0/(2 M(s)^2) >= 0 and ||u(t')||_infty <= M(s); the local statement with N = M(s) gives ||grad^k u(s)||_infty <= c_k (eps_0/2)^{-k/2} M(s)^{k+1}. Taking historical suprema, D(t) <= max{D(s_0), 2^{1/2} c_1 eps_0^{-1/2} M(t)^2} and H(t) <= max{H(s_0), 2 c_2 eps_0^{-1} M(t)^3} for t >= s_0; since M(t) -> infinity as t -> T_*, the second entries dominate after some t_1. Thus C_D = 2^{1/2} c_1 eps_0^{-1/2} and C_H = 2 c_2 eps_0^{-1}; the bound on D is the historical mild smoothing defining C_P in sec. 1.1.
(b) (i) => (ii). At r > 0 the derivative of u in the direction e_theta is (u^r e_theta - u^theta e_r)/r, so |u^theta|/r <= |grad u| (Frobenius norm) and |u^theta|^2 = |Gamma| |u^theta|/r <= G |grad u|; hence S(t)^2 <= G D(t) (Theorem 13(a)). Under (i), G > 0, because G = 0 would give S = 0 while M(t) -> infinity. Then kappa = D/M^2 >= S^2/(G C_S^2 S^2) = 1/(G C_S^2) on [t_0, T_*). (ii) => (iii). By (a), M H <= C_H M^4 <= (C_H/c^2) D^2 at late t, which is (A) with C_* = C_H/c^2; the gradient-record condition is a special case of (ii). (iii) => (i). For late t let s be the last time in [0, t] with ||grad u(s)||_infty = D(t); it exists because ||grad u(.)||_infty is continuous on [0, t], and D(s) = D(t) = ||grad u(s)||_infty, so s is a gradient record. Moreover s -> T_* as t -> T_*: M(t) -> infinity and M(t)^5 <= (24 E_0/pi) D(t)^3 (Proposition 11(vi)) give D(t) -> infinity. Theorem 13(e) gives M(t) <= 18 C_* M(s), and Theorem 13(b) gives M(s) <= C_c S(s) <= C_c S(t) once s >= max(t_0, t_c).
(c) T_* < infinity forces M(t) -> infinity (||u(t)||_infty >= c (T_* - t)^{-1/2} [Ler]), hence S(t) >= M(t)/C_S -> infinity. Since u^theta is continuous, decays at infinity and vanishes on the axis, every value of S is attained at a point with r > 0, so first-crossing swirl records exist. For a record with t_n >= t_0, every time t_n + T_n tau with tau in [-t_n/T_n, 0] precedes t_n, so |u(x, t_n + T_n tau)| <= M(t_n) <= C_S S_n, which is the bound on U_n; the tail bound follows from int_{|y| > L} |y|^{-4} dy = 4 pi/L. The record inequality -r_n u^r(r_n, z_n, t_n) >= 1 of Theorem 1 gives |u(x_n, t_n)|^2 >= S_n^2 + r_n^{-2} = S_n^2 (1 + gamma_n^{-2}), so C_S^2 >= 1 + gamma_n^{-2} > 1 + G^{-2}, and nu_n = 1/gamma_n lies in (1/G, (C_S^2 - 1)^{1/2}]; t_n/T_n = t_n S_n^2/gamma_n -> infinity. Here gamma_n < G strictly: let w = epsilon u^theta with epsilon in {-1, 1} the sign attaining S_n at (r_n, z_n, t_n); then epsilon Gamma = r w <= G everywhere at time t_n, and if gamma_n = G this bound would be attained at the interior point (r_n, z_n), forcing d_r(r w) = 0 there, whereas d_r(r w) = w + r d_r w = S_n > 0 at that point. Finally kappa(s_n) >= 1/(G C_S^2) by (i) => (ii), since s_n -> T_*.
(d) is logic from (b) and (c), and the extraction of Theorem 2 supplies the normalized limit at the records.
Status: proved here; source: own derivation; verification: checked step by step by the author, and in an independent adversarial review that rederived the three implications with their constants, the smoothing bounds and the record consequences, compared the literature, and required the repairs of quantifiers and wording now included (the choice of eps_0 for the derivative orders used, the divergence of D, the finite-prefix qualification, the bounds on C_S and nu_n, the formulation of the uniform condition at all late times, and the qualified literature statement).

Proposition 30 (inflow envelopes at the axis and swirl records). In the setting of sec. 1.1, without assuming (A), (K) or (TAIL), put g(t) := ||(u^r(t))^-||_infty, where (.)^- denotes the negative part; g is continuous on [0, T_*) and g <= M. Let (b_v)_{v >= 0} be a standard one-dimensional Brownian motion with b_0 = 0 and P its law. For 0 < h_0 <= T_*/2, call F : [0, h_0] -> [0, infinity) a lower-class envelope if F is continuous and nondecreasing, F(0) = 0, F(s) s^{-1/2} is nonincreasing on (0, h_0], and
 (KP) int_0^{h_0} F(s) s^{-3/2} exp(-F(s)^2/(4s)) ds = infinity.
For 0 < h <= h_0 and r > 0 put P_{F,h}(r) := P(r + 2^{1/2} b_v + F(v) > 0 for all v in (0, h]).
(a) (Sliding windows; a qualitative form of [Sh, Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 4.2].) If int_{sigma - s}^{sigma} g dt <= F(s) for all sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) and s in (0, h_0], then |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G P_{F,h_0}(r) for all r > 0, z in R and t in [T_* - h_0, T_*), and P_{F,h_0}(r) -> 0 as r -> 0.
(b) (Terminal windows.) If int_{T_* - s}^{T_*} g dt <= F(s) for all s in (0, h_0], then sup_z |Gamma(r, z, t)| -> 0 as (r, t) -> (0, T_*) jointly.
(c) (Records.) If the hypothesis of (a) or of (b) holds for some h_0 and some lower-class envelope F, then gamma_n -> 0 along every sequence of first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity, and S(t)/M(t) -> 0 as t -> T_*. Consequently neither hypothesis holds, for any h_0 and any lower-class envelope F, if some sequence of first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity has limsup gamma_n > 0 (in particular on every Case-1 trajectory, where Theorem 1 gives liminf_{n -> infinity} gamma_n >= (K^2 - 1)^{-1/2} > 0), or if limsup_{t -> T_*} S(t)/M(t) > 0 (in particular under Proposition 29(b)(i)).
(d) (Iterated-logarithm envelope.) In each of the two situations named at the end of (c),
 limsup_{t -> T_*} [ (T_* - t) g(t)^2 - L_2(T_* - t) - (3/2) L_3(T_* - t) ] = +infinity,
where L_1(v) = log(1/v) and L_{k+1} = log L_k; the same holds with L_4 + ... + L_m (any m >= 4) also subtracted inside the bracket. Since g <= M, the same holds with M(t)^2 in place of g(t)^2, and under Proposition 29(b)(i) with C_S^2 S(t)^2 in place of g(t)^2. A Type I bound g(t) <= C (T_* - t)^{-1/2} is the case F(s) = 2 C s^{1/2} of (b), so it is excluded in these situations as well (for all axisymmetric solutions a Type I velocity bound is already excluded by [CSTY2]).
(e) (Inflow near the axis only.) For R > 0 put g_R(t) := sup{(u^r)^-(r, z, t) : 0 < r < R, z in R} <= g(t). If int_{sigma - s}^{sigma} g_R dt <= F(s) for all sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) and s in (0, h_0], then |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G (P_{F,h}(r) + exp(-R^2/(16 h))) for all z, all t in [T_* - h_0, T_*), all h in (0, h_0] with F(h) <= R/4 and all r in (0, R/4]; hence sup_z |Gamma(r, z, t)| -> 0 as r -> 0, uniformly in t in [T_* - h_0, T_*). The conclusions of (c) hold under this hypothesis, and (d) holds with g_R in place of g.

Proof. Step 1 (comparison lemma). Let sigma in (0, T_*), 0 < h <= sigma, t_a := sigma - h, and let Ft : (0, h] -> [0, infinity) satisfy D_sigma(v) := int_{sigma - v}^{sigma} g dt <= Ft(v) for v in (0, h]. We show
 |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G P(r + 2^{1/2} b_v + Ft(v) > 0 for all v in (0, h]) for all r > 0, z in R.   (30.1)
Let X(t) := int_{t_a}^t g for t in [t_a, sigma]: a C^1 nondecreasing function with X(t_a) = 0. Let Omega := {(x, t) : t_a < t <= sigma, x > X(t)}, q0(x) := min{G, M(t_a) x} for x >= 0 (continuous, nondecreasing, q0(0) = 0), and let qt be the bounded solution of qt_t = qt_xx in Omega with qt = 0 on the lateral boundary {x = X(t)} and qt(., t_a) = q0. Since the lateral boundary is C^1, every lateral boundary point is regular, and q0 vanishes at the corner, qt exists, is unique among bounded solutions, is smooth in Omega and continuous on its closure, and is given by the killed Brownian representation
 qt(x, sigma) = E[ q0(x + 2^{1/2} b_h) ; x + 2^{1/2} b_v > X(sigma - v) for all v in (0, h] ]   (30.2)
(the path started at x at time sigma runs backward in time and is killed at the lateral boundary). The bounded maximum principle on Omega (with an arbitrarily small barrier growing in x) gives 0 <= qt <= G. qt is nondecreasing in x: for delta > 0, qt(x + delta, t) - qt(x, t) is a bounded caloric function on Omega, nonnegative at t = t_a (q0 nondecreasing) and on the lateral boundary (qt >= 0); the maximum principle gives qt(x + delta, t) >= qt(x, t). Put Q(r, t) := qt(r + X(t), t) for r >= 0, t in [t_a, sigma]. Then Q is C^{2,1} for r > 0, t_a < t <= sigma (Q_t = qt_t + g qt_x is continuous; it need not be smoother, since g is only continuous), continuous on [0, infinity) x [t_a, sigma], Q(0, t) = 0, Q(., t_a) = q0, 0 <= Q <= G, Q_r >= 0 and Q_t = Q_rr + g(t) Q_r.
For r > 0 let L := d_t + u^r d_r + u^z d_z - (d_rr - r^{-1} d_r + d_zz), so that L Gamma = 0 (the circulation equation). For the z-independent Q, L Q = Q_t + u^r Q_r - Q_rr + r^{-1} Q_r = (g + u^r + r^{-1}) Q_r >= 0, because g >= (u^r)^- >= -u^r and Q_r >= 0. Let rho := (1 + r^2 + z^2)^{1/2}; then rho_rr - rho_r/r + rho_zz = rho^{-3} <= 1 and |u^r rho_r + u^z rho_z| <= |u| <= M(sigma), so psi_eps := eps e^{lambda (t - t_a)} rho with lambda := M(sigma) + 2 satisfies L psi_eps >= eps e^{lambda (t - t_a)} (lambda - M(sigma) - 1) > 0. For a sign epsilon_0 in {-1, 1} put Phi := epsilon_0 Gamma - Q - psi_eps on {r >= 0} x R x [t_a, sigma]. Phi < 0 at r = 0 (Gamma = Q = 0 there), Phi < 0 at t = t_a (|Gamma(r, z, t_a)| <= min{G, r M(t_a)} = q0(r)), and Phi -> -infinity as r^2 + z^2 -> infinity, uniformly in t (|Gamma| <= G). If sup Phi > 0, it is attained at some (r_*, z_*, t_*) with r_* > 0 and t_* > t_a, where d_t Phi >= 0 (one-sided from the past), d_r Phi = d_z Phi = 0, d_rr Phi <= 0 and d_zz Phi <= 0; then L Phi >= 0, contradicting L Phi = -L Q - L psi_eps < 0. Hence epsilon_0 Gamma <= Q + psi_eps, and eps -> 0 gives |Gamma| <= Q on {r > 0} x R x [t_a, sigma]. Finally, by (30.2) with x = X(sigma) + r, Q(r, sigma) <= G P(X(sigma) + r + 2^{1/2} b_v > X(sigma - v) for all v in (0, h]), and the event equals {r + 2^{1/2} b_v + D_sigma(v) > 0 for all v in (0, h]}, which is contained in {r + 2^{1/2} b_v + Ft(v) > 0 for all v in (0, h]}. This proves (30.1).
Step 2 (Kolmogorov's test at the tip). Let F be a lower-class envelope and 0 < h <= h_0. Then almost surely there is v in (0, h] with 2^{1/2} b_v + F(v) < 0. Indeed, put phi(v) := F(v)/(2v)^{1/2}, nonincreasing in v. If phi is bounded, the claim follows from liminf_{v -> 0} b_v/v^{1/2} = -infinity (law of the iterated logarithm). Otherwise apply Kolmogorov's integral test [Erd], [IM, Chapter 1] to -b in its small-time form, obtained from the large-time form by the time inversion t b_{1/t} (which turns phi(v) into the nondecreasing function phi(1/t)): since int_0^{h} phi(v) e^{-phi(v)^2/2} dv/v = 2^{-1/2} int_0^{h} F(v) v^{-3/2} e^{-F(v)^2/(4v)} dv = infinity, almost surely -b_v > v^{1/2} phi(v), i.e. 2^{1/2} b_v < -F(v), for arbitrarily small v > 0. In the language of the heat equation, this integral test concerns the regularity of the tip of the domain {(x, t) : -h < t < 0, x > -F(-t)}, the subject of Petrovskii's criterion [Pet]; it is used here in its full integral form, not only through the leading threshold 2 (v log log(1/v))^{1/2} (cf. [Sh, Remark 4.4]), and that form was not checked against [Pet].
Step 3 (proof of (a)). Apply (30.1) with h = h_0 and Ft = F. Let Y := max_{0 <= v <= h_0} (-2^{1/2} b_v - F(v)) >= 0 (the value at v = 0 is 0). Then {r + 2^{1/2} b_v + F(v) > 0 for all v in (0, h_0]} = {Y < r}, so P_{F,h_0}(r) = P(Y < r) -> P(Y = 0) as r -> 0, and P(Y = 0) = 0 by Step 2. The same argument gives P_{F,h}(r) -> 0 for every h in (0, h_0].
Step 4 (proof of (b)). Let h := h_0/2, sigma = T_* - delta with 0 < delta <= h. Since g >= 0, D_sigma(v) <= int_{T_* - v - delta}^{T_*} g dt <= F(v + delta) for v in (0, h]. By (30.1) with Ft(v) = F(v + delta), sup_z |Gamma(r, z, T_* - delta)| <= G P(E(r, delta)), E(r, delta) := {r + 2^{1/2} b_v + F(v + delta) > 0 for all v in (0, h]}. Let (r_k, delta_k) -> (0, 0). By Step 2, almost surely there is v_* in (0, h] with 2^{1/2} b_{v_*} + F(v_*) < 0, and by continuity of F, r_k + 2^{1/2} b_{v_*} + F(v_* + delta_k) < 0 for all large k; so the indicators of E(r_k, delta_k) tend to 0 almost surely, and dominated convergence gives P(E(r_k, delta_k)) -> 0.
Step 5 (proof of (c)). By (a) or (b), sup_z |Gamma(r, z, t)| -> 0 as (r, t) -> (0, T_*) (under (a), uniformly in t in [T_* - h_0, T_*)). Along first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity we have t_n -> T_* (S is bounded on compact subintervals of [0, T_*)), r_n = gamma_n/S_n <= G/S_n -> 0 and |Gamma(r_n, z_n, t_n)| = gamma_n; hence gamma_n -> 0. For the second claim, if S is bounded then S/M -> 0 because M -> infinity. Otherwise S(t) -> infinity. For late t let a(t) be the first time with S(a(t)) = S(t) (S is continuous and nondecreasing). Then ||u^theta(a(t))||_infty = S(a(t)) (otherwise, by continuity of ||u^theta(.)||_infty, the value S(a(t)) would be attained at an earlier time), the maximum is attained at a point with r > 0 (u^theta is continuous, decays at infinity and vanishes on the axis), and a(t) is a first-crossing swirl record time of the level S(t), with record point (r_a, z_a). The record identity of Theorem 1 gives -r_a u^r(r_a, z_a, a(t)) >= 1, so M(a(t))^2 >= S(a(t))^2 + r_a^{-2} and r_a >= 1/M(a(t)); with gamma(a) := r_a S(a(t)) = |Gamma(r_a, z_a, a(t))| this gives S(t)/M(t) <= S(a(t))/M(a(t)) <= gamma(a). As t -> T_*, S(a(t)) = S(t) -> infinity, so a(t) -> T_* and r_a <= G/S(a(t)) -> 0, hence gamma(a) -> 0. The last sentence of (c) is the contrapositive, with Theorem 1 for Case-1 trajectories and S/M >= 1/C_S under Proposition 29(b)(i).
Step 6 (proof of (d)). Let psi_B(v) := L_2(v) + (3/2) L_3(v) + B with B >= 0, and f(v) := (psi_B(v)/v)^{1/2}. Choose v_0 in (0, 1) with L_2 >= 3/2 on (0, v_0]; there psi_B >= L_2 >= 3/2, psi_B and f are decreasing, and |psi_B'(v)| = (1 + 3/(2 L_2))/(v L_1) <= 2/(v L_1). Suppose that in one of the situations of (c) the bracket in (d) is bounded above, so that for some B >= 0 and t_0 in [T_* - v_0, T_*), g(t) <= f(T_* - t) for t in [t_0, T_*). Take h_0 := min{v_0, T_* - t_0, T_*/2} and F(s) := int_0^s f (finite, since f(v) is of order (L_2(v)/v)^{1/2}). Then int_{T_* - s}^{T_*} g dt <= int_0^s f = F(s) for s in (0, h_0], which is the hypothesis of (b), and (c) gives a contradiction once F is shown to be a lower-class envelope. F is continuous, nondecreasing and F(0) = 0. Since d/dv [2 (v psi_B)^{1/2}] = f(v) - (v/psi_B)^{1/2} |psi_B'(v)| and (v psi_B(v))^{1/2} -> 0 as v -> 0, F(s) = 2 (s psi_B(s))^{1/2} + int_0^s (v/psi_B)^{1/2} |psi_B'| dv. The function (psi_B L_1^2)^{-1/2} is increasing in v, so the last integral is at most 2 (psi_B(s) L_1(s)^2)^{-1/2} int_0^s v^{-1/2} dv = 4 s^{1/2}/(psi_B(s)^{1/2} L_1(s)). Hence
 2 (s psi_B(s))^{1/2} <= F(s) <= 2 (s psi_B(s))^{1/2} (1 + 2/(psi_B(s) L_1(s))).
The left inequality is 2 s f(s) <= F(s), i.e. d/ds (F(s) s^{-1/2}) = (2 s f(s) - F(s))/(2 s^{3/2}) <= 0. The right one gives F^2/(4s) <= psi_B + 4/L_1 + 4/(psi_B L_1^2) <= psi_B + 8 (as psi_B L_1 >= 1 and L_1 >= 1), so, with e^{-psi_B} = e^{-B} L_1^{-1} L_2^{-3/2} and psi_B >= L_2,
 F(s) s^{-3/2} e^{-F(s)^2/(4s)} >= 2 psi_B^{1/2} s^{-1} e^{-psi_B - 8} >= 2 e^{-B-8}/(s L_1(s) L_2(s)),
and int_0^{h_0} ds/(s L_1 L_2) = int_{L_1(h_0)}^infinity dy/(y log y) = infinity, which is (KP). With L_4 + ... + L_m added to psi_B, the same computation (for v_0 small enough that |psi_B'| <= 2/(v L_1) and all L_k >= 1 on (0, v_0]) gives the lower bound 2 e^{-B-8}/(s L_1 L_2 ... L_{m-1}), whose integral also diverges. The statements for M and C_S^2 S^2 follow from g <= M and M <= C_S S. For F(s) = 2 C s^{1/2}, F(s) s^{-1/2} is constant and the integrand of (KP) is 2 C e^{-C^2}/s.
Step 7 (proof of (e)). Fix sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*), h in (0, h_0] with F(h) <= R/4, t_a := sigma - h, and now X(t) := int_{t_a}^t g_R. On the strip Omega_R := {(x, t) : t_a < t <= sigma, X(t) < x < X(t) + R} let qh solve qh_t = qh_xx with qh = 0 on {x = X(t)}, qh = G on {x = X(t) + R} and qh(x, t_a) = qh0(x) := min{G, max{M(t_a), G/R} x} for 0 <= x <= R (continuous, nondecreasing, compatible with the lateral values at both corners). Then 0 <= qh <= G, and qh is nondecreasing in x: for delta in (0, R), qh(x + delta, t) - qh(x, t) is caloric on {X(t) < x < X(t) + R - delta}, nonnegative at t = t_a, at x = X(t) (where qh(X + delta) >= 0) and at x = X(t) + R - delta (where qh(x + delta) = G >= qh(x)). Qh(r, t) := qh(r + X(t), t), 0 <= r <= R, satisfies Qh_t = Qh_rr + g_R Qh_r, Qh(0, t) = 0, Qh(R, t) = G, Qh_r >= 0, so L Qh = (g_R + u^r + r^{-1}) Qh_r >= 0 for 0 < r < R. The comparison of Step 1 on {0 < r < R} x R x [t_a, sigma], with the additional boundary {r = R} where epsilon_0 Gamma <= G = Qh, gives |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= Qh(r, sigma) for 0 < r < R. In the representation of qh by the backward path xi_v := X(sigma) + r + 2^{1/2} b_v, killed at either lateral boundary, Qh(r, sigma) <= G [P(xi_v > X(sigma - v) for all v in (0, h]) + P(xi_v >= X(sigma - v) + R for some v in (0, h])]. The first probability is at most P_{F,h}(r), since X(sigma) - X(sigma - v) <= F(v). For the second, X(sigma) - X(sigma - v) <= F(h) <= R/4 and r <= R/4 force sup_{v <= h} 2^{1/2} b_v >= R/2, whose probability is 2 P(2^{1/2} b_h >= R/2) <= exp(-R^2/(16 h)). Given eps > 0, choose h in (0, h_0] with F(h) <= R/4 and exp(-R^2/(16h)) < eps, and then r_eps in (0, R/4] with P_{F,h}(r) < eps for r < r_eps (Step 3); this gives the uniform decay. Step 5 uses only this decay, so (c) holds; and if (T_* - t) g_R(t)^2 <= psi_B(T_* - t) for t in [t_0, T_*), with t_0 in [T_* - v_0, T_*), then with h_0 := min{v_0/2, (T_* - t_0)/2, T_*/2}, for sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) and s in (0, h_0] we have sigma - s >= t_0 and T_* - t in (0, 2 h_0] subset (0, v_0] for t in [sigma - s, sigma), so, f being decreasing there, int_{sigma - s}^{sigma} g_R dt <= int_{T_* - sigma}^{T_* - sigma + s} f <= int_0^s f = F(s); Step 6 then shows that F is a lower-class envelope, and the hypothesis of (e) holds, which gives (d) for g_R.
Remark. (1) Relation to [Sh]. Under the sliding hypothesis, [Sh, Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 4.2] give a quantitative bound |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= C G exp(-c int_{4 r^2}^{h} F(v) v^{-3/2} e^{-F(v)^2/(4v)} dv), uniform in sigma, so (a) is implicit there; the comparison function of Step 1 is that of [Sh, Lemma 5.1]. [Sh, Corollary 5.4] uses such a quantitative decay, with [Wei], to obtain continuation for all solutions under sliding windows with a coefficient beta < 1/2 in place of 3/2 (the computation of Steps 6 and 7, with a coefficient beta in [0, 1/2) in place of 3/2, turns a bound of the bracket of (d) into the hypothesis of [Sh, Corollary 5.4]; so for every singular solution in the class of [Sh, Theorem 5.3] the conclusion of (d) holds with any coefficient below 1/2 in place of 3/2, conditional on [Sh] and [Wei]), and [Sh, Proposition 4.5] shows that terminal windows do not give a uniform Wei-type rate. Proposition 30 needs only qualitative decay, because along records the circulation is bounded below at radii r_n -> 0; this is why the full Kolmogorov-Petrovskii test applies, terminal windows suffice, and the coefficient 3/2 (with further iterated logarithms) is reached without [Wei]. (2) Proposition 30 is not a regularity criterion: it restricts trajectories that carry records with circulation bounded below, or with swirl comparable to the velocity, to cumulative inflow above every lower-class envelope; Type II growth above such an envelope is not touched. (3) The comparison discards the term r^{-1} Q_r >= 0 of the exact radial operator d_rr - r^{-1} d_r, which is the generator of a Bessel process of dimension 0; Proposition 31 keeps it and raises the coefficient 3/2 to 5/2 (the killing rate of the comparison diffusion for the inflow C (T_* - t)^{-1/2} is then of order C^3 e^{-C^2} instead of C e^{-C^2}). (4) A localization to a bounded neighbourhood of an axis point would need, in addition, control of the axial displacement (exit through the top and bottom of a cylinder), and no swirl-only version follows from the comparison, since no bound of the meridional inflow by the swirl is available.
Status: proved here; sources: [Sh, Lemma 5.1, Theorem 4.2] for the comparison idea and for (a) in quantitative form; Kolmogorov's test [Erd], [IM, Chapter 1] and Petrovskii's criterion [Pet]; (b)-(e) and the record argument are own derivations, (b), the constant G, the instantaneous speed g in (d), the localization (e) and the statement S/M -> 0 in (c) having been proposed in an independent adversarial review and checked by the author (the localization by a different, deterministic comparison); verification: the comparison, the representation, the time inversion, the integral conversion and the inequalities of Step 6 checked step by step by the author and by that review; the inequalities of Step 6 were also checked numerically in high precision for B = 1 and 10^{-57} <= s <= 10^{-3}; a second independent review of the final text rederived Steps 1 to 7 and the reduction of the remark after Proposition 29 to [Sh, (5.6)] and found no failing inequality; the classical integral test is used as stated in [Erd] and [IM], whose exact locations neither review checked against the sources.

Proposition 31 (dimension-zero envelopes; sharpening of Proposition 30). In the setting of sec. 1.1, without assuming (A), (K) or (TAIL), let g, g_R, L_k, P and (b_v) be as in Proposition 30, and let 0 < h_0 <= T_*/2. Call F : [0, h_0] -> [0, infinity) a dimension-zero envelope if F is continuous and nondecreasing, F(0) = 0, F(s) s^{-1/2} is nonincreasing on (0, h_0], and
 (KP_0) int_0^{h_0} (F(s)^2/s)^{3/2} exp(-F(s)^2/(4s)) ds/s = infinity.
Every lower-class envelope of Proposition 30 is a dimension-zero envelope: for F not identically 0, F(s)^2/s >= F(h_0)^2/h_0 > 0, and the integrand of (KP_0) is F(s)^2/s times the integrand of (KP). For beta in R and B >= 0, the function F(s) = 2 (s (L_2(s) + beta L_3(s) + B))^{1/2}, on an interval (0, h_0] on which it is admissible, is a dimension-zero envelope if and only if beta <= 5/2, and a lower-class envelope of Proposition 30 if and only if beta <= 3/2. For r > 0 and 0 < h <= h_0 let Rbar solve Rbar_v = r + 2^{1/2} b_v + F(v) - int_0^v du/Rbar_u for 0 <= v < taubar, where taubar is the first zero of Rbar (taubar = infinity if there is none), and put S_{F,h}(r) := P(taubar > h).
(a) (Sliding windows.) If int_{sigma - s}^{sigma} g dt <= F(s) for all sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) and s in (0, h_0], then |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G S_{F,h_0}(r) for all r > 0, z in R and t in [T_* - h_0, T_*), and S_{F,h_0}(r) -> 0 as r -> 0.
(b) (Terminal windows.) If int_{T_* - s}^{T_*} g dt <= F(s) for all s in (0, h_0], then sup_z |Gamma(r, z, t)| -> 0 as (r, t) -> (0, T_*) jointly.
(c) (Records.) If the hypothesis of (a) or of (b) holds for some h_0 and some dimension-zero envelope F, then gamma_n -> 0 along every sequence of first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity, and S(t)/M(t) -> 0 as t -> T_*. Consequently neither hypothesis holds, for any h_0 and any dimension-zero envelope F, if some sequence of first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity has limsup gamma_n > 0 (in particular on every Case-1 trajectory) or if limsup_{t -> T_*} S(t)/M(t) > 0 (in particular under Proposition 29(b)(i)).
(d) (Iterated-logarithm envelope.) In each of the two situations named at the end of (c),
 limsup_{t -> T_*} [ (T_* - t) g(t)^2 - L_2(T_* - t) - (5/2) L_3(T_* - t) ] = +infinity,
and the same holds with L_4 + ... + L_m (any m >= 4) also subtracted inside the bracket, with M(t)^2 in place of g(t)^2, and under Proposition 29(b)(i) with C_S^2 S(t)^2 in place of g(t)^2.
(e) (Inflow near the axis only.) If the hypothesis of (a) holds with g_R in place of g, then |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G (S_{F,h}(r) + exp(-R^2/(16 h))) for all z, all t in [T_* - h_0, T_*), all h in (0, h_0] with F(h) <= R/4 and all r in (0, R/4]; hence sup_z |Gamma(r, z, t)| -> 0 as r -> 0, uniformly in t in [T_* - h_0, T_*). The conclusions of (c) hold under this hypothesis, and (d) holds with g_R in place of g.
(f) (Every solution.) Suppose that for some beta < 3/2, B >= 0 and h_0 in (0, T_*/2] with h_0 < e^{-e} (so that L_3 > 0 on (0, h_0]),
 ( int_{sigma - h}^{sigma} g dt )^2 <= 4 h (L_2(h) + beta L_3(h) + B) for all sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) and h in (0, h_0].   (31.0)
Then there are C, c, r_1 > 0 with |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= C G exp(-c L_2(r)^{5/2 - beta}) for 0 < r <= r_1, z in R and t in [T_* - h_0, T_*); in particular |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= r_1' (some r_1' > 0), uniformly in z and t in [T_* - h_0, T_*). Hence, by the circulation criterion [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] (a local strong axisymmetric solution with initial value in H^{1/2} and bounded initial circulation which satisfies |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= C_1 |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= delta_0, with some delta_0 in (0, 1/2) and C_1 > 1, all z and all t in its interval of existence, is regular globally in time), applied to the solution restarted at a time t_1 in (T_* - h_0, T_*), the solution would extend smoothly beyond T_*, which is excluded in the setting of sec. 1.1. So every solution in the setting of sec. 1.1 violates (31.0) for every beta < 3/2, B >= 0 and h_0, and satisfies limsup_{t -> T_*} [ (T_* - t) g(t)^2 - L_2(T_* - t) - beta L_3(T_* - t) ] = +infinity for every beta < 3/2.

Proof. If G = 0 then Gamma = 0 and (a), (b), (e), (f) are trivial; in (c) and (d) the records have gamma_n = 0 and S = 0, so the situations named there do not occur. Let G > 0. M(t) >= ||u_0||_infty > 0 for all t, since u_0 is not 0 (the solution is singular). Since u_0 is smooth and decaying, d_t u is bounded on R^3 x [0, sigma] for every sigma < T_*, so g and g_R are Lipschitz on [0, sigma].
Step 1 (dimension-zero comparison function). Let sigma in (0, T_*), 0 < h <= sigma, t_a := sigma - h, g_1 := max_{[t_a, sigma]} g, q0(r) := min{G, M(t_a) r}. Put kappa := 1/g_1 (kappa := 1 if g_1 = 0), B_1 := 2 g_1^2 + 1, A := max{M(t_a)/kappa, G/(1 + kappa)} and b(r, t) := A (r^2 + kappa r) e^{B_1 (t - t_a)}. Then
 b_t - b_rr + r^{-1} b_r - g b_r = A e^{B_1 (t - t_a)} [B_1 (r^2 + kappa r) + kappa/r - g (2 r + kappa)] >= 0 for r > 0,
since for r <= kappa: kappa/r >= g_1 kappa >= g kappa and B_1 kappa r >= 2 g_1 r >= 2 g r; for r >= kappa: B_1 r^2 >= 2 g_1^2 r^2 >= 2 g_1 r >= 2 g r and B_1 kappa r >= 2 g_1 r >= 2 >= g kappa (if g_1 = 0 the bracket is positive). Also b(r, t_a) >= A kappa r >= M(t_a) r >= q0(r) and b >= G for r >= 1. For 0 < eps < 1 and L >= L_0 := 1 + G/M(t_a) let Q^{eps,L} be the solution of Q_t = Q_rr + (g(t) - r^{-1}) Q_r on (eps, L) x (t_a, sigma] with Q = 0 at r = eps, Q = G at r = L and Q(., t_a) = q0^eps, where q0^eps(r) := min{G, M(t_a)(r - eps)} (a uniformly parabolic problem with coefficients smooth in r and Lipschitz in t, with continuous data compatible at both corners, since q0^eps(eps) = 0 and q0^eps(L) = G; Q^{eps,L} is C^{2,1} inside and continuous on the closure). By the maximum principle 0 <= Q^{eps,L} <= min{G, b} (b is a supersolution, b >= q0 >= q0^eps at t = t_a, b >= 0 at r = eps and b >= G at r = L >= 1). Q^{eps,L} increases as eps decreases (for eps' < eps, on (eps, L) the values of Q^{eps',L} at r = eps are >= 0 and q0^{eps'} >= q0^eps), and decreases as L increases (for L' > L, Q^{eps,L'} <= G at r = L). Put Q^L := lim_{eps -> 0} Q^{eps,L}, Q := lim_{L -> infinity} Q^L and Q(., t_a) := q0. Interior parabolic estimates show that Q is C^{2,1} on (0, infinity) x (t_a, sigma] and solves
 Q_t = Q_rr + (g(t) - r^{-1}) Q_r,   0 <= Q <= min{G, b}.   (31.1)
Representation. For t in (t_a, sigma] and r > 0 let R solve R_v = r + 2^{1/2} b_v + X_v - int_0^v du/R_u for 0 <= v < tau_0, where X_v := int_{t - v}^{t} g and tau_0 is the first zero of R (pathwise: Y := R - r - 2^{1/2} b - X solves an ordinary differential equation that is locally Lipschitz while R > 0; R <= r + 2^{1/2} b + X excludes explosion, and at a finite tau_0 the increasing integral int_0^v du/R_u is bounded, so R has a limit there, which must be 0). Let tau_a denote the first hitting time of the level a by R and s := t - t_a. Since dR_v = 2^{1/2} db_v + (g(t - v) - R_v^{-1}) dv, Ito's formula shows that Q^{eps,L}(R_v, t - v) is a martingale up to the exit from (eps, L) and up to v = s (stop first at the exit from (eps + eta, L - eta) and at v = s - eta, and let eta -> 0, using the continuity of Q^{eps,L} on the closure); so, for eps < r < L,
 Q^{eps,L}(r, t) = E[ q0^eps(R_s) ; tau_eps > s, tau_L > s ] + G P(tau_L < tau_eps, tau_L <= s).
As eps -> 0, tau_eps increases to tau_0 and q0^eps increases to q0, so by monotone convergence Q^L(r, t) = E[q0(R_s); tau_0 > s, tau_L > s] + G P(tau_L < tau_0, tau_L <= s). As L -> infinity, tau_L -> infinity almost surely, since R_v <= r + 2^{1/2} b_v + X_v is bounded on [0, s]; hence
 Q(r, t) = E[ q0(R_{t - t_a}) ; tau_0 > t - t_a ] <= G P(tau_0 > t - t_a).   (31.2)
By (31.2) and Q <= b, Q is continuous on [0, infinity) x [t_a, sigma] with Q(0, t) = 0: b(r, t) -> 0 as r -> 0 uniformly in t, and as (r', t) -> (r, t_a) with r > 0, the process started at r' satisfies R_{t - t_a} -> r in probability and P(tau_0 <= t - t_a) -> 0.
Monotonicity. For 0 < r < r' the solutions R, R' driven by the same path satisfy d(R' - R)/dv = (R' - R)/(R R'), so R'_v - R_v = (r' - r) exp(int_0^v du/(R_u R'_u)) > 0 while both are positive; hence R' > R before the first zero of R, R' survives at least as long as R, and since q0 >= 0 is nondecreasing, (31.2) gives Q(r', t) >= Q(r, t). So Q_r >= 0.
Comparison with Gamma. With L as in Proposition 30, L Q = Q_t + u^r Q_r - Q_rr + r^{-1} Q_r = (g + u^r) Q_r >= 0 for r > 0. Moreover |Gamma(., t_a)| <= q0 = Q(., t_a), Gamma = Q = 0 on the axis and Q >= 0, so the maximum-principle argument of Proposition 30, Step 1 (with the barrier psi_eps) gives |Gamma| <= Q on {r > 0} x R x [t_a, sigma]. With (31.2) at t = sigma:
 |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G P(tau_0 > h) for all r > 0 and z in R.   (31.3)
Step 2 (front-loaded comparison). Let Ft : [0, h] -> R be continuous with X_v <= Ft(v) on [0, h] (X for t = sigma) and r + Ft(0) > 0, and let Rt solve Rt_v = r + 2^{1/2} b_v + Ft(v) - int_0^v du/Rt_u with first zero taut. Then tau_0 <= taut, so P(tau_0 > h) <= P(taut > h). Indeed, before the first zero of R or Rt, D := Rt - R = (Ft - X) + int_0^v a D du with a := 1/(R Rt) > 0, so D^-(v) <= int_0^v a D^- du and Gronwall's lemma (a is bounded on compact subintervals) gives D >= 0; thus Rt cannot vanish while R > 0. The same argument shows that the survival probability is monotone in the starting point and in the displacement.
Step 3 (the dimension-zero integral test). Let F be a dimension-zero envelope on [0, h] and Rbar, taubar as in the statement.
(3.1) For 0 < a < b <= h, 0 <= F(b) - F(a) <= F(a)((b/a)^{1/2} - 1) <= F(a)(b - a)/(2a); so F is locally Lipschitz on (0, h], f := F' satisfies 0 <= f <= F/(2v) almost everywhere, and F(b) = int_0^b f.
(3.2) Logarithmic time. For v = e^t put C(t) := F(e^t)/(2 e^{t/2}), Y_t := e^{-t/2} Rbar_{e^t} and Z_t := Y_t - 2 C(t). By (3.1), C is locally absolutely continuous and -C/2 <= C' <= 0 almost everywhere, and e^{t/2} f(e^t) = C + 2C'. With the Brownian motion B given by dB_t = e^{-t/2} db_{e^t}, Ito's formula gives dY = 2^{1/2} dB + (C + 2C' - Y/2 - 1/Y) dt, hence
 dZ = 2^{1/2} dB + ( -Z/2 - 1/(Z + 2C(t)) ) dt on {Z > -2C(t)},
the term 2C' cancelling. For frozen C the generator A_C := d_zz + (-z/2 - 1/(z + 2C)) d_z is symmetric with respect to m_C(z) := (2C/(z + 2C)) e^{-z^2/4} on (-2C, infinity); in the variable y = z + 2C, m_C is proportional to q_C(y) := y^{-1} e^{C y - y^2/4}.
(3.3) Spectral bound. For C >= 2 put lambda_1(C) := inf{ int u_z^2 m_C / int u^2 m_C : u in C_c^infinity(-2C, infinity), u not 0 }. Then lambda_1(C) >= C^3 e^{-C^2}/128. Proof: for u in C_c^infinity(0, infinity) and a positive weight q with A(x) := int_0^x dy/q(y) -> infinity and M(x) := int_x^infinity q < infinity, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives u(x)^2 <= 2 A(x)^{1/2} int_0^x u'^2 q A^{1/2} dy, and integration by parts gives int_y^infinity A^{1/2} q dx <= 2 B A(y)^{-1/2} with B := sup_x A(x) M(x); with Tonelli's theorem, int u^2 q <= 4 B int u'^2 q (the weighted Hardy inequality of [Mu]). For q = q_C, C >= 2, write A_C, M_C, B_C. For 1/C <= x <= 2C: A_C(x) <= int_0^{2C} y e^{-C y/2} dy <= 4/C^2 (as y^2/4 <= C y/2 there), and splitting at y = C, M_C(1/C) <= 2 (log C) e^{3C^2/4} + 2 pi^{1/2} e^{C^2}/C <= 7 e^{C^2}/C (using 2 C log C e^{-C^2/4} <= 8/e), so A_C M_C <= 28 e^{C^2}/C^3. For 0 < x < 1/C: A_C(x) <= x^2/2 and M_C(x) <= e log(1/(C x)) + M_C(1/C), so A_C M_C <= 1/(4C^2) + (7/2) e^{C^2}/C^3 <= 4 e^{C^2}/C^3. For x = 2C + d, d >= 0: A_C(2C) M_C(x) <= 2 pi^{1/2} e^{C^2}/C^3, and the remaining part of A_C(x) M_C(x) is at most [int_0^d e^{w^2/4} dw][int_d^infinity e^{-w^2/4} dw] <= 8 (at most e^{1/4} pi^{1/2} for d <= 1, and at most (4 e^{d^2/4}/d)(2 e^{-d^2/4}/d) for d >= 1), which is <= 8 e^{C^2}/C^3 since e^{C^2}/C^3 >= 1 for C >= 2. So B_C <= 32 e^{C^2}/C^3 and lambda_1(C) >= 1/(4 B_C). (A trial function shows lambda_1(C) <= 5 e^{5/4} C^3 e^{-C^2}, so the order C^3 e^{-C^2} is exact; this is not used.)
(3.4) Backward energy estimate. Suppose C >= 2 on (-infinity, T], T := log v_0 with 0 < v_0 < h. For t <= T and z > -2C(t) let u(t, z) be the probability that the process Z started at z at log-time t is not absorbed on [t, T] and that Rbar, continued from physical time v_0, survives to time h; by the Markov property S_{F,h}(r) = E[ u(log v, Z_{log v}) ; taubar > v ] for 0 < v <= v_0. Put N(t) := int u(t, z)^2 m_{C(t)}(z) dz and E(t) := int u_z^2 m_{C(t)} dz. Then for t_1 < T
 N(t_1) <= N(T) exp[ 5/(2 C(T)) - (1/128) int_{t_1}^T C(t)^3 e^{-C(t)^2} dt ].   (31.4)
Proof: first on truncations eps < y < n (y = z + 2C(t)) with zero Dirichlet data and with C replaced by mollifications (constant extension and mollification preserve C >= 2 and -C/2 <= C' <= 0; on the fixed y-interval the drift C + 2C' - y/2 - 1/y is bounded, and the estimate passes to the limit of the mollifications by bounded-domain stability). There u solves u_t = -A_C u, d_t log m_{C(t)}(z) = C' z/(C (z + 2C)) at fixed z, and the boundary terms vanish, so symmetry gives N' = 2E + C' int z u^2 m_C/(C (z + 2C)) dz. The integrand is >= 0 on z < 0 and >= -|C'| z u^2 m_C/(2C^2) on z >= 0. With J := int_0^infinity z u^2 m_C: on z >= 0, -m_C' >= (z/2) m_C, so with eta := min{z, 1}, int_0^infinity eta z u^2 m_C <= 2 int_0^infinity (eta u^2)' m_C <= 2N + 4 (N E)^{1/2}, and int_0^infinity z (1 - eta) u^2 m_C <= N; hence J <= 3N + 4 (N E)^{1/2} <= 5N + 2E. Thus N' >= (2 - |C'|/C^2) E - (5|C'|/(2C^2)) N >= (lambda_1(C) - 5|C'|/(2C^2)) N, using |C'|/C^2 <= 1/(2C) <= 1/4 and (3.3) (the zero extension of u(t, .) is admissible). Integrating from t_1 to T and using int_{t_1}^T |C'|/C^2 dt = 1/C(T) - 1/C(t_1) <= 1/C(T) gives (31.4) on the truncations. Finally n -> infinity and eps -> 0: the killed representations increase to the untruncated one (a surviving continuous path has a positive minimum and a finite maximum on a compact time interval), and Fatou's lemma passes (31.4) to the limit.
(3.5) Terminal data. Let G_v0(x) be the probability that Rbar, started at x > 0 at physical time v_0, survives to time h. Dropping the drift -1/Rbar (Step 2) and bounding the displacement increment on [v_0, h] by A_0 s with A_0 := F(h)/(2 v_0) >= ess sup_{[v_0, h]} f, the reflection formula for Brownian motion with drift gives, with delta := h - v_0, G_v0(x) <= Phi((x + A_0 delta)/(2 delta)^{1/2}) - e^{-A_0 x} Phi((A_0 delta - x)/(2 delta)^{1/2}) <= min{1, K x}, K := A_0 + (pi delta)^{-1/2}. With C_0 := C(T) and u(T, z) = G_v0(v_0^{1/2}(z + 2C_0)), N(T) = int_0^infinity G_v0(v_0^{1/2} y)^2 (2C_0/y) e^{-(y - 2C_0)^2/4} dy <= 2 C_0 K^2 v_0 int_0^1 y dy + 2 C_0 int_1^infinity e^{-(y - 2C_0)^2/4} dy <= C_0 (K^2 v_0 + 4 pi^{1/2}) =: N_0.
(3.6) Pointwise bound. u(t, .) is nondecreasing (Step 2). For M >= 0 and C >= 2, int_M^{M+1} m_C dz >= j_M := 4 e^{-(M+1)^2/4}/(M + 5), so j_M u(t, M)^2 <= N(t), and (31.4) gives u(t, M) <= (N_0/j_M)^{1/2} e^{5/(4 C_0)} exp[-(1/256) int_t^T C^3 e^{-C^2} ds]. On {taubar > v}, Z_{log v} = v^{-1/2}(Rbar_v - F(v)) <= v^{-1/2}(r + 2^{1/2} b_v). Splitting according to whether Z_{log v} <= M, for 0 < v <= v_0 and M >= r v^{-1/2},
 S_{F,h}(r) <= (N_0/j_M)^{1/2} e^{5/(4 C_0)} e^{-I(v)/256} + exp(-(M - r v^{-1/2})^2/4),   I(v) := int_{log v}^{T} C^3 e^{-C^2} dt = (1/8) int_v^{v_0} (F(s)^2/s)^{3/2} e^{-F(s)^2/(4s)} ds/s.   (31.5)
(3.7) Conclusion: S_{F,h}(r) -> 0 as r -> 0. Since C is nonincreasing in t, either C(t) -> infinity as t -> -infinity, or C is bounded. In the first case choose v_0 with C(log v_0) >= 2; then C >= 2 on (-infinity, log v_0], (KP_0) gives I(v) -> infinity as v -> 0, and in (31.5) one lets r -> 0 at fixed v and M, then v -> 0, then M -> infinity. In the second case let D_1 := max{2, sup C}; then F(v) <= Fbar(v) := 2 D_1 v^{1/2}, Step 2 gives S_{F,h} <= S_{Fbar,h}, and Fbar has C = D_1 >= 2 and I(v) = D_1^3 e^{-D_1^2} log(v_0/v) -> infinity, so the first case applies to Fbar.
Step 4 (proof of (a) and (b)). (a) follows from (31.3) with h = h_0, Step 2 with Ft = F, and Step 3. For (b), let h := h_0/2 and sigma = T_* - delta with 0 < delta <= h. Since g >= 0, X_v <= int_{T_* - v - delta}^{T_*} g <= F(v + delta) =: F_delta(v) for v in [0, h], so by (31.3) and Step 2 sup_z |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G S^delta(r), the survival probability to time h of Rbar^delta_v = r + 2^{1/2} b_v + F_delta(v) - int_0^v du/Rbar^delta_u. If C is bounded, replace F by Fbar of (3.7) throughout (the hypothesis of (b) holds for Fbar). The function C_delta(t) := F_delta(e^t)/(2 e^{t/2}) satisfies C_delta >= C >= 2 on (-infinity, log v_0] and -C_delta/2 <= C_delta' <= 0 (since f(v + delta) <= F(v + delta)/(2(v + delta)) <= F_delta(v)/(2v)), and on {taubar^delta > v} again Z^delta_{log v} <= v^{-1/2}(r + 2^{1/2} b_v); (3.2)-(3.6) on [log v, log v_0] used nothing else. The terminal constants are uniform: C_delta(log v_0) <= F(h_0)/(2 v_0^{1/2}) and K_delta <= F(h_0)/(2 v_0) + (pi(h - v_0))^{-1/2}, so (31.5) holds for S^delta with a constant N_max and the factor e^{5/8}, and with I_delta(v) := int_{log v}^{log v_0} C_delta^3 e^{-C_delta^2} dt. For fixed v, C_delta -> C uniformly on [log v, log v_0] as delta -> 0 (F is uniformly continuous), so I_delta(v) -> I(v). Given eps > 0, choose M >= 0 with exp(-M^2/16) < eps, then v in (0, v_0] with (N_max/j_M)^{1/2} e^{5/8} e^{-I(v)/512} < eps, then delta_1 in (0, h] with I_delta(v) >= I(v)/2 for delta < delta_1. For delta < delta_1 and r <= (M/2) v^{1/2}, sup_z |Gamma(r, z, T_* - delta)| < 2 G eps.
Step 5 (proof of (c)). Proposition 30, Step 5 uses only sup_z |Gamma(r, z, t)| -> 0 as (r, t) -> (0, T_*), which (a) and (b) supply.
Step 6 (proof of (d)). Suppose, contrary to the conclusion, that in one of the situations of (c) the bracket in (d) is eventually bounded above. Then there are B >= 0 and t_0 < T_* with g(t)^2 <= psi_B(T_* - t)/(T_* - t) for t in [t_0, T_*), where psi_B := L_2 + (5/2) L_3 + B (with L_4 + ... + L_m added in the extended case). Proceed as in Proposition 30, Step 6, with v_0 so small that L_2 >= 5/2 and all L_k >= 1 on (0, v_0] and |psi_B'(v)| <= 2/(v L_1(v)) there, f := (psi_B/v)^{1/2} and F(s) := int_0^s f: then 2 (s psi_B)^{1/2} <= F <= 2 (s psi_B)^{1/2} (1 + 2/(psi_B L_1)), so F s^{-1/2} is nonincreasing, F^2/(4s) <= psi_B + 4/L_1 + 4/(psi_B L_1^2) <= psi_B + 8 and (F^2/s)^{3/2} >= 8 psi_B^{3/2}. With e^{-psi_B} = e^{-B} L_1^{-1} L_2^{-5/2} (times (L_3 ... L_{m-1})^{-1} in the extended case) and psi_B >= L_2, the integrand of (KP_0) is at least 8 e^{-B-8} psi_B^{3/2}/(s L_1 L_2^{5/2}) >= 8 e^{-B-8}/(s L_1 L_2) (respectively 8 e^{-B-8}/(s L_1 L_2 ... L_{m-1})), whose integral diverges. The rest is Proposition 30, Step 6 verbatim, with (b) and (c) of the present proposition. The classification in the statement follows from the same computation: for psi = L_2 + beta L_3 + B the integrands of (KP_0) and (KP) are comparable to 1/(s L_1 L_2^{beta - 3/2}) and 1/(s L_1 L_2^{beta - 1/2}), and int_0 ds/(s L_1 L_2^{p}) = int^infinity dy/(y (log y)^p) diverges if and only if p <= 1.
Step 7 (proof of (e)). Fix sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*), h in (0, h_0] with F(h) <= R/4, t_a := sigma - h, and use g_R in place of g in Step 1, on the strip 0 < r < R: put m_R := max{M(t_a), 2G/R}, use the truncations on (eps, R) with 0 < eps < R/2, Q = 0 at r = eps, Q = G at r = R and initial datum min{G, m_R (r - eps)} (compatible at r = R, since m_R (R - eps) >= G), the limit datum q0_R := min{G, m_R r} >= |Gamma(., t_a)|, and the barrier b with A := max{m_R/kappa, G/(1 + kappa)} (so that b(R, t) >= A kappa R >= m_R R >= G). The representation becomes Q(r, sigma) = E[q0_R(R_h); tau_0 > h, tau_R > h] + G P(tau_R < tau_0, tau_R <= h), where tau_R is the first hitting time of the level R. The pathwise ordering of Step 1 gives Q_r >= 0 (a path started higher reaches the level R no later, reaches 0 no earlier, and ends higher if neither happens before time h), and L Q = (g_R + u^r) Q_r >= 0 for 0 < r < R. Q is continuous on [0, R] x [t_a, sigma] with Q = G at r = R (for a fixed eps_0, G >= Q >= Q^{eps_0}, which is continuous with value G at r = R). The comparison on {0 < r < R} x R x [t_a, sigma], with epsilon_0 Gamma <= G = Q on {r = R}, gives |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G [P(tau_0 > h) + P(tau_R < tau_0, tau_R <= h)]. The first probability is at most S_{F,h}(r) by Step 2. At tau_R, R = R_{tau_R} <= r + 2^{1/2} b_{tau_R} + F(h) <= R/2 + 2^{1/2} b_{tau_R} for r <= R/4, so the second is at most P(sup_{v <= h} 2^{1/2} b_v >= R/2) = 2 P(2^{1/2} b_h >= R/2) <= exp(-R^2/(16 h)). The uniform decay, (c) and (d) for g_R follow as in Proposition 30, Step 7.
Step 8 (proof of (f)). Keep h_0 and beta < 3/2 fixed and put psi := L_2 + beta L_3 + B. Choose a working horizon H in (0, h_0] so small that, for 0 < s <= H, psi(s) >= max{4, L_2(s)/2}, 0 <= 1 + beta/L_2(s) <= 2 and psi(s) > (1 + beta/L_2(s))/L_1(s). Then F(s) := 2 (s psi(s))^{1/2}, F(0) := 0, is continuous and nondecreasing on [0, H] (d/ds (s psi) = psi - (1 + beta/L_2)/L_1 > 0), F(s) s^{-1/2} = 2 psi^{1/2} is nonincreasing, and for every sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) condition (31.0) gives X_v <= F(v) for 0 <= v <= H (X for t = sigma). So, by Steps 1 and 2 with horizon H, |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G S_{F,H}(r) for all r > 0, z in R and sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*). Here C(t)^2 = psi(e^t) >= 4. Take v_0 := H/2 in Step 3 and put p := 5/2 - beta > 1 and a := 2^{-3/2} e^{-B}. Since e^{-psi} = e^{-B} L_1^{-1} L_2^{-beta} and psi >= L_2/2, C^3 e^{-C^2} = psi^{3/2} e^{-psi} >= a L_2^{3/2 - beta}/L_1, and since -d/ds [L_2(s)^p] = p L_2(s)^{p - 1}/(s L_1(s)),
 I(v) >= (a/p) (L_2(v)^p - L_2(v_0)^p).
In (31.5), with h = H, take v := r^2 (for r^2 <= v_0) and M := I(r^2)^{1/2}/8 - 1, which is >= 2 for small r. Then j_M^{-1/2} = ((M + 5)/4)^{1/2} e^{I/512} and (M - 1)^2/4 = (M + 1)^2/4 - M >= I/256 - I^{1/2}/8, so S_{F,H}(r) <= N_0^{1/2} ((M + 5)/4)^{1/2} e^{5/8} e^{-I/512} + e^{-I/256 + I^{1/2}/8} <= C_1 e^{-I(r^2)/600} for small r. Since L_2(r^2) = L_2(r) + log 2 >= L_2(r), this gives |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= C G exp(-c L_2(r)^p) with c := a/(600 p), for small r, uniformly in z and sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*). As p > 1, c L_2(r)^p - 2 L_2(r) - log(C G) -> infinity as r -> 0, which gives |Gamma| <= e^{-2 L_2(r)} = |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= r_1', uniformly in z and t in [T_* - h_0, T_*). For t_1 in (T_* - h_0, T_*), u(t_1) lies in H^2, a subspace of H^{1/2}, by the smoothing at positive times of this finite-energy solution, which is regular on (0, T_*), its circulation is bounded by G, and the solution started from u(t_1) is the given one on [t_1, T_*), with maximal time T_* - t_1; with delta_0 := min{r_1', 1/4} and C_1 := 2, [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], used as in step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1, gives smooth continuation beyond T_*. For the pointwise statement it suffices to take 0 <= beta < 3/2, since L_3 > 0 near 0. Suppose, contrary to the conclusion, that the bracket is eventually bounded above: (T_* - t) g(t)^2 <= psi_B(T_* - t) := L_2 + beta L_3 + B for t in [t_0, T_*), with some B >= 0 and t_0 < T_*. With v_0' < e^{-e} so small that psi_B >= 1 and |psi_B'| <= 2/(v L_1) on (0, v_0'] and h_0 := min{v_0'/2, (T_* - t_0)/2, T_*/2}, the computation of Step 6 (as in Proposition 30, Step 7, last part) gives, for sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*) and h in (0, h_0], int_{sigma - h}^{sigma} g <= int_0^h (psi_B(v)/v)^{1/2} dv <= 2 (h psi_B(h))^{1/2} (1 + 2/(psi_B L_1)), hence (31.0) with B + 8 in place of B; this is excluded.

Remark. (1) Proposition 31 implies all conclusions of Proposition 30: every lower-class envelope is a dimension-zero envelope, and S_{F,h} <= P_{F,h}, since Rbar_v <= r + 2^{1/2} b_v + F(v) before taubar. The gain comes from the term -r^{-1} d_r of the radial operator, which Proposition 30 discards: the comparison diffusion is a Bessel process of dimension zero (drift -1/R towards the axis) with the additional outward drift g in backward time, and in self-similar variables its killing rate for the inflow C (T_* - t)^{-1/2} is of order C^3 e^{-C^2} instead of C e^{-C^2}. Within the family F^2/(4s) = L_2 + beta L_3 + B, the test (KP_0) is sharp for this method in the sense that it diverges exactly for beta <= 5/2; for nonzero envelopes with C(t) -> infinity as t -> -infinity, the converse assertion that convergence of (KP_0) implies a positive limit of S_{F,h}(r) as r -> 0 is not established here (for F = 0 the integral vanishes, while S_{0,h}(r) = 1 - e^{-r^2/(4h)} -> 0), so it is not claimed that the radial comparison can give nothing beyond (KP_0). (2) Part (f) improves [Sh, Corollary 5.4], which requires beta < 1/2 in (31.0) (in the normalization ell_{h_0}(h) = log(e + log(h_0/h)) of [Sh], ell_{h_0} - L_2 and log(e + ell_{h_0}) - L_3 tend to 0, so the two hypotheses differ by a bounded amount), by one unit (this concerns the logarithmic inflow criterion only, not the other, differently formulated criteria of [Sh]): the quantitative bound of [Sh] is of the form exp(-c L_2(r)^{3/2 - beta}) and is combined there with [Wei], which needs |Gamma| <= |log r|^{-3/2} = exp(-(3/2) L_2(r)); the bound of Step 8 is of the form exp(-c L_2(r)^{5/2 - beta}), and since c is small and not sharp, a bound of this form with the constants obtained here gives the hypothesis |Gamma| <= C_1 |log r|^{-2} = C_1 exp(-2 L_2(r)) of [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] (and that of [Wei]) when the exponent of L_2 exceeds 1 (with exponent 1, the bound gives the hypothesis of [LZ2] when c >= 2, and that of [Wei] when c > 3/2, or when c = 3/2 and its multiplicative prefactor is at most 1). At beta = 3/2 the bound of Step 8 is a power |log r|^{-c} with a small c and does not suffice. Parts (a)-(e) need no rate and reach the coefficient 5/2 without a circulation criterion. (3) Proposition 31 is not a regularity criterion except in (f), which uses [LZ2, Corollary 1.3]; on a Case-1 trajectory it says only that the cumulative inward radial displacement exceeds every dimension-zero envelope on arbitrarily short terminal windows.
Status: (a)-(e) proved here; (f) proved here from the circulation criterion [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], whose statement was checked in the arXiv version and which is used in the same way in step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1 (an earlier version of (f) used [Wei, Corollary 1.1], whose proof was not re-verified, and was stated as conditional on it; since the exponent 5/2 - beta of Step 8 exceeds 1, the bound also gives the faster decay |log r|^{-2} required by [LZ2]); sources: the comparison idea of [Sh, Lemma 5.1] as in Proposition 30; the weighted Hardy inequality [Mu], rederived with its constant in Step 3; the dimension-zero comparison function, the front-loaded comparison and (b)-(f) were derived for this report, and the proof of the integral test (Step 3) was supplied by a research consultation and rederived step by step by the author; verification: a first independent adversarial review of an earlier version of Steps 1-3 and of (a), (c), (d) found no failing inequality and required repairs (corner control in the construction of the comparison function, regularity C^{2,1} instead of smoothness, the mollification of C separated from the spatial truncation, the Gaussian factor in the bound for N(T), the case G = 0, the explicit contradiction hypothesis in (d), the narrowed sharpness statement); a second review of the extended version found that the corner-compatible smooth approximation proposed there does not exist, that the horizon in (b) must be shortened, that bounded C and the order of the limits in (b) needed explicit treatment and that the barrier constant in (e) must be adjusted, all repaired here by the truncated data, the horizon h_0/2, the reduction to 2 D_1 v^{1/2} and the strip constants; a third independent review of the final text rederived Steps 1-8 and all displayed constants, found (a)-(e) correct, and found a gap in Step 8 for negative beta and in the preservation of the time interval of (f), both repaired in the present Step 8 by the working horizon H and the bound psi >= L_2/2; the Hardy constant was also checked numerically (the ratio of sup_x A_C M_C to e^{C^2}/C^3 is about 2 for C = 2, ..., 5, against the proved 32).

Proposition 32 (critical inflow at the axis: a Feller test). In the setting of sec. 1.1 (in particular G < infinity), without assuming (A), (K) or (TAIL), let L_k be as in Proposition 30 and put Lambda(r, t) := sup_z (-r u^r(r, z, t)) for r > 0 and t in [0, T_*). Let 0 < r_0 < 1 and let eps : (0, r_0] -> (-infinity, 1] be continuous with
 (F_0) int_0^{r_0} r^{-1} exp( - int_r^{r_0} eps(rho) rho^{-1} drho ) dr < infinity.
Put s(r) := int_0^r rho^{-1} exp( - int_rho^{r_0} eps(sigma) sigma^{-1} dsigma ) drho for 0 <= r <= r_0. Then s is continuous, increasing and concave on [0, r_0], s(0) = 0, s is C^2 on (0, r_0] (one-sided at r_0), and s'' + ((1 - eps(r))/r) s' = 0. Negative values of eps are allowed.
(a) (Stationary comparison.) Let t_0 in [0, T_*), assume G > 0 (otherwise Gamma = 0), and put r_1 := min{r_0, G/S(t_0)}. Suppose that -r u^r(r, z, t) <= 2 - eps(r) at every point (r, z, t) with 0 < r < r_1, z in R, t_0 < t < T_* and |Gamma(r, z, t)| > G s(r)/s(r_1) (in particular, if -r u^r <= 2 - eps(r) on (0, r_0) x R x [t_0, T_*)). Then
 |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G s(r)/s(r_1) for 0 < r <= r_1, z in R, t in [t_0, T_*).   (32.1)
In particular sup{|Gamma(r, z, t)| : z in R, t_0 <= t < T_*} -> 0 as r -> 0. If eps also depends on t, with eps(r, t) >= eps_*(r) for a continuous eps_* <= 1 satisfying (F_0), build s_* from eps_* and put Q_*(r) := G s_*(r)/s_*(r_1); if -r u^r(r, z, t) <= 2 - eps(r, t) at every point with 0 < r < r_1, z in R, t_0 < t < T_* and |Gamma(r, z, t)| > Q_*(r), then the hypothesis of (a) holds for eps_*, and (32.1) holds with Q_*(r) on its right-hand side (checking (F_0) separately at each time would not suffice).
(b) (Logarithmic scale.) For kappa in R and an integer m >= 1 put eps_{kappa,m}(r) := sum_{k=1}^{m-1} (L_1(r) ... L_k(r))^{-1} + kappa (L_1(r) ... L_m(r))^{-1} (for m = 1, eps_{kappa,1} = kappa/L_1). Let r_0 > 0 be so small that L_m > 0 and eps_{kappa,m} <= 1 on (0, r_0] (for m = 1 and kappa >= 1: r_0 <= e^{-kappa}). Then (F_0) holds for eps = eps_{kappa,m} if and only if kappa > 1, and in that case s(r) = L_1(r_0) ... L_{m-1}(r_0) L_m(r_0)^kappa L_m(r)^{1-kappa}/(kappa - 1), so that (32.1) reads
 |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G (L_m(r_1)/L_m(r))^{kappa - 1}.   (32.2)
(c) (Records.) If the hypothesis of (a) holds for some t_0, r_0 and eps satisfying (F_0), then gamma_n -> 0 along every sequence of first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity, and S(t)/M(t) -> 0 as t -> T_*. Consequently, if some sequence of first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity has limsup gamma_n > 0 (in particular on every Case-1 trajectory, where Theorem 1 gives liminf_n gamma_n >= (K^2 - 1)^{-1/2} > 0), or if limsup_{t -> T_*} S(t)/M(t) > 0 (in particular under Proposition 29(b)(i)), then for every integer m >= 1
 liminf_{(r, t) -> (0, T_*)} L_1(r) ... L_m(r) [ 2 - Lambda(r, t) - sum_{k=1}^{m-1} (L_1(r) ... L_k(r))^{-1} ] <= 1,   (32.3)
where the joint liminf is taken over shrinking terminal neighbourhoods 0 < r < delta, T_* - delta < t < T_* (that is, it is lim_{delta -> 0} of the infimum over these sets); no assertion along every prescribed approach to (0, T_*) is intended. For m = 1 this says: for every kappa > 1 there are points (r, z, t) with r -> 0, t -> T_* and -r u^r(r, z, t) > 2 - kappa/log(1/r). These points satisfy r > 1/M(t).
(d) (Every singular solution.) There are no t_0 in [0, T_*) and r_0 in (0, e^{-kappa}] with -r u^r <= 2 - kappa/L_1(r) on (0, r_0) x R x [t_0, T_*) if kappa >= 3; under the circulation criterion [Wei, Corollary 1.1] the same holds for every kappa > 5/2. Both statements also hold with the superlevel-set hypothesis of (a) in place of the inequality on the whole cylinder. Hence every solution in the setting of sec. 1.1 satisfies
 liminf_{(r, t) -> (0, T_*)} L_1(r) (2 - Lambda(r, t)) <= 3, and, conditionally on [Wei, Corollary 1.1], <= 5/2 (by letting kappa decrease to 5/2; no continuation statement at the endpoint kappa = 5/2 is asserted).   (32.4)

Proof. Step 1 (the comparison function). The properties of s follow from s'(r) = r^{-1} exp(-int_r^{r_0} eps(rho) rho^{-1} drho) > 0, which is C^1 on (0, r_0] with s''/s' = -(1 - eps(r))/r, and from (F_0). Since G > 0, u_0^theta is not identically 0, so S(t_0) >= ||u_0^theta||_infty > 0 and r_1 is well defined. Put Q(r) := G s(r)/s(r_1) for 0 <= r <= r_1. Then Q is continuous on [0, r_1] and C^2 on (0, r_1], Q(0) = 0, Q(r_1) = G, Q' = G s'/s(r_1) > 0 and Q'' = -((1 - eps)/r) Q' <= 0, since eps <= 1. Q is concave with Q(0) = 0, so Q(r) >= (r/r_1) Q(r_1) = G r/r_1 >= S(t_0) r for 0 <= r <= r_1, by the choice of r_1. For r > 0 let L := d_t + u^r d_r + u^z d_z - (d_rr - r^{-1} d_r + d_zz), so that L Gamma = 0. For the time-independent and z-independent Q,
 L Q = u^r Q' - Q'' + r^{-1} Q' = (u^r + (2 - eps(r))/r) Q',
which is >= 0 at every point where -r u^r <= 2 - eps(r).
Step 2 (comparison; proof of (a)). Fix sigma in (t_0, T_*), eta > 0 and a sign epsilon_0 in {-1, 1}. As in Proposition 30, Step 1, let rho := (1 + r^2 + z^2)^{1/2}, lambda := M(sigma) + 2 and psi := eta e^{lambda (t - t_0)} rho, so that L psi >= eta e^{lambda (t - t_0)} (lambda - M(sigma) - 1) > 0. Put Phi := epsilon_0 Gamma - Q - psi on [0, r_1] x R x [t_0, sigma], with Gamma(0, z, t) := 0. Phi is continuous there, since |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= r S(sigma), and Phi -> -infinity as |z| -> infinity uniformly in (r, t), since |Gamma| <= G and Q >= 0. Phi < 0 on {r = 0}, on {r = r_1} (where epsilon_0 Gamma <= G = Q) and on {t = t_0} (where |Gamma(r, z, t_0)| <= min{G, r S(t_0)} <= Q(r)). If sup Phi > 0, the supremum is attained at a point (r_*, z_*, t_*) with 0 < r_* < r_1 and t_0 < t_* <= sigma. There epsilon_0 Gamma > Q + psi > Q, so |Gamma| > G s(r_*)/s(r_1), the inflow bound holds at (r_*, z_*, t_*) by hypothesis, and L Q >= 0 there by Step 1; moreover d_t Phi >= 0 (one-sided from the past), d_r Phi = d_z Phi = 0, d_rr Phi <= 0 and d_zz Phi <= 0, so L Phi >= 0, while L Phi = -L Q - L psi < 0. This contradiction gives epsilon_0 Gamma <= Q + psi; letting eta -> 0 and then sigma -> T_* gives (32.1). Since s(r) -> 0 as r -> 0, the uniform decay follows.
Step 3 (proof of (b)). Since d/dr L_1(r) = -1/r and d/dr L_{k+1}(r) = -1/(r L_1(r) ... L_k(r)) for k >= 1, one has int_r^{r_0} drho/(rho L_1(rho) ... L_k(rho)) = L_{k+1}(r) - L_{k+1}(r_0) = log(L_k(r)/L_k(r_0)). Hence
 exp(-int_r^{r_0} eps_{kappa,m}(rho) rho^{-1} drho) = prod_{k=1}^{m-1} (L_k(r_0)/L_k(r)) (L_m(r_0)/L_m(r))^kappa,
and s'(r) = c_m r^{-1} (L_1(r) ... L_{m-1}(r))^{-1} L_m(r)^{-kappa} = -c_m L_m(r)^{-kappa} d/dr L_m(r), with c_m := L_1(r_0) ... L_{m-1}(r_0) L_m(r_0)^kappa. Since L_m(r) -> infinity as r -> 0, int_0^{r_0} s' dr = c_m int_{L_m(r_0)}^infinity y^{-kappa} dy, which is finite if and only if kappa > 1, and then s(r) = c_m L_m(r)^{1-kappa}/(kappa - 1). Substituting in (32.1) gives (32.2).
Step 4 (proof of (c)). By (a), sup{|Gamma(r, z, t)| : z, t_0 <= t < T_*} -> 0 as r -> 0. Along first-crossing swirl records with S_n -> infinity, t_n -> T_* and r_n = gamma_n/S_n <= G/S_n -> 0, so gamma_n = |Gamma(r_n, z_n, t_n)| -> 0. The statement S(t)/M(t) -> 0 follows from this uniform decay exactly as in Proposition 30, Step 5. For the second claim, fix m >= 1 and kappa > 1 and take r_0 as in (b). By the first claim and (b), for every t_0 in [0, T_*) and every r_0' in (0, r_0] the inequality -r u^r <= 2 - eps_{kappa,m}(r) fails at some point of (0, r_0') x R x [t_0, T_*). At such a point Lambda(r, t) > 2 - eps_{kappa,m}(r), that is, L_1(r) ... L_m(r) [2 - Lambda(r, t) - sum_{k<m} (L_1(r) ... L_k(r))^{-1}] < kappa. Hence the liminf in (32.3) is at most kappa for every kappa > 1. Finally -r u^r <= r |u| <= r M(t), so at these points r M(t) >= -r u^r > 2 - eps_{kappa,m}(r) >= 1.
Step 5 (proof of (d)). Suppose the inequality holds on (0, r_0) x R x [t_0, T_*) for some kappa > 5/2 and r_0 in (0, e^{-kappa}]. By (32.2) with m = 1, |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= G L_1(r_1)^{kappa - 1} L_1(r)^{1 - kappa} for 0 < r <= r_1, all z and all t in [t_0, T_*). Choose t_1 in (t_0, T_*) with t_1 > 0 and restart the solution there: positive-time regularization gives u(t_1) in H^2(R^3), its circulation is bounded by G, the circulation estimate just stated holds throughout [t_1, T_*), and in shifted time the restarted solution has maximal interval [0, T_* - t_1). If kappa >= 3, then |Gamma| <= C_1 |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= delta_0 := min{r_1, 1/4}, with C_1 := max{2, G L_1(r_1)^{kappa - 1}}, since L_1(r)^{1-kappa} <= L_1(r)^{-2} for L_1(r) >= 1; by [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] (local strong axisymmetric solutions with H^{1/2} data and bounded initial circulation; hypothesis |Gamma| <= C_1 |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= delta_0, uniformly in z and time, with delta_0 in (0, 1/2) and C_1 > 1), used as in step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1, the restarted solution extends beyond T_* - t_1, which contradicts the definition of T_*. If kappa > 5/2, then G L_1(r_1)^{kappa - 1} L_1(r)^{1 - kappa} <= L_1(r)^{-3/2} as soon as L_1(r)^{kappa - 5/2} >= G L_1(r_1)^{kappa - 1}, which holds for 0 < r <= delta_0, with some delta_0 in (0, 1/4]; [Wei, Corollary 1.1] (a strong axisymmetric solution with H^2 data and bounded initial circulation which satisfies |Gamma(r, z, t)| <= |log r|^{-3/2} for 0 < r <= delta_0, with some delta_0 in (0, 1/2), all z and all t in its maximal interval of existence, is regular globally in time; statement checked in the arXiv version, proof not re-verified) gives the same contradiction. At kappa = 5/2 this absorption would need G L_1(r_1)^{3/2} <= 1, which shrinking the radius cannot ensure. The liminf statements (32.4) follow as in Step 4.

Remark. (1) Relation to [Pan] and [ZZ]. For a constant eps in (0, 1), s(r) = r^eps r_0^{-eps}/eps and (32.1) gives |Gamma| <= G (r/r_1)^eps, a power decay at the axis; with [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] this gives continuation under u^r >= -M/r with M = 2 - eps in (1, 2), assumed only for 0 < r < r_0, all z and late times, which proves, for the present classical solution class, a near-axis, terminal-interval version of the fixed-gap condition attributed to [ZZ] in [QZ]. For eps = 1 (M = 1, the condition r u^r >= -1 of [Pan]), (32.1) reads |u^theta(r, z, t)| <= G/r_1 for r <= r_1, so the swirl stays bounded and the argument of step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1 gives continuation. The original texts were not retrieved (for [Pan] only the publisher's abstract, which states regularity of an axisymmetric weak solution under r u^r >= -1, was seen), so it was not checked whether their proofs use the same comparison, what their exact solution classes are, or whether their hypotheses are global. The logarithmic gap in (d) reaches the endpoint M = 2 up to kappa/log(1/r), which no fixed M < 2 gives. A literature search found no criterion at the endpoint 2 for the one-sided quantity -r u^r; this does not establish novelty. (2) Sharpness for the method. The comparison equation is the stationary form of Q_t = Q_rr + ((1 - eps(r))/r) Q_r, the generator of the diffusion dR = 2^{1/2} db + ((1 - eps(R))/R) dv, which for constant eps is a Bessel process of dimension 2 - eps (time-scaled). The diffusion is considered only up to its first endpoint hit (with continuous eps it is well posed up to that time: in the scale variable its diffusion coefficient is locally C^1). Its scale density is p = s' and its speed density 1/p is bounded by r_0, since p(r) >= p(r_0) = 1/r_0; so (F_0), which says that the scale function is finite at 0, makes 0 a regular endpoint [Fel], accessible from the interior, and we choose absorption there with boundary value 0, the outer boundary value being G. For eps = eps_{kappa,m}, (F_0) is exactly kappa > 1, and for eps = 0 (the critical value -r u^r = 2) the generator is the radial Laplacian of R^2, for which the axis is polar. If (F_0) fails and eps <= 1, the only solutions of Q'' + ((1 - eps)/r) Q' = 0 on (0, r_1) bounded near 0 are constants, and the solution of the time-dependent comparison problem on (0, r_1) given by the diffusion representation, with value G at r_1 and any initial data in [0, G] (no independent Dirichlet datum is prescribed at the inaccessible endpoint 0 for this interior representation; for arbitrary bounded initial data the solution is understood through the stopped diffusion), is at least G (1 - r_1^2/(2 s)) at time t_0 + s, at every r: the diffusion exits only at r_1, and Ito's formula for R^2, to which the generator assigns 4 - 2 eps >= 2, gives an expected exit time at most r_1^2/2. So no decay at the axis can be obtained from this radial comparison when (F_0) fails; this is an obstruction for the method, not a Navier-Stokes counterexample. When (F_0) holds, the same computation, with absorption at 0 and h(r) := s(r)/s(r_1) the probability of exit at r_1, gives an expected exit time at most r_1^2 h(r)/2, so the time-dependent solution Q_s satisfies |Q_s(r) - G h(r)| <= G P_r(exit time > s) <= G r_1^2 h(r)/(2 s), so it lies between G h(r)/2 and 3 G h(r)/2 at times t_0 + s with s >= r_1^2: the order of (32.1) cannot be improved within the comparison. (3) Relation to Proposition 23(b) and Theorem 5. Both results test the same scale-density formula, at opposite endpoints; this is an analogy, not a duality theorem. At radial infinity, under the hypotheses of Proposition 23(b), divergence of int^infinity R exp(-(1/nu) int^R b) dR rules out the bound -U^R <= b(R) on the specified near-maximal set and forces a violating point; the divergence says that the scale function of the radial comparison diffusion, with generator nu d_RR + (b(R) - nu/R) d_R, is infinite at infinity. At the axis, with nu = 1 and b(r) := (2 - eps(r))/r, one has r exp(int_r^{r_0} b) = r_0^2 r^{-1} exp(-int_r^{r_0} eps(rho) rho^{-1} drho), so (F_0) says exactly that int_0 r exp(-int_{r_0}^r b) dr < infinity, that is, that the scale function of the diffusion with generator d_rr + (b(r) - 1/r) d_r is finite at 0. In both cases the critical value of -r u^r is 2 (2 nu in normalized variables): at the critical inflow b(r) = 2 nu/r the radial comparison generator is nu (d_rr + r^{-1} d_r), the radial Laplacian in two dimensions; and the logarithmic corrections (2 + 1/log R at infinity, 2 - kappa/log(1/r) with kappa > 1 at the axis) come from the same integral. (4) Relation to Propositions 30 and 31. Those propositions bound the time integral of the inward speed ||(u^r)^-||_infty (or of its near-axis version g_R) and allow any spatial profile; Proposition 32 bounds the scale-invariant quantity -r u^r pointwise near the axis and allows any growth in time. For arbitrary prescribed drift fields neither the time-integral bounds nor the unrefined pointwise radial bound implies the other (for a fixed smooth compactly supported field V and u_a(x, t) = a(t)^{-1} V(x/a(t)), the choice a = (T - t)^2 with sup(-R V^R) <= 1 satisfies the pointwise bound with eps = 1 while the inward speed is not integrable in time, and the choice a = (T - t)^{1/2} with -R V^R = beta > 2 at some point admits the Type I envelope F(s) = 2 C s^{1/2} while the violating radii sweep through every small radius); these are prescribed fields, not Navier-Stokes solutions, and no independence result within the Navier-Stokes solution class is asserted. (5) Case 1. Under the hypotheses giving a Case-1 limit, and along its defining subsequence, Proposition 23(c) gives the stronger conclusion -r u^r > 2 in its specified physical windows, at distances between R_0 r_n and L r_n from the axis. Proposition 32 does not exclude Case 1 from (A), (K) and (TAIL) alone; its additional inflow hypothesis would exclude it through (c). Its content is the universal statement (d) and the record statement (c) without (A), (K) or (TAIL).
Status: (a)-(c) and the case kappa >= 3 of (d) proved here (the latter using [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], as in step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1); the case 5/2 < kappa < 3 of (d) is conditional on [Wei, Corollary 1.1]; sources: the comparison technique of Proposition 30, Step 1 (after [Sh, Lemma 5.1]) with a stationary supersolution built from the scale function, and Feller's boundary classification [Fel] for the interpretation in Remark (2) (not used in the proofs); verification: checked step by step by the author, and by an independent adversarial review, which rederived the comparison (including the refined superlevel-set hypothesis and the boundary pieces), the closed forms of (b), the record argument and the joint liminf, checked the hypotheses of [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] and [Wei, Corollary 1.1] against their published statements and the constants of Step 5, verified the diffusion estimates of Remark (2) and the identity of Remark (3), and required the repairs now included (explicit finiteness of G, the restart at a positive time, the meaning of the joint liminf, the boundary specification of the comparison diffusion, the attribution in Remark (1), and the wording of Remarks (3) to (5)); the closed forms of (b), the differential equation, the constraint eps <= 1, the identity of Remark (3) and the exit-time bounds were also checked numerically in high precision, at radii down to 10^{-50}; the numerical checks do not replace the analytic arguments.

Proposition 33 (circulation absorption by the near-axis strain). In the setting of sec. 1.1, without assuming (A), (K) or (TAIL), put k(t) := ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty for t in [0, T_*), where (.)^- denotes the negative part. Since (u^r/r)(r, z, t) = int_0^1 d_1 u_1(lambda r e_1 + z e_3, t) dlambda, k(t) <= ||grad u(t)||_infty <= D(t) and |k(t) - k(s)| <= ||grad u(t) - grad u(s)||_infty. Hence k is continuous on (0, T_*): for 0 < t_0 < sigma < T_*, the smoothing estimate for bounded mild solutions, applied on [t_0/2, sigma] with the bound M(sigma), shows that d_t grad u is bounded on R^3 x [t_0, sigma]. Integrals of k starting at t = 0 are understood as improper integrals of a nonnegative function, with values in [0, infinity]; if grad u is continuous on [0, sigma] with values in the bounded continuous functions for every sigma < T_* (for example for data in H^m, m > 5/2), k is continuous on [0, T_*). Although k is a supremum over all of space, it is called the near-axis strain because it is used at small r; no localized version is proved. (In terms of the 5D stream potential, u^r/r = -phi_z, so k = ||(phi_z)^+||_infty.)
(a) (Circulation absorption.) Let 0 < h <= sigma < T_*, put I(v) := int_{sigma - v}^{sigma} k(t) dt for 0 <= v <= h and w := (4 int_0^h e^{-2 I(v)} dv)^{-1}. Then
 |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= G (1 - exp(-r^2 w)) for all r >= 0 and z in R,   (33.1)
hence ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= G^2 w and ||q(sigma)||_infty <= G w, and w <= e^{2 I(h)}/(4 h).
(b) (Type I strain.) Let 0 <= t_a < sigma < T_* and C_a >= 0, and suppose k(t) <= C_a/(T_* - t) for t in [t_a, sigma]. Put h := sigma - t_a, delta := T_* - sigma, p := 1 - 2 C_a and J := int_0^h (delta/(delta + v))^{2 C_a} dv, that is, J = delta [1 - (1 + h/delta)^p]/(2 C_a - 1) if C_a > 1/2, J = delta log(1 + h/delta) if C_a = 1/2, and J = delta^{2 C_a} [(delta + h)^p - delta^p]/p if C_a < 1/2. Then ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= G^2/(4 J) and ||q(sigma)||_infty <= G/(4 J). If h >= delta, then
 delta ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= G^2 c(C_a) with c(C_a) := (2 C_a - 1)/(4 (1 - 2^{1 - 2 C_a})) if C_a > 1/2; <= G^2/(4 log(1 + h/delta)) if C_a = 1/2; <= G^2 p (delta/h)^p/(4 (2^p - 1)) if C_a < 1/2.   (33.2)
In particular, if C_a <= 1/2 and the hypothesis holds on [t_a, T_*), then (T_* - sigma) ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 -> 0 as sigma -> T_*.
(c) (Quantitative dichotomy.) For sigma in (T_*/2, T_*) put theta(sigma) := max{1, sup{(T_* - t) k(t) : 2 sigma - T_* <= t <= sigma}}. Then
 (T_* - sigma) ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= G^2 (theta(sigma) - 1/2) and (T_* - sigma) ||q(sigma)||_infty <= G (theta(sigma) - 1/2).   (33.3)
Consequently either limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity (Type II near-axis strain), or there are C_I < infinity and t_1 < T_* with (T_* - t) S(t)^2 <= C_I for t in [t_1, T_*) (Type I swirl, for the historical swirl maximum). The alternatives are not claimed to be exclusive.
(d) (Under historical swirl domination.) Under Proposition 29(b)(i),
 limsup_{t -> T_*} [ G^2 C_S^2 (T_* - t) k(t) - L_2(T_* - t) - (5/2) L_3(T_* - t) ] = +infinity,
with L_k as in Proposition 30, and the same holds with L_4 + ... + L_m (any m >= 4) also subtracted inside the bracket. In particular limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity.
(e) (Case-1 limits.) Assume (K) and (TAIL), let U be a limit given by Theorem 2 along a subsequence with gamma_n -> gamma_*, and put tau_n := (T_* - t_n)/T_n.
 (i) (Type I swirl.) If (T_* - t) ||u^theta(t)||_infty^2 <= C_I for t in [t_1, T_*), then tau_n <= C_I/gamma_n for all n with t_n >= t_1. Along a further subsequence with tau_n -> tau_* (so 0 <= tau_* <= C_I/gamma_*), |U^theta(y, tau)|^2 <= C_I/(gamma_* (tau_* + |tau|)) for all y and tau < 0. Every limit in C^{2,1}_loc of translates U(. + z_k e_3, . + s_k) with z_k in R and s_k -> -infinity is a constant multiple of e_3 (the constant may depend on the sequence); in particular sup{|grad U(y, tau)| : |y'| <= R_0, y_3 in R} -> 0 as tau -> -infinity, for every R_0 < infinity.
 (ii) (Type I strain.) If k(t) <= C_a/(T_* - t) for t in [t_a, T_*), then T_* - t_n <= C_a r_n^2, that is tau_n <= C_a gamma_n, for all n with t_n >= t_a and S_n > S(0) (as in Theorem 1), and C_a > 1/2. Along a further subsequence with tau_n -> tau_* (so 0 <= tau_* <= C_a gamma_*), for all y and tau < 0, with R = |y'|,
 |Gamma_U(y, tau)| <= (G/gamma_*) (1 - exp(-gamma_* (2 C_a - 1) R^2/(4 (tau_* + |tau|)))),   (33.4)
so |U^theta(y, tau)|^2 <= G^2 (2 C_a - 1)/(4 gamma_* (tau_* + |tau|)), and tau_* <= (2 C_a - 1) gamma_*/(4 l_*) <= (2 C_a - 1) G/4, where l_* := log(G/(G - gamma_*)) in (0, infinity] (l_* = infinity, and then tau_* = 0, if gamma_* = G). Moreover the hypothesis of (i) holds, with C_I := G^2 c(C_a) and t_1 := (t_a + T_*)/2, so the conclusions of (i) hold. In particular, on a trajectory satisfying (K) and (TAIL) there is no t_a < T_* with (T_* - t) k(t) <= 1/2 on [t_a, T_*).
(f) (Cumulative strain.) (i) int_{t_0}^{T_*} k(t) dt = infinity for every t_0 in (0, T_*). (ii) At every first-crossing swirl record (r_n, z_n, t_n) (Theorem 1), gamma_n < G and, with l_n := log(G/(G - gamma_n)) >= gamma_n/G,
 int_{t_n - h}^{t_n} k(t) dt >= (1/2) log(4 h l_n/r_n^2) >= (1/2) log(4 h/(G T_n)) for 0 < h <= t_n.   (33.5)
(iii) (Ancient solutions.) Let V be a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution of NS on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] with viscosity nu > 0 and G_V := ||Gamma_V||_infty < infinity, put k_V(tau) := ||(V^R/R)^-(tau)||_infty and Pi_V := int_0^infinity exp(-2 int_{-v}^0 k_V(tau) dtau) dv in (0, infinity]. Then |Gamma_V(R, Z, 0)| <= G_V (1 - exp(-R^2/(4 nu Pi_V))) for all R, Z (with exp(-infinity) = 0 and R^2/infinity = 0). If Pi_V = infinity, V is a constant multiple of e_3. If Pi_V < infinity, then int_{-v}^0 k_V dtau - (1/2) log v -> infinity as v -> infinity; hence V is a constant multiple of e_3 whenever liminf_{v -> infinity} (int_{-v}^0 k_V dtau - (1/2) log v) < infinity, in particular if int_{-infinity}^0 k_V dtau < infinity or if k_V(tau) <= 1/(2 |tau|) for all tau <= -tau_0 < 0. (iv) (Case-1 limits.) Under (K) and (TAIL), every limit U of Theorem 2 satisfies gamma_* < G and
 Pi_U = int_0^infinity exp(-2 int_{-v}^0 k_U(tau) dtau) dv <= gamma_*/(4 l_*) <= G/4, hence int_{-v}^0 k_U(tau) dtau >= (1/2) log(4 v l_*/gamma_*) >= (1/2) log(4 v/G) for all v > 0,   (33.6)
where l_* := log(G/(G - gamma_*)) and k_U(tau) := ||(U^R/R)^-(tau)||_infty, int_{-v}^0 k_U(tau) dtau - (1/2) log v -> infinity as v -> infinity, and G - gamma_* >= G exp(-gamma_* ||grad U||_infty/2). Under the hypothesis of (e)(i) or (e)(ii), moreover k_U(tau) -> 0 as tau -> -infinity, and under that of (e)(ii), k_U(tau) <= C_a/(tau_* + |tau|) for tau < 0.

Proof. Step 1 (supersolution; proof of (a)). If G = 0 then Gamma = 0; assume G > 0. Fix s_1 in (sigma - h, sigma). For s in [s_1, sigma] put phi(s) := 4 int_{s_1}^s exp(-2 int_tau^s k) dtau. Then phi is C^1, phi(s_1) = 0, phi > 0 on (s_1, sigma] and phi' = 4 - 2 k phi; so w_1 := 1/phi is C^1 on (s_1, sigma], w_1' = 2 k w_1 - 4 w_1^2, w_1 >= 0 and w_1(s) -> infinity as s decreases to s_1. Put Psi(r, s) := G (1 - E) with E := exp(-r^2 w_1(s)), for r >= 0 and s in (s_1, sigma]. Then d_s Psi = G r^2 w_1' E, d_r Psi = 2 G r w_1 E, d_rr Psi = 2 G w_1 E - 4 G r^2 w_1^2 E, so (d_rr - r^{-1} d_r) Psi = -4 G r^2 w_1^2 E, and, for L as in Proposition 30, Step 1, since u^r/r >= -k(s) and w_1 >= 0,
 L Psi = G r^2 E [w_1' + 2 (u^r/r) w_1 + 4 w_1^2] >= G r^2 E [w_1' - 2 k w_1 + 4 w_1^2] = 0 for r > 0.
Let B := max_{s_1 <= s <= sigma} ||grad u(s)||_infty. Since u^theta(r, z, s) = u_2(r e_1 + z e_3, s) and u_2 vanishes on the axis, |Gamma(r, z, s)| <= min{G, B r^2}. Fix eps' in (0, 1), put Lambda := log(1/eps') and choose s_0 in (s_1, sigma) with w_1(s_0) >= B/(G eps'). Then |Gamma(r, z, s_0)| <= Psi(r, s_0) + G eps' for all r, z: if r^2 w_1(s_0) >= Lambda, then Psi(r, s_0) >= G (1 - eps'); otherwise, since x -> (1 - e^{-x})/x is decreasing and (1 - e^{-Lambda})/Lambda >= e^{-Lambda} = eps', Psi(r, s_0) >= G eps' r^2 w_1(s_0) >= B r^2. Now fix eta > 0 and a sign epsilon_0 in {-1, 1}, let rho, lambda := M(sigma) + 2 and psi := eta e^{lambda (s - s_0)} rho be as in Proposition 30, Step 1 (so L psi > 0), and put Phi := epsilon_0 Gamma - Psi - G eps' - psi on [0, infinity) x R x [s_0, sigma], with Gamma(0, z, s) := 0. Phi is continuous, Phi < 0 on {r = 0} and on {s = s_0}, and Phi -> -infinity as r^2 + z^2 -> infinity uniformly in s (|Gamma| <= G, Psi >= 0). If sup Phi > 0, it is attained at a point with r_* > 0 and s_0 < s_* <= sigma, where L Phi >= 0 (one-sided time derivative from the past, vanishing gradient, nonpositive second derivatives in r and z), while L Phi = -L Psi - L psi < 0 (L annihilates Gamma and constants).
