By (W2) and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, Cbar(v) - C(v) <= (pi/2)^{1/2} (int_{-infinity}^{log v} (d_l C(e^l))^2 dl)^{1/2} -> 0, so for r below some r_1 the starting state satisfies Y_{l_0} - 2 Ctil(l_0) <= 2^{1/2} N_0 + 3, and
 P_r(tau_0 > h_0) <= P(N_0 > x_0) + K j_{2^{1/2} x_0 + 3}^{-1/2} e^{-c_0 Lambda(r)/2}   for every x_0 > 0,
with K independent of r, sigma and z. The minimum of 1 and the infimum over x_0 defines S^{T'}(r) for r < r_1 (and S^{T'} := 1 otherwise); it tends to 0 by (T''), and x_0 := (c_0 Lambda(r))^{1/2} gives S^{T'}(r) <= K_1' e^{-c_1 Lambda(r)} for every c_1 < c_0/4.
Step 8 (proof of (d)). In logarithmic time d_l C(e^l) = -(kappa/(2 C L_1))(1 + beta/L_2), whose square is O(1/(L_1^2 L_2)) and integrable, so (W2) holds; C is nonincreasing because 1 + beta/L_2 >= 0. By (a), lambda_1(C) is comparable (with constants depending on alpha) to C e^{-H(C)} = C e^{-kappa' B} L_1^{-kappa'} L_2^{-beta kappa'}, and C is comparable to L_2^{1/2}, so, with dl = -dL_1, Lambda(v) is comparable to int^{L_1(v)} L_2^{1/2 - beta kappa'} L_1^{-kappa'} dL_1 up to an additive constant. For kappa' < 1 this is comparable to L_1^{1 - kappa'} L_2^{1/2 - beta kappa'}, which is much larger than L_2; for kappa' = 1 it is comparable to L_2^{3/2 - beta} if beta < 3/2, to L_3 if beta = 3/2, and bounded if beta > 3/2; for kappa' > 1 it is bounded. The stated equivalences follow, since C^2 is comparable to L_2.
Step 9 (proof of (e) and (f)). At first-crossing swirl records, r_n <= G/S_n -> 0 and gamma_n = |Gamma(r_n, z_n, t_n)| <= G S^T(r_n) (or G S^{T'}(r_n)) -> 0 for t_n >= T_* - h_0. On a Case-1 trajectory gamma_n is bounded below (Theorem 1), so the hypotheses cannot hold. If k(t) <= C_a/(T_* - t) on [t_a, T_*), then (S) holds with alpha := C_a > 1/2; given C satisfying (T') on (0, 2 h_0], its restriction to (0, 2 h] satisfies (T') for every h <= min{h_0, (T_* - t_a)/2} (removing a bounded part of Lambda does not affect Lambda/C^2 -> infinity; likewise, under (W2) and (T''), the restriction satisfies (W2) and (T''), since only a finite constant is subtracted from Lambda), so (I) fails on [T_* - 2 h, T_*) for every such h, which gives times t arbitrarily close to T_* with g(t) > C(T_* - t)(T_* - t)^{-1/2}, that is (36.1). Applying (36.1) to C^2 = kappa (L_2 + B) with kappa < 1/rho = 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1) (admissible by (d)) gives limsup (T_* - t) g^2/L_2 >= kappa for each such kappa. For (f), under the hypotheses named there, (b) or (c) together with L_2 = o(Lambda) gives |Gamma(r, z, sigma)| <= K_1 G e^{-c_1 Lambda(r)} <= |log r|^{-2} for 0 < r <= delta_0, some delta_0 in (0, 1/2) (since c_1 Lambda(r) - 2 L_2(r) -> infinity), all z and all sigma in [T_* - h_0, T_*). Put s := T_* - h_0 > 0. Finite-energy dissipation supplies an earlier H^1 time; the first differentiated energy estimate supplies a subsequent H^2 time, and the second differentiated energy estimate propagates H^2 regularity to s, since ||grad u||_infty is bounded on compact positive-time intervals. Thus u(s) is in H^2, a subspace of H^{1/2}, and its circulation is bounded by G. The solution restarted at s has maximal interval of existence [s, T_*) and satisfies the hypothesis of [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] on it, with C_1 := 2, so it is regular globally in time, which contradicts the singularity at T_*. The same shrinking-window argument, with the first assertion of (f) in place of the record property, proves (36.1) for the envelope classes stated in the last assertion of (f) (restriction also preserves Lambda/L_2 -> infinity), and letting kappa increase to 1/rho in the family C^2 = kappa (L_2 + B), which satisfies (T') by (d), gives the bound for the limsup.

Remark. (1) Relation to known criteria and to Propositions 30 and 31. With a constant envelope C, (I) gives u^r >= -C (T_* - t)^{-1/2}, which excludes a singularity by [QZ, Theorem 1.1] without (S); (I) is of interest only for envelopes C(v) -> infinity as v -> 0. Without a strain hypothesis, Proposition 31(d), (f) give the coefficient 1 in front of L_2 (limsup (T_* - t) g^2/L_2 >= 1, on Case-1 trajectories and, by (f) there, on every singular solution). Under (S), (e) raises this coefficient to 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1) > 1 on the Type I strain alternative; by (35.3), C_a >= 1/2 + c_G, so the gain 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1) = 1 + 1/(2 C_a - 1) is at most 1 + 1/(2 c_G) = 1 + min{3^{1/2} mu_0 G^2/4, mu_0^{1/3} G^{4/3}/3}. On the Type II strain alternative of Proposition 33 nothing is added. (2) Mechanism. In the self-similar variable y = R_v/v^{1/2} the inflow cap C pushes the comparison diffusion outward at speed at most C, the strain cap alpha y limits this push near the axis, and the self-similar drift -y/2 confines; the potential psi_C is maximized at y = 2C, and the symmetrizing weight has the form W_C(y) = y^{-1} e^{-(y - 2C)^2/4} for y >= C/alpha; absorption at the axis requires a passage through the region where psi_C is small, at the cost e^{-H(C)} with H(C) = rho C^2. (T') and (T'') state that this escape rate, integrated over logarithmic time, diverges fast enough. (3) Scope. The tests (T'), (T'') are sufficient conditions for the comparison; their necessity for the comparison diffusion is not proved, and nothing is asserted about necessity for Navier-Stokes. The proposition does not exclude Case 1: on the Type I strain alternative it is a necessary growth condition (36.1) for the inflow, and the Type II strain alternative is untouched. (4) Literature. The comparison for the circulation with a time-only drift is the idea of [Sh, Lemma 5.1] and [QZ]; the state-dependent drift min{g, k r}, the logarithmic clock and the spectral bounds were not found in the references checked, and no priority claim is made. (5) Relation to (K) and (TAIL). (36.1) is a limsup over all times and does not locate the times of large inflow. If such a time lies in a record window, t = t_n + T_n tau with -A <= tau <= 0, then T_* - t = T_n (tau_n + |tau|) and (T_* - t) S_n^2 = gamma_n (tau_n + |tau|), so (T_* - t) g(t)^2 >= c L_2(T_* - t) gives sup_y (U_n^R)^-(y, tau) = g(t)/S_n >= (c L_2(T_* - t)/(gamma_n (tau_n + |tau|)))^{1/2}, which tends to infinity as n -> infinity for fixed A; by (K) the inflow maximum then lies outside every fixed ball for large n (by (S), at normalized radius at least (tau_n + |tau|) g(t)/(C_a S_n)). (TAIL) constrains the normalized region occupied by such inflow at those times, but neither (36.1) nor its proof places a time of large inflow inside the windows {-A <= tau <= 0}: in the proof, measured backward from the record time t_n, the spectral factor exp(-c Lambda(r_n)) is accumulated over the lags v between v_0 = r_n and h_0 (the Markov property at v_0 in Step 3, and Steps 6 and 7), while the lags 0 <= v <= A T_n = A r_n^2/gamma_n of the window are smaller than r_n for large n and enter only the starting state at v_0, through the averaged envelope Cbar(r_n) (Steps 5 and 6). So, as proved, (36.1) and the Case-1 witnesses do not interact.
Status: proof with key estimates. The elementary verifications of the numerical constants in (a) (the bounds on A, M and B on the four ranges of x), of the level bookkeeping in Step 6 and of the truncation limits in Steps 6 and 7 are summarized, not reproduced in full. (f) uses [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], whose statement was checked in the arXiv version and which is used in the same way in step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1; an earlier version of (f) used [Wei, Corollary 1.1] and was stated as conditional on it. Derived from a comparison idea of [Sh] and [QZ]; the spectral bounds of (a) and the energy estimate of (c) were supplied by research consultations; the whole argument was refereed by independent reviews in several passes (review 15 in sec. 5), whose repairs are incorporated. Checked by the author: the comparison function and (36.2), the two clock inequalities, the bound lambda_1 <= 1, the starting-state lemma of Step 5 and the bound L_2 = o(Lambda), the exponents in Steps 6 and 7, the explicit family, the record argument, and the restart in (f).

Proposition 37 (strain records on the Type II strain branch; a cylinder barrier for the swirl of Type I swirl limits). In the setting of sec. 1.1, without assuming (A), (K) or (TAIL), let k(t) := ||(u^r/r)^-(t)||_infty be as in Proposition 33, put a := u^r/r, fix t_0 in (0, T_*) and let kbar(t) := max_{t_0 <= s <= t} k(s) for t in [t_0, T_*).
(a) (Strain records.) If limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity (the first alternative of Proposition 33(c)), there are times sigma_j in (t_0, T_*) with sigma_j -> T_*, k(sigma_j) = kbar(sigma_j) =: K_j, K_j -> infinity and (T_* - sigma_j) K_j -> infinity. For each j the infimum of a(., sigma_j) over R^3 is attained at a point x_j with cylindrical coordinates (r_j, z_j) (r_j = 0 is allowed), a(x_j, sigma_j) = -K_j, and at (x_j, sigma_j)
 p_r/r >= q^2 - K_j^2,   (37.1)
where p_r/r is a smooth function on R^5 of (r, z) (p is even in r) with the value p_rr(0, z) on the axis. If r_j = 0, then p_zz(0, z_j, sigma_j) <= -4 K_j^2. For the Burgers vortex u^r = -alpha r/2, u^z = alpha z (alpha > 0, with a smooth z-independent swirl solving its equation; a z-dependent swirl is not compatible with this meridional field, since the two meridional momentum equations give p_r = (u^theta)^2/r - alpha^2 r/4 and p_z = -alpha^2 z, which require d_z (u^theta)^2 = 0), a = -alpha/2 =: -K at every point, and equality holds in (37.1) at every point and in p_zz <= -4 K^2 at every point of the axis; this local model has infinite energy.
(b) (Swirl at strain records.) For sigma in (t_0, T_*), with the value 1/(4 (sigma - t_0)) (the limit as kbar(sigma) -> 0) for the factor kbar(sigma)/(2 (1 - e^{-2 (sigma - t_0) kbar(sigma)})) below when kbar(sigma) = 0,
 ||q(sigma)||_infty <= G kbar(sigma)/(2 (1 - e^{-2 (sigma - t_0) kbar(sigma)})),  ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= mu_0 G^2 kbar(sigma)/(2 (1 - e^{-2 (sigma - t_0) kbar(sigma)})),   (37.2)
with mu_0 = 0.4072... as in Proposition 35. Along the times of (a), S(sigma_j)^2 <= (mu_0 G^2/2 + o(1)) K_j as j -> infinity.
(c) (Cylinder barrier.) Let U be a bounded smooth ancient axisymmetric solution of NS on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] with viscosity nu > 0 whose derivatives of all orders are bounded, and put q_U := U^theta/R, a_U := U^R/R, S_U(tau) := sup_{sigma <= tau} ||U^theta(sigma)||_infty and m(tau) := sup_{sigma <= tau} ||a_U^-(sigma)||_infty, Gbar_U := sup |R U^theta| over R^3 x (-infinity, 0] (possibly infinite), and let F(beta) := beta/(1 - e^{-beta}) for beta > 0, F(0) := 1 (F is continuous and increasing). If tau <= 0, L > 0, beta > 0 and 0 <= A < 2 nu beta are such that a_U >= -A/L^2 on {R < L} x (-infinity, tau], then
 ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(beta) min{S_U(tau)/L, Gbar_U/L^2}.   (37.3)
Consequently ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= (2 mu_0)^{-1/2} S_U(tau) (m(tau)/nu)^{1/2} for every tau <= 0, with mu_0 as in (b) ((2 mu_0)^{-1/2} = 1.108...).
(d) (Type I swirl limits.) Assume (K), (TAIL) and the hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(i), and let U be a limit as there (viscosity nu_* = 1/gamma_*). Then |tau|^{1/2} ||q_U(tau)||_infty -> 0 as tau -> -infinity. Put
 A_* := limsup_{sigma -> -infinity} |sigma| sup{a_U^-(y, sigma) : |y'| < |sigma|^{1/2}} in [0, infinity].
If A_* < infinity, then limsup_{tau -> -infinity} |tau| ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(A_*/(2 nu_*)) min{(C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}, G/gamma_*}.
(e) (Time-integrated compression.) In the setting of (c) let tau <= 0, t_1 < tau, L > 0, beta > 0 and 0 <= A < 2 nu beta, and let mu be a continuous function on [t_1, tau] with a_U(y, sigma) >= -mu(sigma) whenever |y'| < L and t_1 <= sigma <= tau. Then
 ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(beta) w [min{S_U(tau)/L, Gbar_U/L^2} + e^{-c (tau - t_1)} ||q_U(t_1)||_infty],  w := exp(2 int_{t_1}^{tau} (mu(sigma) - A/L^2)^+ dsigma),  c := 2 beta (2 nu beta - A)/((e^beta - 1) L^2).   (37.4)
In the setting of (d) put m_P(s) := sup{a_U^-(y, -s) : |y'| < s^{1/2}} for s > 0 and W_* := limsup_{t -> infinity} int_t^{2t} m_P(s) ds in [0, infinity], and say that U satisfies (CW) if W_* < infinity. A_* < infinity implies (CW), with W_* <= A_* log 2. If (CW) holds, then for all W > W_* and beta > 0, with kappa_beta := 4 nu_* beta^2/(e^beta - 1) and lambda := max{1, (2 W + log(2 F(beta)))/kappa_beta},
 limsup_{s -> infinity} s ||q_U(-s)||_infty <= (4/3) F(beta) e^{2 W} min{(C_I lambda/gamma_*)^{1/2}, G lambda/gamma_*}.   (37.5)

Proof. (a) Choose t'_j -> T_* with (T_* - t'_j) k(t'_j) -> infinity. Since k is continuous on (0, T_*) (Proposition 33), kbar(t'_j) is attained on [t_0, t'_j]; let sigma_j be the largest point of [t_0, t'_j] with k(sigma_j) = kbar(t'_j) =: K_j. Then kbar(sigma_j) = K_j >= k(t'_j), so (T_* - sigma_j) K_j >= (T_* - t'_j) k(t'_j) -> infinity, and K_j >= k(t'_j) >= (T_* - t'_j) k(t'_j)/T_* -> infinity; since k is bounded on [t_0, t'] for every t' < T_*, sigma_j -> T_*, and sigma_j > t_0 for large j (we discard the other indices). At the time sigma_j the function a is continuous on R^3 and tends to 0 at infinity: |a| <= |u^r| for r >= 1, and for r <= 1 the formula a(r, z) = int_0^1 d_1 u_1(lambda r e_1 + z e_3) d lambda gives |a(r, z)| <= sup_{B_1(z e_3)} |grad u|, while u and grad u tend to 0 at infinity for the smooth decaying solution (as in Proposition 14, L^infty budget (i)). Since inf a = -K_j < 0, the infimum is attained at some x_j. For t_0 <= sigma <= sigma_j, a(x_j, sigma) >= -k(sigma) >= -kbar(sigma_j) = a(x_j, sigma_j), so the left derivative of the smooth function sigma -> a(x_j, sigma) at sigma_j is <= 0. The radial momentum equation d_t u^r + b.grad u^r - (u^theta)^2/r = -p_r + (Delta - r^{-2}) u^r, with u^r = r a, b.grad(r a) = r (b.grad a + a^2), (Delta - r^{-2})(r a) = r Delta_5 a and (u^theta)^2/r = r q^2, gives after division by r
 (d_t + b.grad - Delta_5) a = -a^2 + q^2 - p_r/r.
At (x_j, sigma_j) the function a, as a function on R^5, has a global minimum, so grad a = 0 and Delta_5 a >= 0 there; hence 0 >= d_t a = Delta_5 a - a^2 + q^2 - p_r/r >= -K_j^2 + q^2 - p_r/r, which is (37.1). If r_j = 0, put c := d_r u^theta(0, z_j, sigma_j) = q(0, z_j, sigma_j); on the axis d_r u^r = u^r/r = a, so the divergence condition d_r u^r + u^r/r + d_z u^z = 0 gives d_z u^z(0, z_j) = -2 a(0, z_j) = 2 K_j, and Proposition 22(a) gives Delta p = 2 c^2 - (3/2)(2 K_j)^2 = 2 c^2 - 6 K_j^2 there. With Delta p = 2 p_rr + p_zz on the axis and (37.1), p_zz = Delta p - 2 p_rr <= 2 c^2 - 6 K_j^2 - 2 (c^2 - K_j^2) = -4 K_j^2. For the Burgers vortex a = -K is constant, so the equation for a gives p_r/r = q^2 - K^2 at every point; the axial momentum equation gives p_z = -alpha^2 z, so p_zz = -alpha^2 = -4 K^2.
(b) Proposition 33(a) with h := sigma - t_0 gives ||q(sigma)||_infty <= G w and ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= mu_0 G^2 w (the second as in the proof of (35.3)), with 1/w = 4 int_0^h e^{-2 I(v)} dv and I(v) = int_{sigma - v}^{sigma} k <= kbar(sigma) v; hence 1/w >= 4 int_0^h e^{-2 kbar(sigma) v} dv = 2 (1 - e^{-2 h kbar(sigma)})/kbar(sigma) (= 4 h if kbar(sigma) = 0). This is (37.2). The function x -> x/(1 - e^{-c x}) (value 1/c at x = 0) is nondecreasing in x >= 0 (since e^{c x} >= 1 + c x) and nonincreasing in c > 0. Fix t_1 in (t_0, T_*). For j with sigma_j > t_1 and t in [t_1, sigma_j], kbar(t) <= K_j and t - t_0 >= t_1 - t_0, so (37.2) at time t gives ||u^theta(t)||_infty^2 <= mu_0 G^2 K_j/(2 (1 - e^{-2 (t_1 - t_0) K_j})); hence S(sigma_j)^2 <= max{S(t_1)^2, mu_0 G^2 K_j/(2 (1 - e^{-2 (t_1 - t_0) K_j}))}, and K_j -> infinity gives the claim.
(c) Write u^theta = r q in the swirl equation d_t u^theta + b.grad u^theta + u^r u^theta/r = (Delta - r^{-2}) u^theta: since b.grad(r q) = r b.grad q + u^r q and (Delta - r^{-2})(r q) = r Delta_5 q, the function q_U satisfies calL q_U = 0 with calL := d_tau + b.grad + 2 a_U - nu Delta_5. As in Proposition 34, functions of (R, Z) are functions on R^5 through y = (y', y_5), R = |y'|, Z = y_5; q_U(R, Z) = int_0^1 d_1 U_2(lambda R e_1 + Z e_3) d lambda and a_U are smooth and bounded on R^5 x (-infinity, 0], and b.grad = b_5.grad_5 with the smooth bounded drift b_5(y) := (a_U y', U^Z) of the proof of (34.5). For beta > 0 let f(x) := (1 - e^{-beta x})/((1 - e^{-beta}) x) for x > 0, f(0) := F(beta) (the profile of the swirl ratio u^theta/r of a Burgers vortex). Then f is smooth on [0, infinity) and decreasing (because (1 - e^{-v})/v is decreasing), f(1) = 1, (x f)' = beta e^{-beta x}/(1 - e^{-beta}) =: h(x)/2 > 0, and (x f)'' = -(beta/2) h. Put phi(y) := f(|y'|^2/L^2) and x := |y'|^2/L^2. Since phi depends only on R = |y'|, b_5.grad_5 phi = a_U R phi_R = 2 a_U x f'(x), so b_5.grad_5 phi + 2 a_U phi = 2 a_U (x f)' = a_U h(x); and Delta_5 phi = phi_RR + 3 phi_R/R = (4/L^2)(2 f' + x f'') = (4/L^2)(x f)'' = -(2 beta/L^2) h(x). Hence
 calL phi = (a_U + 2 nu beta/L^2) h(|y'|^2/L^2) >= ((2 nu beta - A)/L^2) h(|y'|^2/L^2) >= c phi on {|y'| < L} x (-infinity, tau],  c := (2 nu beta - A) L^{-2} min_{[0, 1]} (h/f) > 0,
and 1 <= phi <= F(beta) on {|y'| <= L}, with phi = 1 on |y'| = L. Let Q_* := sup |q_U| over R^5 x (-infinity, 0] (finite, |q_U| <= ||grad U||_infty) put B := min{S_U(tau)/L, Gbar_U/L^2} (if B = infinity there is nothing to prove) and, for t_1 < tau, Psi(y, sigma) := (B + Q_* e^{-c (sigma - t_1)}) phi(y). Then calL Psi = B calL phi + Q_* e^{-c (sigma - t_1)} (calL phi - c phi) >= 0 on {|y'| < L} x [t_1, tau]. On |y'| = L, Psi = B + Q_* e^{-c (sigma - t_1)} >= min{|U^theta(sigma)|/L, |R U^theta(sigma)|/L^2} = |q_U| for sigma <= tau, and at sigma = t_1, Psi >= Q_* phi >= Q_* >= |q_U|. The comparison principle on {|y'| < L} x R x [t_1, tau] for calL, whose coefficients are bounded, applied to Psi - q_U and Psi + q_U, gives |q_U(y, tau)| <= Psi(y, tau) for |y'| < L: the unbounded y_5 direction is handled by adding eps e^{C (sigma - t_1)} (1 + y_5^2) with C := ||U^Z||_infty + 2 ||a_U||_infty + 2 nu + 1 (then calL of this term is >= eps e^{C (sigma - t_1)} (1 + y_5^2) > 0), the sign-indefinite zero-order coefficient by the weight e^{-lambda (sigma - t_1)} with lambda > 2 ||a_U||_infty, and then eps -> 0. Letting t_1 -> -infinity gives |q_U(y, tau)| <= F(beta) B for |y'| < L, and for |y'| >= L, |q_U| = |U^theta|/R = |R U^theta|/R^2 <= B <= F(beta) B. This is (37.3). If m(tau) = 0, the hypothesis holds for every L with A = 0, and L -> infinity gives q_U(tau) = 0. Otherwise, for beta > 0 and A in (0, 2 nu beta) put L := (A/m(tau))^{1/2}; then a_U >= -m(tau) = -A/L^2 on R^3 x (-infinity, tau], and (37.3) gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(beta) S_U(tau) (m(tau)/A)^{1/2}. Letting A -> 2 nu beta gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= S_U(tau) (m(tau)/(2 nu))^{1/2} beta^{1/2}/(1 - e^{-beta}), and beta^{1/2}/(1 - e^{-beta}) = ((1 - e^{-beta})^2/beta)^{-1/2} equals mu_0^{-1/2} at the maximizer beta = xi_0 of Proposition 35.
(d) U is a bounded mild ancient solution whose derivatives of all orders are bounded (smoothing estimate, sec. 1.1), so (c) applies with nu = nu_*. By Proposition 33(e)(i), |U^theta(y, sigma)|^2 <= C_I/(gamma_* (tau_* + |sigma|)) for sigma < 0, so S_U(tau)^2 <= C_I/(gamma_* |tau|) for tau < 0, and sup{|grad U(y, sigma)| : |y'| <= L} -> 0 as sigma -> -infinity for every L. Since a_U(R, Z) = int_0^1 d_1 U_1(lambda R e_1 + Z e_3) d lambda, |a_U| <= sup{|grad U| : |y'| <= L} on {R < L}. Fix L > 0; there is tau_L < 0 with a_U >= -nu_*/L^2 on {R < L} x (-infinity, tau_L], and (37.3) with A = nu_* and beta = 1 gives |tau|^{1/2} ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(1) (C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}/L for tau <= tau_L. As L is arbitrary, |tau|^{1/2} ||q_U(tau)||_infty -> 0. Since Gamma_U is the limit of Gamma/gamma_n, Gbar_U <= G/gamma_*. If A_* < infinity, fix beta > A_*/(2 nu_*), A in (A_*, 2 nu_* beta) and tau_1 < 0 with a_U^- <= A/|sigma| on {|y'| < |sigma|^{1/2}} for sigma <= tau_1. For tau <= tau_1 let L := |tau|^{1/2}; for sigma <= tau, {|y'| < L} is contained in {|y'| < |sigma|^{1/2}}, so a_U >= -A/|sigma| >= -A/L^2 there, and (37.3) gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(beta) min{S_U(tau)/|tau|^{1/2}, Gbar_U/|tau|} <= F(beta) min{(C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}, G/gamma_*}/|tau|. Let beta decrease to A_*/(2 nu_*) and use the continuity of F.
(e) Put e(sigma) := (mu(sigma) - A/L^2)^+ and w(sigma) := exp(2 int_{t_1}^{sigma} e), a C^1 function on [t_1, tau] with w' = 2 e w and w >= 1. With f, h and phi as in the proof of (c) (f and h evaluated at |y'|^2/L^2), calL(w phi) = w [2 e f + (a_U + 2 nu beta/L^2) h]. On {|y'| < L} write a_U = -A/L^2 - e + d with d >= 0, and f = h/2 + g with g >= 0, which holds since h(x)/f(x) = 2 beta x/(e^{beta x} - 1) <= 2; then 2 e f + (a_U + 2 nu beta/L^2) h = ((2 nu beta - A)/L^2) h + h d + 2 e g >= ((2 nu beta - A)/L^2) h. As v/(e^v - 1) is decreasing on (0, infinity) (the numerator e^v (1 - v) - 1 of its derivative is negative), min_{[0, 1]} h/f = 2 beta/(e^beta - 1), so calL(w phi) >= c w phi on {|y'| < L} x [t_1, tau]. With B as in the proof of (c) and Q_1 := ||q_U(t_1)||_infty, Psi := w (B + Q_1 e^{-c (sigma - t_1)}) phi satisfies calL Psi >= (B + Q_1 e^{-c (sigma - t_1)}) c w phi - c Q_1 e^{-c (sigma - t_1)} w phi = c B w phi >= 0 there, Psi >= B >= |q_U| on {|y'| = L} for t_1 <= sigma <= tau (phi = 1 and w >= 1 there), and Psi >= Q_1 >= |q_U| at sigma = t_1. The comparison argument of the proof of (c) on {|y'| < L} x R x [t_1, tau] gives |q_U(., tau)| <= Psi(., tau) <= F(beta) w(tau) (B + Q_1 e^{-c (tau - t_1)}) on {|y'| < L}, and |q_U(tau)| <= B outside; this is (37.4). Next, m_P is lower semicontinuous, hence Borel, as the supremum over y of the lower semicontinuous functions s -> a_U^-(y, -s) 1_{s > |y'|^2}, and m_P <= ||grad U||_infty. If A_* < infinity and A > A_*, then m_P(s) <= A/s for large s, so int_t^{2t} m_P <= A log 2 for large t, and W_* <= A_* log 2. Assume (CW), let W > W_* and beta > 0, and let t_0 > 0 be such that int_t^{2t} m_P <= W for t >= t_0. For t >= t_0 apply (37.4) with nu = nu_*, tau := -t, t_1 := -2 t, L := (t/lambda)^{1/2}, A := 0 and mu(sigma) := sup{a_U^-(y, sigma) : |y'| < L}; mu is Lipschitz, since d_sigma a_U is bounded (smoothing estimate of sec. 1.1 and the formula for a_U in the proof of (d)), and mu(sigma) <= m_P(|sigma|) for -2 t <= sigma <= -t, since L <= t^{1/2} <= |sigma|^{1/2}. Hence w <= e^{2 W}, c (tau - t_1) = kappa_beta lambda >= 2 W + log(2 F(beta)), and B <= min{(C_I/(gamma_* t))^{1/2} (lambda/t)^{1/2}, G lambda/(gamma_* t)} = C_lambda/t with C_lambda := min{(C_I lambda/gamma_*)^{1/2}, G lambda/gamma_*}, by S_U(-t)^2 <= C_I/(gamma_* t) and Gbar_U <= G/gamma_* (proof of (d)). So Q(t) := ||q_U(-t)||_infty satisfies Q(t) <= alpha/t + Q(2 t)/2 for t >= t_0, alpha := F(beta) e^{2 W} C_lambda, and n iterations give Q(t) <= alpha t^{-1} sum_{j < n} 4^{-j} + 2^{-n} Q(2^n t) <= (4/3) alpha/t + 2^{-n} sup |q_U|; let n -> infinity.

Remark. (1) Comparison. (b) uses only Proposition 33(a). Theorem 13(a) gives S^2 <= G D at every time; since k <= D, at leading order the bound S(sigma_j)^2 <= (mu_0 G^2/2 + o(1)) K_j is the stronger one when mu_0 G K_j/2 < D(sigma_j) (2/mu_0 = 4.91...), and it is stronger for all large j if mu_0 G K_j/2 <= (1 - eps) D(sigma_j) with a fixed eps > 0; this is not an exact criterion at finite j. (37.1) is the strain analogue of the record inequality of Proposition 22(b); it bounds the pressure, not the velocity. The Burgers vortex shows that the local pressure inequality is sharp within the larger class of flows admitting its unbounded linear strain; it does not realize the finite-energy Type II record history of sec. 1.1.
(2) Limits at the strain records (an analysis; it is not used elsewhere). Put M_j := M(sigma_j) and W_j(y, s) := M_j^{-1} u(z_j e_3 + (M_j/K_j) y, sigma_j + s/K_j). It solves NS with viscosity nu_j := K_j/M_j^2 <= D(sigma_j)/M_j^2 <= C_P (late times), and on its past s in [-(sigma_j - t_0) K_j, 0], an interval whose length tends to infinity, |W_j| <= 1 and a_{W_j} >= -1, with a_{W_j} = -1 at the record point rho_j e_1, s = 0, where rho_j := K_j r_j/M_j = |u^r(x_j, sigma_j)|/M_j is in [0, 1]; by (b), |W_j^theta|^2 <= (mu_0 G^2/2 + o(1)) nu_j, and |Gamma_{W_j}| <= nu_j G. Pass to a subsequence with nu_j -> nu_* in [0, C_P] and rho_j -> rho. If nu_* > 0, the smoothing estimate for bounded mild solutions bounds all derivatives of W_j on every fixed backward interval, and a further subsequence converges locally smoothly to a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric NS solution W with viscosity nu_* (mildness passes to the limit through the mild formula on each fixed interval, using |W_j| <= 1 and the integrability of the heat and nonlinear kernels), |W| <= 1, |Gamma_W| <= nu_* G, a_W >= -1 on (-infinity, 0] and a_W(rho e_1, 0) = -1 (the record passes to the limit through a = int_0^1 d_1 u_1(lambda r e_1 + z e_3) d lambda). The swirl of W is not identically 0: otherwise W is a bounded swirl-free axisymmetric ancient solution with positive viscosity, constant by [KNSS, Theorem 5.2 and Remark 6.1], and a_W = 0. Hence there is c > 0 with S(sigma_j) >= c M_j along the subsequence (swirl domination along viscous strain records), and (b) gives nu_* >= 2 c^2/(mu_0 G^2). After normalization of the viscosity by W~(y, s) := nu_*^{-1/2} W(nu_*^{1/2} y, s), which has viscosity 1, |Gamma_{W~}| <= G, a_{W~} >= -1 and a_{W~}((rho/nu_*^{1/2}) e_1, 0) = -1, W~ belongs to LL and carries the additional normalization a >= -1 on the past, a = -1 at a point, which no Liouville theorem known to us uses. This alternative needs Type II swirl. If (T_* - t) ||u^theta(t)||_infty^2 <= C_I for t in [t_1, T_*) (the hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(i)), then S(sigma_j)^2 <= max{S(t_1)^2, C_I/(T_* - sigma_j)} for sigma_j >= t_1, and since M_j^2 = K_j/nu_j >= K_j/C_P -> infinity, the supremum of |W_j^theta|^2 over the past interval of W_j is at most S(sigma_j)^2/M_j^2 <= max{S(t_1)^2/M_j^2, C_I nu_j/((T_* - sigma_j) K_j)}, which tends to 0 because nu_j <= C_P and (T_* - sigma_j) K_j -> infinity. A subsequence with nu_* > 0 would therefore have a swirl-free limit W, constant as above, against a_W(rho e_1, 0) = -1. The displayed estimate gives S(sigma_j)/M_j -> 0 along the whole record sequence, and if nu_j did not tend to 0, the bound nu_j <= C_P would give a subsequence with a positive limit nu_*. So under the Type I swirl bound nu_j -> 0, that is K_j = o(M(sigma_j)^2), and S(sigma_j) = o(M(sigma_j)), without (A) or a gradient bound: the strain records of the Type II strain alternative are inviscid in this normalization, with swirl negligible against the velocity scale M. This concerns the normalization at the strain records, not the Case-1 limits at the swirl records, and the extraction of an Euler limit still needs the hypotheses below. If nu_* = 0, compactness needs additional hypotheses; assume (A) and a gradient bound D(sigma_j) <= C_k K_j. Then ||grad W_j||_infty <= C_k and ||grad^2 W_j||_infty <= M_j H(sigma_j)/K_j^2 <= C_* (D(sigma_j)/K_j)^2 <= C_* C_k^2, and a subsequence converges, as for the Euler limits of Proposition 8(c) (weak limits with C^1 spatial convergence), to a bounded ancient swirl-free axisymmetric Euler flow W with bounded gradient and bounded weak second derivatives, a_W >= -1 on the past and a_W(rho e_1, 0) = -1. A steady vortex ring of the swirl-free Euler equations with Hoelder continuous compactly supported vorticity, viewed in the frame moving with the ring, has, after a rescaling u -> mu u(lambda .), the bounded-velocity, bounded-gradient and compression normalizations listed (its compression u^r/r tends to 0 at infinity and takes negative values, since if u^r >= 0 on a cylinder {r = rho} the axial flux through the disk of radius rho is nonincreasing in z with equal limits at z = +infinity and z = -infinity, so u^r = 0 on that cylinder, and u^r = 0 everywhere would make u^z independent of z and the vorticity zero; hence it attains a negative minimum); such rings exist by the classical theory of steady vortex rings [FB]. The bounded second derivatives of the Euler limits above require more regularity of the ring than Hoelder continuous vorticity, so the comparison is conditional on a ring with this additional regularity; no realization by the singular solution is asserted. So in both regimes the information retained at the strain records sits at the unit scale of the normalization, and neither regime is excluded.
(3) The Type I swirl branch. The Bernstein estimates in the proof of (34.6) give ||q_U(-s)||_infty <= ||grad W(-s)||_infty = O(s^{-1/2}); (d) improves this to o(s^{-1/2}), and to O(1/s) when A_* < infinity; (e) gives O(1/s) under (CW). The same argument gives a derivative estimate for q_U itself: there is C_U, independent of tau, with
 ||grad_5 q_U(tau)||_infty <= C_U sup_{tau - 1 <= sigma <= tau} ||q_U(sigma)||_infty  for tau <= 0.   (D)
Indeed, with P := d_sigma + b_5.grad_5 - nu Delta_5 on R^5 one has P q_U = -2 a_U q_U, hence P(q_U^2) <= 4 ||a_U||_infty q_U^2 - 2 nu |grad q_U|^2 and P |grad q_U|^2 <= -2 nu |grad^2 q_U|^2 + C_0 (|grad q_U|^2 + q_U^2), where C_0 depends on the bounds of a_U, grad a_U and grad b_5; these are bounded, since grad a_U is bounded by the second derivatives of U and |y'| |grad a_U| <= |grad U^R| + |a_U| (R d_R a_U = d_R U^R - a_U, R d_Z a_U = d_Z U^R). On a window [t_0, t_0 + 1] with eps := sup ||q_U||_infty there, H := (sigma - t_0) |grad q_U|^2 + B q_U^2 with 2 nu B >= 1 + C_0 satisfies P H <= C_1 eps^2 and H(t_0) <= B eps^2, and the maximum principle (with a vanishing barrier at infinity) gives |grad q_U(t_0 + 1)|^2 <= (B + C_1) eps^2, which is (D). By (D), ||d_Z(q_U^2)(-s)||_infty <= 2 C_U ||q_U(-s)||_infty sup_{[-s - 1, -s]} ||q_U||_infty. The rate o(s^{-1/2}) then gives an integrand o(1/s) in (34.5), which need not be integrable, so (34.5) gives nothing beyond (34.6); the rate O(1/s), available when A_* < infinity and under (CW), gives ||eta_U(-s)||_infty = O(1/s), short of the bound 1/(8 K_U s^2) that Proposition 34(d)(ii) excludes. An expanding-radius compression bound would close the branch: if there are A >= 0, tau_0 < 0 and a positive function L on (-infinity, tau_0] with L(sigma) >= L(tau) for sigma <= tau <= tau_0, L(tau)/|tau|^{3/4} -> infinity as tau -> -infinity and a_U(., sigma) >= -A/L(sigma)^2 on {R < L(sigma)} for sigma <= tau_0, then for tau <= tau_0 and sigma <= tau the set {R < L(tau)} is contained in {R < L(sigma)} and a_U(., sigma) >= -A/L(tau)^2 there, so (37.3) with beta > A/(2 nu_*) gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(beta) Gbar_U/L(tau)^2 = o(|tau|^{-3/2}); by (D), ||d_Z(q_U^2)(-s)||_infty = o(s^{-3}), by (34.5) ||eta_U(-s)||_infty = o(s^{-2}), and since 0 < K_U < infinity this contradicts Proposition 34(d)(ii). The compression hypothesis is not proved. It is not a consequence of the kinematic information collected here: with s = 1 + |tau|, a smooth nonincreasing cutoff chi (equal to 1 on [0, 1], 0 on [4, infinity)) and alpha > 0 (with K chosen after chi, A, c and alpha, so that the completed field satisfies |U| <= K), the meridional field with 5D stream potential phi = (alpha/s) Z chi((R^2 + Z^2)/s^{3/2}) (U^R = -R phi_Z, U^Z = 2 phi + R phi_R) is divergence free, has a_U = -(alpha/s)(chi + 2 Z^2 chi'/s^{3/2}) >= -alpha/s with equality and eta = 0 on the ball R^2 + Z^2 <= s^{3/2}, |U| = O(alpha s^{-1/4}), and eta of order alpha s^{-7/4} supported in the shell s^{3/2} <= R^2 + Z^2 <= 4 s^{3/2}; with a z-independent circulation A g(R^2/(c s)) (g increasing from g(y) = y near 0 to 1; A, c and alpha chosen suitably, which includes the record normalization at tau = 0 and alpha gamma_* >= 1) it satisfies the following constraints recorded in this report for these limits: the swirl bounds of Proposition 33(e)(i) and Proposition 37(d), the circulation bounds and saturation, the integrated compression requirement of Proposition 34(d)(i), (iii) for alpha > 1/2, the bounds (34.1) and (34.6), and the large-scale statements of Propositions 19(b), 20(d) and 25(b) (but not the bound (34.5), which comes from the equation for eta; see below), while its compression is alpha/s on the whole ball of radius s^{3/4}. It violates the equation for eta: the source d_Z(q_U^2) vanishes and the vorticity on the shell is neither created nor transported from the interior. It also violates the circulation equation: where chi = 1 and g(y) = y the residual of that equation is (1 - 2 alpha) A R^2/(c s^2), nonzero for alpha > 1/2. So the listed kinematic bounds alone do not imply the expanding-radius compression bound; the example does not show that a particular equation or region (for instance the eta equation at radii comparable to L(tau), through a bound on the vorticity flux into {R^2 + Z^2 >= L(tau)^2}) is indispensable, and no estimate sufficient for that compression bound has been obtained. (This kinematic test was carried out independently and checked by the author; it is a test, not a counterexample.) A localized sufficient condition of this kind, also proved independently and refereed: for x in R^5, L > 0 and the Dirichlet Green function of -Delta_5 on the ball B_L(x), a_U(x) = H_L(x) + sigma_4^{-1} int_{B_L(x)} (x_5 - y_5) |x - y|^{-5} eta_U(y) dy (sigma_4 = 8 pi^2/3, H_L(x) the mean of a_U over the sphere dB_L(x)), and |H_L(x)| <= (3 pi/8) K/L for every centre, because |a_U| <= K/R and the spherical mean of 1/R over dB_L(x) is at most its value 3 pi/(8 L) at a centre on the axis (an exact formula for this mean was derived and checked numerically). Hence, if for some delta in (0, 1], lambda in (0, 1) and all sufficiently negative tau the 5D masses m_x(r) := int_{B_r(x)} |eta_U(., tau)| dmu_5 at the points x of {|Gamma_U(., tau)| > lambda} satisfy m_x(r) <= eps_delta r^4 (r/L)^delta/s for 0 < r <= L := 3 pi K s, s = |tau|, eps_delta := sigma_4 delta/(8 (delta + 4)), then a_U^- <= 1/(8 s) + 1/(8 s) = 1/(4 s) on that set, and int_{-v}^0 of the supremum of a_U^- over the superlevel set grows at most like (1/4) log v, contradicting Proposition 34(d)(i). This bound on the vorticity mass near the superlevel sets at radii up to 3 pi K s is not proved either; the kinematic family above violates it by a factor of order alpha s^{delta/4}. The bound with Gbar_U in (37.3) uses the bounded circulation and is the better one for L > Gbar_U/S_U(tau); with L := (A/m(tau))^{1/2} it gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= F(beta) Gbar_U m(tau)/A, and letting first A -> 2 nu beta and then beta -> infinity gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty <= Gbar_U m(tau)/(2 nu), the form of (37.2) for large times (G kbar/2 at viscosity 1). With the quadratic profile 2 - R^2/L^2 in place of f the same argument needs A < 2 nu (with x = R^2/L^2, calL(2 - x) = 4 a_U (1 - x) + 8 nu/L^2, so at the axis the zero-order term 2 a_U offsets the diffusive gain) and gives the factor 2 in place of F(beta); the Burgers profile f permits every finite A, by the choice beta > A/(2 nu). The arguments here exclude neither (CW) (which A_* < infinity implies) nor its failure for a Case-1 limit (see Remark (5)): the compression required by Proposition 34(d)(i), (iii) lives on the superlevel sets {|Gamma_U| > lambda}, which lie beyond rho_lambda(tau) and may lie far outside the parabolic cylinder.
(4) Literature. Albritton and Barker [AB, Theorem 1.1] show that a suitable weak solution with a Type I singular point (in their sense, a bound on the scale-invariant local energy, dissipation and pressure quantities over all parabolic balls in a neighbourhood of the point) exists if and only if there is a non-trivial mild bounded ancient solution whose scale-invariant quantity I (the supremum of these quantities over all parabolic balls) is finite; the forward implication is by blow-up, and the reverse one, the novelty of [AB], by zooming out on the ancient solution, which preserves axial symmetry when the zoom-out is centered on the axis. By [AB, Remark 3.2] a pointwise bound (-t)^{1/2} ||v(t)||_infty <= C alone does not appear to guarantee I < infinity; this is not shown to fail. Seregin [Se20, Theorem 2.1] shows that axisymmetric suitable weak solutions have no Type I singular points (in the sense of [Se20, Definition 1.7], finiteness of the minimum of the limiting centered scale-invariant quantities, which the condition of [AB] implies); its proof uses a Harnack inequality for the circulation [Se20, Lemma 2.2] (after [NU]) whose constant depends only on the ratio M >= 1 of the upper bound to the axis lower bound in its hypotheses [Se20, (2.20)] and on N_R := R^{-1/2} ||u||_{L^4_t L^3_x(Q(R))}, together with uniform bounds on the scale-invariant quantities over all parabolic cylinders Q(R) (it is described here only to locate the obstruction and is not used). Together these results exclude non-trivial axisymmetric mild bounded ancient solutions with I < infinity (bounded circulation is not needed for this implication): a zoom-out centered on the axis would produce an axisymmetric suitable weak solution with a Type I singular point in the sense of [AB], hence in the sense of [Se20], which [Se20, Theorem 2.1] excludes; the published theorem is used here without an independent repair of its auxiliary lemma. They do not reach the limits of Proposition 33(e)(i): the bound on the swirl leaves the meridional field at large scales uncontrolled, and even a bound |U(tau)| <= min{K, C |tau|^{-1/2}} on the whole velocity, which is not available, gives by the elementary mixed-norm estimate only N_R = O(R^{1/2}) on the cylinders Q(R) centered at the origin, so it does not give a uniform bound (such a bound would nevertheless exclude these limits by Proposition 38(b), which does not use I < infinity). A circulation bounded below by g > 0 on a cylinder {r_0 <= r <= R/2, |z| <= R/2} would give R^{-1} int_{B_R} |U|^2 >= 2 pi g^2 log(R/(2 r_0)), so circulation saturation across many intermediate annuli would make the scale-invariant energy grow at least like log R; the supremum saturation of Proposition 23(a) does not establish that distribution. Apart from Proposition 38, which needs a one-sided Type I bound for the inflow on the circulation superlevel sets, no Liouville theorem for this class without I < infinity is known to us.
(5) (The time-integrated condition (CW) of (e).) (a) For every A >= 0, int_t^{2t} m_P <= A log 2 + int_t^{2t} (m_P(s) - A/s)^+ ds, and the excess integrand is at most m_P, so a bound on the dyadic windows for the excess of m_P over a Type I profile A/s is equivalent to (CW). (CW) allows bursts: s m_P(s) may be unbounded along a sequence of times, provided the integrals over the dyadic windows stay bounded. If int_t^{2t} m_P <= B_0 + eps log t for large t (B_0 >= 0, eps > 0), the proof of (37.5), with lambda(t) := max{1, (2 B_0 + 2 eps log t + log(2 F(beta)))/kappa_beta} in place of lambda in each application of (37.4), gives, for Q(t) := ||q_U(-t)||_infty, Q(t) <= C t^{-1 + 2 eps} (1 + log t)^{1/2} + Q(2t)/2 for large t; since sum_{j >= 0} 2^{-(2 - 2 eps) j} (1 + log t + j log 2)^{1/2} <= C' (1 + log t)^{1/2} for eps < 1 and 2^{-n} Q(2^n t) -> 0, ||q_U(-t)||_infty = O(t^{-1 + 2 eps} (log t)^{1/2}) for 0 < eps < 1; for eps >= 1 the same bound follows from the boundedness of q_U. This improves the unconditional rate o(t^{-1/2}) of (d) when eps < 1/4. (b) (A growing envelope.) If m_P(s) <= A(s)/s for large s, with A >= 0 nondecreasing and H(t) := max{nu_*, t sup_{v >= t} A(v)/v} finite, then for large t, with L^2 := nu_* t/H(t) <= t, every v >= t and |y'| < L, a_U^-(y, -v) <= m_P(v) <= H(t)/t = nu_*/L^2, and (37.3) with beta = 1 and nu_* in place of A gives ||q_U(-t)||_infty <= F(1) min{(C_I H(t)/(gamma_* nu_*))^{1/2}, G H(t)/(gamma_* nu_*)}/t. (c) (Failure of (CW).) Each integral int_t^{2t} m_P is finite, so (CW) fails exactly when I_j := int_{t_j}^{2 t_j} m_P -> infinity along some t_j -> infinity; then there are s_j in [t_j, 2 t_j] with m_P(s_j) >= I_j/(2 t_j) and points y_j with |y_j'| < s_j^{1/2} and d_j := a_U^-(y_j, -s_j) >= I_j/(4 t_j), so s_j d_j >= I_j/4 -> infinity. With the decomposition of a_U in Remark (3) at x := y_j and L := 3 pi K/(4 d_j), for which |H_L(x)| <= d_j/2, int_{B_L(x)} (y_5 - x_5) |x - y|^{-5} eta_U(y, -s_j) dy >= sigma_4 d_j/2, and since int_{B_L} |z|^{-4} dz = sigma_4 L, sup_{B_L(x)} |eta_U(., -s_j)| >= d_j/(2 L) = 2 d_j^2/(3 pi K). The radius L = 3 pi K s_j/(4 s_j d_j) may be much larger than s_j^{1/2}, so this does not place potential vorticity in a fixed multiple of the parabolic cylinder. Conversely, by (34.1) applied to U(-s), m_P(s) <= (2 K ||eta_U(-s)||_infty)^{1/2}, so (CW) holds if int_t^{2t} ||eta_U(-s)||_infty^{1/2} ds is bounded for large t, for instance if ||eta_U(-s)||_infty <= C s^{-2}, the rate discussed in Proposition 34, Remark (3); under (CW), Proposition 39(f)(ii) and (xi) give only ||eta_U(-s)||_infty <= C s^{-3/2}, so this does not close. (Radial variation of the strain rate.) For every bounded smooth divergence-free axisymmetric U with bounded derivatives, at every time -s of its domain and for R >= 0 and Z in R, |a_U(R, Z, -s) - a_U(0, Z, -s)| <= (5/pi^{1/2}) R ||eta_U(-s)||_infty. Indeed Delta_5 a_U = d_Z eta_U; with H_v := e^{v Delta_5} and F_v := d_Z H_v eta_U one has a_U = H_V a_U - int_0^V F_v dv, and the difference of H_V a_U at (R, Z) and (0, Z) is at most R ||a_U||_infty (pi V)^{-1/2}, which tends to 0 as V -> infinity (a_U is bounded: a_U(R, Z) = int_0^1 d_1 U_1(t R e_1 + Z e_3) dt, so |a_U| <= ||grad U||_infty), so a_U(R, Z) - a_U(0, Z) = -int_0^infinity [F_v(R, Z) - F_v(0, Z)] dv; here |F_v| <= ||eta_U|| (pi v)^{-1/2} (the L^1 norm of the Z-derivative of the heat kernel), and, F_v being even in R, |F_v(R, Z) - F_v(0, Z)| <= (R^2/2) sup |d_R^2 F_v| <= (R^2/2) ||eta_U|| (pi v)^{-1/2} v^{-1} (the L^1 norm of a second derivative of the one-dimensional heat kernel is E|N^2 - 1|/(2 v) = 2 (2 pi e)^{-1/2}/v < 1/v, N standard normal); the first bound over v < R^2, counted at both points, and the second over v > R^2 give (4 + 1) R ||eta_U||/pi^{1/2}. Under (CW), Proposition 39(f)(ii) and (xi) give ||eta_U(-s)||_infty <= C s^{-3/2} for all sufficiently large s. For L >= 1 put m_{P,L}(s) := sup{a_U^-(y, -s) : R_y < L s^{1/2}}; then m_{P,L}(s) <= m_P(s) + 5 L C/(pi^{1/2} s), since a_U^-(R, Z) <= a_U^-(0, Z) + |a_U(R, Z) - a_U(0, Z)| and the axis point lies in the parabolic cylinder, and consequently limsup_t int_t^{2t} m_{P,L} <= limsup_t int_t^{2t} m_P + 5 L C log(2)/pi^{1/2}. Thus (CW) holds on every fixed multiple of the parabolic cylinder: unbounded dyadic compression integrals cannot be confined to any such fixed multiple (additional compression of order 1/s there is not excluded). (Lagrangian form.) With X the backward diffusion of (39.2) started at (y, -s), Xi(y, s) := E int_0^infinity |d_Z(q_U^2)|(X_u, -s - u) du and Xi_s := sup_y Xi(y, s), the decomposition of Remark (3) and |eta_U(., -s)| <= Xi_s from (39.2) give a_U^- <= (3 pi/8) K/L + L Xi_s for every L, hence m_P(s)^2 <= (3 pi K/2) Xi_s. With psi(u) := (s + u)^{1/2}, Ito's formula for psi q_U(X_u, -s - u)^2 and ||q_U(-beta)||_infty^2 = o(1/beta) from (d) give 4 E int_0^infinity psi a_U^- q_U^2 du = 2 nu E int_0^infinity psi |grad_5 q_U|^2 du + 4 E int_0^infinity psi a_U^+ q_U^2 du + E int_0^infinity psi' q_U^2 du + s^{1/2} q_U(y, -s)^2 (nonnegative terms, possibly infinite on both sides), and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives Xi(y, s) <= 2 Q_2(s)^{1/2} (E int_0^infinity psi |d_Z q_U|^2 du)^{1/2} with Q_2(s) := int_s^infinity beta^{-1/2} ||q_U(-beta)||_infty^2 dbeta = o(s^{-1/2}). Hence sup_y E int_0^infinity psi |d_Z q_U|^2 (X_u, -s - u) du >= m_P(s)^4/(9 pi^2 K^2 Q_2(s)): a compression on the parabolic cylinder must be paid by axial swirl gradients met along the backward paths. Here Q_2(s) > 0, since q_U(-beta) = 0 for all beta >= s would give q_U = 0 at later times by uniqueness for the linear q-equation, against U^theta(e_1, 0) = 1. The identity bounds the Lagrangian axial dissipation above by the compression-weighted swirl energy, which the estimates here control under (CW). No finite upper bound for this dissipation is established here without (CW). These inequalities respect the Navier-Stokes scaling when K is scaled together with U; their weakness is that the global velocity bound of the fixed field U gives, after parabolic rescaling to the scale s^{1/2}, the velocity bound K s^{1/2}, which grows with s. For m_P(s) = Lambda(s)/s the lower bound is Lambda(s)^4/(9 pi^2 K^2 s^4 Q_2(s)); in the comparison where Q_2(s) and the Lagrangian axial dissipation are both of size s^{-3/2} (the parabolic sizes |q_U| ~ 1/s, |d_Z q_U| ~ s^{-3/2}), the ratio of this lower bound to that size is proportional to Lambda(s)^4/(K^2 s), so the condition becomes restrictive only when that ratio is large; this comparison is not an upper bound for the actual dissipation. (Reduction to the axis.) Put m_A(s) := sup_Z a_U^-(0, Z, -s), the compression on the axis. By the radial variation of the strain rate, a_U^-(y, -s) <= a_U^-(0, Z_y, -s) + (5/pi^{1/2}) R_y ||eta_U(-s)||_infty, and the axis lies in the parabolic cylinder, so m_A(s) <= m_P(s) <= m_A(s) + (5/pi^{1/2}) s^{1/2} ||eta_U(-s)||_infty <= m_A(s) + (5/pi^{1/2}) s^{1/2} Xi_s for every bounded smooth divergence-free axisymmetric U with bounded derivatives for which the representation (39.2) holds. For a limit as in (d), (CW) therefore holds if and only if both limsup_t int_t^{2t} m_A < infinity and limsup_t int_t^{2t} s^{1/2} ||eta_U(-s)||_infty ds < infinity: the second condition follows from (CW) by Proposition 39(f)(ii) and (xi), and the converse is the displayed inequality. With the bound for Xi(y, s) above, (m_P(s) - m_A(s))^2 <= (100/pi) s Q_2(s) sup_y E int_0^infinity psi |d_Z q_U|^2 (X_u, -s - u) du; this bound contains no explicit factor K and respects the Navier-Stokes scaling; at the parabolic comparison sizes Q_2(s) = O(s^{-3/2}) and sup_y E int_0^infinity psi |d_Z q_U|^2 (X_u, -s - u) du = O(s^{-3/2}) its right-hand side, and hence (m_P(s) - m_A(s))^2, are O(s^{-2}); no matching lower bound is asserted. (Reduction to the axis inside the cone.) For a bounded smooth divergence-free axisymmetric field with |U| <= K and bounded potential vorticity, an axis point x_0 = (0, Z), rho > 0, E_rho := sup_{B_rho(x_0)} |eta_U| and 0 <= R <= rho/4, |a_U(R, Z) - a_U(0, Z)| <= C (R E_rho + K R^2/rho^3), with an absolute constant C. Indeed, let N be the fundamental solution of -Delta_5 and p := -d_Z N * (eta_U 1_{B_rho(x_0)}) = -int_0^infinity d_Z e^{v Delta_5}(eta_U 1_{B_rho(x_0)}) dv; then H := a_U - p is harmonic in B_rho(x_0), since Delta_5 a_U = d_Z eta_U. The heat-semigroup argument above, applied to p (its density eta_U 1_{B_rho(x_0)} is bounded by E_rho and radial in y'), gives |p(R, Z) - p(0, Z)| <= (5/pi^{1/2}) R E_rho, and |d_Z N(z)| <= C |z|^{-4} gives |p| <= C rho E_rho on B_rho(x_0). Since |a_U| <= K/R_y and int_{B_rho(x_0)} R_y^{-1} dy = (pi^3/4) rho^4 in R^5, ||H||_{L^1(B_rho(x_0))} <= C (K rho^4 + E_rho rho^6); the interior estimate for harmonic functions gives sup_{B_{rho/4}(x_0)} |D^2 H| <= C rho^{-7} ||H||_{L^1(B_rho(x_0))}, H is radial in y', so its y'-gradient vanishes at x_0, and Taylor's formula gives |H(R, Z) - H(0, Z)| <= C R^2 (K/rho^3 + E_rho/rho) <= C (K R^2/rho^3 + R E_rho). For a limit as in (d), A_c > A_3, A' > A_c, delta := A' - A_c, m_C as in Proposition 39(f)(xiii), m_{A,c}(s) := sup{a_U^-(0, Z, -s) : |Z| < A_c s} and E'(s) := sup{|eta_U(y, -s)| : y in C_{A'}(-s)}, take rho := delta s: for R_y < s^{1/2}, |Z_y| < A_c s and s >= 16/delta^2 the ball B_rho((0, Z_y)) lies in C_{A'}(-s), so m_{A,c}(s) <= m_C(s) <= m_{A,c}(s) + C s^{1/2} E'(s) + C K/(delta^3 s^2), and the last term has window integral at most C K/(2 delta^3 t). Hence (CW_loc) holds if limsup_t int_t^{2t} m_{A,c} < infinity and limsup_t int_t^{2t} s^{1/2} E'(s) ds < infinity for some A' > A_c; conversely (CW_loc) implies the first condition and, by Proposition 39(f)(xiii), the second with A' replaced by any E < A_c. This is a reduction between two cones, not an equivalence on one cone, and it does not give m_C - m_{A,c} = o(1/s) pointwise: with beta := 1 + s and F, chi smooth with compact support, F(0) = 0 < F(1/4) and chi = 1 near 0, the stream potential Phi := (Z/beta) F(R^2/beta) chi(Z/beta^{1/2}) (with U^R = -R d_Z Phi, U^Z = 2 Phi + R d_R Phi) gives a smooth bounded divergence-free axisymmetric field with |U| = O(beta^{-1/2}), |eta_U| = O(beta^{-3/2}), a_U(0, Z) = 0 and a_U = -F(1/4)/beta at R = beta^{1/2}/2, Z = 0 (a kinematic field, not a solution). The axis part is not reduced in this way: the same heat-semigroup argument does not bound the variation of a_U(0, ., -s) in Z by ||eta_U(-s)||_infty (the Z-difference of F_v is bounded by |Delta Z| ||eta_U||_infty c/v, which is not integrable at large v), and no bound |a(0, Z_1) - a(0, Z_0)| <= C |Z_1 - Z_0| ||eta||_infty holds for bounded smooth divergence-free axisymmetric fields: with rho := (R^2 + Z^2)^{1/2}, P := Z^2 - R^2/4 (Delta_5 P = 0), chi a smooth cutoff of rho equal to 1 on [0, 1] and to 0 on [2, infinity) and 0 < eps < 1/4, the stream potential Phi_eps := -(1/2) chi(rho) P log(rho^2 + eps^2), with U^R = -R d_Z Phi_eps and U^Z = 2 Phi_eps + R d_R Phi_eps as in (d) below, has velocity and potential vorticity eta = -Delta_5 Phi_eps bounded uniformly in eps (on rho <= 1, eta = P (7 rho^2 + 9 eps^2)/(rho^2 + eps^2)^2, so |eta| <= 7), while a(0, Z) = Z log(Z^2 + eps^2) + Z^3/(Z^2 + eps^2) for |Z| <= 1, so (a(0, eps) - a(0, 0))/eps = log(2 eps^2) + 1/2 is unbounded; and, since d_Z U^Z = -2 a_U on the axis, the mean of a_U(0, ., -s) over [Z_0 - L, Z_0 + L] equals -(U^Z(0, Z_0 + L, -s) - U^Z(0, Z_0 - L, -s))/(4 L), whose absolute value is at most K/(2 L); this controls the signed mean, not the mean of a_U^- or m_A(s). On the axis the strain rate obeys a Riccati equation forced by the pressure: with P_U the pressure of U (so that d_tau U + U.grad U + grad P_U = nu Delta U), the radial momentum equation divided by R gives (d_tau + U^R d_R + U^Z d_Z) a_U = -a_U^2 + q_U^2 - (d_R P_U)/R + nu Delta_5 a_U, and at an axis point grad U has the eigenvalues a_U +- i q_U and -2 a_U, so Delta P_U = -tr((grad U)^2) = 2 q_U^2 - 6 a_U^2 = 2 d_R^2 P_U + d_Z^2 P_U there; hence (d_tau + U^Z d_Z) a_U = 2 a_U^2 + (1/2) d_Z^2 P_U + nu Delta_5 a_U on R = 0 (the explicit swirl terms cancel; Delta_5 a_U = 4 d_R^2 a_U + d_Z^2 a_U there). Without the pressure and diffusion terms, a_U = -m < 0 at an axis point at time tau_0 would give a_U = -m/(1 - 2 m (tau_0 - tau)) along the backward axial characteristic, unbounded within backward time 1/(2 m); so in a bounded ancient solution an axis compression is sustained backward in time only by the axial curvature of the pressure and by diffusion. No bound for these terms is derived here. The following facts on the axis were found in the parallel line of work and checked by the author; write a(Z, tau) := a_U(0, Z, tau) and c := -a. (1) Since d_R^2 P_U = q_U^2 - 3 a^2 - (1/2) d_Z^2 P_U on the axis, along an axis characteristic dZ/dtau = U^Z(0, Z, tau) one has dc/dtau = c^2 + [d_R^2 P_U - q_U^2] + nu Delta_5 c, a Riccati equation in which the swirl term opposes the compression and a radial pressure minimum on the axis drives it. (2) As 2 a + d_Z U^Z = 0 on the axis, |int_{Z_1}^{Z_2} a(Z, tau) dZ| = (1/2) |U^Z(0, Z_2, tau) - U^Z(0, Z_1, tau)| <= K for Z_1 < Z_2. So at time -s the bound a <= -Lambda/(2 s) holds on no interval longer than 2 K s/Lambda, and on every axial interval the integral of a^- exceeds that of a^+ by at most K; a bound on the total measure of disjoint compressed sets does not follow (a = -A cos(2 A Z/K) satisfies the flux bound). Consequently, if a(Z_0, -s) <= -Lambda/s with Lambda > 0, then sup_Z |d_Z a(Z, -s)| >= Lambda^2/(4 K s^2), by the mean value theorem on intervals starting at Z_0 of length slightly above 2 K s/Lambda; the point of large derivative need not lie in the Euler cone: with Phi := (Lambda/s) Z chi((R^2 + Z^2)/(A_c^2 s^2)), chi smooth with compact support and chi = 1 on [0, 2], the bounded divergence-free axisymmetric field U^R = -R d_Z Phi, U^Z = 2 Phi + R d_R Phi has a_U = -Lambda/s and d_Z a_U = 0 on C_{A_c}(-s) (here sup|U| >= 2 Lambda A_c, so Lambda <= K/(2 A_c)). If |Z_0| < A_c s and Lambda > 2 K/A_c, the intervals can be taken from Z_0 toward Z = 0, inside {|Z| < A_c s}, and then an axis compression Lambda/s at a point of the cone violates the first bound of (39.21) at that time unless C_a >= Lambda^2/(4 K); in general (39.21) gives only Lambda <= K/(2 A_c) + C_a A_c at compressed axis points of the cone. (3) Integrating dc/dtau = -2 c^2 - (1/2) d_Z^2 P_U + nu Delta_5 c along a characteristic over [-2t, -t] gives int_{-2t}^{-t} [-(1/2) d_Z^2 P_U + nu Delta_5 c] dtau = 2 int_{-2t}^{-t} c^2 dtau + c(-t) - c(-2t) >= 2 W_c^2/t - m_A(2t) - sup_Z a^+(Z, -t), W_c := int_{-2t}^{-t} c^+ dtau, the compression collected along that characteristic (a large window integral of m_A does not by itself give a characteristic with W_c large). (4) Forward in time, let F_1 := d_R^2 P_U - q_U^2 + nu Delta_5 c on the axis and c_0 := c(Z_0, -s) > 0. For every delta in (1/c_0, s], int_{-s}^{-s + delta} F_1^- dtau > c_0 - 1/delta along the characteristic through (Z_0, -s): otherwise, with y := c along it and G(tau) := int_{-s}^tau F_1^-, the function v := y + G - G(-s + delta) satisfies v <= y, v(-s) >= 1/delta and v' >= y^2 >= v^2 on [-s, -s + delta], so c is unbounded before time 0, while sup |a_U| < infinity. As q_U^2 <= ||q_U(-beta)||_infty^2, int_{-s}^{-s + delta} (d_R^2 P_U + nu Delta_5 c)^- dtau > c_0 - 1/delta - delta sup{||q_U(-beta)||_infty^2 : s - delta <= beta <= s}: a large axis compression needs, within a short later time, a radial pressure maximum on the axis or viscous relaxation of at least this integrated size. (5) Backward in time, put G := (1/2) d_Z^2 P_U + nu d_Z eta_U on the axis (Delta_5 a_U = d_Z eta_U), so that dc/ds' = 2 c^2 + G along the characteristic in the backward time s' := -tau. For every delta > 1/(2 c_0), int_{-s - delta}^{-s} G^- dtau > c_0 - 1/(2 delta) along the characteristic through (Z_0, -s): otherwise, with G_1 := int_s^{s + delta} G^- ds', the function v(s') := c + int_s^{s'} G^- - G_1 satisfies v <= c, v(s) >= 1/(2 delta) and dv/ds' = 2 c^2 + G^+ >= 2 v^2 on [s, s + delta], so c is unbounded before s' = s + delta. For delta = 1/c_0 the mean of G^- over the backward time delta exceeds c_0^2/2. The characteristic stays in the cone {|Z| < A_c beta} at the earlier times -beta if |Z_0| < A_c s, since |U^Z| <= K < A_c. (6) On the axis U^R = 0 and Delta U^Z = -2 eta_U, so the axial momentum equation gives d_Z P_U(0, Z, tau) = -(d_tau w + w d_Z w) - 2 nu eta_U(0, Z, tau), w := U^Z(0, ., .): the axial pressure gradient on the axis is minus the Lagrangian axial acceleration of the axis fluid, up to the viscous term; no swirl term appears (the swirl contributes to P_U through the Poisson equation for P_U, which this identity does not use). Integrating d_Z^2 P_U over [Z_0 - l, Z_0 + l] x [tau_1, tau_1 + t], with |d_Z w| = 2 |a|, bounds the absolute value of its mean by 2 K/(l t) + 2 K a_e/l + 2 nu eta_e/l, where a_e and eta_e are the suprema of |a| and |eta_U(0, ., .)| at the two ends over the time interval (after one integration in Z the convective end term is w d_Z w, not w^2/2). A bound for this signed space-time mean is not comparable with (5), which concerns the negative part of G along one characteristic. Differentiating the identity in Z gives G = -(1/2) d_Z (d_tau w + w d_Z w) on the axis: (5) says that the axial derivative of the Lagrangian axial acceleration of the axis fluid has a large positive part along the characteristic, and dc/ds' = 2 c^2 + G is the derivative of the kinematic identity c = (1/2) d_Z w along it. (7) The axis identities and the velocity bound alone do not exclude a backward axis compression with (-tau) c -> infinity: with S := 1 - tau, the functions w := S^{-1/4} tanh(2 S^{-1/4} Z), eta := 0 and d_Z P := -(d_tau w + w d_Z w) on the axis satisfy the identities of (5) and (6), |w| <= 1, all their derivatives are bounded, c(0, tau) = S^{-1/2} and G(0, tau) = -2 S^{-1} - S^{-3/2}/2, while S^{3/4} sup_Z |d_tau w + w d_Z w| lies between 0.77 and 0.86 for 10 <= S <= 10^4 (symbolic and numerical check). This is a function on the axis, not the axis trace of a solution; so an exclusion of the axis branch must use more than these identities and |U| <= K, and smallness of the axial acceleration, as opposed to its axial derivative, does not suffice. The acceleration does bound the width of a compressed interval from above: two axis particles at Z_- < Z_+ at time -s with separation L and V := w(Z_+, -s) - w(Z_-, -s) > 0 do not meet, and if |d_tau w + w d_Z w| <= F along both over the backward time 2 L/V, their separation d satisfies d = L and d' = -V at s' = s and |d''| <= 2 F, so 0 < d(s + 2 L/V) <= -L + 4 F L^2/V^2, that is F > V^2/(4 L); if c >= c_0/2 on [Z_-, Z_+], then V >= c_0 L and F > c_0^2 L/4. No lower bound L >= eps K/c_0 for the length of a compressed interval holds for bounded smooth divergence-free fields in general (item (2) gives only an upper bound, the fields at the end of item (8) violate such a bound, and item (8) gives a lower bound in terms of the potential vorticity), and for the function above the interval where c >= c(0, tau)/2 has length of order S^{1/4}, while K/c(0, tau) is of order S^{1/2}. (8) (Local envelope and width.) Use the notation of the reduction to the axis inside the cone (A' > A_c, delta := A' - A_c, rho := delta s, E'(s) the supremum of |eta_U(-s)| over C_{A'}(-s)), and let |Z_0| < A_c s; then B_rho((0, Z_0)) lies in C_{A'}(-s) for every s > 0. Since |a_U| <= K/R, that reduction gives c(Z_0, -s) <= K/R + C (R E'(s) + K R^2/rho^3) for 0 < R <= rho/4, and R := min{rho/4, (K/E'(s))^{1/2}} (R := rho/4 if E'(s) = 0) gives m_{A,c}(s) <= C (K E'(s))^{1/2} + C K/(delta s), the cone-local form of the bound m_P(s) <= (2 K ||eta_U(-s)||_infty)^{1/2} of (c). If E'(s) <= B s^{-3/2}, this gives s m_{A,c}(s) <= C (K B)^{1/2} s^{1/4} + C K/delta and int_t^{2t} m_{A,c} <= C (K B)^{1/2} t^{1/4} + C K/delta; these upper bounds are not bounded in t (they do not show that the window integrals diverge). With the inequality for m_C above, (CW_loc) holds if limsup_t int_t^{2t} [(K E'(s))^{1/2} + s^{1/2} E'(s)] ds < infinity for some A' > A_c (the remainders have window integrals C K log(2)/delta and C K/(2 delta^3 t)); so if (CW_loc) fails, this window integral of the potential vorticity is unbounded for every A' > A_c. A field with eta_U = 0 on C_{A'}(-s), for example a uniform axisymmetric strain there, has m_{A,c}(s) <= C K/(delta s). For the function of (7), with S = 1 + s, the envelope shows that for fixed K and delta and all sufficiently large s a field with |U| <= K having that axis trace at time -s has E'(s) >= 1/(4 C^2 K S); the width bound below gives the stronger E'(s) >= c S^{-3/4} for large s, since the interval where c >= c(0, -s)/2 has length arcosh(2^{1/2}) S^{1/4} there. The width of a compressed interval is bounded below in terms of the potential vorticity: if c_0 := c(Z_0, -s) > 0 and J = [Z_-, Z_+] is the maximal interval containing Z_0 on which c(., -s) >= c_0/2 (bounded by item (2)), of length L_1 <= rho/4, then c_0 <= C (E'(s) L_1 + K L_1^2/rho^3) with an absolute constant C. Indeed, with d_+ := Z_+ - Z_0, d_- := Z_0 - Z_- and T g := (d_+ g(Z_-) + d_- g(Z_+))/L_1 - g(Z_0) for functions g on J, T annihilates affine functions, |T g| <= 2 sup_J |g| and |T g| <= (d_+ d_-/2) sup_J |g''| <= (L_1^2/8) sup_J |g''|, and T a(., -s) = c_0/2, since c = c_0/2 at the ends of J. Write a_U = p + H on B_rho((0, Z_0)) as in the reduction. Splitting the density of p at distance 2 L_1 from (0, Z_0), the near part of p is bounded by C E'(s) L_1 on J (|d_Z N(z)| <= C |z|^{-4}) and the far part has |d_Z^2| <= C E'(s)/L_1 on J (|d_Z^3 N(z)| <= C |z|^{-6}), so |T p| <= C E'(s) L_1; and |T H| <= C L_1^2 (K/rho^3 + E'(s)/rho) by the interior estimate of the reduction, J lying in B_{rho/4}((0, Z_0)). For c_0 = Lambda/s item (2) gives L_1 <= 2 K s/Lambda, so L_1 <= rho/4 if Lambda >= 8 K/delta, and K L_1^2/rho^3 <= 4 K^3 c_0/(delta^3 Lambda^3); hence for Lambda >= 8 K/delta and Lambda^3 >= 8 C K^3/delta^3 one has E'(s) > 0 and L_1 >= c_0/(2 C E'(s)), and item (2) then gives c_0^2 <= 4 C K E'(s), the envelope again for these Lambda. The term K L_1^2/rho^3 cannot be dropped: for 0 < t <= 2^{-5/2} the stream potential t^2 Z - Z^3/3 + R^2 Z/4 - t^4 R^2/8, multiplied by a fixed smooth cutoff of (R^2 + Z^2)^{1/2} equal to 1 on [0, 1] and to 0 on [2, infinity), gives smooth divergence-free axisymmetric fields bounded by a constant K_0 independent of t, with a_U = -t^2 + Z^2 - R^2/4 and eta_U = t^4 on the unit ball (symbolic check); at Z_0 = 0 one has c_0 = t^2, L_1 = 2^{1/2} t <= 1/4, and a_U <= -c_0/2 on {R <= L_1} x J; with rho := 1 and E the supremum of |eta_U| on the unit ball, E L_1/c_0 = 2^{1/2} t^3 -> 0, while K_0 L_1^2/(rho^3 c_0) = 2 K_0 stays bounded below, and also L_1 c_0/K_0 = 2^{1/2} t^3/K_0 -> 0 (kinematic fields, not solutions). (9) (Sharpness of the envelope; pressure curvature.) The square root in (8) cannot be removed by kinematics: if V is a bounded smooth divergence-free axisymmetric field with |V| <= 1, a_V(0, 0) = -1 and |eta_V| <= e_0 (such V are obtained from any bounded field with a compressed axis point, for example one of the fields of (8), by the scalings V -> mu V(lambda .)), then U(x) := K V(x/L) has |U| <= K, a_U(0, 0) = -K/L and |eta_U| <= e_0 K/L^2, so a_U^-(0, 0) = (K E/e_0)^{1/2} with E := e_0 K/L^2. So with E'(s) <= C s^{-3/2} the envelope gives only m_{A,c}(s) = O(s^{-3/4}); an improvement needs either a better rate on the cone (E'(s) = O(s^{-2}) suffices, by the envelope and the two-cone inequality) or information, beyond K and the supremum of the potential vorticity, that excludes the persistence of such configurations (potential vorticity of size E at distance of order (K/E)^{1/2} from the axis; dynamical improvements are not excluded). The following inequalities give neither. They are the two-cone inequality, the envelope, the time-integrated barrier for q_U of Proposition 39(f)(xiii) (a bound for q_U on a window in terms of the window integral of the compression), q_U = o(beta^{-1/2}), and an inequality of the form E'(s) <= 2 Q''(s)^{1/2} [(2/nu) int_s^infinity beta^{1/2} m''(beta) f''(beta) dbeta + C s^{-3/2}]^{1/2} + C e^{-c s}, with f''(beta) the supremum of q_U(-beta)^2 over a larger cone C_{A''}(-beta), m'' the compression supremum m_C for that cone and Q''(s) := int_s^infinity beta^{-1/2} f''(beta) dbeta (the cone-local form of the Lagrangian form above, with the backward paths stopped at the exit from C_{A''}, as derived in the parallel line of work; the cones are nested so that the potential vorticity is taken on a cone larger than that of the compression it controls, and the swirl on a cone larger than that of the potential vorticity). This last inequality is not proved here; adding it can only strengthen the system, so the conclusion below does not depend on it. All of these inequalities hold for large s with f''(beta) = c_q beta^{-2}, E'(s) = c' s^{-3/2} and m_C = m'' = m_{A,c} = c s^{-3/4}, c <= C (K c')^{1/2} (the right side of the last inequality is then of order s^{-11/8}), while the window integrals of c s^{-3/4} grow like t^{1/4}. For the term G of (5): with the canonical pressure of the mild formulation, split the source U_i U_j at distance delta s from the axis point; the kernel of d_Z^2 d_i d_j (-Delta)^{-1} on R^3 is homogeneous of degree -5, so the far part contributes at most C K^2 int_{|z| >= delta s} |z|^{-5} dz = 2 pi C K^2/(delta s)^2 to |d_Z^2 P_U|, small against the mean c_0^2/2 = Lambda^2/(2 s^2) of G^- required in (5) once Lambda >> K/delta. The swirl part P_sw of the pressure (Delta P_sw = div(x' q_U^2), x' the horizontal position, from the centripetal force) has a better structure: if Delta_5 w = q_U^2, then F := (2 + R d_R) w solves Delta_3 F = div(x' q_U^2), as Delta_3 = Delta_5 - (2/R) d_R, and F = 2 w on the axis; so, for the canonical swirl pressure and w = -N_5 * (q_U^2), N_5(y) = 1/(8 pi^2 |y|^3) (constants in the pressure are harmless, harmonic additions are not: adding Z^2 - R^2/4 to w preserves Delta_5 w and changes F_ZZ by 4), on the axis d_Z^2 P_sw = -2 d_Z^2 (-Delta_5)^{-1}(q_U^2) = (2/5) q_U^2 + (3/2) lim_{eps -> 0} int int_{R > 0, R^2 + t^2 > eps^2} R^3 (R^2 - 4 t^2)(R^2 + t^2)^{-7/2} q_U(R, Z + t)^2 dR dt, an operator of order zero on q_U^2 whose kernel has mean zero on spheres. The limit is a principal value over five-dimensional spheres: integrating first in t gives 0 for every R > 0, so for a Z-independent q_U the iterated integral is 0 and would leave the contact term, while the spherical principal value equals -(4/15) q_U(0)^2 and cancels it, as it must. Hence, if |q_U| <= Q on the ball of radius L about the axis point, M bounds the five-dimensional gradient of q_U there and (U^theta)^2 <= B/beta everywhere at that time, then |d_Z^2 P_sw| <= C Q^2 (1 + log_+(L M/Q)) + C B/(beta L^2) (the local term read as 0 if Q = 0; split at r_0 = min{L, Q/M}); a one-sided bound q_U <= Q does not suffice (a negative q_U supported in 1 < R < 2, |Z| < 1/10, with zero meridional field, has positive axis curvature at the origin while q_U <= Q for every Q > 0). Under (CW_loc), Proposition 39(f)(xiii) gives |q_U| <= C/beta on each fixed smaller cone, and the bound with L = beta^{1/2} at axis points of a further smaller cone gives a swirl part O(beta^{-2} (1 + log beta)); this assumes (CW_loc), so it cannot be used to prove it, and it does not control the meridional near pressure. The meridional near part and the viscous term nu d_Z eta_U are bounded only through unit-scale bounds for the derivatives of U; so (5) is not contradicted. (10) (Where the potential vorticity of the configuration of (9) can come from.) Let U be a limit as in (d) on the Type I swirl branch, so that |U^theta(x, -beta)|^2 <= B_theta/beta for beta > 0, and let G' >= sup |Gamma|, f(beta) := ||q_U(-beta)||_infty^2 and m_infty(beta) := ||a_U^-(-beta)||_infty. With X the backward diffusion of (39.2) started at (y, -s), R_u := |X_u'|, beta_u := s + u and psi(u) := beta_u^{1/2}, put h(x, beta) := min{f(beta), B_theta/(beta R_x^2), G'^2/R_x^4} (h := f(beta) on the axis), so that q_U(x, -beta)^2 <= h(x, beta), and Theta := E int_0^infinity psi^{-1} h(X_u, beta_u) du, Psi := E int_0^infinity psi a_U^-(X_u, -beta_u) h(X_u, beta_u) du. (a) (Along-path budget.) |eta_U(y, -s)|^2 <= (8/nu) Theta Psi, with Theta <= Q_2(s) < infinity; if Theta = 0 then q_U = 0 along almost every path, so eta_U(y, -s) = 0, and if Psi = infinity the bound is void. Proof: by (39.2) and the Cauchy-Schwarz step of the Lagrangian form above, |eta_U(y, -s)| <= Xi(y, s) <= 2 (E int psi^{-1} q_U^2 du)^{1/2} (E int psi |d_Z q_U|^2 du)^{1/2}; the first expectation is at most Theta since q_U^2 <= h, and the Ito identity above gives 2 nu E int psi |d_Z q_U|^2 du <= 4 E int psi a_U^- q_U^2 du <= 4 Psi. This is the Lagrangian form with the Type I and circulation bounds used at the radius of the path instead of the supremum f. The improvements over f(beta) occur beyond the crossover radii (B_theta/(beta f(beta)))^{1/2} and (G'^2/f(beta))^{1/4}, respectively; under the scalar profile f(beta) of order beta^{-2} both are comparable to the parabolic radius, while for example f(beta) = beta^{-3/2}, which is allowed by f = o(1/beta), gives the smaller radii beta^{1/4} and beta^{3/8}. (b) (Material at the ring distance.) For a measurable r(beta) > 0 let p(beta) := P(R_{beta - s} < r(beta)). Splitting the paths at the radius r and using a_U^- <= K/R outside the cylinder gives Theta <= int_s^infinity beta^{-1/2} [f p + G'^2 r^{-4}] dbeta and Psi <= int_s^infinity beta^{1/2} [m_infty f p + K G'^2 r^{-5}] dbeta, and the same with G'^2 r^{-4} and K G'^2 r^{-5} replaced by B_theta/(beta r^2) and K B_theta/(beta r^3). For r(beta) = kappa beta^{3/4} and p = 0 on [s, infinity) this gives |eta_U(y, -s)|^2 <= (64/45) K G'^4 nu^{-1} kappa^{-9} s^{-19/4}, and the Type I form gives (16/7) B_theta^2 K nu^{-1} kappa^{-5} s^{-15/4}. For the configuration of (9), kappa^2 = K/c', the first bound on |eta_U|^2 is o(c'^2 s^{-3}), so its square root is o(c' s^{-3/2}). The exterior terms alone have the displayed sizes. Exact vanishing of p is unavailable for the nondegenerate diffusion (with nu > 0 and a bounded drift the backward paths enter every open cylinder with positive probability). These formulas neither estimate the law conditioned on avoiding the inner cylinder (conditioning changes the path law and does not preserve the Ito inequality used in (a)) nor exclude a viscous ring, and a bound at the ring points does not bound E'(s); that would need a separate uniform estimate of the inner contributions. If |eta_U(-s)| <= C s^{-19/8} held on all of C_{A'}(-s), the envelope of (8) would give m_{A,c}(s) <= C s^{-19/16} + C K/(delta s), with bounded dyadic window integrals, while the rate s^{-15/16} from the Type I form has window integrals 16 (2^{1/16} - 1) t^{1/16}. (c) (Occupation of the near-axis region; under profile hypotheses that are not established for the limits.) Assume f(beta) <= c_q beta^{-2} and m_infty(beta) <= c_m beta^{-3/4} for beta >= s (the scalar profile of (9), with the compression supremum taken over all of R^5), take r(beta) := lambda beta^{1/2} and suppose p <= p_0 almost everywhere on [s, infinity). The Type I form of (b), with a_U^- <= m_infty also outside the cylinder, gives Theta <= (2/3)(c_q p_0 + B_theta lambda^{-2}) s^{-3/2}, Psi <= (4/5) c_m (c_q p_0 + B_theta lambda^{-2}) s^{-5/4} and |eta_U(y, -s)|^2 <= (64/15)(c_m/nu)(c_q p_0 + B_theta lambda^{-2})^2 s^{-11/4}. Hence, if |eta_U(y, -s)| >= c' s^{-3/2}, then with L_s := (15 nu/(64 c_m))^{1/2} c' s^{-1/8} and lambda^2 := 2 B_theta/L_s (so lambda is of order s^{1/16}), ess sup_{beta >= s} P(R_{beta - s} < lambda beta^{1/2}) >= L_s/(2 c_q): the backward paths from such a point enter the cylinder of radius of order s^{1/16} beta^{1/2} with probability at least of order s^{-1/8} at some backward times (precisely: for every fixed 0 < eps < 1, a set of backward times of positive measure carries probability greater than (1 - eps) L_s/(2 c_q); no lower bound on the measure of that set is given). This concerns the backward diffusion only: it does not say that the source was collected there or that q_U^2 is of size f there, it gives no visit within the current dyadic window and no residence time, and with p_0 = 1 it reduces to the bound of order s^{-11/8} of (9). (d) (Steady orbits.) Let V be a steady bounded smooth axisymmetric divergence-free field with swirl on a region of the meridional half-plane foliated by regular streamlines of its Stokes stream function psi_V (V^R = -d_Z psi_V/R), with Gamma = F(psi_V) there, F smooth. Then q^2 = F(psi_V)^2 R^{-4} and d_Z(q^2) = -2 F F'(psi_V) V^R R^{-3}, so along an orbit segment from radius R_1 to radius R_2 the source integrates in time to F F'(psi_V) (R_2^{-2} - R_1^{-2}), and to 0 along a closed orbit: in the steady setting, production of potential vorticity over many passages needs circulation out of streamline equilibrium. This identity excludes nothing for the time-dependent limits; inviscid transport alone does not bring Gamma to streamline equilibrium. (e) (Hill's spherical vortex.) In the comoving frame let psi_H := (A/10) R^2 (a^2 - R^2 - Z^2) inside the ball of radius a and the potential flow past the sphere outside; the vortex moves at speed W = 2 A a^2/15. Then eta = A inside and 0 outside (a patch, not smooth), a_U = A Z/5 inside, so the axis compression is at most c_0 = A a/5 (attained at the rear stagnation point), the largest laboratory speed is K_h = A a^2/3 (on the axis at the centre), and c_0^2 = (3/25) K_h eta: the snapshot realizes the envelope of (8) with the constant (3/25)^{1/2} at the distance a = (3 K_h/eta)^{1/2}. The interior streamlines are closed with positive minimal radius, attained in the plane Z = 0; only the separatrix (the axis and the sphere) reaches the axis, and the fraction of the interior three-dimensional volume on streamlines entering {R < r} is (3/2)(r/a)^2 log(a/r) + O((r/a)^2) as r/a -> 0, as follows by integrating the sublevel set R^2 (a^2 - R^2 - Z^2) < r^2 (a^2 - r^2) (in the variable X = R^2/a^2 the fraction is 1 - (3/2) int_{d^2}^{1 - d^2} (1 - X - q_d/X)^{1/2} dX with d = r/a and q_d = d^2 (1 - d^2), which is (3/4) q_d log(1/q_d) + O(q_d)). These orbit and volume calculations describe the geometry of a steady Hill cell. They do not test the fixed-start diffusion probability in (c), and (c) gives no exclusion of Hill-like snapshots or of time-dependent exchange between radial scales: (c) concerns the law of the backward diffusion from one point, not the volume of starting points; its cylinder grows with beta, so for a frozen cell of fixed radius the event of (c) holds for all large beta; and a steady cell violates m_infty(beta) <= c_m beta^{-3/4}. A nonzero Hill vortex, regarded as an entire ancient swirl-free field, is not a member of the class represented by (39.2): in that class q = 0 would imply eta = 0. This does not exclude Hill-like spatial configurations in a time-dependent history with nonzero swirl source. (f) (Localizations.) Let C_loc be the constant of Proposition 39(a) and D_Gamma := (G'^2 + 16 nu B_theta)/nu. (i) (Exterior part along every path; no profile hypothesis.) If kappa s^{3/4} >= 3, then for every realization of the backward diffusion from (y, -s), int_0^infinity 1[R_u >= kappa beta_u^{3/4}] |d_Z(q_U^2)|(X_u, -beta_u) du <= 81 C_loc G'^2 kappa^{-4} s^{-2}, so by (39.2) |eta_U(y, -s)| <= 81 C_loc G'^2 kappa^{-4} s^{-2} + E int_0^infinity 1[R_u < kappa beta_u^{3/4}] |d_Z(q_U^2)|(X_u, -beta_u) du. Proof: |d_Z(q_U^2)| <= 162 C_loc G'^2 R^{-4} for R >= 3 (Proposition 39(a)), R_u^{-4} <= kappa^{-4} beta_u^{-3} on the event, and int_0^infinity beta_u^{-3} du = s^{-2}/2. (ii) (A fixed parabolic cylinder; no profile hypothesis.) For every M > 0, E int_0^infinity 1[R_u >= M beta_u^{1/2}] |d_Z(q_U^2)|(X_u, -beta_u) du <= 2^{1/2} G' D_Gamma^{1/2} M^{-4} s^{-3/2}. This is the exterior estimate in the proof of Proposition 39(d)(iii), from (39.9) with the weight s/(s + u) and the radius M beta_u^{1/2}. Hence, if |eta_U(y, -s)| >= c' s^{-3/2} and M^4 >= 2^{3/2} G' D_Gamma^{1/2}/c', at least (c'/2) s^{-3/2} of the absolute source is collected, in expectation, while the backward path is in the fixed parabolic cylinder {R < M beta^{1/2}}. (iii) (The set carrying the envelope.) Let x_0 = (0, Z_0) be an axis point with c_0 := a_U^-(x_0, -s) > 0, L := 3 pi K/(4 c_0), E_L the supremum of |eta_U(-s)| on B_L(x_0) and S := {y in B_L(x_0) : |eta_U(y, -s)| >= c_0^2/(3 pi K)}. Then |S|_5 >= (sigma_4/5)(c_0/(4 E_L))^5 = pi^2 c_0^5/(1920 E_L^5), and its meridional trace S_2 has int_{S_2} R dR dZ >= c_0^7/(2160 pi^2 K^2 E_L^5). Proof: in the decomposition a_U = H_L + sigma_4^{-1} int_{B_L(x)} (x_5 - y_5) |x - y|^{-5} eta_U(y) dy of Remark (3), |H_L(x_0)| <= c_0/2 by the choice of L, so int_{B_L(x_0)} |x_0 - y|^{-4} |eta_U| dy_5 >= sigma_4 c_0/2; on B_L(x_0) minus S, |eta_U| < c_0/(4 L) and int_{B_L} |z|^{-4} dz = sigma_4 L, so int_S |x_0 - y|^{-4} dy_5 >= sigma_4 c_0/(4 E_L); among sets of given five-dimensional measure this integral is largest for the centred ball, for which it equals sigma_4 rho with measure sigma_4 rho^5/5; finally |S|_5 = 2 pi^2 int_{S_2} R^3 dR dZ and R < L on S. If the compression supremum is not attained, apply this at axis points with compression d -> c_0. For the configuration of (9), c_0 = c s^{-3/4} and E_L <= c' s^{-3/2} (B_L(x_0) lies in the larger cone for large s, since L is of order s^{3/4}), so |S|_5 >= pi^2 c^5 s^{15/4}/(1920 c'^5), and the potential vorticity guaranteed on S is c^2 s^{-3/2}/(3 pi K), not c' s^{-3/2}. (iv) (Residence; under the hypotheses of (c).) Assume f(beta) <= c_q beta^{-2} and m_infty(beta) <= c_m beta^{-3/4} for beta >= s. Fix lambda_0 > 0, put lambda^2 := lambda_0^2 s^{1/4}, tau_* := (nu/(8 c_m))^{1/2} c'/c_q, N(s) := max{(8/(3 tau_*))^{2/3} s^{1/12}, (16/(5 tau_*))^{4/5} s^{1/10}}, and let T_in := int_0^{(N(s) - 1) s} 1[R_u < lambda beta_u^{1/2}] du. If s^{1/8} >= 16 B_theta/(5 c_q tau_* lambda_0^2) and |eta_U(y, -s)| >= c' s^{-3/2}, then E[T_in] >= (tau_*/2) s^{7/8}. Proof: split Theta and Psi into the parts from the cylinder at ages beta <= N s, from outside the cylinder, and from the cylinder at ages beta > N s. The first parts are at most c_q s^{-5/2} E[T_in] and c_m c_q s^{-9/4} E[T_in]; by the Type I form of (b) the second are at most (2/3)(B_theta/lambda_0^2) s^{-7/4} and (4/5) c_m (B_theta/lambda_0^2) s^{-3/2}; by h <= f the third are at most (2/3) c_q (N s)^{-3/2} and (4/5) c_m c_q (N s)^{-5/4}. If E[T_in] < T_* := (tau_*/2) s^{7/8}, the conditions on s and N(s) make each second and third part at most half of the first part evaluated at T_*, so Theta < c_q tau_* s^{-13/8} and Psi <= c_m c_q tau_* s^{-11/8}, and (a) gives |eta_U(y, -s)|^2 < (8/nu) c_m c_q^2 tau_*^2 s^{-3} = c'^2 s^{-3}, a contradiction. The inverse strain scale is c^{-1} s^{3/4}; the residence lower bound of (iv) exceeds it by a factor proportional to s^{1/8}, and no estimate of an individual passage time is asserted; this is a lower bound for the backward diffusion, not a statement about material cylinders. (g) (Verdict.) The arguments in (a) to (f) do not establish the improved envelope m_{A,c}(s) <= C s^{1/2} E'(s) + C K/(delta s), which would remove the square root of (8), and no exclusion of time-dependent exchange between the near-axis region and the ring distance has been obtained here; the estimates extracted here from the potential-vorticity equation along backward paths with the global supremum f, from the circulation bounds of Proposition 33 and from the axis Riccati constraint of (5) have not yielded it. Whether the standing hypotheses and the full coupled equations imply this estimate or (CW_loc) remains open, and no counterexample among the limits is known. Part (f)(ii) localizes a necessary expected absolute-source contribution to a fixed parabolic cylinder; the residence alternative of (iv) concerns its explicitly larger, s-dependent cylinder of radius lambda_0 s^{1/8} beta^{1/2}. Under the hypotheses of (c), with c' replaced in (ii) and in (iv) (including tau_*, N(s) and T_in) by the amplitude c_S := c^2/(3 pi K) guaranteed on the set S of (iii), either of the following would exclude the configuration of (9): a bound sup_{y in S} E_y[T_in] = o(s^{7/8}); or, for one M with M^4 >= 2^{3/2} G' D_Gamma^{1/2}/c_S, a bound o(s^{-3/2}), uniform over y in S, for the axial swirl dissipation E int_0^infinity 1[R_u < M beta_u^{1/2}] beta_u^{1/2} |d_Z q_U|^2(X_u, -beta_u) du collected inside the fixed parabolic cylinder (by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality with E int_0^infinity beta_u^{-1/2} q_U^2 du <= (2/3) c_q s^{-3/2}, the source collected there is then o(s^{-3/2}), against the half of c_S s^{-3/2} required by (ii)). Neither bound is proved. One possible additional ingredient is a quantitative relation between source collection along backward paths and compression-weighted residence near the axis; the present calculations do not prove that every successful argument must take this form. Where a_U = -c < 0 the backward radial drift c R + 3 nu/R is outward, so forward convergence does not give long backward residence near the axis. (h) (Energy form of the core criterion.) With the notation of (f), put 1_in := 1[R_u^2 < M^2 beta_u], psi := beta_u^{1/2}, D_nu := G'^2 + (32/3) nu B_theta, J_M(y, s) := E int_0^infinity 1_in psi (a_U^- q_U^2)(X_u, -beta_u) du (the compression-weighted swirl energy collected inside the fixed parabolic cylinder), A_Z := E int_0^infinity psi |d_Z q_U|^2(X_u, -beta_u) du and A_M := E int_0^infinity 1_in psi |d_Z q_U|^2(X_u, -beta_u) du.
