(i) For every M > 0, with no profile hypothesis, 2 nu E int_0^infinity 1_in psi |grad_5 q_U|^2 du + nu M^{-4} E int_0^infinity (1 - 1_in) beta_u^{-3/2} |grad_5 Gamma_U|^2 du <= 4 J_M + M^{-4} D_nu s^{-3/2}, hence A_Z <= (4/nu) J_M + D_nu s^{-3/2}/(nu M^4); and, with A_out := E int_0^infinity (1 - 1_in) psi |d_Z q_U|^2(X_u, -beta_u) du, A_Z = A_M + A_out (as extended nonnegative quantities) and A_out <= D_nu s^{-3/2}/(nu M^4). (ii) If f(beta) <= c_q beta^{-2} for beta >= s and |eta_U(y, -s)| >= c_eta s^{-3/2}, then A_Z >= (3 c_eta^2/(8 c_q)) s^{-3/2}, so J_M(y, s) >= (3 nu c_eta^2/(32 c_q) - D_nu/(4 M^4)) s^{-3/2} and A_M >= (3 c_eta^2/(8 c_q) - D_nu/(nu M^4)) s^{-3/2}, and both lower bounds are at least half of their leading terms once M^4 >= 16 c_q D_nu/(3 nu c_eta^2). So, if the profile f(beta) <= c_q beta^{-2} holds for all large beta with a fixed c_q (a global hypothesis, as in (c); the cone-local profiles of (9) do not supply it), then, with c_eta = c^2/(3 pi K) on the set S of (f)(iii), a bound J_M = o(s^{-3/2}) uniform over S (for one fixed M satisfying the threshold) would exclude a solution realizing the configuration of (9) together with that profile, in addition to the two criteria of (g); by (i), J_M is the only term on the compression side, the swirl dissipation inside the cylinder and the weighted circulation dissipation outside being paid by J_M up to D_nu s^{-3/2}/M^4. No such bound is proved. Under the bounds of (c), direct substitution of a_U^- <= m_infty(beta) and q_U^2 <= f(beta) gives only J_M <= (4/5) c_m c_q s^{-5/4}. A visit to a region inside a fixed cylinder {R < rho} where a_U <= -c_* < 0, stopped on leaving that region, lasts in expectation at most (2 c_*)^{-1} log(1 + c_* rho^2/nu); for a visit stopped also at the age 2s, with the fixed enclosing radius rho = M (2s)^{1/2}, c_* comparable to s^{-3/4} and the bounds of (c), its contribution to J_M is O(s^{-3/2} log s). Neither estimate controls the number of visits or gives the uniform o(s^{-3/2}) bound, and neither shows that the actual J_M fails to satisfy it. Proof. (i) Follow the proof of Proposition 39(f)(ii) with the interface R^2 = s replaced by R^2 = M^2 beta_u: Y_u := R_u^2 - M^2 beta_u, V := q_U^2 on {Y < 0} and V := M^{-4} beta^{-2} Gamma_U^2 on {Y >= 0}, which agree on {Y = 0} since Gamma_U = R^2 q_U; V = q_U^2 + H Y^+ with H := q_U^2 (R^2 + M^2 beta)/(M^4 beta^2) >= 0, so V has a nonnegative outward normal derivative jump at the interface and, with the symmetric local time L^0(Y), the interface contributes q_U^2/(M^2 beta) dL^0(Y) >= 0 to dV (the quadratic variation rate of Y is 8 nu R_u^2 > 0 on the interface, and the moving boundary only adds -M^2 du to the drift of Y). Inside, d(psi q_U^2) has drift psi' q_U^2 + 4 psi a_U q_U^2 + 2 nu psi |grad_5 q_U|^2 >= 2 nu psi |grad_5 q_U|^2 - 4 psi a_U^- q_U^2; outside, as in that proof, d(M^{-4} beta^{-3/2} Gamma_U^2) has drift at least M^{-4} (nu beta^{-3/2} |grad_5 Gamma_U|^2 - ((3/2) G'^2 + 16 nu B_theta) beta^{-5/2}). Integrate over [0, T], take expectations (localization as there), drop -s^{1/2} V(y, s) <= 0, use int_s^infinity ((3/2) G'^2 + 16 nu B_theta) beta^{-5/2} dbeta = D_nu s^{-3/2} and E psi(T) V_T <= beta_T^{1/2} max{f(beta_T), G'^2 M^{-4} beta_T^{-2}} -> 0 (f = o(1/beta)), and let T -> infinity. For A_Z: inside |d_Z q_U| <= |grad_5 q_U|; outside |d_Z q_U| = |d_Z Gamma_U|/R^2 <= |grad_5 Gamma_U|/(M^2 beta), so psi |d_Z q_U|^2 <= M^{-4} beta^{-3/2} |grad_5 Gamma_U|^2 there, and nu A_Z is at most the left side of (i). For A_out: (39.9) on [0, T] with the nonincreasing weight w(u) := (s/(s + u))^{3/2}, and monotone convergence as T -> infinity, give nu E int_0^infinity w |grad_5 Gamma_U|^2 du <= G'^2 + 16 nu B_theta int_0^infinity w beta_u^{-1} du = D_nu, since int_0^infinity w beta_u^{-1} du = 2/3, and outside the cylinder psi |d_Z q_U|^2 <= M^{-4} s^{-3/2} w |grad_5 Gamma_U|^2. (ii) By (39.2) and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, |eta_U(y, -s)| <= 2 (E int_0^infinity beta_u^{-1/2} q_U^2 du)^{1/2} A_Z^{1/2}, and E int_0^infinity beta_u^{-1/2} q_U^2 du <= c_q int_s^infinity beta^{-5/2} dbeta = (2/3) c_q s^{-3/2}; so A_Z >= (3 c_eta^2/(8 c_q)) s^{-3/2}, and the two lower bounds follow from (i). For the visit: F(r) := (2 c_*)^{-1} log(1 + c_* r^2/nu) has F' = r/(nu + c_* r^2) > 0, and since the backward radial drift is -a_U R + 3 nu/R >= c_* R + 3 nu/R there, the radial part of the backward generator gives at least nu F'' + (c_* r + 3 nu/r) F' = 1 + nu (3 nu + c_* r^2)/(nu + c_* r^2)^2 >= 1; the stopped Ito formula bounds the expected duration by F(rho). (i) (Forward depletion along a compressed tube; conditional.) Let 0 < T < s and let gamma(t) = (r(t), z(t)), 0 <= t <= T, be the forward trajectory of y = (R_0, Z_0) under the meridional velocity U_m at the times -s + t, N := -int_0^T a_U(gamma(t), -s + t) dt (so r(T) = R_0 e^{-N}) and beta_1 := s - T > 0. Let rho > 0, ell >= 0 continuous, rho(t) := rho exp(-int_0^t ell), and assume for 0 <= t <= T: (i1) rho(t) <= r(t)/2; (i2) (x - gamma(t)).(U_m(x) - U_m(gamma(t))) >= -ell(t) |x - gamma(t)|^2 on the meridional disc B_{rho(t)}(gamma(t)) at time -s + t; (i3) with m := |Gamma_U(y, -s)| > 0, sigma its sign and 0 < alpha <= 1, sigma Gamma_U(-s) >= alpha m on B_rho(y). Put j := nu int_0^T rho(t)^{-2} dt and delta := 2^{3/2} e^{-1/(8 j)}. If delta < 1, then
 alpha (1 - delta) |Gamma_U(y, -s)| <= R_0 e^{-N} (B_theta/beta_1)^{1/2} + G' delta,   so q_U(y, -s)^2 <= [e^{-N} (B_theta/beta_1)^{1/2} R_0^{-1} + G' delta R_0^{-2}]^2/(alpha^2 (1 - delta)^2).
If sigma Gamma_U >= 0 on the lateral boundary of the tube, the term G' delta can be omitted. In the affine regime r(t) = R_0 e^{-ct}, ell = c, rho = eta R_0 (eta <= 1/2) one has N = cT and 1/(8 j) = eta^2 N L/(4 (1 - e^{-2N})) with L := r(T)^2/(nu T), so delta = o(e^{-pN}) for every p when eta is fixed and N, L -> infinity. None of (i1) to (i3) has been derived for the limits. The compression threshold does not control the ell of (i2) by a constant multiple of the compression: the divergence-free kinematic field (-cR, 2cZ + h R^2) (unbounded, not a solution) has a_U = -c and a meridional symmetric gradient with entries -c, hR, hR, 2c, whose least eigenvalue c/2 - (9 c^2/4 + h^2 R^2)^{1/2} is arbitrarily negative (smoothness alone gives some ell, from a bound for the negative part of the symmetric gradient). The axis identity of (5) alone, without estimates for its forcing, gives no quantitative lifetime of {c >= c_0/2}: every smooth history satisfies it with the forcing defined by the identity, which need not come from a solution. The plateau (i3) cannot be replaced by the Type I and circulation bounds alone: for the drift (-cR, 2cZ), with w' = 2 c w - 4 nu w^2, w(0) = w_0, theta(t) := (1 - e^{-4ct})/(4c) and D := eps^2 + 2 nu theta, the function Gamma_eps := A_1 (1 - e^{-w R^2}) (eps/D^{1/2}) exp(-e^{-4ct} Z^2/(2 D)) is an exact bounded nonnegative solution of the circulation equation that vanishes quadratically at the axis, Gamma_eps(R_0, 0, 0) = A_1 (1 - e^{-w_0 R_0^2}) does not depend on eps, and sup Gamma_eps(T) <= A_1 eps (eps^2 + 2 nu theta(T))^{-1/2} -> 0 as eps -> 0 (axial diffusion erases a thin peak). On a fixed interval [0, T] with T < s, the choices A_1 <= G' and A_1^2 max{w_0, c/(2 nu)} <= B_theta/s give the circulation bound and the Type I bound uniformly in eps (w stays below max{w_0, c/(2 nu)} and (1 - e^{-w R^2})/R <= w^{1/2}), while Gamma_eps(R_0, rho/2, 0)/Gamma_eps(R_0, 0, 0) = e^{-rho^2/(8 eps^2)} -> 0 for each fixed rho, so these upper bounds do not imply (i3) with a prescribed radius and alpha bounded below. This concerns the scalar circulation equation with a prescribed unbounded affine drift on a finite interval; it is not a counterexample among the limits. If (i1) to (i3) held at points of S with alpha >= alpha_0 > 0 and N = kappa log s, and in addition R_0 >= r_* s^{1/2}, beta_1 >= b_* s and delta = o(s^{-kappa}) uniformly at these points (none of which follows from the definition of S, which bounds only the distance from the axis point), (i) would give q_U^2 = O(s^{-2 - 2 kappa}) there. In the affine regime with c comparable to s^{-3/4} and eta fixed, T = N/c = O(s^{3/4} log s), so beta_1 is comparable to s and L >= C s^{1/4 - 2 kappa}/log s -> infinity when 0 < kappa < 1/8, which gives delta = o(s^{-p}) for every p. Even if q_U^2 = O(beta^{-2 - 2 kappa}) held throughout the core at every age beta >= s, with a_U^- = O(beta^{-3/4}) there, direct integration gives only J_M = O(s^{-5/4 - 2 kappa}), which for kappa < 1/8 does not give the o(s^{-3/2}) of (h). Proof of (i): f := |x - gamma(t)|^2/rho(t)^2 satisfies |grad f|^2 = 4 f/rho^2 and, for the circulation operator calL := d_t + U_m.grad - nu (d_R^2 - R^{-1} d_R + d_Z^2), calL f = 2 (x - gamma).(U_m(x) - U_m(gamma))/rho^2 + 2 ell f - 4 nu/rho^2 + 2 nu (R - r)/(R rho^2) >= -6 nu/rho^2 on the disc, by (i2) and R >= r - rho >= rho. With J(t) := int_0^t rho^{-2}, A_0 := 1/(8 nu J(T)), A := A_0/(1 - 4 nu A_0 J) (the denominator is at least 1/2) and C := (3/2) log(A/A_0), one has A' = 4 nu A^2/rho^2 and C' = 6 nu A/rho^2, so Q := exp(A f - A_0 + C) satisfies calL Q/Q = A' f + A calL f + C' - 4 nu A^2 f/rho^2 >= 0, Q <= 1 at t = 0 and Q >= 1 on {f = 1}. Hence v := alpha m - (alpha m + G') Q satisfies calL v <= 0, v <= sigma Gamma_U at t = 0 by (i3) and on the lateral boundary since |Gamma_U| <= G', the maximum principle on the moving tube (which (i1) keeps at distance at least min_t rho(t) > 0 from the axis, so that calL has bounded coefficients and is uniformly parabolic there) gives v <= sigma Gamma_U there, and at the terminal centre Q = 2^{3/2} e^{-A_0} = delta while |Gamma_U| <= r(T) (B_theta/beta_1)^{1/2} by the Type I swirl bound. The affine regime is the computation of J; the exact solution and the identity calL f + 6 nu/rho^2 = [6 c (Z - z(t))^2 + 4 nu - 2 nu r(t)/R]/rho(t)^2 in the affine model (z(t) = Z_0 e^{2ct}, rho(t) = eta R_0 e^{-ct}) were confirmed by symbolic computation. Under the standing hypotheses, (1) to (10) do not give m_A(s) = O(1/s) or bounded dyadic window integrals of m_A or of m_{A,c}; the envelope gives sufficient conditions in terms of the decay or the window integrability of the potential vorticity, and these are not established. So a failure of (CW) means that limsup_t int_t^{2t} m_A = infinity or limsup_t int_t^{2t} s^{1/2} ||eta_U(-s)||_infty ds = infinity (the alternatives are inclusive and may occur on different windows; no spatial localization of the large potential vorticity is asserted). (d) (A kinematic test of (CW).) Let 1/2 < b < 1, t_n := 4^n, l_n := t_n^b, zeta >= 0 smooth with support in (1, 2) and zeta = 1 on [5/4, 7/4], chi a smooth cutoff equal to 1 on [0, 1] and to 0 on [2, infinity), v > 0, and F_0(r) := sum_{j >= 0} r^{2j}/(4^j j! (j + 1)!) (= 2 I_1(r)/r, the even radial solution of F_0'' + 3 F_0'/r = F_0, that is Delta_4 F_0 = F_0 on R^4). For s = -sigma >= 0 put Phi := v sum_{n >= 1} zeta(s/t_n) F_0(R/l_n) chi(R/l_n) sin(Z/l_n), U^R := -R Phi_Z, U^Z := 2 Phi + R Phi_R and U^theta := 0. At each time at most one summand is nonzero; the field is smooth, axisymmetric and divergence free, with bounded velocity and bounded space-time derivatives of all orders (spatial derivatives bring factors l_n^{-1}, time derivatives factors t_n^{-1}). Its potential vorticity eta = -Delta_5 Phi vanishes on {R < l_n} (there chi = 1 and Delta_5 [F_0(R/l) sin(Z/l)] = l^{-2} (F_0 - F_0) sin(Z/l) = 0), hence on {R < s^{1/2}} for large s, while for 5/4 <= s/t_n <= 7/4, a_U = -(v/l_n) F_0(R/l_n) cos(Z/l_n) on {R < l_n}, so m_P(s) >= v/l_n (F_0 >= 1, Z = 0) and int_{t_n}^{2 t_n} m_P >= (v/2) t_n^{1 - b} -> infinity. So (CW) fails, with zero potential vorticity in the parabolic cylinders at large times and q_U = 0. The field violates the equation for eta: at s = 2 t_n, between two episodes, eta = 0, and P eta = d_Z(q_U^2) = 0 would keep eta = 0 at later times by the comparison principle, whereas eta is not identically 0 during the episode n. (Adding U^theta := c_0 R/(1 + s + R^2), c_0 > 0, gives bounded circulation, |U^theta|^2 <= c_0^2/(4 (1 + s)) and zero source, and violates both scalar evolution equations.) So (CW) does not follow from smoothness, boundedness of the velocity and of its space-time derivatives, axisymmetry, incompressibility and eta = -Delta_5 Phi, even with eta = 0 on {R < s^{1/2}} for all large s, nor, for the swirl variant, together with bounded circulation and Type I swirl. The field is not a solution, and it does not satisfy the normalization -gamma_* U^R(e_1, 0) >= 1 of the limits (its meridional part vanishes for s <= 4); whether the failure of (CW) is compatible with all properties of Case-1 limits is not known, and the example does not show that a proof of (CW) must use a particular evolution equation.
Status: (a), (b) and (c) proved here, (d) proved from (c) and Proposition 33(e)(i); the estimate (D) and the conditional exclusion in Remark (3) are proved there; Remark (2) gives compactness under the hypotheses stated there and a comparison with vortex rings subject to the cited existence and regularity input, and Remark (4) records implications of cited theorems and conditional large-scale comparisons. (a) and (b) were derived twice, independently, and refereed by an independent review (review 21 in sec. 5), which required the convention for kbar(sigma) = 0 in (37.2), supplied the present proof of the bound for S(sigma_j) and repaired the compactness statements of Remark (2) (the position of the record relative to the axis, compactness without a gradient bound when nu_* > 0, and the use of the pressure-free weak formulation in [KNSS]); the author checked each step by hand, including the equation for a, the sign of Delta_5 a - d_t a at the record, the axis identity and the Burgers equalities. The barrier was supplied with the quadratic profile 2 - R^2/L^2 by a research consultation (review 22 in sec. 5), and the conditional rate in (d) for that profile was derived separately; an independent referee of both (review 23 in sec. 5) supplied the profile f and the present form of (37.3) and (d). The author rederived the identities for f and h, the computation of calL phi, the comparison argument and the choice of L, and added the optimization over beta in the consequence of (c) and the bound with Gbar_U in (37.3). The literature statements of Remark (4) were checked by the author in the arXiv texts of [AB] and [Se20]; [NU] and [FB] were not retrieved. A hostile referee of the whole package (review 24 in sec. 5) confirmed (a) to (d), corrected the Burgers example, the convention at kbar(sigma) = 0, several qualifications of Remarks (1) to (4) and the summaries, and supplied the proof of (D); the author checked every finding and rederived (D). Part (e) and Remark (5) were derived by the author and, independently, by a research consultation, which supplied the dyadic window in the proof of (37.5) (the author's version used windows of length (2^k - 1) |tau| and the decay of (d)), the rate in Remark (5)(a), the bound in Remark (5)(b) and the kinematic test in Remark (5)(d); the author rederived (37.4), including the identity for calL(w phi) (also checked symbolically), the iteration with its constants, the rate, the bound (b), the concentration bound (c) and the test. An independent check in the parallel line of work confirmed (37.4), (37.5) and the joined-energy bound under (CW) of Proposition 39(f)(xi); the sufficient condition through (34.1) in (c) was noted there, in a form with the Lagrangian source budget along the backward paths, and checked by the author. A hostile independent referee (review 39 in sec. 5) confirmed (e) and Remark (5)(a) to (c) and the construction in (d), asked for the iteration in (5)(a) to be written out and restricted the scope of (d) (its field does not satisfy the normalization of the limits); applied. A further hostile referee (review 40 in sec. 5) confirmed these repairs and the decay discussion of Remark (3), and required the case eps >= 1 in Remark (5)(a) and the withdrawal of a sentence of Remark (3) stating that a proof of the compression bound must use the eta equation at radii comparable to L(tau) (the kinematic field there also violates the circulation equation); applied. The observation in Remark (2) that the viscous alternative needs Type II swirl was derived by the author from the Type I swirl hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(i), the bound nu_j <= C_P and the swirl-free Liouville theorem; an independent referee (review 41 in sec. 5) confirmed it, including the historical swirl bound, the covered past interval, the compactness at positive viscosity and the axis case of the normalization, and asked for the normalized field W~ in the statement on LL and for the separation of vanishing viscosity from Euler compactness; applied; a further hostile referee (review 42 in sec. 5) confirmed the repaired statement. The bound for the radial variation of the strain rate and the Lagrangian form in Remark (5)(c) were found in the parallel line of work (the first by an independent referee there) and checked by the author by hand, including the heat-kernel constants and the Ito identity; review 43 (sec. 5) confirmed them, with repairs now applied (the divergence-free hypothesis, the bound for the large-time term, the form of the localization conclusion, the positivity of Q_2 and the scaling sentence). The reduction to the axis in Remark (5)(c) is an own corollary of the radial variation estimate and of Proposition 39(f)(ii), (xi); review 45 (sec. 5) confirmed it, with a repair of the statement on the order of the bound for m_P - m_A, and supplied the example showing that the axial variation of a_U on the axis is not bounded by ||eta||_infty. Item (10) of Remark (5)(c) was derived in the parallel line of work and refereed there (the referee confirmed the constants and the orbit identity, corrected the claims on the Hill orbits and restricted the scope of the conclusions); the author checked (a) to (e) by hand, including the Ito step, the exponents and constants of (b) and (c), the orbit identity and the Hill constants, and corrected the volume fraction in (e). Review 56 (sec. 5) confirmed the constants in (10)(a) to (c), the signed orbit identity and the Hill snapshot constants, and supplied an analytic proof of the orbit-volume asymptotic; it required correction of the crossover-radius sentence in (a), withdrawal of the deterministic-orbit inference from (c) in (e), and qualification of the ancient-state and nonimplication conclusions in (e) and in the verdict; these repairs are applied. Part (f) of item (10) was obtained in the parallel line of work and refereed there ((i) and (iii) confirmed by independent referees, (iv) confirmed with repairs of the comparison step and of the horizon, now applied; (ii) is the exterior estimate of the proof of Proposition 39(d)(iii)); the author checked each step by hand (the integration in (i), the constant of (ii) from (39.9), the bathtub step and both volume constants of (iii), the three-part split of the paths and the four threshold conditions of (iv)). Review 57 (sec. 5) confirmed (f)(i) to (iv) with their constants and thresholds; it withdrew a sentence equating the inverse strain with a passage time, asked for the guaranteed amplitude c^2/(3 pi K) in both alternatives of (g) and narrowed the localization sentence of (g); these repairs are applied. Part (h) was also obtained in the parallel line of work and refereed there (the localization of the stochastic integrals and the bound for A_Z - A_M from (39.9) were supplied by that referee); the author checked each step by hand (the continuity of V at the moving interface and the sign of its normal derivative jump, both drifts, the constant D_nu, the weight integral 2/3, the Cauchy-Schwarz step and the supersolution F). Part (i) was obtained by a research consultation in the parallel line of work and refereed there (that referee qualified the asymptotics and the scope of the obstruction); the author checked each step by hand (the bound for calL f with the radial term, the equations for A and C, the boundary values of Q, the terminal value delta and the affine form of j) and confirmed the exact solution Gamma_eps and the affine identity by symbolic computation. Review 66 (sec. 5) independently confirmed the stochastic energy inequality and the exterior dissipation estimate of (h) and the conditional tube barrier, the affine formula for j and the exact solution Gamma_eps of (i); it required the exterior part A_out as a separate quantity, the global form of the profile hypothesis in the exclusion of (h)(ii), a stopping convention for the single-visit estimate, the range 0 < T < s, the axial centre z(t) in the affine identity, the scope of the strain and thin-peak examples, and the scale and uniformity hypotheses of the scaling consequence of (i); these repairs are applied, and the author rederived each of them (the affine identity again by symbolic computation). Items (h) and (i) do not establish the uniform bound J_M = o(s^{-3/2}) and do not exclude the Type I limit configuration.


Proposition 38 (a circulation barrier in similarity variables; Type I inflow on circulation superlevel sets). Let nu > 0 and let U be a bounded smooth axisymmetric solution of the Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity nu on R^3 x (-infinity, 0], with circulation Gamma = R U^theta, |Gamma| <= G. No decay, integrability, mildness or pressure hypothesis is used in (a). Let tau_* > 0, C >= 0, theta in [0, 1/2) and lambda in [0, G). For rho > 0 put m(rho) := rho^{-1} exp((C rho - (1 - 2 theta) rho^2/4)/nu) and
 F(rho) := int_0^rho (nu m(r))^{-1} (int_r^infinity m(s) ds) dr.
F is finite, continuous and increasing on [0, infinity), F(0) = 0, and F(rho) ~ (1/2 - theta)^{-1} log rho as rho -> infinity.
(a) Suppose that
 U^R(x, tau) >= -C (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} - theta R (tau_* - tau)^{-1}   at every point (x, tau), tau <= 0, with |Gamma(x, tau)| > lambda.   (38.1)
Then |Gamma| <= lambda on R^3 x (-infinity, 0]. Quantitatively: if tau_0 <= 0, T > 0 and (38.1) holds at the points of {|Gamma| > lambda} with tau_0 - T <= tau <= tau_0, then for every x
 |Gamma(x, tau_0)| <= lambda + (G - lambda) F(R (tau_* - tau_0)^{-1/2}) / log(1 + T/(tau_* - tau_0)).   (38.2)
(b) If (38.1) holds with lambda = 0 and U is mild, then U is a constant axial field b e_Z; if in addition sup_x |U(x, tau)| -> 0 along some sequence tau -> -infinity, then U = 0. In particular a bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solution with bounded circulation and |U(x, tau)| <= C (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} vanishes; only the one-sided bound for U^R enters, and no spatial decay or bound on scale-invariant quantities is needed.
(c) (Case-1 limits.) Let U be a Case-1 limit as in sec. 1.1 (viscosity nu_* = 1/gamma_*, |Gamma_U| <= G/gamma_*, U^theta(e_1, 0) = 1), on either branch of Proposition 33(c). For every lambda in [0, 1), C >= 0 and theta in [0, 1/2) there are s_j -> infinity and points x_j with |Gamma_U(x_j, -s_j)| > lambda and
 U^R(x_j, -s_j) < -C s_j^{-1/2} - theta R_j/s_j,  in particular  (U^R/R)^-(x_j, -s_j) > theta/s_j  and  (U^R)^-(x_j, -s_j) > C s_j^{-1/2}.
On the Type I swirl branch, for lambda in (0, 1), R_j >= rho_lambda(-s_j), with rho_lambda as in Proposition 34(d)(iii) (for lambda = 0 the bound is trivial). The kinematic family of Remark (3) after Proposition 37 satisfies these necessary conditions (for alpha > 1/2: at the points with Z = 0 and (1 + |tau|)^{1/2} << R <= (1 + |tau|)^{3/4} the cutoff of the family equals 1 and its circulation tends to its supremum, which is at least 1 > lambda, and there its inflow alpha R/(1 + |tau|) exceeds C |tau|^{-1/2} + theta R/|tau| for large |tau|; the inflow formula does not hold on the whole superlevel set, which also contains points outside the support of the meridional field), so they do not by themselves exclude the branch; an exclusion by (a) needs the bound (38.1) for the limit, which was not derived.
(d) (Time-integrated form.) In the setting of (a) put, for tau <= 0 and a := tau_* - tau,
 k(tau) := sup{ a ((U^R)^-(x, tau) - C a^{-1/2})^+ / R : |Gamma(x, tau)| > lambda }   (sup of the empty set := 0),
the least theta' >= 0 for which (38.1) holds at time tau with theta' in place of theta. Then k is lower semicontinuous with values in [0, infinity], M_{C,theta} := sup_{rho > 0} rho F'(rho) is finite, and for tau_0 <= 0, T > 0, a_0 := tau_* - tau_0 and every x
 |Gamma(x, tau_0)| <= lambda + (G - lambda) [F(R a_0^{-1/2}) + M_{C,theta} int_{tau_0 - T}^{tau_0} (k(tau) - theta)^+ d tau/(tau_* - tau)] / log(1 + T/a_0).   (38.3)
No inflow bound is assumed; (38.2) is the case k <= theta. For C = 0, rho F'(rho) = beta^{-1} x e^x E_1(x) with beta := 1/2 - theta and x := beta rho^2/(2 nu), so M_{0,theta} = 2/(1 - 2 theta); for C > 0, M_{C,theta} grows rapidly with C (numerically about 2.65, 9.97 and 349 for nu = 1, theta = 0 and C = 1, 2, 3). For a Case-1 limit (x = e_1, tau_0 = 0, nu = nu_*, G/gamma_* in place of G), (38.3) gives, for every tau_* > 0, lambda in [0, 1), C >= 0, theta in [0, 1/2) and T > 0,
 int_{-T}^0 (k(tau) - theta)^+ d tau/(tau_* - tau) >= (1 - lambda) log(1 + T/tau_*) / ((G/gamma_* - lambda) M_{C,theta}) - F(tau_*^{-1/2})/M_{C,theta}:   (38.4)
in particular liminf_{T -> infinity} (log T)^{-1} int_{-T}^0 (k - theta)^+ d tau/(tau_* - tau) >= (1 - lambda)/((G/gamma_* - lambda) M_{C,theta}) > 0, that is, the spatial supremum over the superlevel set {|Gamma_U| > lambda} of the normalized excess (tau_* - tau) [(U^R/R)^- - C R^{-1} (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} - theta (tau_* - tau)^{-1}]^+ has a positive lower average in logarithmic time, which strengthens (c). This is an average statement; it does not by itself give a positive logarithmic density of the set of times at which the excess is positive. For C = 0, a logarithmic lower bound of the same form follows from (34.3), with the larger coefficient 1/2 - theta of log T, since then k = (tau_* - tau) kappa_lambda and int_{-T}^0 (k - theta)^+ d tau/(tau_* - tau) >= int_{-T}^0 kappa_lambda d tau - theta log(1 + T/tau_*). The new content relative to this comparison is the allowance C. On the Type I swirl branch, let 0 < lambda < 1 and D := C (C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}/lambda. Since the parameter tau_* of Proposition 34(d)(iii) is nonnegative, that proposition places the superlevel set at time tau < 0 in R > lambda (gamma_*/C_I)^{1/2} |tau|^{1/2}; hence, for the parameter tau_* > 0 of (38.4) and tau <= -1, (k(tau) - theta)^+/(tau_* - tau) >= kappa_lambda(tau) - theta/(tau_* - tau) - D ((tau_* - tau) |tau|)^{-1/2}. For T >= 1 the integrals of the last two terms over [-T, -1] are at most (theta + D) log T, and kappa_lambda is bounded, so (34.3) gives a logarithmic lower bound of the same form, with coefficient 1/2 - theta - C (C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}/lambda of log T, whenever this is positive; for larger C this comparison gives no positive logarithmic coefficient. Without the Type I swirl hypothesis (the alternatives of Proposition 33(c) are not exclusive) it gives none for any C > 0: the bound |Gamma_U| <= R ||U||_infty places the superlevel set only in R > lambda/||U||_infty, which leaves a negative term of order T^{1/2}. Like (c), (38.4) is a necessary condition only.
(e) (Localization.) In the setting of (a) put K := ||U||_infty, let tau_0 <= 0 and tau_* > tau_0 (in (e) tau_* need not be positive), T > 0, a_0 := tau_* - tau_0, S := log(1 + T/a_0), A >= K + nu and c >= 0, and let Omega be the set of (x, tau) with tau_0 - T <= tau <= tau_0 and max{R, |Z|} < A (c + tau_0 - tau). If (38.1) holds at the points of Omega with |Gamma| > lambda, then for every x
 |Gamma(x, tau_0)| <= lambda + (G - lambda) F(R a_0^{-1/2})/S + G (e^{R - A c} + e^{Z - A c} + e^{-Z - A c}).   (38.5)
So the circulation at time tau_0 is controlled by the inflow inside a backward cone of speed A, up to an error exponentially small in A c. For a Case-1 limit (nu = nu_*, G' := G/gamma_*, K := ||U||_infty), for every lambda in [0, 1), C >= 0, theta in [0, 1/2) and p > p_* := 1 + (G' - lambda)/((1 - 2 theta)(1 - lambda)) there is T_1 such that for every T_0 >= T_1 there is a point (x, -s) with
 T_0 <= s <= T_0^p,   max{R, |Z|} < 2 (K + nu_*) s,   |Gamma_U(x, -s)| > lambda,   U^R(x, -s) < -C s^{-1/2} - theta R/s.   (38.6)
This localizes (c) in space, to the Euler cone max{R, |Z|} < 2 (K + nu_*) s, and in time, to every window [T_0, T_0^p] of polynomial length; p_* does not depend on C, and (38.6) holds on both branches of Proposition 33(c).

Proof. (a) Put a := tau_* - tau, sigma := -log a, rho := R a^{-1/2}, zeta := Z a^{-1/2} and g(rho, zeta, sigma) := Gamma(a^{1/2} rho, a^{1/2} zeta, tau_* - a), B^R := a^{1/2} U^R, B^Z := a^{1/2} U^Z at the corresponding point. Since d tau/d sigma = a and d a^{1/2}/d sigma = -a^{1/2}/2, the circulation equation Gamma_tau + U^R Gamma_R + U^Z Gamma_Z = nu (Gamma_RR - R^{-1} Gamma_R + Gamma_ZZ) becomes
 d_sigma g = calM g,  calM := nu (d_rhorho - rho^{-1} d_rho + d_zetazeta) - (B^R + rho/2) d_rho - (B^Z + zeta/2) d_zeta,
and (38.1) reads -B^R <= C + theta rho on {|g| > lambda}. Put f := F'. By definition (m f)' = -m/nu, that is nu f' + (C + theta rho - rho/2 - nu/rho) f = -1, and f > 0. As rho -> 0, int_rho^infinity m ~ log(1/rho) and m ~ 1/rho, so f(rho) ~ (rho/nu) log(1/rho) and F(0) = 0; as rho -> infinity, l'Hopital's rule applied to int_rho^infinity m and 2 nu m/((1 - 2 theta) rho) gives f(rho) ~ ((1/2 - theta) rho)^{-1}, so F(rho) -> infinity logarithmically. Hence, on {|g| > lambda},
 calM F = nu f' - (B^R + rho/2 + nu/rho) f <= nu f' + (C + theta rho - rho/2 - nu/rho) f = -1.
Fix sigma_0 <= -log tau_*, S > 0 and sigma_1 := sigma_0 - S, so that [sigma_1, sigma_0] corresponds to [tau_0 - T, tau_0] with S = log(1 + T/(tau_* - tau_0)). On this window a <= e^{-sigma_1}, so |B^Z| <= b_S := ||U||_infty e^{-sigma_1/2} and |g| <= ||U||_infty e^{-sigma_1/2} rho. With P(zeta) := 1 + zeta^2 one has calM P = 2 nu - 2 B^Z zeta - zeta^2 <= 2 nu + b_S^2; put kappa := 2 nu + b_S^2 + 1. Fix a point (rho_0, zeta_0), choose L > rho_0 with F(L) >= S, eps > 0, Z_eps > |zeta_0| with eps (1 + Z_eps^2) >= G, delta in (0, rho_0), and let
 H := lambda + ((G - lambda)/S)(F(rho) + sigma_0 - sigma) + eps e^{kappa (sigma - sigma_1)} P(zeta) + ||U||_infty e^{-sigma_1/2} delta.
Then (d_sigma - calM) H >= (G - lambda)/S (-1 - calM F) + eps e^{kappa (sigma - sigma_1)} (kappa P - calM P) >= 0 on {|g| > lambda}. Let D be the set of (rho, zeta, sigma) with delta < rho < L, |zeta| < Z_eps, sigma_1 < sigma <= sigma_0 and g > lambda. The coefficients of calM are smooth and bounded on the closure of D, calM is uniformly parabolic there, and (d_sigma - calM)(g - H) <= 0 in D. On the parabolic boundary of D one has g - H <= 0: where g = lambda (H >= lambda); at sigma = sigma_1 and at rho = L, where H >= G >= g; at |zeta| = Z_eps, where the eps term is at least G; and at rho = delta, where g <= ||U||_infty e^{-sigma_1/2} delta. The weak maximum principle gives g <= H on D, and g <= lambda <= H outside D. The same argument applies to -g on {g < -lambda}. At (rho_0, zeta_0, sigma_0), letting eps -> 0 and delta -> 0 for fixed S gives |g| <= lambda + (G - lambda) F(rho_0)/S, which is (38.2). If (38.1) holds for all tau <= 0, S is arbitrary, and S -> infinity gives |Gamma| <= lambda.
(b) By (a), Gamma = 0. A bounded weak ancient axisymmetric solution without swirl has the form b(tau) e_Z [KNSS, Theorem 5.2] (stated for viscosity 1; apply it to nu^{-1} U(x, tau/nu)). For a spatially constant field the nonlinear term of the mild formula vanishes and the heat semigroup preserves constants, so b(tau_2) = b(tau_1) for tau_1 < tau_2 <= 0, and b = 0 under the stated decay.
(c) Suppose that for some lambda in [0, 1), C >= 0, theta in [0, 1/2) and s_0 > 0 the inequality U^R >= -C s^{-1/2} - theta R/s (s = -tau) holds at every point of {|Gamma_U| > lambda} with tau <= -s_0. Enlarging s_0 we may assume theta' := theta (1 + 1/s_0) < 1/2. With tau_* := 1, for s >= s_0 one has C s^{-1/2} <= C (1 + 1/s_0)^{1/2} (1 + s)^{-1/2} and theta R/s <= theta' R/(1 + s), and for -s_0 <= tau <= 0 one has U^R >= -||U||_infty >= -||U||_infty (1 + s_0)^{1/2} (1 + s)^{-1/2}. So (38.1) holds for U with tau_* = 1, theta', nu = nu_*, G/gamma_* in place of G, and C' := max{C (1 + 1/s_0)^{1/2}, ||U||_infty (1 + s_0)^{1/2}}, and (a) gives |Gamma_U| <= lambda < 1, contradicting Gamma_U(e_1, 0) = U^theta(e_1, 0) = 1. The two consequences follow by dividing by R_j and since theta R_j/s_j >= 0. On the Type I swirl branch |Gamma_U| <= R |U^theta| gives R_j >= rho_lambda(-s_j) as in Proposition 34(d). For the kinematic family write ell := 1 + |tau| (its s). Its radial velocity is U^R = -(alpha R/ell)(chi + 2 Z^2 chi'/ell^{3/2}) with chi evaluated at (R^2 + Z^2)/ell^{3/2}, so U^R = -alpha R/ell on the ball R^2 + Z^2 <= ell^{3/2}. At the points Z = 0, R = ell^{5/8} its circulation A g(R^2/(c ell)) tends to A >= 1 > lambda, and (alpha |tau|/ell - theta) R |tau|^{-1/2} -> infinity when alpha > theta, so that alpha R/ell > C |tau|^{-1/2} + theta R/|tau| for large |tau|. At Z = 0, R = 3 ell^{3/4} the meridional field vanishes while the circulation is still close to A, so the inflow bound fails only on part of the superlevel set.
(d) If |Gamma(x, tau)| > lambda, the same holds near (x, tau), and there R > 0 (Gamma vanishes on the axis) and a ((U^R)^- - C a^{-1/2})^+/R is continuous; a supremum of such functions over an open set is lower semicontinuous in tau. As rho -> 0, rho f(rho) ~ (rho^2/nu) log(1/rho) -> 0, and rho f(rho) -> 1/beta as rho -> infinity, so M := M_{C,theta} < infinity. For C = 0, int_rho^infinity m = E_1(x)/2 gives the formula for rho f, and x e^x E_1(x) increases from 0 to 1. Assume that the integral in (38.3) is finite (otherwise there is nothing to prove) and keep the notation of the proof of (a); in similarity variables k = sup{((B^R)^- - C)^+/rho : |g| > lambda} at time sigma, and d tau/(tau_* - tau) = d sigma. Replace sigma_0 - sigma in H by
 A(sigma) := sigma_0 - sigma + M int_{sigma_1}^{sigma} (k - theta)^+ d sigma',
which is absolutely continuous, satisfies A(sigma_1) = S and A >= sigma_0 - sigma >= 0 on [sigma_1, sigma_0], and equals M int_{sigma_1}^{sigma_0} (k - theta)^+ d sigma at sigma_0. The boundary comparison of (a) uses only A(sigma_1) = S and A >= 0, so it is unchanged, and with eps (1 + Z_eps^2) > G one has g < H on the whole parabolic boundary of D. Since H is only absolutely continuous in sigma, the weak maximum principle is replaced by a first-contact argument. Suppose g >= H somewhere on the closure of D (a compact set on which g - H is continuous), let sigma_* be the least sigma at which this happens and (rho_*, zeta_*) a point where it happens at sigma_*. This point is not on the parabolic boundary, so it lies in D; hence g < H at (rho_*, zeta_*, sigma) for sigma in some interval (sigma_* - h_0, sigma_*), and, by the same reasoning at the other points of D at time sigma_*, g - H attains at (rho_*, zeta_*) its spatial maximum 0 over D at time sigma_*. The function kappa_*(sigma) := ((-B^R(rho_*, zeta_*, sigma) - C)/rho_*)^+ is continuous, and k >= kappa_* near sigma_* because |g(rho_*, zeta_*, sigma)| > lambda there. Hence liminf_{h -> 0+} h^{-1} (A(sigma_*) - A(sigma_* - h)) >= -1 + M (kappa_*(sigma_*) - theta)^+, and, since -B^R <= C + kappa_* rho_* at the point,
 calM F <= nu f' + (C + kappa_* rho_* - rho_*/2 - nu/rho_*) f = -1 + (kappa_* - theta) rho_* f <= -1 + M (kappa_*(sigma_*) - theta)^+.
At the contact point d_sigma g >= liminf_{h -> 0+} h^{-1} (H(sigma_*) - H(sigma_* - h)) and calM g <= calM H, so
 0 = d_sigma g - calM g >= ((G - lambda)/S) (-1 + M (kappa_*(sigma_*) - theta)^+ - calM F) + eps e^{kappa (sigma_* - sigma_1)} (kappa P - calM P) >= eps e^{kappa (sigma_* - sigma_1)} > 0,
a contradiction. So g < H on D, and the same holds for -g on {g < -lambda}; letting eps -> 0 and delta -> 0 at (rho_0, zeta_0, sigma_0) gives (38.3). For a Case-1 limit, (38.3) at x = e_1, tau_0 = 0, with nu_* and G/gamma_* >= |Gamma_U(e_1, 0)| = 1 > lambda, rearranges to (38.4).
(e) Put l(tau) := c + tau_0 - tau and calP := d_tau + U^R d_R + U^Z d_Z - nu (d_RR - R^{-1} d_R + d_ZZ), so that calP Gamma = 0. For phi(x, tau) = psi(R a^{-1/2}, Z a^{-1/2}, -log a), a := tau_* - tau, the change of variables in the proof of (a) gives a calP phi = (d_sigma - calM) psi (this uses only a > 0). Hence h := lambda + ((G - lambda)/S)(F(R a^{-1/2}) + log(a/a_0)) satisfies a calP h = ((G - lambda)/S)(-1 - calM F) >= 0 at the points with R > 0 where (38.1) holds. The functions W_1 := G e^{R - A l}, W_+ := G e^{Z - A l} and W_- := G e^{-Z - A l} satisfy calP W_1 = (A + U^R - nu + nu/R) W_1 >= 0 and calP W_+- = (A +- U^Z - nu) W_+- >= 0, since A >= K + nu. Fix x_0 with R_{x_0} > 0 (Gamma vanishes on the axis), eps > 0 and delta in (0, R_{x_0}), and put
 H := h + W_1 + W_+ + W_- + K delta + eps (1 + tau - tau_0 + T),
so that calP H >= eps at the points of Omega with R > 0 where (38.1) holds. Let D be the set of (x, tau) in Omega with tau > tau_0 - T, R > delta and Gamma > lambda, and call parabolic boundary of D the set of points of its closure at which tau = tau_0 - T, max{R, |Z|} = A l, R = delta or Gamma = lambda. D is bounded, and Gamma < H on the parabolic boundary: all terms of H are nonnegative (F >= 0 and a >= a_0); at tau = tau_0 - T one has h >= G; where max{R, |Z|} = A l one of W_1, W_+, W_- is at least G; at R = delta, Gamma <= R |U^theta| <= K delta; where Gamma = lambda, H > lambda. A point of the closure of D outside the parabolic boundary lies in D, together with all nearby points (y, tau') with tau' <= tau, since the conditions defining D other than tau' <= tau_0 are open. Suppose Gamma >= H somewhere on the closure of D (a compact set on which Gamma - H is continuous), let tau_1 be the least time at which this happens and x_1 a point where it happens at tau_1. Then (x_1, tau_1) is in D, Gamma - H < 0 at (y, tau) for tau < tau_1 and (y, tau) in the closure of D, so Gamma - H <= 0 on a neighbourhood of x_1 at time tau_1, with equality at x_1. Hence d_tau (Gamma - H) >= 0, d_R (Gamma - H) = d_Z (Gamma - H) = 0 and d_RR (Gamma - H), d_ZZ (Gamma - H) <= 0 at (x_1, tau_1), so calP(Gamma - H) >= 0 there, while calP(Gamma - H) = -calP H <= -eps, since (38.1) holds at this point of Omega with |Gamma| > lambda. So Gamma < H on D, and Gamma <= lambda < H at the other points of Omega with R > delta. If max{R_{x_0}, |Z_{x_0}|} < A c, then (x_0, tau_0) is in Omega, and letting eps and delta tend to 0 gives (38.5) for Gamma; otherwise one of the exponentials in (38.5) is at least 1 and (38.5) holds since |Gamma| <= G. The same argument applies to -Gamma on {Gamma < -lambda}.
Case-1 limits. Put K' := K + nu_*, fix lambda, C, theta and p > p_*, and fix eps in (0, 1/8) with 1 - 4 eps > lambda + (G' - lambda)/((p - 1)(1 - 2 theta)), which is possible since p > p_* (with tau_* := 0 below, F is the function of (a) with nu = nu_*). Backward localization. For T_0 > 0 put Z_1 := K' T_0 + log(3 G'/eps), let B be the set of x with R < 1 + Z_1 and |Z| < Z_1, and m := max{0, sup{Gamma_U(x, -T_0) : x in B}}. For delta in (0, 1) and eps' > 0 put
 H_1 := m + G' e^{K' (tau + T_0)} (e^{R - 1 - Z_1} + e^{Z - Z_1} + e^{-Z - Z_1}) + K delta + eps' (1 + tau + T_0).
Since calP e^{K' (tau + T_0) + R} = (K + U^R + nu_*/R) e^{K' (tau + T_0) + R} >= 0 and calP e^{K' (tau + T_0) +- Z} = (K +- U^Z) e^{K' (tau + T_0) +- Z} >= 0, one has calP H_1 >= eps' for R > 0. On the cylinder {delta < R < 1 + Z_1, |Z| < Z_1} x [-T_0, 0] one has Gamma_U < H_1 at tau = -T_0 (where Gamma_U <= m), on the lateral boundary (where one exponential term is at least G') and at R = delta (where Gamma_U <= K delta), so the first-contact argument above, without a superlevel set, gives Gamma_U < H_1 on the cylinder. At (e_1, 0) this gives 1 < m + 3 G' e^{K' T_0 - Z_1} + K delta + eps' (1 + T_0) = m + eps + K delta + eps' (1 + T_0), so m >= 1 - eps > 0, and there is y_0 = (R_0, Z_0) in B with Gamma_U(y_0, -T_0) > 1 - 2 eps. Window. Suppose that (38.6) has no solution for some T_0 > 1. Then, with tau_* := 0 (so a = s), (38.1) holds at the points with |Gamma_U| > lambda of the set Omega of (e) for tau_0 := -T_0, T := T_0^p - T_0, A := 2 K' and c := T_0, since Omega is the set of (x, -s) with T_0 <= s <= T_0^p and max{R, |Z|} < 2 K' s. Here a_0 = T_0 and S = (p - 1) log T_0, and (38.5) at y_0 gives
 1 - 2 eps < lambda + (G' - lambda) F(R_0 T_0^{-1/2})/((p - 1) log T_0) + G' (e^{R_0 - 2 K' T_0} + e^{Z_0 - 2 K' T_0} + e^{-Z_0 - 2 K' T_0}).
As R_0, |Z_0| < 1 + Z_1, the last term is at most 9 e G'^2 eps^{-1} e^{-K' T_0}, which tends to 0 as T_0 -> infinity; as F is increasing and F(rho) ~ (1/2 - theta)^{-1} log rho, F(R_0 T_0^{-1/2}) <= F((1 + Z_1) T_0^{-1/2}) = (1 + o(1)) (1 - 2 theta)^{-1} log T_0. So the limsup as T_0 -> infinity of the right side is at most lambda + (G' - lambda)/((p - 1)(1 - 2 theta)) < 1 - 4 eps (R_0 depends on T_0, and only the upper bound for F(R_0 T_0^{-1/2}) is used), and there is T_1 such that the displayed inequality fails for every T_0 >= T_1; for these T_0, (38.6) has a solution.

Remark. (1) (a) is the ancient form, with a superlevel-set localization and a linear allowance theta R/(tau_* - tau), of the constant-envelope criterion [QZ, Theorem 1.1] for singular solutions (used in Remark (1) after Proposition 36). In similarity variables the drift -rho/2 dominates a Type I inflow at large normalized radius, and the operator d_rhorho - rho^{-1} d_rho, the generator of a Bessel process of dimension zero absorbed at the axis (as in Proposition 31), removes the circulation over the unbounded logarithmic time of an ancient solution. The Burgers comparison of Propositions 33 and 34(b), (c) removes the circulation above lambda when Pi_lambda = int_0^infinity exp(-2 int_{-v}^0 kappa_lambda) dv is infinite, a condition on the time-integrated compression at the critical rate 1/(2|tau|) that allows some logarithmic excess (for instance int_{-v}^0 kappa_lambda = (1/2) log v + (1/2) log log v + O(1)). In physical variables (38.1) bounds the compression by (U^R/R)^- <= C R^{-1} (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} + theta (tau_* - tau)^{-1}, so it allows any compression C/(R (tau_* - tau)^{1/2}) near the parabolic radius, at the price of the strict bound theta < 1/2 for the remaining part; replacing tau_* - tau by |tau| is an asymptotic description.
(2) By (b), the full Type I bound |U(tau)| <= min{K, C |tau|^{-1/2}} discussed in Remark (4) after Proposition 37 would exclude the Type I swirl limits; the bound I < infinity of [AB] is not needed for this axisymmetric conclusion with bounded circulation, and only the one-sided bound for U^R on the circulation superlevel sets is used. In particular, let V be a smooth bounded axisymmetric vector field on R^3 with sup rho |V^theta(xi)| < infinity (rho the distance of xi to the axis), and suppose that U(x, tau) := (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} V(x (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2}) is a mild solution on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] (a backward self-similar solution). Then V = 0: U is bounded with |U| <= ||V||_infty (tau_* - tau)^{-1/2} and |Gamma_U| <= sup rho |V^theta|, so (b) applies with lambda = theta = 0 and C = ||V||_infty. No integrability or decay of the meridional part of V is assumed.
(3) (Growing envelopes; the endpoint theta = 1/2.) (38.2) can be used with a frozen envelope. Suppose that U^R >= -C(a) a^{-1/2} - theta R/a, a = tau_* - tau, on {|Gamma| > lambda}, with C >= 0 locally bounded, and for the window ending at tau_0 = tau_* - a_0 put C_S := sup{C(a) : a_0 <= a <= a_0 e^S}. Then |Gamma(x, tau_0)| <= lambda + (G - lambda) F_{C_S, theta}(R a_0^{-1/2})/S, where F_{C, theta} is the function F with constants C and theta. For fixed rho > 0, F_{C, theta}(rho) ~ nu^{3/2} (2 pi beta)^{1/2} C^{-3} exp(C^2/(2 beta nu)) as C -> infinity, beta := 1/2 - theta (Laplace's method: the outer integral int_0^rho (nu m)^{-1} is asymptotic to nu/C^2 and the inner mass int m concentrates near s = C/beta). Hence |Gamma| <= lambda as in (a) whenever exp(C_S^2/((1 - 2 theta) nu))/((1 + C_S)^3 S) -> 0 as S -> infinity, for example when C(a)^2 <= (1 - 2 theta) nu log log a + O(1) for large a. For C = 0 the endpoint theta = 1/2 is allowed: lambda + (G - lambda)(1 - exp(-rho^2/(4 nu (sigma - sigma_1)))) solves the radial equation without drift, is increasing in rho and is a supersolution where -B^R <= rho/2; the comparison of (a), with the outer-boundary error (G - lambda) exp(-L^2/(4 nu S)) removed by L -> infinity, gives |Gamma(x, tau_0)| <= lambda + (G - lambda)(1 - exp(-R^2/(4 nu (tau_* - tau_0) S))). This endpoint case is also covered by the Burgers comparison of Proposition 34(c)(i).
(4) (The threshold 1/2 and the model of the Type I strain sub-branch.) For theta > 1/2, A > 0, nu > 0 and tau_* > 0 put a := tau_* - tau, b := (2 theta - 1)/(4 nu) and U^R = -theta R/a, U^Z = 2 theta Z/a, Gamma = A (1 - exp(-b R^2/a)), with pressure P = theta (1 - theta) R^2/(2 a^2) - theta (1 + 2 theta) Z^2/a^2 + int_0^R Gamma(s, tau)^2 s^{-3} ds. This collapsing Burgers vortex is a smooth solution of the Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity nu on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] (checked by a symbolic computation; the meridional field is a linear strain, Gamma = (A b/a) R^2 + O(R^4) at the axis, and for Gamma = g(R^2/a) the circulation equation reduces to 4 nu g'' = (1 - 2 theta) g', whose bounded nonconstant solutions with g(0) = 0 exist only for theta > 1/2). Its circulation is bounded by A; with x := b R^2/a one has |U^theta|^2 = (A^2 b/a)(1 - e^{-x})^2/x <= mu_0 A^2 b/a, where mu_0 := max_{x > 0} (1 - e^{-x})^2/x = 4 x_0/(1 + 2 x_0)^2 = 0.40726... and x_0 = 1.25643... is the positive root of e^x = 1 + 2 x; (U^R/R)^- = theta/a everywhere, Gamma is not identically 0, and, for 0 <= lambda < A and every C >= 0, (38.1) on {|Gamma| > lambda} holds with theta' in place of theta exactly when theta' >= theta (the set contains all large R, where a (U^R)^-/R = theta), in particular for no theta' < 1/2. Its meridional field is unbounded, so it is not a counterexample to (a); it rules out an extension of (a) that both drops the boundedness of U and permits an allowance theta > 1/2. It does not settle the endpoint theta = 1/2 (for C = 0 see Remark (3)). For nu = nu_*, A = G/gamma_* and theta = C_a its circulation is the right side of (33.4). The point normalization Gamma(e_1, 0) = 1 holds exactly when A > 1 and tau_* = b/log(A/(A - 1)); this alone does not give the normalization of the Case-1 limits (|U^theta| <= 1 = U^theta(e_1, 0) and -gamma_* U^R(e_1, 0) >= 1): for A = 2 and b/tau_* = log 2 one has U^theta(e_1, 0) = 1 but d_R U^theta(e_1, 0) = 2 log 2 - 1 > 0. The full normalization holds for b/tau_* = x_0 and A = (1 - e^{-x_0})^{-1} = 1.39795...: then max |U^theta| over space and time is attained at (e_1, 0), and for nu = nu_* one has -gamma_* U^R(e_1, 0) = gamma_* theta/tau_* = 4 theta x_0/(2 theta - 1) > 1, that is tau_* < theta gamma_*, as Proposition 33(e)(ii) requires; with this A the circulation is at most the right side of (33.4) whenever G/gamma_* >= A. In all cases it has Type I swirl and the global compression bound of Proposition 33(e)(ii), and, when A >= 1, it satisfies (c) (take R = D s^{1/2} with D large). With the same tau_* in (38.4) and A > 1 it satisfies (38.4) for every T > 0: here k = theta for every C >= 0 and lambda < A, so with theta' < 1/2 the allowance in (38.4) the left side is (theta - theta') log(1 + T/tau_*), while the coefficient of log(1 + T/tau_*) on the right is at most 1/2 - theta', since (1 - lambda)/(A - lambda) <= 1 and M_{C,theta'} >= M_{0,theta'} = (1/2 - theta')^{-1} (rho F'(rho) is nondecreasing in C). Its velocity gradient is bounded (by a constant depending on theta, A, nu and tau_*), but its velocity is not. So the equations and the bounds it shares with the Type I strain sub-branch do not alone exclude that sub-branch: an exclusion must use a property that this example does not have, the bound |U| <= K being one. Inside the ball R^2 + Z^2 <= s^{3/2}, s = 1 + |tau|, the stream-potential construction of Proposition 37, Remark (3), with tau_* = 1, alpha = theta, c = 4 nu_*/(2 theta - 1) and its profile replaced by g(y) = 1 - e^{-y} (which is only asymptotic to y at 0), coincides with this solution; outside the ball it is not a solution. Four further facts concern the missing information. First, on the Type I swirl branch the meridional vorticity of the limit is produced entirely by the swirl: the eta equation is a drift-diffusion equation in R^5 with bounded smooth drift and source d_Z(q_U^2), so ||eta_U(tau)||_infty <= ||eta_U(tau')||_infty + int_{tau'}^{tau} ||d_Z(q_U^2)(s)||_infty ds for tau' < tau (comparison with the barrier eps e^{M(s - tau')} (1 + |y|^2)^{1/2}, M > ||b_5||_infty + 5 nu, on expanding balls, then eps -> 0; no spatial decay and no divergence condition on the 5D drift are needed), and (34.6) lets tau' tend to -infinity (the right side may then be infinite). In particular, if d_Z(q_U^2) = 0 then eta_U = 0, and a bounded divergence-free meridional field without vorticity is constant, so its radial component vanishes: the strain of a bounded limit cannot be the vorticity-free strain of the collapsing Burgers vortex, whose swirl does not depend on Z; it has to be produced by vorticity created where the swirl varies along the axis. No quantitative localization of that vorticity follows. Second, consider the drift-free linear response, assuming convergence of the heat-history integral Q(tau) := int_{-infinity}^{tau} e^{nu (tau - s) Delta_5} q^2(s) ds (on the Type I strain sub-branch (33.4) gives ||q(s)||_infty = O((tau_* + |s|)^{-1}), so Q converges in L^infty) and choosing the Newton potential with no added harmonic term. Then eta = d_Z Q solves d_tau eta = nu Delta_5 eta + d_Z(q^2), and the strain is U^R/R = -phi_Z = d_ZZ Delta_5^{-1} Q =: T Q. The Fourier symbol of T is xi_Z^2/|xi|^2, so int (U^R/R) Q dmu_5 >= 0 for Q in L^2(R^5) by Plancherel's identity; but this sign is not local. Away from the origin the kernel of T is c (3 |x|^{-5} - 15 Z^2 |x|^{-7}) with c = 1/(8 pi^2) (the full distributional kernel also contains delta_0/5), which equals -12 c d^{-5} at the point of the axis at distance d, so a swirl history Q concentrated near the axis at axial distance d induces inflow at the origin. For the Gaussian weight w = exp(-|y|^2) take Q_d = f + d^6 f(. - d e_5), with f a fixed nonnegative smooth radial bump supported in the unit ball: the cross term int w f T(d^6 f(. - d e_5)) is negative of order d, the other cross term is negative, the first self term is bounded and the distant weighted self term is O(d^{12} e^{-(d - 1)^2}), so int w Q_d T Q_d < 0 for large d; short nonnegative source pulses approximate these Q_d, so the heat-history form does not remove the example. Bounded circulation alone does not ensure convergence of the unweighted pairing; spatial and temporal integrability must be checked separately (an axially periodic source with a nonzero axial mode gives a nonconvergent whole-space pairing). Third, the axial Galilean transformations U_c(R, Z, tau) := U(R, Z - c tau, tau) + c e_Z preserve the listed properties of the normalized ancient limit (equations, mildness, circulation, swirl and compression bounds, normalization), with K replaced by K + |c|, without asserting realization by the same finite-energy trajectory; so a Type I estimate for U^Z must specify the Galilean frame (no estimate modulo a constant is established here), while the radial component is translated in Z, so its spatial bounds and the hypothesis of (a) are invariant. Fourth, local information does not determine the strain. Let chi be smooth and nonincreasing on [0, infinity), equal to 1 on [0, 1] and to 0 on [4, infinity), let 1/2 < p < 1, ell := ell_0 (a/tau_*)^p, and take the stream potential phi = (theta Z/a) chi(u), u := (R^2 + Z^2)/ell^2 (so U^R = -R phi_Z, U^Z = 2 phi + R phi_R), with the circulation A (1 - exp(-b R^2/a)) of the collapsing Burgers vortex. These fields are divergence free, satisfy U^R/R = -(theta/a)(chi + 2 Z^2 ell^{-2} chi') >= -theta/a, are bounded on tau <= 0 (the meridional part by C_chi theta ell/a <= C_chi theta ell_0/tau_*), satisfy the circulation bound and, when the parameters satisfy the point normalization above, Gamma(e_1, 0) = 1 (the full record normalization needs the parameter choice above and ell_0 >= 1), coincide with the collapsing Burgers vortex on the ball |x| < ell, and have eta = -(theta Z/(a ell^2))(14 chi'(u) + 4 u chi''(u)), supported in the shell ell <= |x| <= 2 ell, with ||eta(tau)||_infty <= C_chi theta/(a ell) and ||omega^theta(tau)||_infty <= C_chi theta/a (checked by a symbolic computation). Under the blow-down U^L(y, tau) := L U(L y, L^2 tau) they converge smoothly on compact subsets of R^3 x (-infinity, 0) to the Burgers formula with a = -tau, and for every delta > 0 the blown-down eta, L^3 eta(L y, L^2 tau), tends to zero uniformly on R^5 x (-infinity, -delta] (it is O(L^{1 - 2 p})); neither statement includes tau = 0. They are not solutions: the circulation equation has the residual (2 A theta/a) x e^{-x} (1 - chi - 2 Z^2 ell^{-2} chi'), x = b R^2/a, which vanishes on the ball and equals 2 A theta/(e a), of the critical size, at Z > 2 ell, R^2 = 4 nu a/(2 theta - 1) (checked by a symbolic computation); since d_Z(q^2) = 0 for them while eta is not 0, the first fact also shows that they are not bounded ancient solutions. They show that local convergence and uniform smallness of eta on negative time intervals do not by themselves preserve the recovery of the strain from the vorticity; since they are not solutions, they do not establish a limitation on every Navier-Stokes blow-down argument.
Status: proved here. The comparison argument for (a) with lambda = theta = 0 under a two-sided Type I bound on the whole meridional velocity, and the deduction (b), were supplied by a research consultation (review 25 in sec. 5); the author rederived every step, added the one-sided, superlevel-set and theta forms, the quantitative bound (38.2) and part (c), and checked the change of variables, the equation for F' and the axial bound calM P <= 2 nu + b_S^2 by a symbolic computation and the asymptotics of F' at 0 and at infinity numerically. [KNSS, Theorem 5.2] is used as stated in the source. An independent referee of the whole proposition (review 26 in sec. 5) confirmed (a), (38.2) and (b) and required the repairs of the kinematic passage in (c) and of Remarks (1) and (3), all applied; Remark (3) in its present form is from that review, and the author checked its envelope asymptotics numerically and the endpoint supersolution by hand. Part (d) was added later: the author derived it from the proof of (a), with the first-contact argument written out, checked M_{0,theta} = 2/(1 - 2 theta) in closed form and the values of M_{C,theta} for C > 0 numerically; an independent referee (Review 27) confirmed it and supplied the corrections applied here. The consequence for backward self-similar solutions in Remark (2) was pointed out in a parallel line of work and checked by the author. Remark (4) was added by the author after that review, with the equations checked by a symbolic computation; of its four further facts, the non-local sign, the Galilean invariance and the cut-off fields were supplied by a research consultation (review 28 in sec. 5) and checked by the author by hand and by a symbolic computation. An independent referee of Remark (4) (review 29 in sec. 5) confirmed the exact solution, the constants and the four facts as computations and required qualifications of the normalization, of the blow-down statement and of the conclusions drawn from the examples, all applied; the author checked each repair. Part (e) and the consequence (38.6) were added later by the author: the identities calP W = (A + U^R - nu + nu/R) W, (A +- U^Z - nu) W for the three exponential barriers of (e), the corresponding identities for the barriers of the backward localization, and the identity a calP phi = (d_sigma - calM) psi were checked by a symbolic computation, and the first-contact arguments were written out by hand. An independent referee of (e) and (38.6) (review 37 in sec. 5) confirmed the identities, the parabolic boundary, the first-contact argument, the backward localization and the threshold p_*, and required one repair (only an upper bound for the limsup of the right side of the final inequality is proved), applied.

Proposition 39 (the vorticity behind the compression on the Type I swirl branch; conditional exclusions). Assume (K), (TAIL) and the hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(i) (the Type I swirl branch), and let U be a limit as in Proposition 37(d), so that Proposition 34(d)(iii) applies; its viscosity is nu := nu_* = 1/gamma_*, and K := ||U||_infty, G' := G/gamma_* >= sup |Gamma_U|. Write q := U^theta/R, a_U := U^R/R and eta := omega^theta_U/R, viewed as functions on R^5 through y = (y', y_5), R = |y'|, Z = y_5 (as in the proof of Proposition 34(a)), b_5 := (a_U y', U^Z) (so |b_5| <= K), P := d_sigma + b_5.grad_5 - nu Delta_5, sigma_4 := 8 pi^2/3 (the area of the unit sphere of R^5), s := |tau| and Q_1(tau) := sup_{tau - 1 <= sigma <= tau} ||q(sigma)||_infty.
(a) (Localized derivative bound and the source.) There is C_loc, depending only on nu, K, ||a_U||_infty, ||grad_5 a_U||_infty and ||grad_5 b_5||_infty, such that for all y_0 in R^5 and tau <= 0
 |grad_5 q(y_0, tau)| <= C_loc sup{ |q(y, sigma)| : |y - y_0| <= 2, tau - 1 <= sigma <= tau }.   (39.1)
Consequently |d_Z(q^2)(y, tau)| <= 2 C_loc Q_1(tau)^2 everywhere, and |d_Z(q^2)(y, tau)| <= 2 C_loc G'^2 (R - 2)^{-4} <= 162 C_loc G'^2 R^{-4} where R = |y'| >= 3.
(b) (Feynman-Kac representation.) For x in R^5 and tau <= 0 let X solve dX_u = -b_5(X_u, tau - u) du + (2 nu)^{1/2} dW_u, X_0 = x, with W a Brownian motion in R^5, and put R_u := |X_u'|. Then
 eta(x, tau) = lim_{v -> infinity} E int_0^v d_Z(q^2)(X_u, tau - u) du,   |eta(x, tau)| <= E int_0^infinity |d_Z(q^2)|(X_u, tau - u) du,   (39.2)
and, with a scalar Brownian motion B, dR_u = (-U^R(X_u, tau - u) + 3 nu/R_u) du + (2 nu)^{1/2} dB_u on every time interval on which R_u > 0.
(c) (Compression from Type I vorticity bounds.) Let s > 0, M_1 >= 1, C_omega >= 0, eps_v >= 0 and delta in (0, 1] be such that
 |omega^theta_U(y, -s)| <= C_omega/s for R_y < M_1 s^{1/2},   |omega^theta_U(y, -s)| <= eps_v (M_1 s^{1/2}/R_y)^delta/s for R_y >= M_1 s^{1/2}.   (39.3)
Then for M' >= 2 M_1, every x with R_x >= M' s^{1/2} and every L > 0
 a_U^-(x, -s) <= (3 pi/8) K/L + [ (2/3) C_omega (M_1/(M' - M_1))^3 + sigma_4^{-1} C_2(delta) (2 M_1/M')^delta eps_v ]/s,   (39.4)
where C_1(delta) := 4 pi^2 3^{3 - delta}/(3 - delta) and C_2(delta) := C_1(delta)(1 + 4/delta) + 4 sigma_4/5.
(d) (Occupation of the parabolic cylinders under exterior inflow.) Let M >= 1 and a_1 > 0, and assume
 (H2) U^R(y, sigma) <= 0 whenever sigma <= -a_1 and R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2}.
Put c := 1 - 2^{-1/2} (so 4/c^2 = 24 + 16 2^{1/2}).
 (i) If moreover A_* < infinity (Proposition 37(d)), so that, after enlarging a_1, Q_1(sigma)^2 <= C_q |sigma|^{-2} for sigma <= -a_1 with a constant C_q, then for a >= max{a_1, 9/M^2} and r := R_x >= 2 M a^{1/2}
 |eta(x, -a)| <= 2 C_loc [ M^2 C_q + 81 G'^2 (5/M^2 + (24 + 16 2^{1/2}) nu/M^4) ] r^{-2}.   (39.5)
 (ii) Suppose instead that, with constants C', C'' >= 0, for every sigma <= -a_1
 (H3) |d_Z(q^2)(y, sigma)| <= C' |sigma|^{-5/2} where R_y < M |sigma|^{1/2},   (H4) |d_Z(q^2)(y, sigma)| <= C'' R_y^{-5} where R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2}.
Then (H3) and (H4) alone give |eta(y, -a)| <= C_eta a^{-3/2} for all y and a >= a_1, with C_eta := (2/3)(C' + C'' M^{-5}), and (H2), (H3) and (H4) give, for a >= a_1 and r := R_x >= 2 M a^{1/2},
 |eta(x, -a)| <= A' r^{-3},  A' := C' [Gamma(3/2) (4 nu/c^2)^{3/2} + (16/3) M^3] + C'' [(2^{1/2} + 16/3) M^{-2} + Gamma(3/2) (4 nu/c^2)^{3/2} M^{-5}].   (39.6)
 (iii) Suppose instead (H3), and put B_theta := C_I/gamma_* (so that |U^theta(y, sigma)|^2 <= B_theta/|sigma| by Proposition 33(e)(i)) and Lambda := Gamma(3/2) (4 nu/c^2)^{3/2}. Then (H3) gives |eta(y, -a)| <= C_eta' a^{-3/2} for all y and a >= a_1, with C_eta' := (2/3) C' + 2^{1/2} G' M^{-4} (G'^2/nu + 16 B_theta)^{1/2}, and (H2) and (H3) give, for a >= a_1 and r := R_x >= 2 M a^{1/2},
 |eta(x, -a)| <= A'' r^{-3},  A'' := C' [Lambda + (16/3) M^3] + 4 G'^2 M^{-1} (1/nu + 8/M^2)^{1/2} + 2 G' M^{-4} J^{1/2} [2 (4 nu/c^2)^3 + 32 M^6]^{1/2},   (39.8)
where J := G'^2/nu + 16 B_theta (1 + (nu/(c^2 M^2)) e^{-c^2 M^2/nu}). No bound on the exterior source beyond the circulation bound, and no bound on the compression, is assumed in (iii).
(e) (Conditional exclusion.) There are no M >= 1, C' >= 0 and a_1 > 0 for which U satisfies (H2) and (H3); in particular there are no M >= 1, C', C'' >= 0 and a_1 > 0 for which U satisfies (H2), (H3) and (H4). (By (f)(v), (H2) is also incompatible with A_* < infinity.)
(f) (Type I compression on the parabolic cylinders; the Type I strain branch.) Assume A_* < infinity (Proposition 37(d)). Fix A > A_* and C_q > [F(A_*/(2 nu)) min{(C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}, G'}]^2 (F as in Proposition 37(c)), and a_1 > 0 such that a_U^-(y, sigma) <= A/|sigma| where R_y < |sigma|^{1/2}, and ||q(sigma)||_infty^2 <= C_q sigma^{-2}, for sigma <= -a_1. Put D_1 := 4 A C_q + (3/2) G'^2 + 16 nu B_theta, E_q := 4 D_1/(3 nu) + 16 B_theta/3 and C_eta'' := 2 (2 C_q E_q/3)^{1/2}.
 (i) (The Type I strain branch.) Suppose the hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(ii) holds, k(t) <= C_a/(T_* - t) on [t_a, T_*), and U is a limit along a subsequence with tau_n -> tau_* as there; the hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(i) then holds (with C_I := G^2 c(C_a)), so U is a limit as in Proposition 37(d). Then a_U^-(y, tau) <= C_a/(tau_* + |tau|) for all y and tau < 0; hence A_* <= C_a, and (ii) to (v) apply. In this case (ii) holds also with C_eta'' := (4/3) C_q (2 C_a/nu)^{1/2}, for C_q > [F(C_a/(2 nu)) min{(C_I/gamma_*)^{1/2}, G'}]^2 and a_1 as above.
 (ii) Let a >= a_1, x in R^5, and X as in (b) with tau = -a. For every bounded stopping time rho of X,
 E int_rho^infinity |d_Z(q^2)|(X_u, -a - u) du <= C_eta'' E (a + rho)^{-3/2}.   (39.10)
In particular |eta(y, -a)| <= C_eta'' a^{-3/2} for all y and a >= a_1, and, by (34.1) applied to U(-a), ||(U^R/R)(-a)||_infinity <= (2 K_U C_eta'')^{1/2} a^{-3/4} (consistent with Proposition 34(d)(ii), since a^2 C_eta'' a^{-3/2} is unbounded); at R comparable to a^{1/2} this bounds |U^R| by a multiple of a^{-1/4}, not by the size a^{-1/2} of (H2_kappa) there. No hypothesis on the source, such as (H3), is used.
 (iii) If moreover U satisfies (H2) with some M >= 1 (a_1 enlarged if necessary), then for a >= a_1 and r := R_x >= 2 M a^{1/2}
 |eta(x, -a)| <= A''' r^{-3},  A''' := 4 G'^2 M^{-1} (1/nu + 8/M^2)^{1/2} + C_eta'' [(3/2) Lambda + 8 M^3],   (39.11)
with Lambda as in (d)(iii).
 (iv) Let kappa in [0, 1) and M >= max{1, (8 nu)^{1/2}}, and suppose that (a_1 enlarged if necessary)
 (H2_kappa) U^R(y, sigma) <= kappa R_y/|sigma| whenever sigma <= -a_1 and R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2}.
Put kappa_1 := max{kappa, 1/4}, p := 3/(1 + 2 kappa_1) (in (1, 2]), p_1 := (1 + p)/2 and eps_1 := 3 (p - 1)/(8 p). Then for a >= a_1 and r := R_x >= 2 M a^{1/2}
 |eta(x, -a)| <= A_kappa r^{-p_1} a^{-(3 - p_1)/2},  A_kappa := 2 G'^2 eps_1^{-1/2} M^{p_1 - 4} (1/nu + 16/(eps_1 M^2))^{1/2} + 2^{p_1 - p} M^{p_1} C_eta''.   (39.12)
 (v) (Exclusion.) There are no M >= 1, kappa in [0, 1) and a_1 > 0 for which U satisfies (H2_kappa); in particular (kappa = 0) there are no M >= 1 and a_1 > 0 for which U satisfies (H2), and there are no M >= 1, C_d >= 0 and a_1 > 0 with U^R(y, sigma) <= C_d |sigma|^{-1/2} whenever sigma <= -a_1 and R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2} (this implies (H2_kappa) for every kappa > 0, with max{M, C_d/kappa} in place of M). Thus every limit as in Proposition 37(d) either violates (CW) of Proposition 37(e) (by (xi); then in particular A_* = infinity), or, for all M >= 1, kappa in [0, 1) and a_1 > 0, there are sigma <= -a_1 and y with R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2} and U^R(y, sigma) > kappa R_y/|sigma|. Consequently (by (i)), on a trajectory satisfying (K) and (TAIL) with k(t) <= C_a/(T_* - t) on [t_a, T_*), there are no kappa in [0, 1), M_0 >= 0 and t_b < T_* such that
 u^r(x, t) <= kappa r/(T_* - t) whenever t_b <= t < T_* and r >= M_0 (T_* - t)^{1/2};   (39.13)
in particular u^r is not nonpositive on all the regions {r >= M_0 (T_* - t)^{1/2}}, t_b <= t < T_*, for any M_0 and t_b.
 (vi) (A vorticity form.) Let M >= 1 and a_1 > 0, and let w >= 0 be a Borel function on [M, infinity) with w(xi) -> 0 as xi -> infinity and int_M^infinity w(xi) dxi/xi < infinity (this holds if sum_k sup{w(xi) : 2^k <= xi < 2^{k+1}, xi >= M} < infinity, and, for nonincreasing w, if and only if sum_k w(2^k) < infinity). Then U does not satisfy
 |omega^theta_U(y, -s)| <= s^{-1} w(R_y/s^{1/2}) whenever s >= a_1 and R_y >= M s^{1/2}.   (39.14)
By (39.12) (|omega^theta_U| = R |eta|), (H2_kappa) with M >= max{1, (8 nu)^{1/2}} implies (39.14) with 2 M in place of M, a_1 enlarged, and w(xi) := A_kappa xi^{1 - p_1} (p_1 > 1), so (vi) contains (v). (39.14) is a bound for the vorticity alone on the exterior, asking that s |omega^theta_U| decay from the parabolic radius outward at a rate that is Dini-summable in log(R/s^{1/2}); it is not implied by the bounds of (ii), which give only s |omega^theta_U(y, -s)| <= C_eta'' R_y/s^{1/2}. Without A_* < infinity the same conclusion holds if U satisfies (H3).
 (vii) (A mass form.) For s > 0 and x in R^5 with r := R_x > 0 and z := x_5, let d(R, Z) := ((R - r)^2 + (Z - z)^2)^{1/2} be the meridional distance from (r, z) and, for M >= 1 and d > 0,
 kappa_x(d, s) := int int_{d <= d(R, Z) < 2 d, R >= M s^{1/2}} |omega^theta_U(R, Z, -s)| dR dZ,   T_M(x, s) := sum_{k >= 0} d_k^{-2} kappa_x(d_k, s),  d_k := 2^{k - 1} r,
 n_x(s) := int int_{d(R, Z) < r/2} |omega^theta_U(R, Z, -s)| dR dZ,   N_x(s) := r^{-1} int int_{d(R, Z) < r/2} |omega^theta_U(R, Z, -s)| d(R, Z)^{-1} dR dZ
(masses of |omega^theta_U| in the meridional half-plane, that is unsigned circulations). Let M >= 1, a_1 > 0 and eps_1, delta >= 0 with 3 delta/8 + 3 eps_1/4 < 1/2. Then U does not satisfy
 T_M(x, s) <= eps_1/s  and  N_x(s) <= delta/s  whenever s >= a_1 and R_x >= 2 M s^{1/2}.   (39.15)
With C_0 := C_eta'' (the constant of (ii)), the second condition in (39.15) follows, with delta := 2 (3 pi C_0 eps_2/2)^{1/2}, from n_x(s) <= eps_2 R_x/s^{1/2}. (39.14) implies (39.15) with M' in place of M, for every M' >= M, with eps_1 := 32 int_{M'}^infinity w(xi) dxi/xi and delta := pi sup{w(xi) : xi >= M'} (possibly infinite for small M', since w need not be locally bounded); under the hypotheses of (vi) both are finite for M' large and tend to 0 as M' -> infinity, so (vii) contains (vi). (39.15) bounds weighted circulations of |omega^theta_U| outside the cylinders, at the scale of the distance from each exterior point, and not the vorticity pointwise. Without A_* < infinity the same conclusion holds if U satisfies (H3), with C_eta' in place of C_eta''.
 (viii) (A source form.) Let a_1 > 0 and B_0 >= 0. Then U does not satisfy
 int_s^T int_0^infinity int_R R |d_Z(q^2)(R, Z, -beta)| dZ dR dbeta <= B_0 (1 + log(T/s)) whenever a_1 <= s <= T.   (39.16)
The inner integral is (2 pi)^{-1} ||d_Z(q^2)(-beta)||_{L^1(R^3)}, and (39.16) holds if it is at most B_0/beta for beta >= a_1, which is the size of the total unsigned source of a self-similar field q = s^{-1} Q(R/s^{1/2}, Z/s^{1/2}) with int int rho |d_zeta(Q^2)(rho, zeta)| dzeta drho < infinity. (39.16) is a bound for the source alone, over all of R^3 including the whole axis; besides the standing setting and either A_* < infinity or (H3), no condition on the meridional field is imposed. Bounds of the pointwise forms (H3) and (H4) give no axial integrability: Q(rho, zeta) = (2 + sin zeta)(1 + rho^2)^{-5/4} satisfies bounds of both forms, and its source is not integrable in Z (this concerns the estimates only, not solutions). Without A_* < infinity the same conclusion holds if U satisfies (H3), with C_eta' in place of C_eta''.
 (ix) (Euler-local forms.) Put A_0 := 2 (K + nu), l_0 := 3 pi K, A_2 := 2 A_0 + 4 l_0 and A_3 := A_2 + K + 2, and let T_M^l(x, s) be the sum T_M(x, s) restricted to the k with d_k < l. (1) Let M >= 1, a_1 > 0 and eps_1, delta >= 0 with 3 delta/8 + 3 eps_1/4 < 3/8. Then U does not satisfy
 T_M^{2 l_0 s}(x, s) <= eps_1/s  and  N_x(s) <= delta/s  whenever s >= a_1, R_x >= 2 M s^{1/2} and max{R_x, |x_5|} < A_0 s.
(2) Let a_1 > 0 and B_0 >= 0. Then U does not satisfy
 int_s^T int int_{max{R, |Z|} < A_3 beta} R |d_Z(q^2)(R, Z, -beta)| dR dZ dbeta <= B_0 (1 + log(T/s)) whenever a_1 <= s <= T <= A_3^2 s^2.   (39.19)
Unlike (39.16), (39.19) counts at time -beta only the source in the box of size A_3 beta, a fixed multiple of the Euler scale, and not the source on the whole axis. For example (this concerns the bound only, not solutions), let q = beta^{-1} Q(R/beta^{1/2}, Z/l(beta)) at time -beta, with 0 < l(beta) <= beta, Q 1-periodic in its second variable, |d_zeta(Q^2)(rho, zeta)| <= m(rho), int_0^infinity rho m(rho) drho < infinity and c_1 := int_0^1 int_0^1 rho |d_zeta(Q^2)(rho, zeta)| dzeta drho > 0. For beta >= A_3^{-2} the inner double integral in (39.19) lies between A_3 c_1/l(beta) and 2 A_3 int_0^infinity rho m(rho) drho/l(beta). So (39.19) holds if l(beta) >= c beta for a constant c > 0 and fails if l(beta)/beta -> 0, while (39.16) fails for every such q. Thus, for these fixed-amplitude periodic profiles, (39.19) allows any number of Euler-scale axial cells along the axis, and it holds exactly when int_s^{2s} dbeta/l(beta) is bounded for all large s (a time-integrated bound on the inverse wavelength, not a pointwise lower bound on l(beta)/beta); for general sources the amplitude and the radial distribution matter as well as the axial scale. Since the integrand is nonnegative, (39.19) holds for some B_0 if and only if the integral over [s, 2s] alone is bounded for all large s (dyadic partition of [s, T]). The slab budget int_s^T int int_{|Z - z| <= w} R |d_Z(q^2)(R, Z, -beta)| dR dZ dbeta <= B_0 (1 + log(T/s)) + B_1 w/s, for all z in R, w > 0 and a_1 <= s <= T, implies (39.19) with (B_0 (1 + log 2) + 2 A_3 B_1)/log 2 in place of B_0, because on each block [2^j s, min{2^{j+1} s, T}] the box lies in the slab |Z| <= 2^{j+1} A_3 s; the impossibility of the slab budget was also proved in a parallel line of work, independently of Proposition 38(e), by localizing the mass bound (39.18) in Z along the backward paths (the axial displacement of a path in time u is at most K u plus a Gaussian term). Without A_* < infinity the same conclusions hold if U satisfies (H3).
 (x) (Axial regularity of the strain at the Euler scale.) Let A_c > A_3 (A_3 as in (ix)); the standing assumption A_* < infinity of (f) is not used in (x). There are no C_a >= 0, eps in [0, 1) and beta_0 > 0 such that, for every beta >= beta_0,
 |d_Z a_U(y, -beta)| <= C_a beta^{-2}  and  R_y d_R a_U(y, -beta) <= eps/beta  whenever max{R_y, |y_5|} < A_c beta.   (39.21)
This is a hypothesis on the meridional field alone: only the one-sided bound on R d_R a_U enters, C_a need not be small, and no compression hypothesis (neither A_* < infinity nor (CW)) is assumed: by the proof, (39.21) implies |a_U| <= (K/(2 A_c) + C_a A_c)/beta on the cone, and this bound, used on smaller cones, takes the place of the compression hypothesis. It is not implied by the Type I bound for eta (Remark (8)).
 (xi) (Time-integrated compression.) Assume (CW) of Proposition 37(e) in place of A_* < infinity. Fix W > W_*, C_q > (limsup_{s -> infinity} s ||q(-s)||_infty)^2 (finite by (37.5)) and a_1 > 0 such that int_t^{2t} m_P(s) ds <= W for t >= a_1 and ||q(sigma)||_infty^2 <= C_q sigma^{-2} for sigma <= -a_1, and put D_W := 6 C_q W/(1 - 2^{-3/2}) + (3/2) G'^2 + 16 nu B_theta. Then (ii) to (x) hold with D_W in place of D_1 throughout the energy estimates and their uses, including the definitions of E_q, C_eta'' and C_J and the exterior-energy coefficient in the forced part of the proof of (x). In particular every limit as in Proposition 37(d) violates (CW) or, for all M >= 1, kappa in [0, 1) and a_1 > 0, has points sigma <= -a_1 and y with R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2} and U^R(y, sigma) > kappa R_y/|sigma|; and under (CW) each of (39.14), (39.15), (39.16), (39.19) and (39.21) is excluded without (H3) (by (xiii) the first four, and the bound of (H2_kappa) on the Euler cone, are excluded under the weaker (CW_loc), and by (x) (39.21) needs no compression hypothesis).
 (xii) (Time-integrated Type I strain.) On a trajectory satisfying (K) and (TAIL), with k as in Proposition 33, suppose that there are W_k < infinity and h_0 in (0, T_*/2] with
 int_{T_* - 2h}^{T_* - h} k(t) dt <= W_k for 0 < h <= h_0.   (39.24)
Then (T_* - sigma) ||u^theta(sigma)||_infty^2 <= G^2 e^{2 W_k}/4 for T_* - h_0 <= sigma < T_*, so the hypothesis of Proposition 33(e)(i) holds with C_I := G^2 e^{2 W_k}/4 and t_1 := T_* - h_0; and every limit U of Theorem 2 satisfies int_t^{2t} sup_y a_U^-(y, -s) ds <= W_k for all t > 0. In particular every limit as in Proposition 37(d) satisfies (CW) with W_* <= W_k, and (xi) applies to it. For (CW) only the compression near the singular point and inside the parabolic cylinders matters: if U is the limit along a subsequence with gamma_n -> gamma_* and z_n -> z_*, and for some delta > 0 and eps > 0 the function k_P(t) := sup{(u^r/r)^-(x, t) : r < ((gamma_* + eps)(T_* - t))^{1/2}, |z - z_*| < delta} satisfies limsup_{h -> 0} int_{T_* - 2h}^{T_* - h} k_P(t) dt <= W_P, then int_t^{2t} m_P <= W_P for all t > 0, so U satisfies (CW) with W_* <= W_P; this needs neither (39.24) nor Type I swirl (W_P < infinity is part of the hypothesis). Consequently, on a trajectory satisfying (39.24) there are no kappa in [0, 1), M_0 >= 0 and t_b < T_* with (39.13); on a trajectory with Type I swirl the localized hypothesis, at the point z_* of the subsequence used in the proof, gives the same conclusion. The hypothesis of (i) implies (39.24) with W_k = C_a log 2, and so does limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) k(t) < C_a. Conversely (39.24) does not bound (T_* - t) k(t): as a condition on a function k >= 0 it holds, with W_k = 2 + 2 log 2, whenever k(t) <= 1/(T_* - t) on [T_* - 2 h_0, T_*) outside intervals I_j contained in the dyadic windows [T_* - 2^{1 - j} h_0, T_* - 2^{-j} h_0] (j >= 0) with |I_j| <= 2^{-j} h_0/H_j, and k(t) <= H_j/(T_* - t) on I_j, for arbitrary H_j >= 1; with H_j -> infinity and equality at a point of each I_j, limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity. So (xii) applies also to trajectories, if any, of the Type II strain alternative of Proposition 33(c) whose strain integrals over the dyadic windows are bounded, and these have Type I swirl. The negation of (39.24), limsup_{h -> 0} int_{T_* - 2h}^{T_* - h} k(t) dt = infinity, implies limsup_{t -> T_*} (T_* - t) k(t) = infinity.
 (xiii) (Cone-local compression.) Let U be a limit as in Proposition 37(d), let A_c > A_3, write C_E(-beta) := {y : max{R_y, |y_5|} < E beta} for E > 0, and put m_C(beta) := sup{a_U^-(y, -beta) : R_y < beta^{1/2}, |y_5| < A_c beta}, the compression on the part of the parabolic cylinder inside the Euler cone. Assume, in place of A_* < infinity,
 limsup_{t -> infinity} int_t^{2t} m_C(beta) dbeta < infinity.   (CW_loc)
(CW_loc) follows from (CW) (m_C <= m_P), hence from A_* < infinity, and from the bound |a_U| <= kappa/beta on the cone implied by (39.21). Then for every D in (K, A_c) there is C with |q(y, -beta)| <= C/(beta + R_y^2) on C_D(-beta), and for every E < A_c there is C' with |eta(y, -beta)| <= C' beta^{-3/2} on C_E(-beta), for all large beta; and U satisfies none of (39.14), (39.15) (with 3 delta/8 + 3 eps_1/4 < 1/2), (39.16), the bounds excluded in (ix)(1) and (39.19), nor, for any M >= 1, kappa in [0, 1) and a_1 > 0, the bound of (H2_kappa) at the points of C_{A_c} (in particular, U does not satisfy (H2_kappa)). The global estimates (ii) to (iv) are not recovered under (CW_loc): the stopped energies of the proof give no bound along paths started outside the cone, and the exclusions use only their stopped forms on the cone.
 (xiv) (Source bounds without compression hypothesis.) Let U be a limit as in Proposition 37(d). For H > 0 let (39.19_H) be the bound (39.19) with the boxes max{R, |Z|} < A_3 beta replaced by C_H(-beta) (so (39.19_{A_3}) is (39.19), and (39.19_H) implies (39.19_{H'}) for H' < H), and for A > 0 put n_A(s) := sup{a_U^-(y, -s) : R_y < s^{1/2}, |y_5| < A s} (so n_{A_c} = m_C). No compression hypothesis is assumed. (1) (Smoothing in three-dimensional measure.) Let S(sigma, sigma_0) be the evolution, from time sigma_0 to time sigma > sigma_0, of the source-free equation g_sigma + U.grad g = nu (Delta_3 + (2/R) d_R) g on axisymmetric functions (the equation P g = 0 of (b) read in the measure dx_3). Then S is positive and contracts L^1(dx_3) and L^infty, and ||S(sigma, sigma_0) g||_infty <= C_N (nu (sigma - sigma_0))^{-3/2} ||g||_{L^1(dx_3)} with an absolute constant C_N (no norm of U enters); hence, for I_1 h(x) := int |x - y|^{-2} |h(y)| dx_3(y), ||I_1 (S(sigma, sigma_0) g)||_infty <= C (nu (sigma - sigma_0))^{-1} ||g||_{L^1(dx_3)}. (2) (The near-field kernel at all radii.) For every x and L > 0, a_U^-(x, -s) <= (3 pi/8) K/L + (3/(4 pi)) int_{B_L(x)} |x - y|^{-2} |eta(y, -s)| dx_3(y), and 3/(4 pi) may be replaced by 3/(8 pi) at axis points. (3) (A logarithmic window bound.) If (39.19_H) holds for some H > K, then for every A in (0, H) there is C with int_t^{2t} n_A(s) ds <= C (1 + log t) for all large t, and n_A(s) = o(s^{-2/5}) as s -> infinity. (4) (A sufficient source condition.) If (39.19_H) holds for some H > A_c and |d_Z(q^2)(y, -beta)| <= F beta^{-5/2} on C_H(-beta) for all large beta, then m_C(s) <= C/s for all large s; so U satisfies (CW_loc) and (39.19), which (xiii) excludes. The pointwise bound holds if ||q(-beta)||_infty <= C beta^{-5/4} for all large beta. Neither hypothesis was derived; under (CW_loc) the rate obtained in (xiii) is |q| <= C/(beta + R^2) on the cone, which gives only |d_Z(q^2)| <= C beta^{-2} there. (5) (Limits of the method.) (a) (39.19) does not bound the source mass on windows of length o(s): it is compatible with bursts of source mass of order one on the windows [S, S + S^{4/5}], S = 16^n, with |d_Z(q^2)| <= C S^{-2} on the bursts and with q^2 <= C (beta + R^2)^{-2}, Type I swirl and bounded circulation (an explicit profile is in the proof). So int_s^{s + h} ||d_Z(q^2)(-beta)||_{L^1(C_H(-beta))} dbeta is bounded only by a constant for h << s, not by C h/s, and the source mass released at lag h behind -s enters the unsigned pointwise estimate with the factor (nu h)^{-1}; after integration over the observation times s in [t, 2t] (Fubini's theorem), the lags between 1 and t give the factor log t of (3), through int_1^t dh/h = log t. This is a limitation of the unsigned estimate used in (3), which keeps only the source mass and the time lag; it is not a lower bound for the compression of any solution. (b) The dyadic barrier argument leading to (37.5) does not recover the rate q = O(1/s) used in (xiii) from the logarithmic window bound: in (37.4) the window integral enters through the factor exp(2 W), so a bound int_t^{2t} n_A <= c log t allows an amplification as large as t^{2c} where (37.5) has a constant. As a scalar recursion, Q(t) <= C (1 + W(t)) e^{2 W(t)}/t + Q(2t)/2 with W(t) = c log t is satisfied by Q(t) = t^{-p} for every p with max{1/2, 1 - 2c} < p < 1, which is compatible with the Type I rate Q(t) = o(t^{-1/2}). This concerns the dyadic use of (37.4); it does not exclude a refined use of the equations.
