(c) In the model without drift the sign structure of the source removes the logarithm: if 0 <= q^2(y, -beta) <= C_q^2 (beta + R_y^2)^{-2} for beta >= s, then the strain generated by the source in the heat flow, a_lin(x, -s) := -int_0^infinity d_Z^2 (-Delta_5)^{-1} e^{nu u Delta_5} q^2(., -s - u)(x) du (the strain that the equation for eta would produce if the drift b_5 were removed), satisfies |a_lin(x, -s)| <= C C_q^2 (1 + log^+(1/nu))/s for R_x <= s^{1/2}, with no mass hypothesis. For a general Z-dependent drift d_Z need not commute with S (the commutator of d_Z with P is (d_Z b_5).grad_5; a Z-independent drift commutes with d_Z), and no estimate sufficient to recover this bound with drift is established here; the unsigned estimate of (1) uses the drift only through div U = 0 and does not retain the cancellation. (d) (The logarithm is attained for prescribed drifts.) For all nu, K, B > 0 and H, A, lambda > 0 there are a smooth bounded divergence-free meridional field V on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] with |V| <= K and bounded derivatives, and smooth sources h >= 0 and phi >= 0 with bounded derivatives, such that |d_Z phi| = h, the supports of h(-beta) and phi(-beta) lie in C_H(-beta) for all large beta, int_r^{2r} ||h(-beta)||_{L^1(dx_3)} dbeta <= B for all large r and ||h(-beta)||_infty = o(1/beta), and such that the Duhamel solutions g and eta (vanishing at the ancient end) of g_sigma + V.grad g = nu (Delta_3 + (2/R) d_R) g + h and of the same equation with source d_Z phi satisfy, along a sequence t_n -> infinity and with c > 0 independent of n, int_{t_n}^{2 t_n} sup{D_x(lambda s)(-s) : R_x < s^{1/2}, |x_5| < A s} ds >= c (B/nu) log t_n and int_{t_n}^{2 t_n} sup{a_eta^-(x, -s) : R_x < s^{1/2}, |x_5| < A s} ds >= c (B/nu) log t_n, where D_x(L) := int_{B_L(x)} |x - y|^{-4} g(y) dy_5 is the functional of (2) (for g in place of |eta|) and a_eta := Delta_5^{-1} d_Z eta (the canonical Newtonian inverse) is the reconstructed strain generated by eta. On the n-th window the field has critical radial outflow R V^R = 2 nu and V^Z = 0 on a region {R > a_n, |Z| < l_n} with a_n << t_n^{1/2} << l_n, on which the source-free equation agrees with the three-dimensional heat equation, and the comparison with heat flow killed on the boundary of this region retains a fixed positive fraction of the released mass (this does not exclude absorption at the axis for the full solution, which may enter R < a_n); both lower bounds also hold for a strictly subcritical modification with R V^R < 2 nu everywhere (with the deficit nu t_n^{-2} on the n-th window), whose equation on that region has a small additional radial drift. The field is prescribed: it is not generated by eta (in the central region V^R/R >= 0, while a_eta takes the negative values just stated), and phi is not a Type I swirl profile (R^2 phi is of order B at some points during a pulse, while Type I swirl requires R^2 q^2 = O(1/t_n) there, and R^2 phi^{1/2} is unbounded, so the circulation bound fails too). So the logarithm in (3) is sharp for the estimate (1). In the class of prescribed bounded smooth divergence-free drifts and signed sources d_Z phi with phi >= 0, the stated source budget does not give a uniform dyadic window bound for the reconstructed strain a_eta^-, so the logarithmic estimate is sharp in this enlarged linear class. The construction does not settle whether (39.19_H) implies (CW_loc) for Navier-Stokes limits; a stronger result restricted to those limits may use additional structure absent here, including the velocity-vorticity coupling Delta_5 a_U = d_Z eta, the swirl evolution, or the Type I and circulation bounds. (e) (No logarithm without radial velocity.) If V^R = 0 (so V^Z = W(R, sigma) by incompressibility), with W smooth and bounded of any size, and h >= 0 satisfies int_r^{2r} ||h(-beta)||_{L^1(dx_3)} dbeta <= B for r >= r_*, then the Duhamel solution g of the equation of (d) satisfies int_t^{2t} sup_{x in R^5} D_x(lambda s)(-s) ds <= C B/nu for t >= r_* and every lambda > 0, with an absolute constant C, the supremum over all x inside the time integral, and no box or supremum hypothesis on h. (f) (A fixed-point dual criterion; the feeding flux.) For a fixed axis point x = (0, z_0), if (V^R/R)(Z - z_0)^2 - V^Z (Z - z_0) <= (1 - eps) nu everywhere on a time interval I, with 0 < eps <= 1, and g >= 0 solves the equation of (d) with h >= 0, in the bounded classical class or in the nonnegative Duhamel class obtained by monotone approximation, then int_I int |x - y|^{-4} g dy_5 dsigma <= int g(inf I) psi dy_5 + (pi/(2 eps nu)) int_I int h dx_3 dsigma with psi := |y - x|^{-2}/(2 eps nu) (more precisely, for sigma_0 < sigma_1 in I, int_{sigma_0}^{sigma_1} int |x - y|^{-4} g dy_5 dsigma + int g(sigma_1) psi dy_5 <= int g(sigma_0) psi dy_5 + (pi/(2 eps nu)) int_{sigma_0}^{sigma_1} int h dx_3 dsigma, and if inf I = -infinity the first term on the right is read as the lim inf of int g(sigma_0) psi dy_5 as sigma_0 -> -infinity, which need not vanish when g -> 0); this is a fixed-point estimate and does not bound the supremum over x inside the time integral. If R V^R = 2 nu on the circle R = a for |Z| <= l, then a^2 >= 4 nu l/K, and this critical outflow fixes only the disk average (2/a^2) int_0^a R (-d_Z V^Z/2) dR = 2 nu/a^2: it does not force expansion at the axis (the field of (d) with the radial profile replaced by one equal to -kappa R^2/a^2 near the axis has V^R/R = -2 nu kappa/a^2 there and critical outflow for R >= a; it is used only for this kinematic statement, since it need not keep the sign Z V^Z <= 0 used for the signed source in (d)). (6) (Consequences of the coupling.) Assume (39.19_H) for some H > K, and let E in (0, H), h_beta, M(beta), F_* and B be as in the proof of (3), so that int_r^{2r} M <= B for r >= r_B. Put gamma := min{H - E, H - K}^2/(20 nu), eps_s := 10 F_* e^{-gamma s}/gamma, Phi(d) := sum_{j >= 0} min{1, d 2^{-3j/2}} for d >= 0 and, at time -s, Q_{rho,l}(z_0) := {R < rho, |Z - z_0| < l} and M_{rho,l}(z_0) := int_{Q_{rho,l}(z_0)} |eta(-s)| dx_3. One may take C_N = 2 6^{1/2}/pi^2 in (1). (a) (Vorticity mass at the parabolic scale.) For s >= r_B and every axisymmetric measurable set D in C_E(-s) of volume V in dx_3, int_D |eta(-s)| dx_3 <= B (1 + Phi(C_N V (nu s)^{-3/2})) + V eps_s, where Phi(d) <= d/(1 - 2^{-3/2}) and Phi(d) <= (2/3) log_2^+ d + 1/(1 - 2^{-3/2}). In particular M_{rho,l}(z_0) <= (1 + 2 pi C_N/(1 - 2^{-3/2})) B + 2 pi rho^2 l eps_s if rho, l <= (nu s)^{1/2} and Q_{rho,l}(z_0) lies in C_E(-s): the vorticity mass of such a cylinder at time -s is O(B) as s -> infinity for fixed B > 0 (the term 2 pi rho^2 l eps_s is exponentially small), without the logarithm of (3). (b) (Signed height averages of the strain.) Let 0 < A < E, kappa > 0, 0 < lambda < (E - A)/2, l := kappa (nu s)^{1/2}, and let w >= 0 be Lipschitz with support in [-l, l], w(-l) = w(l) = 0, int w = 1 and ||w'||_infty <= d_1/l^2. Put J_kappa := 1 + 1/(1 - 2^{-3/2}) + (2/3) log_2^+(16 pi C_N kappa^3) and C_av := ((8 + d_1/4) J_kappa + 64/3)/pi. Then for 0 <= r <= l, |z_0| <= A s and s >= max{r_B, kappa^2 nu/(E - A - lambda)^2},
 |int w(Z - z_0) a_U(r, Z, -s) dZ| <= 3 pi K/(8 lambda s) + C_av B/(kappa^2 nu s) + lambda s eps_s.   (39.26)
Consequently, if c_* > 0, r <= l and R U^R(r, Z, -s) >= c_* nu for |Z - z_0| < l, then r^2/(nu s) >= c_*/(3 pi K/(8 lambda) + C_av B/(kappa^2 nu) + lambda s^2 eps_s). So an outflow R U^R >= c_* nu, for example the critical outflow R U^R = 2 nu of (5)(d), cannot persist across the height kappa (nu s)^{1/2} at a radius r = o(s^{1/2}) as s -> infinity, uniformly for |z_0| <= A s, and no condition on d_R(R U^R) is needed. (39.26) bounds signed height averages against Lipschitz weights of half-width kappa (nu s)^{1/2}, uniformly in the radii r <= l and the centres |z_0| <= A s; it does not bound an average of a_U^-, the supremum in height, or an average against transported mass, and it leaves open outflow on shorter axial segments or on irregular sets. Since it holds at each time for every centre, the exclusion also applies to intervals of height kappa (nu s)^{1/2} whose centres z_0(s) move arbitrarily within |z_0| <= A s. (c) (Critical circles.) At a fixed time, if R U^R = 2 nu and d_R(R U^R) = 0 at R = rho for |Z - z_0| < l, then for every integer m >= 1, with M := M_{rho,l}(z_0) and q_m := 2 m^2 rho^2/l^2, nu <= (M rho^2/(2 pi l^2)) sum_{j=0}^{m-1} q_m^j + (K rho^2/l) q_m^m; in particular nu <= M rho^2/(2 pi l^2) + 2 K rho^4/l^3, and nu <= M/(pi d^2) + (K l/d^2) 2^{-floor(d/2)} if d := l/rho >= 2. With (a), such a critical circle with l a fixed multiple of (nu s)^{1/2} and Q_{rho,l}(z_0) in C_E(-s) is impossible along any sequence s -> infinity with rho log l = o(l); in particular the critical annular plateau of (5)(d), at radii of order t_n^{1/3}, cannot occur in the meridional field of a limit satisfying (39.19_H). (d) (What these bounds do not give.) (i) A fixed subcriticality gap for the height averages does not remove the logarithm from the estimate (1): for all nu, K, mu > 0 and lambda > 0 there are, for each large t, smooth prescribed fields V as in (5)(d) with |V| <= K, critical outflow R V^R = 2 nu and V^Z = 0 on {R > t^{1/3}, |Z| < L_0 (nu t)^{1/2}} (L_0 a fixed constant), and int w_tr(Z - z_0) R V^R(R, Z) dZ <= nu for all R and z_0, where w_tr is the trapezoidal weight of half-width l = D L_0 (nu t)^{1/2} with a fixed D (equal to 2/(3 l) for |Z| <= l/2 and decreasing linearly to 0 at |Z| = l), together with a source pulse h >= 0 of mass mu, released during a unit time just before -2t inside C_H(-beta) and with supremum O(mu t^{-5/4}), such that int_t^{2t} sup{D_x(lambda s)(-s) : R_x < s^{1/2}, |x_5| < A s} ds >= c (mu/nu) log t for the unsigned solution g, with c > 0 independent of t; these fields and pulses can be assembled into one ancient field with the same averages at every time (half-width a fixed multiple of (nu beta)^{1/2} at time -beta). By (c) the core vorticity mass of such a field grows like t^{1/3}, so the pair formed by V and its own potential vorticity cannot satisfy the ancient evolution, with vanishing terminal term, and the source budget used in (a). A pointwise gap R V^R <= (2 - eps) nu would instead make R^p, 0 < p <= eps, a supermartingale for the radial mass process, the diffusion with generator nu d_R^2 + (V^R - nu/R) d_R + nu d_Z^2 + V^Z d_Z that carries the mass density 2 pi R g and is killed at the axis; a height average does not control the drift at the position of the mass. (ii) The static consequences of the coupling do not imply (CW_loc). For tau > 0 let L := (nu tau)^{1/2}, r := R/L, z := Z/L, w := r^2 + z^2 and phi := mu Z L^{-2} e^{-w}; then U^R := -R phi_Z = -(mu/L) r (1 - 2 z^2) e^{-w} and U^Z := 2 phi + R phi_R = (2 mu/L) z (1 - r^2) e^{-w} define a smooth divergence-free field with |U| <= 2 mu/L, eta := -Delta_5 phi = (mu/L^3) z (14 - 4 w) e^{-w} is exactly its omega^theta/R, so Delta_5 a = d_Z eta with a := U^R/R = -(mu/L^2)(1 - 2 z^2) e^{-w}, ||eta||_{L^1(dx_3)} = pi (6 + 44 e^{-7/2}) mu for every tau, |int w a(r, Z) dZ| <= d_1 (6 + 44 e^{-7/2}) mu/(4 l^2) for every weight as in (b), and a^-(0, 0) = mu/(nu tau). With tau := 2t - s + tau_0 on [t, 2t] and 2 mu (nu tau_0)^{-1/2} <= K, int_t^{2t} n_A >= (mu/nu) log(1 + t/tau_0), and with tau_0 := t^alpha (0 < alpha < 1) these windows assemble into one smooth ancient kinematic field with bounded velocity and derivatives and bounded vorticity mass for which (CW_loc) fails. It is not an evolution under the source budget: the source it requires, eta_tau + U.grad eta - nu Delta_5 eta, has L^1(dx_3) norm at least 4 pi (10 + 8 e^{-7/2}) mu/tau, so its total over the window is at least 4 pi (10 + 8 e^{-7/2}) mu log(1 + t/tau_0), also on the boxes C_H(-beta) up to o(1), which contradicts (39.19_H) for large t. (e) (The first missing implication.) Parts (a) to (c) do not improve the logarithm of (3), and no coupled solution with logarithmic window growth was constructed. What is missing is an estimate converting the averaged bounds (a) and (b) into control of the source-weighted transport, or of the signed strain, at all lags and centers: a survival or occupation estimate for the radial mass process of (d)(i) derived from the coupled mass bounds rather than from a pointwise gap; or a dual inequality as in (5)(f) with the supremum over the centers inside the time integral, derived from the coupled equations; or a cancellation estimate for the signed source d_Z(q^2) along the Z-dependent evolution that replaces the unsigned bound C/(nu tau) of (1) by a summable one. The target is limsup_t int_t^{2t} m_C < infinity, with the supremum over the centres taken before the time integration, so a bound at a fixed centre does not suffice; for the route to (CW_loc) the source boxes must be wider than the compression cone, H > A_c. These routes are possible sufficient mechanisms; none is claimed to be necessary.
(7) (Multiscale counting, the averaged radial flux, survival under a pointwise gap, the zero budget and an exact forced expansion.) Assume nu > 0 and (39.19_H) for some H > K, take the hypotheses and notation of (6), with 0 < A < E < H, and put c := R U^R; the estimates that use the source budget B are for s >= r_B, and U_mer := U^R e_R + U^Z e_Z denotes the meridional velocity, which is the part of the velocity reconstructed from eta. On C_E(-s) write eta = eta_0 + eta_1 with eta_0 := sgn(eta)(|eta| - eps_s)_+, so that |eta_1| <= eps_s and (6)(a) holds for eta_0 without the term V eps_s. Put C_0 := 1 + 2 pi C_N/(1 - 2^{-3/2}) < 5.825, J_0 := 1 + 1/(1 - 2^{-3/2}) + (2/3) log_2(2 pi C_N) < 3.641 and J_1 := J_0 + 2. For u > 0 and an axis height z_0 let Q_u := Q_{u,u}(z_0) and let W_u := int_{Q_u} (R^2/u^2) |eta_0(-s)| dx_3 be the weighted mass of Q_u at time -s (with |eta_0| replaced by |eta_0| 1_Omega when a set Omega is indicated). (a) (Weighted packing.) For u_j := 2^j u_0, 0 <= j <= J, sum_j W_{u_j} <= (4/3) int_{Q_{u_J}} |eta_0| dx_3; if u_J <= (nu s)^{1/2} and Q_{u_J} lies in C_E(-s), the sum is at most (4/3) C_0 B, so, for every delta > 0, at most 4 C_0 B/(3 delta nu) indices have W_{u_j} >= delta nu. The same holds after integrating all W_{u_j} against one probability measure in time, with measurable z_0(sigma) and u_0(sigma). It gives nothing when each scale is averaged over its own time interval: w_j(tau) := nu 1_{[4^j, 4^{j+1})}(tau) has sum_j w_j = nu at every tau >= 1 and average nu over its own interval for every j, so 'at most N_0 active scales at each instant' does not imply 'at most N_0 active scales along the successive ages of a packet'; an expanding structure occupies one dyadic scale after another in this way. (b) (Outflow counting with the far field.) Let L, r_* > 0, let Omega := {R < L + r_*, |Z - z_0| < L + r_*} lie in C_E(-s), let 0 < r <= r_*, compute W_u with |eta_0| 1_Omega, and let w >= 0 be Lipschitz with integral 1, support in [-r, r], w(-r) = w(r) = 0 and ||w'||_infty <= d_1/r^2. Then
 |int w(Z - z_0) c(r, Z, -s) dZ| <= 3 pi K r^2/(8L) + (d_1/pi) W_{2r} + (24/pi) sum_{k >= 1} 4^{-k} W_{2^{k+1} r} + r^2 L eps_s.   (39.27)
For r_* := kappa (nu s)^{1/2} with 0 < kappa <= 1, r_j := 2^{j - J} r_* (0 <= j < J) and w_j the tent of half-width r_j and integral 1 (d_1 = 1), sum_{j < J} |int w_j(Z - z_0) c(r_j, Z, -s) dZ| <= D B + pi K r_*^2/(8L) + L r_*^2 eps_s/3 with D := 12 C_0/pi + (32/pi)(J_0/3 + 8/9) < 43.665. Hence, with L := lambda s, 0 < lambda < E - A, |z_0| <= A s and s large, for each d > 0, the number of dyadic radii r_j <= kappa (nu s)^{1/2} with c(r_j, Z, -s) >= d nu for all |Z - z_0| < r_j is at most D B/(d nu) + pi K kappa^2/(8 d lambda) + o(1), uniformly in J; if B <= nu/(4D) and kappa^2 <= min{1, lambda/(pi K)}, no such radius with d = 1 exists at large times. This concerns uniform height outflow at one time and is not a smallness threshold for (CW_loc). (c) (Averaged radial flux.) Under the containment of (b) and 0 < r <= r_*,
 r^{-3} int_{Q_r} |c(-s)| dx_3 <= 3 pi^2 K r^2/(8L) + 8 W_{2r} + 24 sum_{k >= 1} 4^{-k} W_{2^{k+1} r} + pi r^2 L eps_s,   (39.28)
and if also r <= (nu s)^{1/2} the right side is at most C_c B + 3 pi^2 K r^2/(8L) + pi r^2 L eps_s with C_c := 16 J_1 + 64/3 < 111.6. The analogue of (39.28) for r^{-2} int_{Q_r} |U_mer| dx_3 with the same weighted masses fails for general smooth fields at a fixed time (this does not refute a coarser bound of order B or an estimate specific to the limits of Navier-Stokes solutions): for the smooth vortex ring eta := Gamma a_0^{-3} f(R/a_0, Z/a_0) with a fixed profile f >= 0 supported in {1/2 < R < 3/2, |Z| < 1/4}, and its canonical decaying velocity, r^{-2} int_{Q_{r,r}(0)} |U_mer| dx_3 >= (W'_r/4) log(r/(4096 a_0)) for r >= 4096 a_0, where W'_r := int_{Q_{r,r}(0)} (R^2/r^2) |eta| dx_3 = I/(pi r^2) with I := int eta dy_5 (r > 2 a_0), while the weighted masses of the larger dyadic cylinders are smaller by powers of 4; with Gamma proportional to a_0 the velocity stays below any K and the vorticity mass tends to 0. For the canonical decaying meridional velocity one has only the unweighted weak bound ||U_mer||_{L^{2,infinity}(dR dZ)} <= (2 pi)^{-1/2} ||eta||_{L^1(dx_3)}, with ||f||_{L^{2,infinity}} := sup_{l > 0} l |{|f| > l}|^{1/2}. (d) (Survival under a pointwise gap.) Let X be the diffusion with generator nu d_R^2 + (U^R - nu/R) d_R + nu d_Z^2 + U^Z d_Z, killed at the axis, which carries the forward mass density 2 pi R g of a nonnegative source-free solution g of the equation of eta (time running forward from the release). If c <= lambda nu on {R < R_*} during an age interval of length tau, with 0 <= lambda < 2 and 0 < R_* <= infinity, then for a start at radius r_0 < R_*,
 P(X survives for the age tau) <= P(1 - lambda/2, r_0^2/(4 nu tau)) + (r_0/R_*)^{2 - lambda},   P(alpha, y) := gamma(alpha, y)/Gamma(alpha) <= min{1, y^alpha/Gamma(1 + alpha)},
without the second term if R_* = infinity; for U^R = 0, lambda = 0 and R_* = infinity it is an equality with first term 1 - e^{-r_0^2/(4 nu tau)}. Since |U| <= K, for 0 < lambda < 2 and K > 0 the hypothesis holds on {R < lambda nu/K} for every flow, but then the second term does not decay in the age. (e) (Conditional summation; the zero budget.) Suppose each h_beta (beta >= s) is decomposed into nonnegative packets of masses d mu_beta(xi) with int d mu_beta = M(beta) and release lengths l_{beta,xi} > 0, and that the potential sigma_4^{-1} D_x(lambda s) at time -s of each evolved packet of unit mass is at most (C_*/(nu (beta - s))) b_*(nu (beta - s)/l_{beta,xi}^2) for all x with R_x < s^{1/2}, |Z_x| < A s, where b_*(v) := v^{1/2} for v <= 1 and b_*(v) := theta^{max(0, floor(log_4 v) - N_0)/3} for v > 1, 0 < theta < 1, N_0 a nonnegative integer. Then int_0^infinity (nu tau)^{-1} b_*(nu tau/l^2) d tau = nu^{-1} [2 + log 4 (N_0 + 1 + theta^{1/3}/(1 - theta^{1/3}))] for every l, and limsup_t int_t^{2t} n_A <= C K + C B/nu + 2 C_* B nu^{-1} [2 + log 4 (N_0 + 1 + theta^{1/3}/(1 - theta^{1/3}))], with C depending on lambda only; with A = A_c and H > A_c this is (CW_loc), and (xiii) applies. The normalization by the release length cannot be dropped: for zero drift and the heat-scaled data f_l(x) := l^{-3} f(x/l) the potential at the axis at the age l^2/nu is l^{-2} times a fixed positive number, with no factor tending to 0 with the age. If B = 0, that is, if the source vanishes on the boxes C_H(-beta) for almost every large beta, then |eta| <= eps_s on C_E(-s), n_A(s) <= 3 pi K/(8 lambda s) + lambda s eps_s and limsup_t int_t^{2t} n_A <= (3 pi K/(8 lambda)) log 2, so (CW_loc) holds when H > A_c and (xiii) excludes the limit. (f) (Coupled identities for decaying fields.) Let U^R = -R psi_Z, U^Z = 2 psi + R psi_R, eta = -Delta_5 psi, with eta a solution of the equation of eta with source d_Z(q^2), and assume enough decay to discard the outer fluxes (not available for the limits in general). Then d/dsigma int eta dy_5 = 0; the first axial moment calJ := int Z eta dy_5 satisfies calJ' = pi int (2 (U^Z)^2 - (U^R)^2 - (U^theta)^2) dx_3, whose meridional part has no sign; if eta is odd in Z, negative on {Z > 0} with no other sign change, and q^2 is even and nonincreasing in Z on {Z > 0}, then p := -eta on {Z > 0} and m := ||eta||_{L^1(dx_3)} satisfy m' + 8 pi nu int_0^infinity p(0, Z) dZ + 4 pi nu int_0^infinity R p_Z(R, 0) dR = ||d_Z(q^2)||_{L^1(dx_3)}: axis absorption and cancellation at the plane Z = 0 must be paid by the source. For a fixed shape p = G L^{-3} f(R/L, Z/L) with L^2 = D_* tau this cost is nu G C_f/(D_* tau), C_f := 8 pi int_0^infinity f(0, z) dz + 4 pi int_0^infinity r f_z(r, 0) dr, that is (nu G C_f/D_*) log 2 per doubling of the age. (g) (An exact forced expanding pair.) Let 0 < b <= nu, tau > 0, L^2 := 6 nu tau, r := R/L, z := Z/L, w := r^2 + z^2, F(w) := (1/4) int_0^1 u^{3/2} e^{-u w} du and psi := -(b/L) z F(w). Then eta := -Delta_5 psi = -(b/L^3) z e^{-w}, U^R = (b/L) r (F + 2 z^2 F'), U^Z = -(2b/L) z (F + r^2 F'), |U_mer| <= b/L, ||eta(tau)||_{L^1(dx_3)} = pi b, and h := eta_tau + U.grad eta - nu Delta_5 eta = (2 b z/L^5) e^{-w} [-nu (w + 1) + b ((1 + r^2 - 2 z^2) F + r^2 F')], which is odd in z and negative for z > 0. So phi := -int_Z^infinity h(R, zeta, tau) d zeta on {Z >= 0}, extended evenly, is positive and smooth with d_Z phi = h, and with q := phi^{1/2} the triple (U, eta, q) solves the equation of eta with source d_Z(q^2) exactly; it is a forced meridional Navier-Stokes flow, and q is not claimed to solve the swirl equation. Its axis strain satisfies a^-(0, 2L, tau) >= b/(40 L^2) = b/(240 nu tau), and its source cost is exactly ||h(tau)||_{L^1(dx_3)} = 4 pi nu b/L^2 + 2 pi nu b/L^2 = pi b/tau (axis absorption plus cancellation at the plane). On a window with tau := 2t - s + tau_0, s in [t, 2t] and 1 <= tau_0 <= t, int_t^{2t} n_A >= (b/(240 nu)) log(1 + t/tau_0) for large t, while int_t^{2t} ||h(-s)||_{L^1(dx_3)} ds = pi b log(1 + t/tau_0), also on C_H(-s) up to o(1): logarithmic compression is paid by a logarithmic source, which (39.19_H) forbids for tau_0 = t^alpha with 0 <= alpha < 1 and b constant on each window; with b of order 1/log t the window stays bounded. Moreover (U^theta)^2 = R^2 phi >= b/(4 e tau) at R = L, Z = 0, so the young part of such a window violates the Type I swirl bound. This sharpens (6)(d)(ii). (h) (The first missing implication, refined.) Parts (6) and (7) bound, at each time, the vorticity mass of parabolic cylinders, the sum of the weighted masses over dyadic families below the parabolic radius (larger scales enter (b) and (c) through summable coefficients), the averaged radial flux c and signed height averages of a; (d) gives one sufficient survival estimate, under an additional pointwise gap, and does not show that such a gap is necessary. What is missing is the transport step: an estimate, derived from the coupled evolution, that gives the hypothesis of (e) with release lengths and uniformly over the observation centres, or a positive source charge for each repeated activation of a dyadic scale along a packet history, which (a) shows the instantaneous count cannot provide, or an alternative signed cancellation or dual estimate sufficient for a bounded compression window. No prescribed moving-structure example is used here as a proved result. Item (8) shows that the time-integrated bound for the pointwise strain which the budget implies does not by itself give the transport step.
(8) (Time-integrated strain bounds.) Assume the hypotheses of (7), let K < E' < E < H and 0 < lambda < E - E', and put alpha(v) := sup_{C_{E'}(-v)} |a_U(., -v)|. (a) (The time-integrated strain.) For all sufficiently large s and every interval I in [s, 4s],
 int_I alpha(v) dv <= C_1 + kappa log(1 + |I|),   kappa := C_3 B/nu,   C_3 := (27/(4 pi)) (4 6^{1/2}/pi)^{2/3} < 4.59,   C_1 := (3 pi K/(8 lambda)) log 4 + C_3 B/(2 nu) + 2.   (39.29)
(b) (Survival under a time-integrated strain bound.) Let X be the diffusion of (7)(d) started at radius r_0 > 0, and let alpha_0 >= 0 be deterministic and locally integrable with a_U(X_u) <= alpha_0(u) before absorption for 0 <= u <= tau. (The bound (a) supplies such an alpha_0 only up to the exit of X from C_{E'}; applied to X stopped at that exit, the bound below holds for the event that X survives and does not leave C_{E'} before the age tau, and a bound for unconditional survival must add the probability of an exit before tau.) With A(u) := int_0^u alpha_0 and calT(tau) := int_0^tau e^{-2 A(u)} du, P(X survives for the age tau) <= 1 - exp(-r_0^2/(4 nu calT(tau))); if A(u) <= C_1 + kappa log(1 + u) with kappa < 1/2 and tau >= 1, this is at most min{1, e^{2 C_1} r_0^2/(2 nu (1 + tau)^{1 - 2 kappa})}. The numerator is r_0^2. If kappa = 0 the bound decays in the normalized age nu tau/r_0^2 (it is at most e^{2 C_1} r_0^2/(2 nu tau) for tau >= 1; for zero drift the survival probability is exactly 1 - exp(-r_0^2/(4 nu tau))). If 0 < kappa < 1/2, the hypothesis on alpha_0 alone gives no survival bound that tends to zero with nu tau/r_0^2 uniformly in r_0: for the linear strain U^R = alpha_0 R, U^Z = -2 alpha_0 Z with alpha_0(u) = kappa/(1 + u), a field that grows linearly in space and so lies outside the class |U| <= K, the bound is an equality, and at the age tau = r_0^{2/(1 - 2 kappa)}, where nu tau/r_0^2 = nu r_0^{4 kappa/(1 - 2 kappa)} -> infinity, the survival probability tends to 1 - exp(-(1 - 2 kappa)/(4 nu)) > 0 as r_0 -> infinity. (c) (Radial occupation.) Let tau_max >= 1 and assume the hypothesis of (b) for all ages up to tau_max. The radial occupation functional J(x) := int_1^{tau_max} E_x[min{1/(nu t), 1/R_t^2}; X survives for the age t] dt satisfies
 nu J(x) <= 2 + 2 E_x int_1^{tau_max} a_U^+(X_t) min{1, nu t/R_t^2} 1_{X survives for the age t} dt <= 2 + 2 int_1^{tau_max} alpha_0(t) dt,   (39.30)
where a_U is evaluated along the path at the time of age t. If moreover A(t) <= C_1 + kappa log(1 + t) for all t >= 0, then J(x) <= (2 + 2 C_1)/nu uniformly in x and tau_max when kappa = 0, and J(x) <= nu^{-1} [2 + 2 C_1 + 1/p + 2 kappa log(1 + L_x)], L_x := max{1, (e^{2 C_1} R_x^2/(2 nu))^{1/p}}, p := 1 - 2 kappa, when 0 < kappa < 1/2. J is an occupation functional; it is not shown to be comparable with the potential that a packet started at x produces at a given axis point, which depends on the axial position of the packet (for zero drift and tau_max = 2 the time integral of that potential at a fixed axis point tends to zero as the starting height tends to infinity, while J does not change). (d) (Two obstructions, for prescribed drifts.) In this part a prescribed smooth bounded divergence-free axisymmetric field V without swirl, with |V| <= K and bounded derivatives, takes the place of U, alpha_V(t) := sup_{R, Z} |V^R/R| at time t is its absolute strain, and kappa > 0 is a coefficient prescribed independently of the source budget (the choice kappa = C_3 B/nu matches (39.29)). (i) Fix nu, K > 0 and 0 < kappa < 1/2. For all sufficiently large r there is such a drift V_r with int_I alpha_{V_r} <= kappa log(1 + |I|) for every interval I in [0, infinity), an inequality of the form (39.29) with additive constant zero, for which the occupation functional of (c) at x_r := ((nu r)^{1/2}, 0) with tau_max = infinity satisfies c kappa log r/(nu log log r) <= J_{V_r}(x_r) <= C kappa log r/(nu log log r), with c, C > 0 independent of r. So no bound for J in terms of nu, K, kappa and the additive constant holds uniformly in the drift and the starting point. (ii) Fix nu, K, B, kappa > 0 and lambda > 0. There are one such drift V and a smooth nonnegative source h = d_Z phi, phi := int_{-infinity}^Z h dz (nonnegative and not compactly supported in Z; no swirl equation is claimed for phi), with source mass at most B on every late dyadic window and beta ||h(-beta)||_infty -> 0, such that int_I alpha_V <= kappa log(1 + |I|) for every interval I in [s, 4s] with s large, and the passive solution with that source and zero ancient end satisfies int_{T_n}^{2 T_n} D_0(lambda s)(-s) ds >= c (B/nu) log log T_n - C along a sequence T_n -> infinity, at the axis point 0, which lies in every cone. In particular the packet bound of (7)(e) fails for it with any fixed constants. Neither is a coupled example. For 0 <= t <= t_r and r large (where the cutoffs equal 1 on the region considered), the drift of (i) has potential-vorticity mass 2 pi h nu, with h of order log log r, on the part {1/2 <= R/l <= 1} of the cylinder of radius and half-height l := (nu (r + t))^{1/2} about the axis, and mass at most C h nu on the whole cylinder; where these cylinders are eligible for (6)(a), this is incompatible with a fixed budget B as r -> infinity. The drift of (ii) has mass 4 pi J_F epsilon nu (s/T_n) log T_n on the cylinders of radius and half-height (nu s)^{1/2} about the axis, s in [T_n, 2 T_n], with constants J_F, epsilon > 0 of the construction; this is unbounded and violates (6)(a). Its averaged radial flux r^{-3} int_{Q_r} |R V^R| dx_3 at the radii r_n := (nu T_n)^{1/2} (log T_n)^{-1/4} tends to 4 pi nu, while at these radii (r_n^2/s -> 0) the right side of (7)(c) tends to C_c B; so (7)(c) fails for it when B < 4 pi nu/C_c (about 0.1126 nu). These are masses of the vorticity of the prescribed drift, which the passive source budget does not control, since no forced evolution connects them to it. So the interval strain inequality, even with additive constant zero, together with the source budget and the decay of the source supremum, implies neither a uniform occupation bound nor the packet bound of (7)(e) for prescribed bounded smooth drifts; the examples leave open arguments that use the coupled vorticity-mass bounds, the vorticity evolution, the swirl equation or another structure of the limits.

Remark. (1) (The hypotheses.) None of (H2), (H3) and (H4) was derived for the limits. A_* < infinity was not derived on the Type I swirl branch alone, nor was its time-integrated form (CW) of Proposition 37(e), or the cone-local form (CW_loc) of (xiii) (Proposition 37, Remark (5)(d), shows that (CW) does not follow from the regularity, boundedness and kinematic properties verified there, which do not include the normalization of the limits); on the Type I strain branch, (f)(i) gives A_* <= C_a. In place of (H3) and (H4), (a) gives |d_Z(q^2)| <= 2 C_loc Q_1^2, which is O(s^{-2}) when A_* < infinity, and the circulation bound 162 C_loc G'^2 R^{-4}. (H3) is the self-similar size of the core source (an axial derivative of order |q| s^{-1/2} with |q| = O(1/s)); (H4) holds when the exterior swirl varies axially on the scale R, |d_Z q| <= C |q|/R for R >= M s^{1/2}, since then |d_Z(q^2)| <= 2 C G'^2 R^{-5}; (H2) excludes forward outflow outside the moving parabolic cylinders. The collapsing Burgers vortex of Proposition 38, Remark (4) satisfies (H2), (H3) and (H4) (its radial velocity is -theta R/(tau_* - tau), q does not depend on Z, and eta = 0) and has compression theta/(tau_* - tau) with theta > 1/2; it is not a Case-1 limit because its meridional field is unbounded. Besides the setting (smoothness and the bounds used in (a)), the bound |U| <= K enters the proof of (e) through the harmonic term (3 pi/8) K/L of (39.7): for the Burgers vortex a_U = -theta/(tau_* - tau) is spatially constant and eta = 0, so the harmonic part equals the whole compression for every L, which no bound of the form K/L allows. Bounded kinematic fields show that the equation for eta is also essential: with a := 1 - tau, ell := a^p (1/2 < p < 1), a smooth nondecreasing odd f with bounded derivatives, equal to its argument near 0 and constant outside a compact interval, and a nonnegative cutoff chi equal to 1 near 0, the field U^R = -R phi_Z, U^Z = 2 phi + R phi_R with phi := (theta ell/a) f(Z/ell) chi(R^2/ell^2) is divergence free, bounded by C ell/a, equal to the Burgers strain (-theta R/a, 2 theta Z/a) near the core and satisfies U^R <= 0 everywhere; with a Z-independent swirl it satisfies (H2), (H3) and (H4) with C' = C'' = 0 and has compression theta/a at the core. It is not a solution: eta = -Delta_5 phi does not vanish while the source does, against (39.2). (H2) is restrictive: by the divergence theorem on {R < rho, |Z| < L}, |int_{-L}^{L} U^R(rho, Z, sigma) dZ| <= K rho for every L, so under (H2) int_R |U^R(rho, Z, sigma)| dZ <= K rho for rho >= M |sigma|^{1/2}, sigma <= -a_1: the exterior inflow is integrable in Z at every such radius, and a Z-periodic exterior inflow is excluded unless it vanishes. The hypothesis (H2_kappa) of (f)(iv) allows outflow, and |U| <= K gives it at the radii R_y >= K |sigma|/kappa (kappa > 0); it is a hypothesis on the intermediate region M |sigma|^{1/2} <= R_y < K |sigma|/kappa only.
(2) (Without (H3) and (H4).) Under (H2) and A_* < infinity alone, (39.5) gives |omega^theta_U(x, -a)| <= A/r with A := 2 C_loc [M^2 C_q + 81 G'^2 (5/M^2 + (24 + 16 2^{1/2}) nu/M^4)] for r >= 2 M a^{1/2} and a >= max{a_1, 9/M^2}, hence the Type I bound eps/a for r >= max{2 M a^{1/2}, A a/eps}; it does not establish that bound on 2 M a^{1/2} <= r < A a/eps. The two terms of (39.5) are of the same order: the inner one is the core budget from the backward time of order r^2/M^2 needed to reach the cylinders, the exterior one is the circulation-bound source at radii of order r accumulated over a time of order r^2. A self-similar core bound (H3) lowers only the inner term; with the unsigned exterior bound c_0 R^{-4} the occupation argument cannot give r^{-3}: for U^R = 0 on the exterior, which (H2) allows, with a fixed and L -> infinity, a source envelope of size c_0 L^{-4} on L/2 < R < 3 L/2 at backward times a + u <= L^{8/5} is compatible with that bound and with a global bound C |sigma|^{-5/2}, and the backward paths started at R = L stay in that shell up to time L^{8/5} with probability tending to 1 as L -> infinity, so the bound obtained from this envelope is of order L^{-12/5}, larger than L^{-3}. This concerns the envelope only, not a solution. (H4) removes this term; so does the circulation equation itself, through the energy identity (39.9) along the backward paths: the envelope would need |Gamma_Z| of order 1 along a typical path for a backward time of order L^{8/5}, while (39.9) bounds the gradient energy collected along the path by a constant. Accordingly, under (H2) alone the exterior part of (39.2) is O(r^{-3}) (the proof of (d)(iii) does not use (H3) for that part), and the binding term is the inner one, the core budget, which is what (H3) lowers; when A_* < infinity (in particular on the Type I strain branch) the budget after the first entrance is controlled by the joined energy of q and Gamma, (39.10), without (H3).
(3) (The form of (39.3).) In the estimate (39.7), without the factor (M_1 s^{1/2}/R_y)^delta (delta = 0) each dyadic shell of radii between max{R_x, M_1 s^{1/2}} and L can contribute an amount of order eps_v/s to D_x(L), so for R_x of order s^{1/2} and L of order K s one obtains in the worst case only a bound of order eps_v log(s)/s. An inner bound at the level of (39.3) is also needed, and |eta| <= C/s on the inner cylinder does not suffice: with x_5 = 0, the signed column eta = (C/s) 1_{|y'| < M_1 s^{1/2}} sgn(y_5) has compression sigma_4^{-1} (2 C/(3 s)) int_{|y'| < M_1 s^{1/2}} |x' - y'|^{-3} dy' >= (C/(8 s)) M_1^4 s^2 (R_x + M_1 s^{1/2})^{-3} at x, which is of order s^{-1/2} at R_x = M' s^{1/2}. These are statements about the Biot-Savart law, not about solutions.
(4) (Trapping.) The bound |U| <= K alone gives no smallness of the occupation: in the scalar model in which a forward outflow U^R >= k > 0 persists along the backward paths (as an all-time hypothesis this is incompatible with the regularity at the axis, and it is not claimed to be realized by a solution), the radial part is dominated by the positive recurrent diffusion Y, dY = (-k + 3 nu/Y) du + (2 nu)^{1/2} dB, Y_0 = r, with invariant density (k/nu)^4 y^3 e^{-k y/nu}/6. With b := 6 nu/k the drift of Y is at most -k/2 above b, so the entrance time tau_b := inf{u >= 0 : Y_u <= b} satisfies E tau_b <= 2 (r - b)^+/k, and after tau_b, Y is at most b plus a stationary copy started at tau_b with an independent initial value of the invariant law and driven by the later increments of B (synchronous coupling; the drift -k + 3 nu/y is decreasing). Hence, for fixed parameters, P{R_u < h(u)} >= 1 - eps for u >= max{4 (r - b)^+/(k eps), (b + z_eps)^2/M^2} with z_eps the upper (eps/2)-quantile of the invariant law, and, with u_eps the threshold just displayed (of order r/k for fixed parameters and large r), the weighted occupation int_0^infinity Q_1(-a - u)^2 P{R_u < h(u)} du is at least (1 - eps) int_{u_eps}^infinity Q_1(-a - u)^2 du, that is, (1 - eps) times the tail of the envelope budget int Q_1(-a - u)^2 du that (a) gives. This is a lower bound only: the occupation before u_eps is not controlled by the tail. The envelope budget is an upper bound for the budget of |d_Z(q^2)|, not comparable to it in general (a Z-independent q has no source).
(5) (A weaker form of (H4).) (H4) can be replaced in (d)(ii) and (e) by (H4') |d_Z(q^2)(y, sigma)| <= C'' |sigma|^{-1/2} R_y^{-4} for R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2}, sigma <= -a_1, which (H4) implies with C'' M^{-1} in place of C''. In the proof of (d)(ii) the global constant becomes (2/3)(C' + C'' M^{-4}), and the coefficient of C'' in A' becomes (4 + 16/3) M^{-1} + Lambda M^{-4}, the first term from int_0^{t_*} (a + u)^{-1/2} du <= 2 t_*^{1/2} = r/M. Since |d_Z(q^2)| = 2 |Gamma| |Gamma_Z| R^{-4}, (H4') says |Gamma Gamma_Z| <= (C''/2) |sigma|^{-1/2} on the exterior: where the circulation is saturated, its axial scale is at least of the order of the parabolic length. Pointwise neither (H4) nor (H4') follows from the circulation equation with |U| <= K and |Gamma| <= G' on a patch: in the bounded divergence-free field U^R = s (R^2 - R_0^2)/(2 R), U^Z = -s (Z - Z_0) near (R_0, Z_0) (cut off away from the patch), Gamma = G' (1 + erf((Z - Z_0) (s/(2 nu))^{1/2}))/2 is an exact steady solution of the circulation equation on the patch with |d_Z(q^2)| of order G'^2 (s/nu)^{1/2} R_0^{-4} at the front, for every R_0. Part (iii) uses instead the circulation-energy identity (39.9), which bounds the gradient energy met along the backward paths, and so needs no exterior hypothesis.
(6) (Weaker forms of (H2).) In (d)(ii), (d)(iii), (e) and (f)(iii), (H2) enters only through the hitting bound, and that bound uses only a lower bound for the radial drift -U^R + 3 nu/R of the backward paths on the exterior. If, instead of (H2), U^R(y, sigma) <= C_2/R_y whenever sigma <= -a_1 and R_y >= M |sigma|^{1/2}, with a constant C_2 >= 0 and M^2 >= C_2/(2^{1/2} c), then for u < D with u <= t_* the drift is at least -2^{1/2} C_2/r, so R_u >= r - 2^{1/2} C_2 t_*/r + (2 nu)^{1/2} B_u >= r - c r/2 + (2 nu)^{1/2} B_u, and the reflection principle gives P{D <= u} <= exp(-A_0/(4 u)) for u <= t_*. The proofs of (d)(ii), (d)(iii), (e) and (f)(iii) then apply with A_0/4 in place of A_0 (in the constants, 4 nu in place of nu in Lambda, in the last bracket of (39.8) and in the last factor of J). For C_2 <= 3 nu the drift is nonnegative and A_0 itself can be kept. (d)(i) uses (H2) itself, through the supermartingale R^{-2}. In physical variables, u^r <= C/r on {r >= M_0 (T_* - t)^{1/2}} for t near T_* is U_n^R <= C nu_n/R on the corresponding regions, and gives this form with C_2 = C nu for the limits (as in the proof of (f)(v)). When A_* < infinity these forms are also covered by (f)(iv): C_2/R <= R/(2 |sigma|) for R >= (2 C_2 |sigma|)^{1/2}, so U^R <= C_2/R on the exterior implies (H2_kappa) with kappa = 1/2 and max{M, (2 C_2)^{1/2}} in place of M; on the Type I strain branch, u^r(x, t) <= C/r on {r >= M_0 (T_* - t)^{1/2}} (any C, M_0) implies (39.13) with kappa = 1/2 and max{M_0, (2 C)^{1/2}} in place of M_0.
(7) (A kinematic obstruction.) The bounds |U| <= K and |Gamma| <= G', the Type I swirl and compression bounds, the elliptic relation between eta and U and the unsigned source and circulation-energy budgets used above do not imply (H2_kappa) or (39.14): the following field satisfies all of them (it is not claimed to have the other properties of the limits). Let chi be a smooth even function with 0 <= chi <= 1, chi = 1 on [-1, 1] and chi = 0 outside [-2, 2], put g(zeta) := chi(zeta) - chi(zeta - 5)/2 - chi(zeta + 5)/2 and f(zeta) := int_0^zeta g (f is smooth and odd, vanishes outside [-7, 7], f(zeta) = zeta for |zeta| <= 1 and -1/2 <= f' <= 1), and for s := -tau >= 0 put sigma := s + chi(2 s) (so sigma >= 1/2, and sigma = s for s >= 1), H := chi(R/sigma) and, with a constant c > 0,
 phi := H [c (sigma + R^2)^{1/2}/sigma - f(Z/sigma)],   U^R := -R phi_Z,   U^Z := 2 phi + R phi_R,   U^theta := 2 R/(sigma + R^2).
This is a smooth bounded divergence-free axisymmetric field on R^3 x (-infinity, 0] with bounded derivatives; eta := -Delta_5 phi is exactly its omega^theta/R; Gamma = 2 R^2/(sigma + R^2), so |Gamma| <= 2 and Gamma = 1 at R = 1, tau = 0; (U^theta)^2 <= 1/sigma <= 1/s; q is independent of Z, so d_Z(q^2) = 0 and every source budget vanishes; |grad_5 Gamma|^2 = 16 sigma^2 R^2/(sigma + R^2)^4 <= 4 Gamma^2/R^2, so (39.9) holds; a_U = H f'(Z/sigma)/sigma >= -1/(2 s); and |eta| <= C s^{-3/2}, |omega^theta| <= C/s. For s >= 1 and R <= s, |Z| <= s one has U^R = R/s, so (H2_kappa) fails for every kappa < 1, and eta = -c (4 s + 3 R^2)/(s (s + R^2)^{3/2}), so that s omega^theta(R, 0, -s) -> -3 c as R/s^{1/2} -> infinity with R <= s: the vorticity has the critical size 1/s on the whole range s^{1/2} << R <= s, and (39.14) fails. The outflow is produced by the axial part -H f(Z/sigma) of the stream function, whose vorticity is of size 1/s at distances of order s, with return inflow a_U = -1/(2 s) in the slabs |Z/s - 5| <= 1 and |Z/s + 5| <= 1, R <= s; the Z-independent part c H (sigma + R^2)^{1/2}/sigma produces no radial velocity (it contributes only to U^Z), and on the central cylinder {R <= s, |Z| <= s} (s >= 1) all of eta comes from it, since there the axial part is -Z/s, which is harmonic. The field is not a solution. On {R < s, |Z| < s} (s >= 1), P eta = -3 c [(1 + 2 nu) R^4 + (5 + 8 nu) R^2 s + (4 + 16 nu) s^2]/(2 s (R^2 + s)^{7/2}), which is nonzero while the source vanishes (so (39.2) fails), and the circulation residual d_tau Gamma + U^R Gamma_R + U^Z Gamma_Z - nu (Gamma_RR - R^{-1} Gamma_R + Gamma_ZZ) equals 2 R^2 (s + R^2)^{-2} [1 + 2 s a_U + 8 nu s/(s + R^2)] > 0 for R > 0, s >= 1; also its compression satisfies k_V(tau) <= 1/(2 |tau|), which Proposition 33(f)(iii) excludes for bounded mild ancient solutions with nonzero circulation. The member c = 0 shows that the axial flux identity int_{z_1}^{z_2} U^R dZ = -R [phi(R, z_2) - phi(R, z_1)], which with |phi| <= K/2 bounds the mean of U^R over every axial window of length 2 L by K R/(2 L), gives no barrier against arrival: in the central cylinder U^R = R/s and U^Z = -2 Z/s, the backward path X_u from R = a/2, Z = 0 at time -a coincides, until it leaves the central cylinder, with the solution Xbar_u of the linear equations dXbar' = -Xbar' (a + u)^{-1} du + (2 nu)^{1/2} dW', dZbar = 2 Zbar (a + u)^{-1} du + (2 nu)^{1/2} dW^5 driven by the same Brownian motion. With U := a^{4/3}, maximal inequalities for the explicit martingales bound the probability that Xbar leaves {|X'| < a + u, |Z| < a + u} before u = U by C nu (a^{-1} + (a + U)^2 a^{-3}) -> 0, and Xbar'_U/(a + U)^{1/2} is Gaussian with mean a^2 e_1/(2 (a + U)^{3/2}) -> e_1/2 and covariance (2 nu/3)(1 - (a/(a + U))^3) I_4 (the path X itself is not exactly Gaussian; it is so only asymptotically after this rescaling). Hence for each M the cylinder {R <= M (a + u)^{1/2}} is reached before the backward time a^{4/3} = o(a^2) with probability at least P(|N(e_1/2, (2 nu/3) I_4)| < M) - o(1) as a -> infinity. Conversely a_U <= 1/s everywhere for s >= 1, so the arrival argument in the proof of (iv) applies with beta = 1 and gamma = -1 and gives, for a > 4 M^2 and T the first time with R_u <= M (a + u)^{1/2}, P(T <= U) <= 2 M a^{-2} (a + U)^{3/2}, which tends to 0 if U = o(a^{4/3}): the arrival time scale is the one given by the arrival bound of (iv) at kappa = 1 (the occupation bound and the exclusion of (iv) do not extend to kappa = 1). In the scalar model with a prescribed outflow U^R = G R/s, the Z-independent profiles eta = s^{-3/2} F(R/s^{1/2}) with P eta = 0 satisfy (3/2) F + (G + 1/2) xi F' - nu (F'' + 3 F'/xi) = 0, whose power tails F ~ xi^{-p} have p = 3/(1 + 2 G), the exponent of (iv) with G = kappa_1; for G = 1 the tail is s |omega^theta| ~ const, that of the family (this is a tail computation only: by the maximum principle no nonzero solution F is regular at the axis and tends to 0 at infinity, so such a tail occurs only together with a source or a singularity at smaller radii). On the central cylinder the family is, for R/s^{1/2} -> infinity, close to the swirl-free field U_E := s^{-1} (R, -2 Z + 3 c R), an exact Euler solution on R > 0 with pressure -(R^2 + Z^2)/s^2, omega^theta = -3 c/s and transported eta = -3 c/(s R) (U_E is smooth on R > 0, but for c != 0 it is not differentiable across the axis; U^R = U_E^R on the central cylinder and U^Z - U_E^Z = c/(2 R) + O(c s/R^3)); the two residuals above, relative to |eta|/s and to Gamma/s, are -(nu + 1/2) s/R^2 (1 + O(s/R^2)) and 3 s/R^2 (1 + O(s/R^2)). So on the intermediate range s^{1/2} << R <= s, within the central cylinder, both residuals are O(s/R^2) relative to these scales, and the leading meridional field and vorticity agree with an exact Euler solution on R > 0. The residuals are nevertheless nonzero throughout the central cylinder, of relative size one at parabolic radii, while d_Z(q^2) = 0. (Along a path of U_E in the central cylinder R s is constant, so s/R^2 is a multiple of s^3 and its integral against ds/s is one third of its increment: the relative transport defect stays small over an unbounded number of e-foldings as long as the path stays where s/R^2 is small. This is not a matching or stability statement.) In a self-similar model the circulation is incompatible with the outflow. Let Gamma = g(R/s^{1/2}) be bounded, independent of Z and a solution of the circulation equation. On a range R >= M s^{1/2} where U^R = G R/s with G > -1/2, g' is a multiple of xi exp((1/2 + G) xi^2/(2 nu)), so g is constant there. If the equation holds for all R > 0 with a locally bounded U^R, then at each fixed (Z, s) the function g' solves the homogeneous linear equation nu g'' = (nu/xi + xi/2 + s^{1/2} U^R) g' on (0, infinity), so g' = 0, and g(0) = 0 (bounded U^theta) gives g = 0. The exterior equation alone does not suffice: a function vanishing near 0 and constant for xi >= M satisfies it. The threshold kappa = 1 appears also at the inviscid level: if U = s^{-1} W with W swirl-free, axisymmetric, homogeneous of degree 1 and C^2 on {R > 0}, then in polar coordinates (r, theta) of the meridional half-plane, with stream function s R^2 phi = r^3 F(theta) for W, the components of W/r are w_r = F'/sin(theta) and w_theta = -3 F/sin(theta), eta = s^{-1} r^{-1} h(theta) with h = (cot(theta) F' - F'' - 6 F)/sin^2(theta), and the transport equation of eta reduces to 3 F h' + (F' - sin(theta)) h = 0; so on every invariant ray theta_0 in (0, pi) (F(theta_0) = 0) either h(theta_0) = 0 or the radial rate w_r(theta_0) is exactly 1 (for U_E, F = c sin^3(theta) - sin^2(theta) cos(theta), h = -3 c/sin(theta), and the invariant ray cot(theta_0) = c has w_r = 1). Write mu := cos(theta) and A(mu) := s U^R/R for the rate of such a field. On a sector where A is a constant G, s R^2 phi = r^3 (C sin^3(theta) - G sin^2(theta) cos(theta)) = C R^3 - G R^2 Z for a constant C, U^Z = (3 C R - 2 G Z)/s, omega^theta = -3 C/s, and the residual of the source-free equation for eta, diffusion included, is exactly P eta = (1 - G) eta/s + nu eta/R^2; so on such a sector a nonzero vorticity is compatible with the inviscid dynamics only for G = 1. Write s R^2 phi = r^3 p(mu); then A = -p' - 3 mu p/(1 - mu^2). If the field is moreover symmetric under Z -> -Z (so p is odd and p(0) = 0), with 0 < mu_1 <= mu_2 < 1, A = -theta_c on |mu| <= mu_1, A = G on mu_2 <= mu < 1, A <= G everywhere and G + theta_c > 0, then on the polar sector C = int_0^{mu_2} (G - A(m)) (1 - m^2)^{-3/2} dm >= (G + theta_c) mu_1 (1 - mu_1^2)^{-1/2} > 0, so an equatorial inflow forces a polar vorticity of size at least 3 (G + theta_c) mu_1 (1 - mu_1^2)^{-1/2}/s. Since this sector reaches the axis and C != 0, U^Z = (3 C R - 2 G Z)/s is not differentiable across the axis: among fields that are C^1 across the axis away from the origin this configuration does not exist. The transport equation excludes even this. If the field is C^2 on {R > 0} and symmetric in Z, and A(0) = -vartheta with vartheta > 0 (equatorial inflow), then it is the Burgers field s R^2 phi = vartheta R^2 Z, that is U^R = -vartheta R/s and U^Z = 2 vartheta Z/s, with zero vorticity and no outflow anywhere. Indeed, with p as above, p'(0) = vartheta and H := -h = p'' + 6 p/(1 - mu^2), the transport equation reads 3 p H' + (p' + 1) H = 0. For 0 < mu < delta with delta small, p > 0 and (p' + 1)/(3 p) >= alpha/mu for some alpha > 0, so |H(mu)| >= |H(delta)| (delta/mu)^alpha. Since H is bounded near mu = 0 (the vorticity is continuous at the plane), H(delta) = 0; the same holds for mu < 0. Hence H = 0 near mu = 0, and p = vartheta mu (1 - mu^2) there, by uniqueness for p'' + 6 p/(1 - mu^2) = 0 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = vartheta. This profile does not vanish on (-1, 0) or (0, 1), so the transport equation stays nonsingular and p = vartheta mu (1 - mu^2) on (-1, 1) by continuation. For analytic fields the same conclusion follows from the power series at every order: with p = sum_{j >= 0} a_j mu^{2j+1}, a_0 = vartheta, and H = sum_{k >= 1} b_k mu^{2k-1}, one has b_k = 2k (2k + 1) a_k + 6 sum_{j < k} a_j and [1 + (6k - 2) vartheta] b_k + sum_{j=1}^{k-1} (6k - 4j - 2) a_j b_{k-j} = 0, so b_k = 0 for every k. The regularity at the plane cannot be dropped: linearized at the Burgers profile, the transport equation has the indicial polynomial beta (beta - 1)(3 vartheta beta - 5 vartheta + 1), whose root beta_* = 5/3 - 1/(3 vartheta) exceeds 1 exactly when vartheta > 1/2, and the corresponding odd perturbations |mu|^{beta_*} sgn(mu) have h of order |mu|^{beta_* - 2}, unbounded at the plane (the indicial computation proves the existence of no such solution). So in this class an equatorial inflow and a vortical outflow sector are incompatible with the inviscid transport of eta. These statements concern exactly homogeneous fields; a limit need not be asymptotically homogeneous on the intermediate range. Hence a derivation of (H2_kappa), or of (39.14), needs information beyond the bounds, the elliptic relation and the unsigned budgets listed at the beginning of this remark, for instance from the evolution equations of eta and Gamma; the field violates both, so the example does not show that either equation is indispensable. In these terms the missing estimate is the decay of s |omega^theta_U(., -s)| from the parabolic scale R ~ s^{1/2} to the Euler scale R ~ s.
(8) (On (39.21).) (a) The Type I bound for eta does not give (39.21): d_Z a_U = -d_Z^2 phi with -Delta_5 phi = eta is a singular integral of order zero of eta, and at the level of the elliptic relation phi_beta(y) := beta^{-1/2} Psi(y/beta^{1/2}), with Psi smooth, compactly supported and axisymmetric, gives eta_beta := -Delta_5 phi_beta = O(beta^{-3/2}), meridional velocity O(beta^{-1/2}) and d_Z a_U of exact order beta^{-3/2} for suitable Psi (a kinematic statement, not a solution). Heuristically, in the scenario left open by (ix)(2), axial structure of the core swirl on the scale beta^{1/2} produces through the source d_Z(q^2) potential vorticity of order beta^{-3/2} varying on that scale, hence a strain derivative of order beta^{-3/2}, a factor beta^{1/2} above (39.21). (b) (Linearized loop at the collapsing Burgers vortex; a model computation.) For U^R = -theta R/s, U^Z = 2 theta Z/s with theta > 1/2 and q_B := G R^{-2} (1 - e^{-R^2/L_B^2}), L_B^2 := 4 nu s/(2 theta - 1) (an unbounded field, not in the class considered), linearizing P q = -2 a_U q, P eta = d_Z(q^2), a_U = -d_Z phi, -Delta_5 phi = eta about (q_B, 0) gives, for d := d_Z(delta q) and e := delta eta, P_B d = -J_B d_Z(delta a_U) and P_B e = 2 q_B d, with J_B = (2 G/L_B^2) e^{-R^2/L_B^2} (the stretching and compression terms cancel in the first equation). With ||f||_{X_1} := sup (1 + rho^2) |f|, the loop d -> e -> d over one unit of t (no inherited e) has gain at most gamma := g^2 z_0^2/4 = G^2 (2 theta - 1) s_0 k_0^2/(4 nu), by calA (1 + rho^2)^{-m} <= 0 (m = 1, 2), F (1 + rho^2)^{-1} <= 2 (1 + rho^2)^{-2}, (-Delta_4)^{-1} (1 + rho^2)^{-2} <= 1/4 and (1 + rho^2) e^{-rho^2} <= 1. So the one-unit loop map is contractive if gamma < 1, that is, for axial wavelengths l = 1/|k_0| with l/L_B(s_0) > |g|/2, equivalently G^2 (2 theta - 1) s_0 < 4 nu l^2. This condition is sufficient, not necessary: keeping the damping -c_0 z^2 in both equations, with |z| >= z_min := |z_0| e^{-(2 theta + 1/2)} on the unit interval and ||(-Delta_4 + z^2)^{-1}||_{infinity -> infinity} <= z^{-2}, the same comparisons bound the gain also by 2 g^2/(c_0^2 z_min^4), which is less than 1 for short wavelengths (for example theta = nu = s_0 = G = 1 and z_0 = 100). At fixed nonzero z_0 and fixed theta the loop map is -g^2 times a nonzero positivity-preserving operator independent of G, so it is not contractive uniformly in G; this sign is not an energy estimate and implies neither stability nor instability of the coupled evolution, and nothing here supplies the nonlinear smallness, the radial localization or the proximity to the Burgers profile that a bootstrap would need. In an energy topology the coupled linear evolution of each nonzero axial mode decays at a rate independent of G. Let k_0 != 0 (for k_0 = 0 the system is triangular, and for d = d_Z(delta q) this mode has d = 0 and e_t = calA e). Take complex amplitudes, the inner product <f, h> := int conj(f) h rho^3 drho on radial functions, K := (-Delta_4 + z^2)^{-1}, B := (e^{rho^2} - 1)/rho^2 = e^{rho^2} F and E := z^2 <e, K e> + <d, B d> (a quadratic form depending on t through z). Since B e^{-rho^2} = F, the two coupling contributions to dE/dt are 2 g z^2 Re <K e, F d> and -2 g z^2 Re <F d, K e>, which cancel. With D_r := 2 rho d_rho one has D_r^* = -D_r - 8 and [D_r, -Delta_4] = 4 Delta_4, hence Re <K e, D_r e> = -4 <e, K e> - 2 R_e with R_e := ||(-Delta_4)^{1/2} K e||^2; the divergence form calA = c_0 e^{-rho^2} rho^{-3} d_rho(e^{rho^2} rho^3 d_rho) gives Re <B d, calA d> = -c_0 J - 2 c_0 Y with Y := <d, B d> and J := int B |d_rho d|^2 rho^3 drho, and d(z^2 K)/dt = 2 z z' K (-Delta_4) K.
