and z z' = -(2 theta + 1/2) z^2 <= 0 and J = int rho (e^{rho^2} - 1) |d_rho d + 2 rho d|^2 drho + 4 Y + 4 ||d||^2 >= 4 Y give dE/dt <= -8 c_0 E - c_0 J, for every real g. On radial L^2(R^4), calA generates the semigroup T(h) f(x) = (e^{a_h Delta_4} f)(e^{2 c_0 h} x), a_h := (e^{4 c_0 h} - 1)/4, with ||T(h)||_{2 -> 2} <= e^{-4 c_0 h}; the identity for Re <B d, calA d> and J >= 4 Y give ||T(h) d||_B <= e^{-6 c_0 h} ||d||_B on the dense class above, so T extends to a strongly continuous semigroup on L^2(B rho^3 drho). The multiplication terms and the couplings are bounded operators on the product space L^2(rho^3 drho) x L^2(B rho^3 drho), continuous in t (||F d||_2 <= ||d||_B since F^2/B = e^{-rho^2} F <= 1, and ||e^{-rho^2} z^2 K e||_B <= ||e||_2 since B e^{-2 rho^2} <= 1 and ||z^2 K||_{2 -> 2} <= 1), so the nonautonomous bounded-perturbation construction gives a unique mild evolution on that space. Approximating the data by smooth compactly supported radial data gives strong convergence on compact time intervals, convergence of the energies and a space-time L^2 bound for the weighted radial derivatives, and weak lower semicontinuity gives e^{8 c_0 (t - s)} E_t(e(t), d(t)) + c_0 int_s^t e^{8 c_0 (r - s)} J(r) dr <= E_s(e(s), d(s)), the subscript recording the dependence of the form on t; in particular E_t <= e^{-8 c_0 (t - s)} E_s. This concerns data in that product space, not every e with finite z^2 <e, K e> and infinite L^2 norm. This decay of the coupled evolution does not make the feedback iteration contractive: at fixed theta and z_0 != 0 that loop is -g^2 times a fixed nonzero operator, so its norm grows like g^2 in every norm in which that operator is bounded. The energy has three limitations. First, its e-part is weaker than the L^2 norm: the multiplier z^2/(|xi|^2 + z^2) tends to 0 at high radial frequencies for fixed z and as z -> 0 at fixed xi, so the estimate gives no uniform decay in L^2 or in X_1. Second, physical exterior modulations d ~ rho^{-2} have Y = infinity. If d_x solves the uncoupled equation (d_x)_t = calA d_x - c_0 z^2 d_x with the exterior data and d_c := d - d_x (a choice of decomposition, which assigns all feedback to d_c), the pair (e, d_c) is forced only in the equation for e, by g F d_x, and its energy E_c obeys d/dt E_c^{1/2} <= -4 c_0 E_c^{1/2} + |g| ||F d_x||_2 (by z^2 |<K e, f>| <= X^{1/2} ||f||_2, from z^2 K <= 1), in integrated form E_c(t)^{1/2} <= e^{-4 c_0 (t - s)} E_c(s)^{1/2} + int_s^t e^{-4 c_0 (t - r)} |g| ||F d_x(r)||_2 dr, which also covers times with E_c = 0; a forcing proportional to g. Under a weighted bound on the tail a factor |z| is gained: z^2 K <= z^2 (-Delta_4)^{-1} and ||(-Delta_4)^{-1/2} f||_2 <= ||rho f||_2 (dual to Hardy's inequality on R^4) bound the forcing term by |g z| ||rho F d_x||_2, and ||rho F d_x||_2 <= (2/3)^{1/2} ||d_x||_{X_1} by F <= 2/(1 + rho^2). Third, the energy bounds the model analogue of the box source of (39.19) only after integration in time: Hardy's inequality on R^4 gives int rho F |d| drho <= (J/2)^{1/2} + c_2^{1/2} E^{1/2}, with c_2 = (E_1(1) - E_1(2))/2 = 0.0852... (E_1 the exponential integral), and for the homogeneous evolution dE/dt <= -8 c_0 E - c_0 J gives int_s^infinity J <= E_s/c_0 and, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality with the weight e^{8 c_0 (r - s)}, int_s^infinity J^{1/2} <= E_s^{1/2}/(2 2^{1/2} c_0); in the forced core problem the dissipation estimate contains the forcing work, and global time integrability needs control of that term. None of this verifies (39.19) for a limit, and none of it addresses the nonlinear problem or the passage from the Burgers background to a limit. (c) (Radial damping on the axis.) With Q(Z, tau) := q(0, Z, tau) > 0, v := U^Z(0, Z, tau), h := d_Z log Q and C_rad := d_R^2 q(0, Z, tau)/Q, the equation for q on the axis gives h_tau + d_Z(v h) = v_ZZ + nu h_ZZ + nu d_Z(h^2) + 4 nu d_Z C_rad, so d/dtau int |h| dZ <= int |v_ZZ| dZ + 4 nu int sgn(h) d_Z C_rad dZ on the whole axis, in the distributional sense in tau, provided the displayed integrals are finite and locally integrable in time and the boundary fluxes vanish; the axial stretching does not damp this total variation. The radial term damps only under a relation between curvature and amplitude: for the fixed-circulation profiles q = G R^{-2} (1 - e^{-R^2/l(Z)^2}) one has C_rad = -Q/G and 4 nu d_Z C_rad = -(4 nu/l^2) h, but the profiles q = Q(Z) (1 - e^{-c(Z) R^2})/(c(Z) R^2) have d_R Gamma = 2 Q R e^{-c R^2} >= 0 and C_rad = -c(Z), and with Q = Q_0 (1 + eps' cos k Z), c = s^{-1} (c_0' - delta' cos k Z) (0 < eps' < 1, 0 < delta' < c_0') the radial term has the sign of h (it amplifies), although Gamma increases in R and d_R^2 q(0, Z) <= -(c_0' - delta') Q/s. Such a relation is also not propagated by the equation: the evolution of C_rad involves 48 nu q_4/Q, with q_4 the coefficient of R^4 in the expansion of q at the axis; for instance, at an instant at which the meridional velocity vanishes and q is a fixed-circulation profile with Q_Z not identically 0, C_rad = -Q/G holds but d_tau(C_rad + Q/G) = -2 nu Q_Z^2/(G Q), so the relation fails immediately where Q_Z != 0.
Status: (a), (b), (c) and (d)(i) were derived in a parallel line of work and refereed there by independent referees, which repaired the inner coefficient of (c), the passage to the limit in (b) (monotone convergence) and the occupation bound of (d)(i) (the supermartingale and hitting-time arguments above replace a comparison argument that was wrong); the author rederived every step and constant and uses the exact coefficient C_1(delta). The bound everywhere and (39.6) in (d)(ii), and the exclusion under (H2), (H3) and (H4), were derived by the author; that (H2), (H3) and (H4) would suffice together with a separate compression bound at the inner points was noted in the parallel line of work, and the inner points are handled here by the decay (39.6) inside (39.7). A first independent referee of the proposition ((a) to (e) without (d)(iii)) confirmed (a), (b), (d)(i), (d)(ii) and (e), found one false comparison in the proof of (c) (the short-radius case, coefficient sigma_4/2 corrected to sigma_4; (39.4) is unchanged) and asked for the qualifications now in Remarks (1) to (4); the kinematic fields of Remark (1) and the quantitative form of Remark (4) were supplied by that referee and checked by the author. Part (d)(iii) rests on the pathwise circulation-energy identity (39.9), a Lagrangian fluctuation-dissipation relation of the kind derived by Drivas and Eyink for scalars [DE17a, DE17b]; it was found in the parallel line of work in the form of a budget before the first entrance into the cylinders, its combination with the hitting bound, the weights and (39.8) are the author's, and the weaker form (H4') of Remark (5) was found independently in both lines. A second independent referee, of (d)(iii), (e), Remark (5) and the sentences of Remark (2) on the circulation-energy identity, confirmed them with every constant, and observed that the Type I swirl bound of Proposition 33(e)(i) makes unnecessary the compression hypothesis A_* < infinity of the first version of (d)(iii) (the bound by B_theta replaces a bound obtained from A_*), so that (e) holds under (H2) and (H3) alone; it corrected Remark (4) (the entrance time tau_b, and the comparison with the tail, which is a lower bound only) and asked for f with bounded derivatives in Remark (1) and for the uniform bounds on q in place of smoothness in the proof of (iii). The joined energy of the proof of (f)(ii) (q^2 inside the unit parabolic cylinders, |tau|^{-2} Gamma^2 outside, with the favorable kink at the interface), and with it the incompatibility of (H2), and of the exterior bound U^R <= C_d |tau|^{-1/2}, with A_* < infinity, were found in the parallel line of work, with research consultations, and refereed there by an independent referee; the author rederived the argument and added the weight psi = (a + u)^{1/2} and the stopping-time form (39.10). The global compression rate a^{-3/4} in (ii) was noted in the parallel line of work. The global energy of q under the Type I strain bound (the second constant in (i)), (f)(i), (iii), (iv), the outflow hypothesis (H2_kappa), the general form of the proof of (e) and Remark (6) are the author's; the arrival and occupation bounds in (f)(iv) are supermartingale arguments with R^{-beta} (a + u)^gamma. The generator identities for Gamma, Gamma^2, q^2, the two weighted parts of the joined energy and R^{-beta} (a + u)^gamma, and the interface relations of the joined energy, were checked by a symbolic computation, and the constants (4/c^2 = 24 + 16 2^{1/2}, the integrals of u^{-k} e^{-A/u}, the layer-cake integral Gamma(5/2) A^{-3/2}, the exponent identities of (f)(iv), the exponential-integral bound, the weighted integrals, the Gaussian tail bound, the inner coefficient 2/3 and C_1(delta)) by a symbolic and numerical computation; a Monte Carlo simulation of the radial comparison process agreed with the arrival bound of (f)(iv). Two further independent referees, one of (f), the general form of the proof of (e) and Remark (6), the other of the joined energy and its uses in (f), confirmed the Tanaka step with its local-time coefficient q^2/s, both drift bounds, the passage to the limit, (39.10) with E_q and C_eta'', (f)(i), (iii) and (iv) with every exponent identity and constant, the reduction of the bound C_d |tau|^{-1/2} to (H2_kappa), the physical rescaling of (f)(v) and Remark (6). Both found that the general form of the proof of (e) used a reversed inequality (s^{-(3 - p)/2} <= r^{p - 3} for r >= s^{1/2}, false for p < 3); the inner-point estimate above is the corrected one, which keeps the factor s^{-(3 - p)/2} and uses p > 1, and was rederived by the author and checked by a symbolic computation. They also asked for the finite-horizon integrability in the proof of (ii), for the weight comparison with random stopping times, and for the qualification of Remark (1) on A_*; all were applied. Part (f)(vi) and Remark (7) were obtained with a research consultation; the author checked (vi) step by step, with its constants, and the formulas of Remark (7) (divergence, strain, vorticity, the two residuals, the swirl and gradient bounds, the integral pi/(2 d^3) and the covariance and second moment of the linear comparison process for the member c = 0) by a symbolic computation. An independent referee of (vi), Remark (7) and the corresponding summaries confirmed (vi) with its constants (asking for the value J(0)) and the formulas of Remark (7), including both residuals and the similarity equation. It found that the path of the member c = 0 is not exactly Gaussian (the linear comparison process is, and the arrival statement follows by coupling, as now written), that the example shows the insufficiency of the listed bounds and budgets but not that either evolution equation is indispensable, that the Z-independent part produces no radial velocity but carries all the vorticity of the central cylinder, and that the tail computation for the similarity equation is conditional; all were applied after checking. It also observed that in (vi) the condition w -> 0 may be replaced by eventual boundedness of w (split the middle region at |X' - Y'| = epsilon rho), that neither condition can simply be dropped, and that the arrival bound of (iv) extends to kappa = 1 for this field. The comparison with the Euler solution U_E, the relative residuals and the reduced transport equation for homogeneous fields were checked afterwards by a symbolic computation; the statement on self-similar circulations was found in the parallel line of work and rederived by the author; the constant-rate identity, the forced polar vorticity and the series statement for symmetric analytic fields through mu^15 were found in the parallel line of work and checked by the author (the first and the series by a symbolic computation, the second by hand). A sixth independent referee, of these additions, confirmed the comparison with U_E, both relative residuals with their expansions, the reduced transport equation and the ray rule, the constant-rate identity and the integral formula for the polar vorticity. It found an error in the normalization of the stream function of the homogeneous fields (s R^2 phi, not R^2 phi), a gap in the statement on self-similar circulations (the exterior equation forces only a constant; the global equation and continuation give zero), the missing conditions G + theta_c > 0 and smoothness of U_E only on R > 0, the singularity at the axis of a vortical polar sector, and too categorical wording on the global failure; it supplied the recursion at all orders, the argument from bounded vorticity (found independently, in an equivalent form, in the parallel line of work and refereed there), the indicial polynomial and the identity for the paths of U_E. The author checked all of these (the recursion and the indicial polynomial also by a symbolic computation) and applied them. Parts (f)(vii) and (viii) were obtained with a research consultation (the exact angular kernel and its monotonicity in R, the inner points through an auxiliary point at the radius L s^{1/2}, the layer-cake corollary, the reduction of (vi), and the source budget); the author checked every step and constant (the closed form of the kernel against numerical quadrature, its R-derivative and the layer-cake integral by a symbolic computation) and wrote the mass bound (39.18) in the form above, through the subinvariance of dx_3 and the finite-horizon Ito identity. An independent referee of (vii), (viii) and the corresponding summaries confirmed the kernel, every constant of both proofs, the duality direction and the subinvariance argument of (39.18); it found that the reduction of (vi) holds only for M' large (w need not be locally bounded), that the dyadic annuli have area at most, not exactly, 3 pi d_k^2, and that the statement of (viii) overstated the absence of hypotheses on the meridional field (A_* < infinity is one), and it supplied the explicit approximation of |d_Z(q^2)| from below and the example of a profile with bounds of the forms (H3), (H4) and a source not integrable in Z; all were applied after checking. Part (f)(ix) was added later by the author, after the localization 38(e): it repeats the proofs of (vii) and (viii) with the ball radius l_0 s in (39.7) and with the exit probability of the paths from the Euler box bounded by a Gaussian tail; every constant was checked by hand. An independent referee (review 37 in sec. 5) confirmed the Biot-Savart localization, the harmonic term, the inner-point reduction, the localized mass bound (39.20) with its Gaussian tail and every constant, and the example, and required that the conclusions drawn from the example be stated as sufficient conditions for the fixed-amplitude periodic profiles only; applied. It also observed that a budget on the dyadic windows [s, 2s] is equivalent to (39.19), now stated after the example. Part (f)(x) and Remark (8) were obtained with a research consultation; the author checked every step of the proof of (x) (the identity (39.22) also through the equation of omega^r/r, the cylinder identity, the supermartingale, the stopping and averaging arguments, the exit bound and every exponent and constant) and, by a symbolic computation, the formulas of Remark (8)(b), (c) (the similarity form of the background operator, the two inequalities for (1 + rho^2)^{-m}, the potential at the origin, the value of gamma, the Taylor coefficients and the amplifying profile); the axis identity of (c) was derived by hand. The identity (39.22) and its Feynman-Kac representation were also derived in a parallel line of work, where a version of (x) was proved under the additional hypotheses |J| <= C/beta on the tubes {R <= A beta} and |d_Z Gamma_U| <= C/beta for R >= M beta^{1/2}; the second one is needed there because a bound |D| <= C a^{-2} uniform in R leaves a factor log a in the budget from the region a^{1/2} << R << a, which the radial decay factor (1 + R_x/a^{1/2})^{-delta} of the forced part removes in the proof above. An independent referee of (x), Remark (8) and the corresponding summaries (review 38 in sec. 5) confirmed the proof with every constant and found no gap in the implication from (39.21) to the dyadic budget; it required the qualification of the parenthetical remark on R-independent strains, the attribution of the derivative bound in the exit part, separate letters for the compression constant A of (f) and the cone width A_c of (x), the sufficient (not necessary) character of the wavelength condition in Remark (8)(b) together with the short-wavelength bound, the integrability proviso in (8)(c), and the hypothesis A_* < infinity in the summaries. The author checked each finding (including the short-wavelength bound and the formula for d_tau(C_rad + Q/G)) and applied it. Part (f)(xi) was derived by the author and, independently, by a research consultation, which also confirmed that the proof of (x) uses, besides (39.10), the energy bounds of the proof of (ii); the author checked the dyadic bound for g and every place where the compression constant enters the proofs of (ii) to (x). A hostile independent referee (review 39 in sec. 5) confirmed (xi) and the inventory of the uses of the compression hypothesis, and asked for the precise form of the replacement of D_1 (including its occurrence in the forced part of the proof of (x)) and for an unambiguous form of the sentence of (v) on A_* and (CW); applied. Part (f)(xii) was derived by the author, from Proposition 33(a) and Fatou's lemma; it was checked step by step in the parallel line of work (which noted that the factor mu_0 of Proposition 33 may be kept); a hostile independent referee (review 40 in sec. 5) confirmed it with its constants, the window inclusion, the Fatou step, the use of (xi) and the spike example, without repair. The localized form for (CW) was found in the parallel line of work and checked by the author; a hostile independent referee (review 42 in sec. 5) confirmed it, with the supremum defining m_P taken after the pointwise limit, and found that its consequence for (39.13) had been stated without the Type I swirl hypothesis that the proof uses; repaired. Whether the failure of (39.24) forces some limit to fail (CW) is open: only the one-way transfers stated in (xii) and in Proposition 37, Remark (5)(c), are proved; possible obstructions (compression at radii R with R/s^{1/2} unbounded, compression near other points, windows not aligned with the records) were listed in the parallel line of work, none is constructed, and none is shown compatible with the equations. The energy identity of Remark (8)(b), its extension to the mild evolution and the Hardy bound were found in the parallel line of work and refereed there by an independent referee; the author rederived the cancellation, the commutator and divergence-form identities, the square completion and the value of c_2 by hand, and replaced the constant of the forcing bound for exterior modulations (a factor z_0 there is not justified when z < 1; the bound above uses only K <= z^{-2}). The hostile referee of review 40 confirmed the identity term by term, the semigroup bounds, the coupling bounds, the Hardy bound and c_2, and required the restriction k_0 != 0, the sign condition z z' <= 0 in place of z' < 0, a regularity class for the identity and the semigroup construction of the mild evolution, the separation of the decay of the coupled evolution from contractivity of the feedback iteration (a sentence on the weighted supremum norm and on numerical transients was withdrawn), the degeneration of the e-part also at high radial frequencies, the decomposition of the exterior modulations as a choice, and the distinction between the homogeneous and the forced problems in the time integrability; it supplied the factor |z| under a weighted bound on the tail. The author checked these and applied them; the Gronwall justification of the regularity class is the author's. The form of (x) without A_* < infinity and part (xiii): the localization of (x) to the Euler cone was derived in the parallel line of work and refereed there by two independent referees; a hostile independent referee (review 46 in sec. 5) confirmed it with repairs (the energy stopped at the exit time with the terminal term retained, the conditional form for events determined at the stopping time, a sharper exit bound) and supplied the halving recursion for the rate of q under (CW_loc), the bound for the remote part of the core in (vii) and the scope of (xiii); the author checked each step and the constants by a symbolic computation. The exclusion of the bound of (H2_kappa) on the cone in (xiii) was found in the parallel line of work, confirmed there by an independent referee and by a hostile check of the exclusions of (xiii) (review 48 in sec. 5), and checked by the author against the proofs of (iv) and (e). Part (f)(xiv) was obtained by the author with an independent research consultation, which supplied the L^p form of the Nash iteration, the comparison of the kernels at all radii, the localization on smaller cones, the burst profile and the bound without drift, and corrected two steps of the author's first argument (boxes of slope A_3 do not localize the source for points of C_{A_c}, and (39.19) does not bound the source mass on short windows); the author checked each step by hand (the radial integration by parts and the sign of the axis term, the Nash iteration and its constant, the angular comparison, the union bound, the dyadic and Fubini summations, the choice of h, the burst profile and the kernel bound of (5)(c)). Refereed in Review 55. Parts (5)(d), (e), (f) were obtained in a further research consultation (the drift construction, the source pair, the retained-mass estimate, the axial tail bound for the signed solution, the Girsanov comparison, the ring bound of (e) and the dual identity of (f)); the author checked each step by hand (the stream-function formulas and the axis smoothness, the logarithmic ratio and the admissibility of the observation points, the erfc comparison and the two potential bounds, the contribution of older pulses, the Girsanov exponent, the sphere average and the source summation of (e), the adjoint identity and the disk average of (f)). Refereed in Review 56, which confirmed the logarithmic lower bounds for the prescribed-drift linear problem, including the signed-source and strictly subcritical versions, the uniform shear bound of (e) with an absolute constant for every lambda, and the fixed-point dual and flux identities of (f), and required explicit integration over the pulse release times, the localization of the dual calculation, and conclusions that distinguish the reconstructed strain from the prescribed drift and do not assert sharpness or a necessary proof mechanism for Navier-Stokes limits; these repairs are applied. Part (6) was obtained in a further research consultation (the parabolic mass bound with the explicit Nash constant, the signed representation and ring kernel of (b) with the shell summation, the iterated critical-circle identity of (c) and the two constructions of (d)); the author checked each step by hand (the four-ball flux identity, the union bound, the dyadic summation and both bounds for Phi, the Nash constant, Newton's theorem on S^3 and the constants 3 pi/8, 1/(4 pi), 24/pi and 8 J_kappa + 64/3, the containment of Omega, the Green identities, the bound for C_j and the derivative bounds of the test weight in (c), the stream function, the averaging bound and the logarithmic ratio in (d)(i)), and confirmed the identities of (d)(ii) and of the mass process (divergence, vorticity, Delta_5 a = d_Z eta, the mass and axis constants and the required source) by exact symbolic computation. An independent referee (Review 57 in sec. 5) checked the constants, differential identities, estimates and examples of part (6) and asked for repairs of the regularity statement for the Green function, the averaging scale in (d)(i), the description of the required source in (d)(ii) and the scope of the conclusions; these are applied. The estimates of (6) do not establish (CW_loc). Part (7) was obtained in a further research consultation (the weighted packing and the change of quantifiers, the outflow counting with the far field and its constants, the averaged radial flux, the ring example and the weak bound, the survival comparison, the conditional summation with release lengths and the zero-budget case, the coupled identities and the forced expanding pair); the author checked each step by hand (the geometric packing constant, the shell coefficients 9/pi and (32/pi) 4^{-m}, the constants C_0, J_0, J_1, D and C_c, the layer-cake bound, the ring expansion and its error constants, the weak-type constant, the residual of the survival comparison and the scale-function barrier, the substitution in the conditional summation, the zero-budget localization and the half-space balance), recomputed the constants numerically, confirmed the stream function, the coupling, the source, the potential, the exact cost and the moment identity of the forced pair by exact symbolic computation, and checked on a numerical grid the source cost (1.6916 against pi b/tau = 1.6916 in the test units), the sign of the source above the plane and the moment identity. The additive barrier in (d), which removes the hypothesis at large radii, was checked by the author by hand and agrees with a form derived and checked independently in a parallel line of work. An independent referee (Review 58 in sec. 5) checked the constants, estimates, identities and examples of part (7) and asked for explicit standing hypotheses, for the meridional velocity in place of the full velocity in the ring example, the weak bound and the expanding pair, for the exit event in (d) stopped at the given age and the parameter ranges of its equality case and of the small-radius remark, for the parameter ranges in (g) and for a conditional form of (h); these are applied. Part (7) does not establish (CW_loc) for B > 0. Part (8) was obtained in two further research consultations; the author checked by hand the strain envelope and both cases of its window bound, the comparison and the time change and the generator inequality of the occupation bound. An independent referee (Review 59 in sec. 5) confirmed (a) with its constants, the comparison, the time change, the survival bound and the occupation bound with its constants, found that the sentence on the normalized age was wrong for kappa = 0, that the Bessel clock was misnamed, that the description of J as a packet potential was unproved and that the proof of (d) then given was a description rather than a proof, and supplied the optimal constant 1/2 in the generator inequality and the constructions of (d) in the form above (the compensating radial terms and the cutoff estimates of (i), the release radius, the annulus estimate and the kernel bound of (ii), the vorticity masses and the choice of radii for (7)(c)). The author checked each of these steps by hand (the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reduction, the interval bound in both cases, the vorticity of both drifts, the masses 2 pi h nu and 4 pi nu J_F l^2/a^2, the flux formula, the logarithmic ratio and the window integral, the threshold 4 pi/C_c), checked the two inequalities for f also by a numerical computation, derived the pathwise form (39.30) and applied the repairs. Part (8) does not establish (CW_loc) for B > 0.

Proposition 40 (absorption of the backward circulation paths under a small source budget on boxes of large slope). Let U be a limit as in Proposition 37(d) (by the proof of Proposition 37(d), a bounded mild ancient solution whose derivatives of all orders are bounded, with sup |Gamma_U| <= G/gamma_* < infinity), with viscosity nu, K := ||U||_infty and A := sup Gamma_U, put a := U^R/R and a^- := max{-a, 0}, and let X = (R_s, Z_s), s >= 0, be the backward diffusion of the circulation equation of Proposition 26(l) from the record point e_1 at time 0, dR_s = (2 nu)^{1/2} dB_s - (U^R + nu/R)(R_s, Z_s, -s) ds, dZ_s = (2 nu)^{1/2} dB'_s - U^Z(R_s, Z_s, -s) ds, killed at the axis at the time zeta, and p(s) := P(zeta > s). Assume (39.19_H) for some H > K, and let M(beta), F_*, B and r_B be as in the proof of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(3), so that int_r^{2r} M <= B for r >= r_B. With C_N := 2 6^{1/2}/pi^2 (the constant of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(1)) and q_0 := 2^{-3/2} put
 C_ann := (3/(4 pi)) (1 + 1/(1 - q_0) + (2/3) log_2(4 pi C_N/3) + 1/log 2),   A_N := 3 2^{3/2} C_N,   C_abs := A_N + 3 C_N/(1 - q_0) + C_ann.   (40.1)
Numerically C_ann = 1.12052..., A_N = 4.21184... and C_abs = 7.63590...; without numerics, C_N < 3/5, q_0 < 1/2, 2^{3/2} < 3, 4 pi C_N/3 < 4, 1/log 2 < 2 and 3/(4 pi) < 1/4 give C_abs < 27/5 + 18/5 + 19/12 = 127/12.
(a) (The compression averaged over the surviving law.) Let K < E' < E < H, 0 < lambda < E - E' and kappa := 3 pi K/(8 lambda), and let eps_s be the remainder of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(6) for this E. Then for all sufficiently large s
 E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= [(kappa + (C_abs - A_N) B/nu) p(s) + A_N (B/nu) p(s/2)]/s + e(s) <= (kappa + C_abs B/nu) p(s/2)/s + e(s),   (40.2)
with e(s) := 3 ((nu s)^{1/2} + lambda s) eps_s + 3 ||a||_infty exp(-(E' - K)^2 s/(16 nu)), which is integrable on a half-line.
(b) (The cost of eternal survival.) For the killed diffusion above started at any point and time (only the smoothness of U and the finiteness of ||U||_infty and ||a||_infty are used here), the time-integrated compression calH_t := int_0^{t wedge zeta} a^-(X_u) du, with a evaluated along the path at the time of age u, satisfies calH_t - (1/2) log t -> infinity almost surely on {zeta = infinity}. The constant 1/2 cannot be increased in this statement when fields growing linearly in space are admitted: for the linear strain U^R = -k R/(1 + s), U^Z = 2 k Z/(1 + s) at the age s, with k > 1/2, the path survives forever with probability 1 - exp(-(2 k - 1) R_0^2/(4 nu)) > 0 from the radius R_0, while calH_t = k log(1 + (t wedge zeta)). This field lies outside the class |U| <= K; the bounded kinematic version in Remark (9)(h) shows that 1/2 cannot be increased among bounded smooth fields either. Nothing is claimed for the limits.
(c) (Exclusion.) If 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + C_abs B/nu < 1/2, then p(s) -> 0, which contradicts p >= 1/A (Proposition 26(l)); so no limit as in Proposition 37(d) satisfies (39.19_H) with such H and B. Under this condition the backward diffusion from every point (x, t), t <= 0, is killed almost surely, and Gamma_U = 0 identically. For example H >= (1 + 3 pi) K together with B <= nu/32 suffices.
Proof. Fix E', E, lambda and kappa as in (a), put l_s := (nu s)^{1/2} and L_s := lambda s, let gamma and eps_s be as in Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(6) for this E, and put L_a := ||a||_infty, which is finite because U^R vanishes on the axis and grad U is bounded.
Step 1 (two-sided kernel bound). For every x, every L > 0 and every time,
 |a(x)| <= 3 pi K/(8 L) + (3/(4 pi)) int_{B_L(x)} |x - y|^{-2} |eta(y)| dx_3(y);   (40.3)
this is the two-sided form of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(2), obtained in the proof of (xiv)(8)(a) from the Green representation, which is linear in the pair (a, eta). In detail: Delta_5 a = d_Z eta; the Dirichlet Green function of -Delta_5 on the ball B_L(x) of R^5 with pole at its centre is (|x - y|^{-3} - L^{-3})/(3 sigma_4), so a(x) is the mean of a over the sphere plus int_{B_L(x)} d_{y_5} G eta dy_5 (no boundary term, G vanishing on the sphere), and |d_{y_5} G| <= sigma_4^{-1} |x - y|^{-4}; the mean of |y'|^{-1} over a sphere of radius L is a radial superharmonic function of the centre x' in R^4 (approximate |y'|^{-1} by (|y'|^2 + eps^2)^{-1/2}), hence largest on the axis, where it equals 3 pi/(8 L), and |a| <= K/R gives the first term; with D(theta) := R^2 + r^2 - 2 R r cos theta + (z - Z)^2 the angular reduction of sigma_4^{-1} |x - y|^{-4} dy_5 to dx_3 compares r^3 sin^2 theta/D(theta)^2 with r/D(theta) pointwise, through D(theta) - r^2 sin^2 theta = (R - r cos theta)^2 + (z - Z)^2 >= 0, the cutoff D(theta) < L^2 being kept, and this gives the second term.
Step 2 (the envelope on arbitrary sets). The proof of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(6)(a) does not use the axisymmetry of D: it bounds |eta(-s)| on C_E(-s) pointwise by int_s^infinity S(-s, -beta) h_beta dbeta + eps_s and integrates this bound over D using only positivity, the contraction of L^1(dx_3) and the bound of (xiv)(1). Hence, for s >= r_B and every measurable set D in C_E(-s) of volume V, int_D |eta(-s)| dx_3 <= B (1 + Phi(C_N V l_s^{-3})) + V eps_s.
Step 3 (splitting). Put f_s := |eta(-s)| 1_{C_E(-s)} and m_s := C_N B/((1 - q_0) l_s^3) + eps_s. Since Phi(d) <= d/(1 - q_0), Step 2 gives int_D f_s dx_3 <= B + m_s |D| for every measurable D in C_E(-s); for the bounded set D := {f_s > m_s} this says int (f_s - m_s)_+ dx_3 <= B. So f_s = g_s + b_s with g_s := (f_s - m_s)_+, ||g_s||_{L^1(dx_3)} <= B and 0 <= b_s := min{f_s, m_s} <= m_s.
Step 4 (the annulus). Let s >= max{r_B, nu/lambda^2}, so that l_s <= L_s, and let x lie in C_{E'}(-s); then every ball B_r(x) with r <= L_s lies in C_E(-s). For l_s <= r <= L_s one has d := (4 pi/3) C_N (r/l_s)^3 >= 4 pi C_N/3 > 1, and Step 2 with the second bound for Phi in (xiv)(6)(a) gives M_x(r) := int_{B_r(x)} |eta(-s)| dx_3 <= B (c_* + 2 log_2(r/l_s)) + (4 pi/3) r^3 eps_s with c_* := 1 + 1/(1 - q_0) + (2/3) log_2(4 pi C_N/3). Integration by parts in r gives int_{l_s <= |x - y| < L_s} |x - y|^{-2} |eta(y, -s)| dx_3(y) <= L_s^{-2} M_x(L_s) + 2 int_{l_s}^{L_s} r^{-3} M_x(r) dr. Since c_* + 2 log_2(r/l_s) is nondecreasing in r, L_s^{-2} (c_* + 2 log_2(L_s/l_s)) <= 2 int_{L_s}^infinity r^{-3} (c_* + 2 log_2(r/l_s)) dr, so the part of the right side carrying B is at most 2 B int_{l_s}^infinity r^{-3} (c_* + 2 log_2(r/l_s)) dr = B l_s^{-2} (c_* + 1/log 2), and the part carrying eps_s is at most 4 pi L_s eps_s. Since (3/(4 pi)) (c_* + 1/log 2) = C_ann,
 (3/(4 pi)) int_{l_s <= |x - y| < L_s} |x - y|^{-2} |eta(y, -s)| dx_3(y) <= C_ann B/(nu s) + 3 lambda s eps_s.   (40.4)
Step 5 (the density of the surviving law). Lift the sub-probability law F -> P(X_s in F, zeta > s) to an axisymmetric measure mu_s on R^3 (uniform in the azimuth). We show that mu_s has a density rho_s with respect to dx_3 with int rho_s dx_3 = p(s) and
 ||rho_s||_infty <= C_N (nu s/2)^{-3/2} p(s/2) = 2^{3/2} C_N l_s^{-3} p(s/2).   (40.5)
Let U_mer := U^R e_R + U^Z e_Z, V(y, sigma) := -U_mer(y, -sigma), and let S_V(sigma, sigma_0) be the evolution of g_sigma + V.grad g = nu (Delta_3 + (2/R) d_R) g on axisymmetric functions. V is smooth, bounded, divergence-free and axisymmetric with bounded derivatives, and the proof of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(1) uses nothing else, so S_V is positive, contracts L^1(dx_3) and maps L^1(dx_3) to L^infty with norm at most C_N (nu (sigma - sigma_0))^{-3/2}. The generator of X at the age sigma is L_sigma := nu (Delta_3 - (2/R) d_R) - U_mer(., -sigma).grad. Fix an axisymmetric psi >= 0, smooth with compact support in {R > 0}, and let u(sigma, y) := E[psi(X_s) 1_{zeta > s} | X_sigma = y] for s/2 <= sigma <= s. For axisymmetric w one has L_sigma(R^2 w) = R^2 (nu Delta_5 w - b_5.grad_5 w - 2 a w), with b_5 the lifted meridional velocity at the time -sigma; let w be the bounded smooth solution of w_sigma + nu Delta_5 w - b_5.grad_5 w - 2 a w = 0 on [s/2, s] with w(s) = psi/R^2 (smooth with compact support). Then R^2 w is bounded (by the Feynman-Kac formula |w| <= e^{2 L_a s} ||psi/R^2||_infty, and w has Gaussian tails, the drift being bounded), solves d_sigma v + L_sigma v = 0 and vanishes on the axis, and Ito's formula along X, stopped at {R = eps} and at the exit from a large ball, followed by the limits (R^2 w is bounded and vanishes on the axis, and X does not explode), gives u = R^2 w. For smooth compactly supported axisymmetric g, d/dsigma int (S_V(sigma, s/2) g) u(sigma) dx_3 = 0 on [s/2, s]: the transport terms cancel because div U_mer = 0, and integration by parts in R with the weight 2 pi R gives int ((Delta_3 + (2/R) d_R) f) v dx_3 = int f (Delta_3 - (2/R) d_R) v dx_3 - 4 pi int f(0, Z) v(0, Z) dZ for smooth axisymmetric f and v with sufficient decay (here supplied by the Gaussian tails of S_V g used in the proof of (xiv)(1)), whose axis term vanishes for v = u. Hence int (S_V(s, s/2) g) psi dx_3 = int g u(s/2) dx_3, and by duality ||u(s/2)||_infty <= C_N (nu s/2)^{-3/2} ||psi||_{L^1(dx_3)}. The Markov property at the age s/2 gives int psi d mu_s = E[u(s/2, X_{s/2}); zeta > s/2] <= ||u(s/2)||_infty p(s/2), which is (40.5): duality bounds the essential supremum of u(s/2), which is continuous; mu_s is invariant under rotations about the axis, so averaging a nonnegative test function over these rotations reduces the bound to axisymmetric psi; and mu_s does not charge the axis.
Step 6 (proof of (a)). Let s >= max{r_B, nu/lambda^2, 2/(E' - K)} and x in C_{E'}(-s). By (40.3) with L = L_s, the splitting of Step 3 on B_{l_s}(x), which lies in C_E(-s), the identity int_{|z| < l} |z|^{-2} dz = 4 pi l and (40.4),
 a^-(x, -s) <= kappa/s + (3/(4 pi)) int_{|x - y| < l_s} |x - y|^{-2} g_s(y) dx_3(y) + 3 l_s m_s + C_ann B/(nu s) + 3 lambda s eps_s.
Integrate against rho_s over C_{E'}(-s). By Tonelli's theorem and (40.5) the term with g_s contributes at most (3/(4 pi)) ||rho_s||_infty 4 pi l_s ||g_s||_{L^1(dx_3)} <= A_N (B/(nu s)) p(s/2), and the other terms contribute at most (kappa/s + 3 C_N B/((1 - q_0) nu s) + C_ann B/(nu s) + 3 (l_s + lambda s) eps_s) p(s). Off C_{E'}(-s): before the killing the radial drift -U^R - nu/R is at most K and |U^Z| <= K, so R_s <= 1 + (2 nu)^{1/2} B_s + K s and |Z_s| <= (2 nu)^{1/2} |B'_s| + K s; for s >= 2/(E' - K) the Gaussian tail bound gives P(zeta > s, X_s not in C_{E'}(-s)) <= 3 exp(-(E' - K)^2 s/(16 nu)) (a bound at the age s only; no exit time from the moving cone is involved), and this event contributes at most L_a times that bound. This is (40.2), and e is integrable because eps_s decays exponentially.
Step 7 (proof of (b)). Put J_t := int_0^{t wedge zeta} a(X_u) du, T_t := int_0^t 1_{u < zeta} e^{2 J_u} du and, before the killing, Y_t := e^{J_t} R_t. By Ito's formula dY = (2 nu)^{1/2} e^J dB - nu e^{2J} Y^{-1} dt; the strain term -a R dt of dR cancels against d e^J. The local martingale int e^J dB has quadratic variation T, so with the clock tau = T_t it becomes a Brownian motion W up to T_infinity (Dambis, Dubins and Schwarz; extended by an independent Brownian motion on an enlarged probability space if T_infinity is finite), and Yhat_tau := Y at the age T^{-1}(tau) solves dYhat = (2 nu)^{1/2} dW - nu Yhat^{-1} dtau while it is positive. This equation has pathwise unique solutions up to the hitting time of 0 (its coefficients are locally Lipschitz on (0, infinity)), and its solution from R_0 stays positive on [0, n] with probability 1 - exp(-R_0^2/(4 nu n)) (its square Q satisfies dQ = (8 nu Q)^{1/2} dW, a squared Bessel process of dimension zero at the time 2 nu tau, with E exp(-lambda Q_tau) = exp(-lambda R_0^2/(1 + 4 nu lambda tau)), as in Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(8)(b); the diffusion there has the drift +U_mer, so the strain enters with the opposite sign there, and only this zero-strain law is used). On {zeta = infinity, T_infinity > n} the process Yhat is positive on [0, n]; hence P(zeta = infinity, T_infinity > n) <= 1 - exp(-R_0^2/(4 nu n)) -> 0, and T_infinity < infinity almost surely on {zeta = infinity}. No independence of the clock and the time-changed process is used. Since J_t >= -calH_t, int_0^infinity e^{-2 calH_u} du <= T_infinity < infinity there, and since calH is nondecreasing, (t/2) e^{-2 calH_t} <= int_{t/2}^t e^{-2 calH_u} du -> 0, that is, calH_t - (1/2) log t -> infinity. For the linear strain of (b), J_t = -k log(1 + t) before the killing, the clock computed with this deterministic function has the limit 1/(2 k - 1), and the survival probability is the probability 1 - exp(-(2 k - 1) R_0^2/(4 nu)) that the zero-dimensional process stays positive up to the clock time T_infinity.
Step 8 (proof of (c)). By continuity choose E' close to K, E close to H and lambda close to E - E' with kappa + C_abs B/nu < 1/2. For the record start p(s) >= 1/A by Proposition 26(l), and p_infinity := lim p(s) = P(zeta = infinity). By Tonelli's theorem, E[calH_t 1_{zeta = infinity}] <= int_0^t E[a^-(X_u, -u); zeta > u] du. The integral over [0, s_0] is at most L_a s_0, and on [s_0, t] the bound (40.2), with (1/log t) int_{s_0}^t p(u) du/u -> p_infinity and the same for p(u/2) (split the integral where p is within epsilon of p_infinity), gives limsup_t E[calH_t 1_{zeta = infinity}]/log t <= (kappa + C_abs B/nu) p_infinity. By (b) and Fatou's lemma along the integers n, (1/2) p_infinity <= liminf_n E[calH_n 1_{zeta = infinity}]/log n, and since E[calH_t 1_{zeta = infinity}] is nondecreasing in t and log(n + 1)/log n -> 1, the same holds as t -> infinity through the reals. Hence (1/2 - kappa - C_abs B/nu) p_infinity <= 0, so p_infinity = 0, which contradicts p >= 1/A. For a start (x, t) the same steps apply with the physical time t - u at the age u: the envelope, (40.3) and (40.4) are used at the time t - u, that is with l and L computed at s := u + |t|, the bound (40.5) at the age u, and the cone tail with the coordinates of x; the coefficients of p(u)/u and p(u/2)/u in the resulting form of (40.2) exceed those of (40.2) at most by the factor (1 + |t|/u)^{1/2} -> 1, so the limiting inequality is unchanged and P(zeta = infinity) = 0. Since Gamma_U is a bounded smooth solution of the circulation equation that vanishes on the axis, Ito's formula, as in Proposition 26(l), gives Gamma_U(x, t) = E[Gamma_U(X_s, t - s) 1_{zeta > s}] from every point, so |Gamma_U(x, t)| <= sup |Gamma_U| P(zeta > s) -> 0, where sup |Gamma_U| <= G/gamma_* is finite. For the example, H - K >= 3 pi K gives 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) <= 1/8, and C_abs/32 < 127/384 < 3/8.
Remark. (1) (Where the logarithm goes.) The deterministic bound (39.29) controls the supremum of |a_U| over C_{E'}(-v) only on age intervals inside [s, 4s], where it bounds its integral over an interval of length l by C_1 + (C_3 B/nu) log(1 + l), and it applies along a path only while the path stays in the cone; so through the time change of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(8)(b) it gives only a survival bound for paths stopped at their exit from the cone, not the unconditional bound needed here. (A bound C_1 + kappa_0 log(1 + u) along the whole path with kappa_0 <= 1/2 would give decay for a fixed starting radius.) In (40.2) the singular near part of the kernel is integrated against the surviving law, whose density is at most of order (nu s)^{-3/2} p(s/2) by (40.5), so the part g_s of the potential vorticity, of L^1 mass at most B, contributes O(B/(nu s)) with no logarithm, and the bounded part b_s and the annulus contribute O(B/(nu s)) by the envelope. The prescribed drifts of (xiv)(8)(d) violate the vorticity mass bound of (xiv)(6)(a) for their own vorticity (shown in (xiv)(8)(d)) and are not counterexamples to (40.2).
(2) (What is not proved.) (39.19_H) was not derived for the limits, and the smallness of B relative to nu is used: if 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + C_abs B/nu >= 1/2, the inequality (1/2) p_infinity <= (kappa + C_abs B/nu) p_infinity is consistent with p_infinity > 0. Proposition 40 neither establishes nor uses (CW_loc) or a window bound for the compression. Steps 7 and 8 use only the averaged bound: any estimate E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= c p(s/2)/s + e(s) along the record paths with c < 1/2 and e integrable would exclude the limit in the same way, without (39.19_H). The endpoint c = 1/2 is excluded as well. Suppose that E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= p(s/2)/(2s) + e(s) for s >= s_0, with s_0 >= 1 and e integrable on [s_0, infinity). Put b_t := t wedge zeta, and let T_t and T_infinity := lim_{t -> infinity} T_t be the clock of Step 7. The argument of Step 7 applies on the whole probability space: on {T_infinity > v} the time-changed process Yhat is defined and positive on [0, v] (it is evaluated at ages before zeta), so P(T_infinity > v) <= 1 - exp(-1/(4 nu v)) for every v > 0 (the start has R_0 = 1), and hence E[log^+ T_infinity] <= 1 + log^+(1/(4 nu)). Since J_u >= -calH_u >= -calH_t for u <= b_t, we have b_t e^{-2 calH_t} <= T_t <= T_infinity, so D_t := calH_t - (1/2) log^+ b_t >= -(1/2) log^+ T_infinity. On {zeta = infinity}, of probability p_infinity := P(zeta = infinity) >= 1/A, D_n -> infinity by (b), and Fatou's lemma applied to the nonnegative variables D_n + (1/2) log^+ T_infinity gives E[D_n] -> infinity. On the other hand, Tonelli's theorem gives E[calH_t] = int_0^t E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] ds and, for t >= 1, E[log^+ b_t] = int_1^t p(s) ds/s, so for t >= 2 s_0
 E[D_t] <= ||a||_infty s_0 + int_{s_0}^infinity |e(s)| ds + (1/2) int_{s_0}^t (p(s/2) - p(s)) ds/s <= ||a||_infty s_0 + int_{s_0}^infinity |e(s)| ds + (1/2) log 2,
because int_{s_0}^t (p(s/2) - p(s)) ds/s = int_{s_0/2}^{s_0} p(u) du/u - int_{t/2}^t p(u) du/u <= log 2. This contradiction excludes the limit. The lower half of the argument is a necessary condition for every limit: for t >= 1, E[D_t] = int_0^t E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] ds - (1/2) int_1^t p(s) ds/s, and E[D_t] -> infinity as t -> infinity through the reals, since on [n, n + 1] the first term is nondecreasing and the second term changes by at most (1/2) log(1 + 1/n). Hence any estimate that keeps this difference bounded along some sequence t_k -> infinity excludes the limit; the bound with c = 1/2 above is one such estimate. The same argument on {zeta = infinity}, where b_t = t, excludes the limit under the bound E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta = infinity] <= p_infinity/(2s) + e(s). Neither bound has been derived for the limits, and for c > 1/2 the bound does not force killing for the bounded smooth fields of Remark (9)(h)(i).
(3) (The split radius.) The radius l_s of the near ball in Steps 3 and 6 may be replaced by c l_s for any fixed c in (0, 1], with the level m_s, the annulus bound of Step 2 and the outer radius L_s unchanged. The near term then becomes c A_N (B/(nu s)) p(s/2), the bounded part contributes 3 c C_N B/((1 - q_0) nu s), and the annulus, now c l_s <= |x - y| < L_s, is treated as in Step 4 with M_x(r) <= B (1 + Phi(d)) + (4 pi/3) r^3 eps_s, d = (4 pi/3) C_N (r/l_s)^3, using Phi(d) <= d/(1 - q_0) for d <= 1 and the logarithmic bound for d >= 1 (1 + Phi(d) is nondecreasing in r, so the boundary term is absorbed as before). With x_0 := (3/(4 pi C_N))^{1/3} = 0.78349..., the point where d = 1, this gives (40.2) and (c) with C_abs replaced by
 C_abs(c) := c (A_N + C_N/(1 - q_0)) + (3/(4 pi)) (c^{-2} + x_0^{-2} (3/(1 - q_0) + 1/log 2)),   0 < c <= x_0,
which is minimal at c_0 := (3/(2 pi (A_N + C_N/(1 - q_0))))^{1/3} = 0.45770... with C_abs(c_0) = 5.78467...; for c = 1/2 one gets C_abs(1/2) = 5.81064... . So the exclusion of (c) holds under 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + 5.79 B/nu < 1/2. (For c = 1 > x_0 the formula above does not apply and Step 4 gives (40.1).) This changes the constant only; the hypothesis (39.19_H) and the smallness of B/nu remain.
(4) (A smaller kernel constant.) In Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(1) one may take C_N = (3 N/2)^{3/2} for any constant N in Nash's inequality ||v||_2^{10/3} <= N ||grad v||_2^2 ||v||_1^{4/3} on R^3. Indeed, the energy identity and Nash's inequality, as in the proof of (xiv)(1) at p = 1, give ||S(sigma_0 + h, sigma_0)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^2} <= (3 N/(4 nu h))^{3/4}. The adjoint of S(sigma, sigma_0) in L^2(dx_3) is the evolution, backward from sigma, of -v_tau = nu (Delta_3 - (2/R) d_R) v + U.grad v with v = 0 on the axis (the integration by parts identity of Step 5, whose axis term vanishes for such v, with the justification given there). It is positive and contracts L^1(dx_3), being dual to the L^infty contraction of S on every subinterval, and it satisfies the same energy identity in its own time direction: the transport term vanishes since div U = 0, and int v (2/R) d_R v dx_3 = -2 pi int v(0, Z)^2 dZ = 0. Hence the adjoint obeys the same L^1 to L^2 bound, so ||S(sigma, m)||_{L^2 -> L^infty} <= (3 N/(4 nu (sigma - m)))^{3/4} by duality, and with m := (sigma + sigma_0)/2 one gets ||S(sigma, sigma_0)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^infty} <= (3 N/(2 nu (sigma - sigma_0)))^{3/2}. The same holds for S_V of Step 5. In the Fourier bound of the proof of (xiv)(6), ||v||_2^2 <= alpha r^3 + r^{-2} ||grad v||_2^2 with alpha := ||v||_1^2/(6 pi^2), the optimal radius r^5 = 2 ||grad v||_2^2/(3 alpha) gives N = (5/3)^{5/3} (3/2)^{2/3} (6 pi^2)^{-2/3} = 0.20207..., hence C_N = 0.16688...; the sharp constant of Carlen and Loss [CLo], N = 5^{5/3}/(3 2^{2/3} k^2 (4 pi/3)^{2/3}) = 0.058515... with k = 4.49340... the least positive root of tan k = k (the Nash quotient of the optimizer j_0(k |x|) - j_0(k) on the unit ball, j_0(x) = sin x/x, described in [CLi, sec. 4]; a direct quadrature of this quotient agrees with the formula to 24 digits), gives C_N = 0.026004... . In this proposition C_N enters only through (xiv)(1): in the envelope of (xiv)(6)(a) used in Step 2, in the level m_s, in the annulus and in (40.5). Remark (3) holds for every fixed c in (0, x_0], also for c > 1, once s >= c^2 nu/lambda^2 is added to the lower bounds on s in Steps 4 and 6 (so that B_{c l_s}(x) lies in C_E(-s)): in the first inequality of (40.2) A_N is replaced by c A_N and C_abs by C_abs(c), and e(s) by the integrable remainder e_c(s) := 3 (c (nu s)^{1/2} + lambda s) eps_s + 3 ||a||_infty exp(-(E' - K)^2 s/(16 nu)); the second inequality of (40.2) and (c) then hold with C_abs(c). (For both new values 4 pi C_N/3 < 1, so (40.1), whose Step 4 uses 4 pi C_N/3 > 1, is not evaluated with them; the constants below come from the two-regime bound of Remark (3).) C_abs(c_0) is proportional to C_N^{2/3}, and c_0/x_0 = 0.584... does not depend on C_N. This gives C_abs(c_0) = 2.79688... (c_0 = 0.65824...) with the elementary constant and C_abs(c_0) = 0.80990... (c_0 = 1.22322...) with the sharp one. So the exclusion of (c) holds under 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + 2.80 B/nu < 1/2, and, by the sharp Nash inequality, under 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + 0.81 B/nu < 1/2; for H >= (1 + 3 pi) K the budgets B <= nu/8 and B <= 2 nu/5 suffice, respectively. The constants of the later estimates that use (xiv)(1) can be recomputed with these values of C_N, after checking the places where a lower bound on C_N was used (in the shell estimate of (xiv)(7)(b) the condition 2 pi C_N > 1 is then replaced by 2 pi C_N 8^m >= 16 pi C_N > 1 for m >= 1); this is not used here. Among Nash constants the sharp one gives the least value of this argument, C_N = 0.026004... . More generally, no bound that uses only the contraction of L^1(dx_3) and the bulk energy inequality d ||g||_2^2/dsigma <= -2 nu ||grad g||_2^2 (the axis term discarded) can have a prefactor below (4 pi)^{-3/2} = 0.022448..., since the three-dimensional heat semigroup on axisymmetric functions satisfies both and has exactly this prefactor. For U = 0 the exact norm is ||S(sigma_0 + h, sigma_0)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^infty} = e^{-1} (4 pi nu h)^{-3/2}, with prefactor 0.008258...: the kernel of S relative to dx_3 is (4 pi nu h)^{-3/2} e^{-w} sum_{m >= 0} (e^{-x} x^m/m!) (e^{-y} y^{m+1}/(m+1)!) with x := R^2/(4 nu h), y := r^2/(4 nu h), w := (Z - z)^2/(4 nu h) (angular integration of the five-dimensional heat kernel), and e^{-y} y^n/n! <= e^{-n} n^n/n! <= e^{-1} for n >= 1, with equality at x = w = 0, y = 1. This smaller value uses the absorption at the axis, which the energy inequality discards. This changes the constants only; (39.19_H) and the smallness of B/nu remain.
(5) (The heat constant.) In Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(1) one may take C_N = (4 pi)^{-3/2} = 0.022448..., the value of the three-dimensional heat semigroup, and no smaller constant holds for all fields to which the proof of (xiv)(1) applies (smooth, bounded, divergence free, axisymmetric, with bounded derivatives). Proof of the bound. By positivity and |S g| <= S |g| it suffices to take data f >= 0, f not identically 0, smooth with compact support; approximation extends the bound to L^1(dx_3) data as in (xiv)(1). Let g(sigma) := S(sigma, sigma_0) f. If g vanishes at some time there is nothing to prove afterwards, so let N(sigma) := ||g(sigma)||_{p(sigma)} > 0, where p is a C^1 function with values in [2, infinity) and p' > 0, and F := g^{p/2}/N^{p/2}, so that ||F||_2 = 1. The identity of the proof of (xiv)(1) (its justification by the Gaussian tails also covers the derivative in the exponent) gives d/dsigma int g^p dx_3 = p' int g^p log g dx_3 - (4 nu (p - 1)/p) ||grad g^{p/2}||_2^2 - 4 pi nu int g(0, Z)^p dZ, hence, after dropping the axis term, d/dsigma log N <= (p'/p^2) int F^2 log F^2 dx_3 - (4 nu (p - 1)/p^2) ||grad F||_2^2. We use the logarithmic Sobolev inequality on R^3 in its Euclidean form ([Gr]; see also [LL]; it is derived below from Gross's inequality): for F in H^1(R^3) with ||F||_2 = 1 and every a > 0, int F^2 log F^2 dx <= (a^2/pi) ||grad F||_2^2 - 3 (1 + log a). (It follows from Gross's inequality int h^2 log h^2 dgamma - (int h^2 dgamma) log int h^2 dgamma <= 2 int |grad h|^2 dgamma for the standard Gaussian measure gamma on R^3: for F with int |x|^2 F^2 dx finite, which suffices here, the substitution h := (2 pi)^{3/4} e^{|x|^2/4} F gives h^2 dgamma = F^2 dx and int |grad h|^2 dgamma = ||grad F||_2^2 - 3/2 + int |x|^2 F^2 dx/4, since int x.grad(F^2) dx = -3, which is the case a = (2 pi)^{1/2}; the scaling F(x) -> lambda^{3/2} F(lambda x) gives every a. Equality holds when F^2 is a centered Gaussian density of variance a^2/(2 pi) in each coordinate.) With a^2 := 4 pi nu (p - 1)/p' the gradient terms cancel, and d/dsigma log N <= -(3 p'/p^2) (1 + (1/2) log(4 pi nu (p - 1)/p')). Let h > 0 and p(sigma) := 2 h/(h - (sigma - sigma_0)), so that p(sigma_0) = 2 and p' = p^2/(2 h), and stop at the time sigma_P < sigma_0 + h where p = P > 2. Then 4 pi nu (p - 1)/p' = 8 pi nu h (p - 1)/p^2, and with p as the variable of integration log(N(sigma_P)/||f||_2) <= -3 int_2^P p^{-2} (1 + (1/2) log(8 pi nu h) + (1/2) log((p - 1)/p^2)) dp. Since S contracts L^P, ||g(sigma_0 + h)||_P <= N(sigma_P). As P -> infinity, ||g(sigma_0 + h)||_P tends to ||g(sigma_0 + h)||_infty (the function lies in L^2 and in L^infty), and the right side tends to -(3/4) log(8 pi nu h), because int_2^infinity p^{-2} dp = 1/2 and int_2^infinity p^{-2} log((p - 1)/p^2) dp = -1 (integration by parts gives int_2^infinity p^{-2} log(p - 1) dp = log 2 and int_2^infinity p^{-2} log p dp = (1 + log 2)/2). Hence ||S(sigma_0 + h, sigma_0)||_{L^2(dx_3) -> L^infty} <= (8 pi nu h)^{-3/4}, the value for e^{nu h Delta_3}. The adjoint of Remark (4) is positive and contracts L^1(dx_3) and L^infty, and for p >= 2 its L^p norms satisfy, in its own time direction and with the justification given there, the same identity with zero axis term (the transport term vanishes since div U = 0, and int v^{p - 1} (2/R) d_R v dx_3 = -(4 pi/p) int v(0, Z)^p dZ = 0). In detail: for axisymmetric data smooth with compact support in {R > 0} (dense in L^1(dx_3) and in L^2(dx_3)), and in the time t of the adjoint, v = R^2 w, where w solves the five-dimensional equation w_t = nu Delta_5 w + U.grad w + 2 a w (U at the corresponding physical time), whose coefficients are smooth and bounded (a = U^R/R is smooth because U is smooth and axisymmetric); so w and its derivatives have Gaussian tails on bounded time intervals, v = O(R^2) and d_R v = O(R) at the axis, and this justifies the integrations by parts, the derivative in the exponent and the pairing d/dt int (S g) v dx_3 = 0 that identifies v with the adjoint (as in Step 5 for the reversed field); approximation extends the bounds. The zero trace on the axis is essential: for the adjoint the formal axis term would have the unfavourable sign. So the argument above applies to it without change and gives ||S(sigma, m)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^2} <= (8 pi nu (sigma - m))^{-3/4} by duality. With m := sigma_0 + h/2, ||S(sigma_0 + h, sigma_0)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^infty} <= ||S(sigma_0 + h, m)||_{L^2 -> L^infty} ||S(m, sigma_0)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^2} <= (4 pi nu h)^{-3/2}. The same holds for S_V of Step 5, which is the same evolution with the admissible field V in place of U. This is the method of [Da] (a time-dependent exponent combined with the logarithmic Sobolev inequality); the field enters only through div U = 0, and the axis term only through its sign. It uses the L^p identities for all p >= 2, not only the L^1 contraction and the energy inequality, and it reaches the floor (4 pi)^{-3/2} of Remark (4). Sharpness. Let 0 < eps < L and psi(R, Z) := 2 nu Z alpha(R) beta(R) gamma(Z), with smooth cutoffs such that alpha = 0 for R <= eps/2 and alpha = 1 for R >= eps, beta = 1 for R <= L and beta = 0 for R >= 2 L, gamma = 1 for |Z| <= L and gamma = 0 for |Z| >= 2 L, and let U^R := psi_Z/R, U^Z := -psi_R/R, U^theta := 0. This field is smooth (psi vanishes near the axis), compactly supported and divergence free, and on D := {eps < R < L, |Z| < L} one has U^R = 2 nu/R and U^Z = 0, so the equation reads g_sigma = nu Delta_3 g in D (the device of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(5)(d)). For f >= 0 smooth with support in D and M_f := ||f||_infty, the function B := M_f (log(L/R)/log(L/eps) + (R^2 + Z^2 + 6 nu (sigma - sigma_0))/L^2) solves the heat equation in D (Delta_3 log R = 0 for R > 0 and Delta_3 (R^2 + Z^2) = 6), is nonnegative in D and at least M_f on its boundary, while e^{nu (sigma - sigma_0) Delta_3} f <= M_f and g >= 0; so the maximum principle in D gives g(sigma) >= e^{nu (sigma - sigma_0) Delta_3} f - B there. Take f of unit mass in dx_3 with support in {delta < R < 2 delta, |Z| < delta}, delta > eps, and the point x := (delta, 0, 0). Then |x - y|^2 <= 10 delta^2 on the support, so e^{nu h Delta_3} f(x) >= (4 pi nu h)^{-3/2} e^{-5 delta^2/(2 nu h)}, while B(x) at sigma = sigma_0 + h is at most M_f (log(L/delta)/log(L/eps) + (delta^2 + 6 nu h)/L^2), and these are successive finite choices: given delta and f, choose a finite L > 2 delta with M_f (delta^2 + 6 nu h)/L^2 small, and then eps in (0, delta) with log(L/delta)/log(L/eps) small (for fixed eps and delta the ratio tends to 1 as L -> infinity, so the order matters). Repeating these choices along delta -> 0 shows that no bound ||S(sigma_0 + h, sigma_0)||_{L^1(dx_3) -> L^infty} <= C (nu h)^{-3/2} with C < (4 pi)^{-3/2} holds for all these fields. (Each field is bounded with bounded derivatives, but not uniformly in eps and L; the bound of (xiv)(1) uses no such norm.) A smaller constant therefore needs properties of the limit field beyond smoothness, boundedness and div U = 0; for U = 0 the value is e^{-1} (4 pi)^{-3/2} (Remark (4)). Consequences. Since C_N^{2/3} = 1/(4 pi), Remark (3) gives x_0 = (3 (4 pi)^{1/2})^{1/3} = 2.19909..., c_0 = 1.28466... < x_0 and C_abs(c_0) = 0.73428... . As for the values of Remark (4), 4 pi C_N/3 = 0.0940... < 1, so the constants come from the two-regime bound of Remark (3) with the added lower bound on s for c_0 > 1, and the condition 16 pi C_N > 1 of the shell estimate of (xiv)(7)(b) still holds (16 pi C_N = 1.128...). So the exclusion of (c) holds under 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) + 0.735 B/nu < 1/2 (0.735 rounds C_abs(c_0) = 0.734284... up); for H >= (1 + 3 pi) K, where 3 pi K/(8 (H - K)) <= 1/8, the budget B <= nu/2 suffices (the threshold is (3/8)/C_abs(c_0) = 0.5107... with the unrounded constant and (3/8)/0.735 = 0.5102... with the rounded one). By the sharpness statement, 0.734284... is the least value obtainable from the closed form of Remark (3), optimized in c, with a scalar kernel constant valid for all such fields; it is not shown to be an optimal constant for the exclusion, and other estimates entering Remark (3) may be improvable. This changes the constants only; (39.19_H) and the smallness of B/nu remain.
(6) (Envelope form; a limitation.) Example (nu = 1). Let 0 < C <= 1, r_j := 4^j and B_j := r_j^4 for j >= 1, let chi_0 be smooth with 0 <= chi_0 <= 1, chi_0 = 0 on (-infinity, 1] and chi_0 = 1 on [2, infinity), and let f_0 be smooth with support in [1, 2], 0 <= f_0 <= 1 and f_0 = 1 on [5/4, 7/4]. and U^theta := 0 at times >= 0 (the sum vanishes for beta <= B_1). On R^5 = R^4 x R the heat semigroup factorizes, and e^{u Delta_5} [g_0(|y'|/r_j) cos(Z/r_j)] = (P_u g_j)(y') e^{-u/r_j^2} cos(Z/r_j), with P_u the heat semigroup of R^4 and g_j := g_0(|.|/r_j). Since ||g_0||_infty <= 1 and ||g_0||_{L^1(R^4)} = 2 pi^2 int_1^2 rho f_0(rho)^2 d rho <= 3 pi^2, int_0^infinity ||P_u g_0||_infty du <= 1 + 3 pi^2/(4 pi)^2 = 19/16 (contraction for u <= 1, the kernel bound (4 pi u)^{-2} for u >= 1), and by scaling int_0^infinity ||P_u g_j||_infty du <= (19/16) r_j^2. As s + u >= B_j on the support of the j-th term, the integral defining eta converges absolutely and uniformly, with |eta(-s)| <= (19 C^2/48) max{s, B_1}^{-1} sum_j r_j^{-1} = (19 C^2/144) max{s, B_1}^{-1}; the same estimates for the derivatives of the source (each derivative adds a factor of order 1/r_j or 1/B_j) show that eta is smooth with bounded derivatives and solves eta_t = Delta_5 eta + d_Z(q^2). Substituting u = r_j^2 v,

and alpha_{s,j}(v) -> 1 as s -> infinity for fixed j and v. With h_0(y') := int_0^infinity e^{-v} (P_v g_0)(y') dv, which satisfies 0 < h_0 <= 1 (g_0 >= 0 is not identically zero and the heat kernel is positive), and Q_0(R, Z) := (C^2/3) sum_j r_j^{-1} h_0(R/r_j) cos(Z/r_j), dominated convergence (for counting measure in j times dv, since sum_j r_j^{-1} < infinity and ||P_v g_0||_infty <= 1) gives ||s eta(-s) - Q_0||_infty -> 0. and L_j -> infinity as j -> infinity. Suppose (E_M) held for this E with some M, s_E and eps_s. Choose j with L_j > 8 M. So (E_M) fails for every E > 0, every M >= 0 and every remainder eps_s >= 0 with (nu s)^{1/2} eps_s and s eps_s integrable, already on axisymmetric sets of volume o(l_s^3) (without the integrability restriction the pointwise bound above gives (E_M) with M = 0 and eps_s = (19 C^2/144) max{s, B_1}^{-1}). In this example a_U = 0, so every compression bound holds; the mass comes from annuli of radius r_j << l_s on which a source component of amplitude of order C^2/(s r_j^3) with axial wavelength 2 pi r_j is maintained for times much longer than r_j^2 and produces an axial Fourier component of eta of amplitude of order C^2/(s r_j), and the cosine test above gives a mass lower bound of order C^2 r_j on a cylinder of length of order s. The example is not a solution: its eta is not omega^theta/R of its velocity (which is 0), so Delta_5 a_U = d_Z eta fails; and the swirl equation fails, since for beta > 2 B_j the j-th term gives Gamma = C beta^{-1/2} p_j(R, Z) near the annulus with a fixed nonnegative nonzero profile p_j, and at a positive local maximum of p_j one has Gamma_t = (C/2) beta^{-3/2} p_j > 0 >= Gamma_RR - R^{-1} Gamma_R + Gamma_ZZ. Hence the Type I swirl bound, boundedness, regularity and the linear properties of S (or of its adjoint, in a divergence form of the source) do not imply (E_M); a derivation for the limits must use some property not shared by this example, such as the circulation equation or the identification of eta with the potential vorticity of the drift (the example also vanishes for -B_1 <= t and does not satisfy the normalization of the limits). The arguments here do not establish (E_M) for the limits, with M of order S_theta := sup_beta beta ||U^theta(-beta)||_infty^2 or otherwise; S_theta/nu is dimensionless and invariant under the scaling of the equations, so it cannot be made small by the choice of scale, and no estimate giving the required smallness is derived here. Induced strain of the example. The example has a_U = 0. The auxiliary strain a_eta defined below, which eta would induce through Delta_5 a = d_Z eta, satisfies an inequality of the numerical form of Remark (2) when averaged against the fixed paths of the example, which have zero meridional drift; these are not the paths of a velocity whose strain is a_eta. Precisely, for s >= 1 let F(-s) be a bounded solution of Delta_5 F = eta(-s) on R^5 (unique up to an additive constant, since bounded harmonic functions on R^5 are constant) and a_eta(-s) := d_Z F(-s); it is the strain V^R/R of the divergence-free meridional field V^R := R d_Z F, V^Z := -2 F - R d_R F, whose omega^theta/R equals Delta_5 F = eta(-s). Then, for the killed diffusion X of the example (U^R = U^Z = 0, nu = 1),
 s E[|a_eta|(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= 0.16 C^2 s^{-1/2} p(s/2)   (s >= 1),
so E[a_eta^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= c p(s/2)/s for s >= 1 with the fixed constant c = 0.16 C^2 <= 0.16 < 1/2 and e = 0 (indeed with 0.16 C^2 s^{-1/2} in place of c). Proof. By the formula for eta above, eta(-s) = sum_j A_{j,s}(R) cos(Z/r_j) with A_{j,s}(y') = (C^2/3) r_j^{-1} int_0^infinity chi_0((s + r_j^2 v)/B_j)^2 (s + r_j^2 v)^{-1} e^{-v} (P_v g_0)(y'/r_j) dv; the integrand vanishes unless v >= v_j := (B_j - s)_+/r_j^2, so 0 <= A_{j,s}(y') <= (C^2/(3 s r_j)) H_{j,s}(y'/r_j) with H_{j,s} := int_{v_j}^infinity e^{-v} P_v g_0 dv, and ||H_{j,s}||_infty <= e^{-v_j}. Put K_{j,s} := (r_j^{-2} - Delta_4)^{-1} A_{j,s} >= 0 (resolvent of the heat semigroup of R^4, a positive operator of norm r_j^2 on L^infinity), so ||K_{j,s}||_infty <= C^2 r_j e^{-v_j}/(3 s) and sum_j ||K_{j,s}||_infty < infinity. Since Delta_5 [K(y') cos(Z/r)] = -((r^{-2} - Delta_4) K)(y') cos(Z/r), F := -sum_j K_{j,s}(y') cos(Z/r_j) is a bounded solution, and a_eta(-s) = sum_j r_j^{-1} K_{j,s}(R) sin(Z/r_j). The function R^2 is annihilated by the radial generator d_RR - R^{-1} d_R of X (nu = 1, U^R = U^Z = 0), and the h-transform of the killed radial process with h = R^2 is the radial part of a Brownian motion on R^4 with generator Delta_4; hence E[f(X_s); zeta > s] = E[f(|Y'_s|, Y''_s) |Y'_s|^{-2}] for measurable f >= 0, where (Y', Y'') is the Brownian motion on R^4 x R with generator Delta_5 started at (e, 0), |e| = 1 (f = 1 gives p(s) = 1 - e^{-1/(4 s)}). The density of Y'_s is at most (4 pi s)^{-2}, and |sin| <= 1, so

For t > 0, e^{t Delta_4} |y'|^{-2} = (1 - e^{-|y'|^2/(4t)}) |y'|^{-2} <= |y'|^{-2}; by symmetry of the semigroup, int (e^{t Delta_4} k) |y'|^{-2} dy' <= int k |y'|^{-2} dy' for k >= 0, hence int K_{j,s} |y'|^{-2} dy' <= r_j^2 int A_{j,s} |y'|^{-2} dy' <= (C^2 r_j^3/(3 s)) int H_{j,s}(w) |w|^{-2} dw <= (C^2 r_j^3/(3 s)) e^{-v_j} int g_0(w) |w|^{-2} dw, and int_{R^4} g_0(w) |w|^{-2} dw = 2 pi^2 int_1^2 f_0(rho)^2 rho^{-1} d rho <= 2 pi^2 log 2. Therefore E[|a_eta|(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= (log 2/24) C^2 s^{-3} S(s) with S(s) := sum_j r_j^2 e^{-v_j}. The terms with B_j <= s sum to at most (16/15) s^{1/2} (geometric with ratio 1/16 below r_J^2 <= s^{1/2}). For B_j > s write r_j^2 = x s^{1/2} with x > 1; the term equals s^{1/2} x e^{-s^{1/2}(x - 1/x)}, which is at most s^{1/2} phi(x) for s >= 1, phi(x) := x e^{-(x - 1/x)}, which decreases on [1, infinity) from phi(1) = 1, and successive values of x grow by the factor 16, so these terms sum to at most s^{1/2}(1 + sum_{k >= 1} phi(16^k)) < 1.0001 s^{1/2}. Thus S(s) <= 2.07 s^{1/2} for s >= 1. Finally p(s/2) = 1 - e^{-1/(2 s)} >= 3/(8 s) for s >= 1, and (8/3)(2.07 log 2)/24 < 0.16. This computation uses the explicit transition law available when U^R = U^Z = 0 (in Step 6 the average over the law of X_s is bounded only through its total mass p(s), the density bound (40.5) and a Gaussian tail bound outside the cone); it does not remove any of the structural or path hypotheses retained in Proposition 40. Near the axis the individual terms are not small compared with 1/s: if 2 B_j <= s, then chi_0 = 1 in the formula for A_{j,s} and s + r_j^2 v <= 2 s for v <= s/r_j^2, where s/r_j^2 >= (2 s)^{1/2} > 1, so A_{j,s}(y') >= (C^2/(6 s r_j)) h_1(y'/r_j) with h_1 := int_0^1 e^{-v} P_v g_0 dv, and the amplitude r_j^{-1} K_{j,s}(0) of the j-th term of a_eta(-s) on the axis is at least c_1 C^2/s with c_1 := ((1 - Delta_4)^{-1} h_1)(0)/6 > 0, which depends only on f_0; the killed law gives the region near the axis a small weight, P(R_s <= L, zeta > s) <= (4 pi s)^{-2} int_{|y'| <= L} |y'|^{-2} dy' = L^2/(16 s^2). A numerical evaluation in the parallel line of work (one profile f_0 with cos^2 ramps, C = 1, the limiting coefficients of the fully active annuli, the axial Gaussian replaced by the average over a period) gave values of s E[|a_eta|(X_s, -s); zeta > s]/p(s/2) smaller than 0.16 s^{-1/2} by factors between 47 and 290 at s = 10^4, 10^6, 10^8 and 10^12, and, at the same s, values below 0.021 for the largest value of (s/p(s/2)) int a_eta^- rho dx_3 over all densities 0 <= rho <= 2^{3/2} C_N (nu s)^{-3/2} p(s/2) of mass at most p(s/2) carried by the cone with E = 2, that is, under the information on the law that Step 6 uses (the extremal density is the cap on a superlevel set of a_eta^-). These are computations at four values of s, not proofs. The parallel line of work reports these values as lower approximations to a discretized optimum, and a refined value of approximately 0.0224 near the activation times s = 2 B_j; no certified comparison with the optimum for the exact coefficients A_{j,s} is established here. A bound uniform in s that uses only the density bound on the cone holds with a larger constant. Since K_{j,s} >= 0, a_eta^-(-s) <= sum_j r_j^{-1} K_{j,s}(R) sin^-(Z/r_j).
