By (40.5) the density of the killed law at time s on the cone is such a density. With the heat constant C_N = (4 pi)^{-3/2} of Remark (5), which applies to the meridional field of the example (it is zero), the right side is at most C^2 (0.122 E + 0.373 s^{-3/4}); it is below 1/2 for E <= 2, C <= 1 and s >= 2 (below 0.466 at E = 2, s = 2). The bound holds for every f_0 as above and includes all annuli with their exact coefficients A_{j,s}. It concerns the event that X_s lies in the cone; the bound over all space proved above is a separate statement. So, for this auxiliary source, the failure of (E_M) is compatible with the averaged inequality for its induced strain under the fixed driftless killed law, also when the average over the cone is bounded through the density bound (40.5) alone: the example obstructs the derivation of (E_M) from the uncoupled linear properties listed above, and it is neither a counterexample to nor a proof of the averaged criterion for the strain and the paths of one velocity field. This remark does not change the hypotheses of the proposition beyond replacing (39.19_H) by (E_M); the smallness of M/nu remains.
(7) (Every Type I swirl in the driftless linear model.) The averaged bound for the induced strain in Remark (6) is not special to the example. Let U^theta(., -beta), beta > 0, be any axisymmetric swirl, with no equation imposed on it, such that U^theta e_theta is a smooth vector field across the axis with bounded derivatives on every time slab R^3 x [-beta_1, -beta_0], 0 < beta_0 < beta_1 < infinity, and |U^theta(., -beta)| <= C beta^{-1/2} for all beta > 0. Then q := U^theta/R and its radial lift to R^5 are smooth with bounded derivatives on every such slab (q(R, Z, -beta) = int_0^1 d_R U^theta(lambda R, Z, -beta) d lambda), and f^sw_beta := q^2(., -beta) satisfies 0 <= f^sw_beta <= C^2 beta^{-1} w_inv, with w_inv(y') := |y'|^{-2}. Define eta(-s) := int_0^infinity e^{u Delta_5} [d_Z(q^2)(-s - u)] du as in Remark (6) (nu = 1, b_5 = 0), and a_eta(-s) := d_Z F, where F is a bounded classical solution of Delta_5 F = eta(-s) on all of R^5, whose existence is proved in (iii); two such solutions differ by a bounded harmonic function, hence by a constant, so a_eta(-s) is well defined. With X the driftless killed diffusion of Remark (6) (nu = 1, U^R = U^Z = 0, started at (R, Z) = (1, 0)), for every s > 0
 E[|a_eta|(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= (2 pi e)^{-1/2} sigma_3 C^2/(8 s^2),   sigma_3 := sum_{n >= 1} n^{-3} = 1.2020...,
and hence, since p(s/2) = 1 - e^{-1/(2s)} >= (1 - e^{-1/2})/s for s >= 1 by concavity,
 s E[|a_eta|(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= 0.0925 C^2 p(s/2)   (s >= 1).
So the induced strain of every such swirl satisfies, under the fixed driftless law, an inequality of the form of Remark (2) with c = 0.0925 C^2 (below 1/2 for C <= 2) and e(s) = 0. Proof. (i) Let h_t be the heat kernel of d_ZZ. Its second derivative h_t'' = (Z^2/(4 t^2) - 1/(2 t)) h_t is negative for |Z| < (2 t)^{1/2}, positive for |Z| > (2 t)^{1/2}, and has integral zero, so int (h_t'')_+ dZ = int (h_t'')_- dZ = -2 h_t'((2 t)^{1/2}) = (2 pi e)^{-1/2}/t. Since e^{t Delta_5} = e^{t Delta_4} e^{t d_ZZ}, and for fixed y' the axial convolutions of a function 0 <= g(y', .) <= m(y') against the two parts of h_t'' both lie between 0 and (2 pi e)^{-1/2} m(y')/t, |d_Z^2 e^{t Delta_5} g| <= ((2 pi e)^{-1/2}/t) e^{t Delta_4} m wherever the right side is finite. (ii) With w_inv = int_0^infinity e^{-lambda |y'|^2} d lambda and e^{t Delta_4} e^{-lambda |.|^2}(x) = (1 + 4 t lambda)^{-2} exp(-lambda |x|^2/(1 + 4 t lambda)), the substitution b = lambda/(1 + 4 t lambda) gives e^{t Delta_4} w_inv(x) = int_0^{1/(4t)} e^{-b |x|^2} db = (1 - e^{-|x|^2/(4t)}) |x|^{-2} <= min{|x|^{-2}, 1/(4t)}, the identity used in Remark (6) (at x = 0 the quotient is read by continuity as 1/(4t)). (iii) Fix s and put m_1 := sup_{0 <= u <= 1} ||f^sw_{s+u}||_infty. Since ||h_u'||_{L^1} = (pi u)^{-1/2}, (ii) gives ||d_Z e^{u Delta_5} f^sw_{s+u}||_infty <= m_1 (pi u)^{-1/2} for 0 < u <= 1 and <= C^2 pi^{-1/2} u^{-3/2}/(4 (s + u)) for u >= 1, so the integral defining eta(-s) converges absolutely in the uniform norm, and eta(-s) is smooth (differentiate the source on bounded time intervals and the Gaussian kernel in the remote-past tail). The integral F_s := -int_0^infinity du int_u^infinity d_Z e^{t Delta_5} f^sw_{s+u} dt also converges absolutely in the uniform norm, with ||F_s||_infty <= (C^2/(4 pi^{1/2})) int_0^infinity t^{-3/2} log(1 + t/s) dt = pi^{1/2} C^2/(2 s^{1/2}). For 0 < epsilon < L < T, by Delta_5 e^{t Delta_5} = d_t e^{t Delta_5} the Laplacian of the integral truncated to epsilon <= u <= L and u <= t <= T is int_epsilon^L d_Z e^{u Delta_5} f^sw_{s+u} du - int_epsilon^L d_Z e^{T Delta_5} f^sw_{s+u} du; the second term tends to zero uniformly as T -> infinity, and the bounds above allow epsilon -> 0 and L -> infinity, so Delta_5 F_s = eta(-s) in the sense of distributions, and F_s is a classical solution by local elliptic regularity. F_s may be differentiated once more in Z under the integral: by (i), the part 0 <= u <= t <= 1 contributes at most (2 pi e)^{-1/2} m_1 in the uniform norm, and the part t >= 1 at most (2 pi e)^{-1/2} (C^2/4) int_1^infinity t^{-2} log(1 + t/s) dt (take m := C^2 w_inv/(s + u) and use (ii)). Hence a_eta(-s) = -int_0^infinity du int_u^infinity d_Z^2 e^{t Delta_5} f^sw_{s+u} dt. (iv) By (i) with m := C^2 w_inv/(s + u), Tonelli's theorem and int_0^t du/(s + u) = log(1 + t/s), for R > 0, |a_eta(R, Z, -s)| <= (2 pi e)^{-1/2} C^2 int_0^infinity t^{-1} log(1 + t/s) (e^{t Delta_4} w_inv)(R) dt (this majorant is infinite at R = 0, where a_eta(-s) is bounded by (iii)). (v) By the h-transform identity of Remark (6), E[|a_eta|(X_s, -s); zeta > s] <= (2 pi e)^{-1/2} C^2 int_0^infinity t^{-1} log(1 + t/s) W_s(t) dt with W_s(t) := E[w_inv(Y'_s) (e^{t Delta_4} w_inv)(Y'_s)] (only the law of Y'_s enters, since the majorant does not depend on Z). By (ii), w_inv e^{t Delta_4} w_inv = int_0^infinity da int_0^{1/(4t)} db e^{-(a + b) |y'|^2}, and the Gaussian formula of (ii) at time s, with its exponential factor dropped, gives W_s(t) <= int_0^{1/(4t)} db int_0^infinity (1 + 4 s (a + b))^{-2} da = log(1 + s/t)/(16 s^2). (vi) With t = s x and then r = x/(1 + x), int_0^infinity x^{-1} log(1 + x) log(1 + 1/x) dx = int_0^1 log r log(1 - r) (r (1 - r))^{-1} dr = 2 int_0^1 r^{-1} log r log(1 - r) dr = 2 sigma_3, by the expansion -log(1 - r) = sum_{n >= 1} r^n/n and int_0^1 r^{n - 1} (-log r) dr = n^{-2}. This proves the first bound; (2 pi e)^{-1/2} sigma_3/(8 (1 - e^{-1/2})) = 0.09240... gives the second, and a_eta^- <= |a_eta|. Among the assumptions on the source, the numerical estimates use only |U^theta(., -beta)| <= C beta^{-1/2} and q^2 >= 0; they also use nu = 1 and the exact driftless killed law started at (1, 0). The boundedness of q on slabs is used for the convergence and the differentiation near zero heat time, and the smoothness for the classical interpretation of the fields; no derivative bound uniform over the whole past, no bound on R U^theta, no evolution equation for the source, no time monotonicity, no restriction on the phases, no fixed axial wavelength and no vanishing near time zero is used. For R > 0, splitting the integral in (iv) at R^2/4 and s when R^2 <= 4 s, and only at s (with R^{-2} <= (4 s)^{-1} below s) when R^2 > 4 s, gives the envelope |a_eta(R, Z, -s)| <= ((2 pi e)^{-1/2} C^2/(4 s)) (1 + 2 log 2 + log_+(4 s/R^2)), with log_+ v := max{log v, 0} (the integral of log(1 + x)/x^2 over x >= 1 is 2 log 2); so s |a_eta(-s)| <= 0.23 C^2 on {R >= s^{1/2}} for every such source, while near the axis this upper envelope grows logarithmically (it is an upper bound, not a statement that a_eta diverges at the axis). The bound concerns the auxiliary strain constructed from the displayed source integral, under the fixed driftless killed law with nu = 1 and start (1, 0); it does not estimate the strain and the paths of a single velocity field. For the limits of Case 1, (39.2) uses a five-dimensional backward diffusion with drift -b_5, not killed, started at the evaluation point and time, while the average in (c) uses the circulation diffusion, with radial drift -U^R - nu/R, killed at the axis; the actual eta and a_U = U^R/R are coupled to the same velocity; the absence of a homogeneous term in eta follows for the limits from the decay in the remote past used in (39.2) (the source-only definition here permits none); in the units of the limits the coefficient of the driftless computation is 0.0925 C^2/nu = 0.0925 C_I (Proposition 33(e)(i): C^2 = C_I/gamma_* and nu = 1/gamma_*), and no smallness of C_I is established; and the limits satisfy the circulation equation and the record normalization, which are not imposed on this model. Thus arbitrary time and axial dependence of the source does not defeat this driftless auxiliary estimate, in contrast with (E_M) (the example above); no conclusion about the averaged criterion for the limits, or about the cause of its possible failure, follows, and this remark does not change the hypotheses of the proposition.
(8) (The density bound and the mass alone do not give a uniform cone estimate.) For a general drifted law the proof of Remark (7) cannot be applied using only (40.5) and the mass; the properties of the law at the age s used on the cone in Step 6 (the integration against rho_s) are its mass, p(s) <= p(s/2), and (40.5), which with nu = 1 and the heat constant of Remark (5) reads rho_s <= A_h s^{-3/2} p(s/2), A_h := 2^{3/2} (4 pi)^{-3/2} = (2 pi)^{-3/2}. Consider the auxiliary strain a_eta of Remark (7) (nu = 1), the cone C^0_E(-s) := {max(R, |Z|) < E s}, E >= 1, and k_e := (2 pi e)^{-1/2}. For each fixed s, the best constant c that these two properties alone give in the cone estimate s int_{C^0_E(-s)} a_eta^-(., -s) rho_s dx_3 <= c p(s/2) (the cone part of an inequality of the form of Remark (2) with e(s) = 0) is, by the bathtub principle,
 B^mass(s) := A_h s^{-1/2} sup{int_calS a_eta^-(., -s) dx_3 : calS measurable, calS in C^0_E(-s), |calS| <= s^{3/2}/A_h},
which equals (s/p(s/2)) sup{int_{C^0_E(-s)} a_eta^-(., -s) rho dx_3 : 0 <= rho <= A_h s^{-3/2} p(s/2), int rho dx_3 <= p(s/2)} for every value p(s/2) > 0 (|calS| is the volume in dx_3). (a) For every source as in Remark (7) and every s >= 1, B^mass(s) <= (k_e C^2/4)(2 + 2 log 2 + log(8 pi E A_h) + (1/2) log s); for E = 2 this is at most C^2 (0.2751 + 0.0303 log s). (b) For E = 2 there is a source as in Remark (7) with C = 1, |R U^theta| <= 2 and U^theta = 0 for beta <= e^{32}, such that B^mass(s_n) >= (log s_n)/9216 - 1 - (3 log 2)/1024 for s_n := e^{32 n}, n >= 1; this lower bound exceeds 1/2 first at n = 433. Multiplying the source by C > 0 multiplies a_eta and B^mass by C^2. Thus, for every C > 0, these two properties alone give no constant c, uniform in s and over the sources of Remark (7), in the cone estimate with e(s) = 0, whereas the exact driftless law gives c = 0.0925 C^2 (Remark (7)). Since (b) bounds B^mass from below only at the ages s_n, it does not exclude an estimate with an integrable remainder e(s) as allowed in Remark (2) (if p(s/2) <= c'/s, (a) itself gives one with c = 0), and since Step 8 uses (40.2) only through the averages (1/log t) int^t of the coefficients of p(u)/u and p(u/2)/u, (b) does not show that these two properties fail to give what Step 8 needs; (d) shows that they do not give it uniformly over the densities with the cap (40.5) and a prescribed mass with 0 < p_0 <= p(s) <= p(s/2) <= 1, as for the record start.
Proof of (a). By the envelope of Remark (7), a_eta^-(., -s) <= (k_e C^2/(4 s))(1 + 2 log 2 + log_+(4 s/R^2)). Let M_vol := s^{3/2}/A_h and calS be as above. calS lies in the cylinder {R < E s, |Z| < E s}, which meets {log_+(4 s/R^2) > v}, v >= 0, in a volume at most 8 pi E s^2 e^{-v}, so the layer-cake formula gives int_calS log_+(4 s/R^2) dx_3 <= int_0^infinity min{M_vol, 8 pi E s^2 e^{-v}} dv = M_vol (1 + log(8 pi E A_h s^{1/2})), since 8 pi E A_h s^{1/2} > 1. With A_h s^{-1/2} M_vol/s = 1 this gives (a).
Proof of (b). Let b(x) := e^{-1/x} for x > 0, b(x) := 0 for x <= 0, and st(x) := b(x)/(b(x) + b(1 - x)), a smooth function with 0 <= st <= 1, st = 0 on x <= 0 and st = 1 on x >= 1. For s = s_n put Lambda_s := 16 s^{1/2}, chi^t_s(u) := st(u) st(2 - 2u/s), chi^r_s(R) := st(4 - R^2/s), m^r_s(R) := chi^r_s(R)^2/(1 + R^2) and Theta_{s,v}(Z) := sum_{k in Z} e^{-(Z - k Lambda_s)^2/(4 v)} for v > 0, a smooth Lambda_s-periodic function of Z (on a period cell the series and all its derivatives in Z and v converge uniformly for v in [1, 2 s], and periodicity gives the same bounds on the whole axis). The source is
 U^theta(R, Z, -beta) := R chi^t_{s_n}(beta - s_n) chi^r_{s_n}(R) (beta (1 + R^2))^{-1/2} (1 - Theta_{s_n, beta - s_n + 1}(Z)/2)^{1/2} for s_n < beta < 2 s_n, n >= 1,
and U^theta := 0 for all other beta > 0 (the windows (s_n, 2 s_n) are disjoint). Hypotheses: for 1 <= v <= 2 s the lattice points other than the one nearest to Z lie at distances at least (j - 1/2) Lambda_s from Z, at most two for each j >= 1, so Theta_{s,v} <= 1 + 2 sum_{j >= 1} e^{-32 (j - 1/2)^2} <= 1 + 2/(e^8 - 1) < 3/2 and the radicand exceeds 1/4. Hence q = U^theta/R is a smooth function of R^2, Z and beta on each window, with bounded derivatives there; chi^t_s is flat at both ends of its window, so U^theta e_theta is smooth across the axis and across the window ends, with bounded derivatives on every time slab (a slab meets finitely many windows). All factors other than R (beta (1 + R^2))^{-1/2} are at most 1, so |U^theta| <= beta^{-1/2}; since chi^r_s vanishes for R^2 >= 4 s and beta > s, |R U^theta| <= R^2 (beta (1 + R^2))^{-1/2} <= R beta^{-1/2} <= 2.
Representation. Fix n and s := s_n. By (iii) of Remark (7), a_eta(-s) = -int_0^infinity dt int_0^t du d_Z^2 e^{t Delta_5} f^sw_{s+u}, and f^sw_{s+u} = (chi^t_s(u)^2/(s + u)) m^r_s (1 - Theta_{s,u+1}/2) for 0 < u < s. One has e^{t d_ZZ} e^{-Z^2/(4 v)} = (v/(t + v))^{1/2} e^{-Z^2/(4(t + v))}, with second derivative G_{t,v}(Z) := v^{1/2} (2 (t + v)^{3/2})^{-1} (Z^2/(2(t + v)) - 1) e^{-Z^2/(4(t + v))}, and d_Z^2 annihilates the part of the source that does not depend on Z, so the window (s, 2s) contributes
 a_n(R, Z) := (1/2) int_0^infinity (e^{t Delta_4} m^r_s)(R) int_0^{min(t, s)} (chi^t_s(u)^2/(s + u)) sum_k G_{t,u+1}(Z - k Lambda_s) du dt,
absolutely convergent, since sum_k |G_{t,u+1}(Z - k Lambda_s)| <= (|h_t''| * Theta_{s,u+1})(Z) <= 3 k_e/t by (i) of Remark (7) and Theta_{s,u+1} < 3/2, and e^{t Delta_4} m^r_s <= min{1, 1/(4t)} by (ii) of Remark (7) (m^r_s <= min{1, w_inv}).
Three kernel facts. (1) If 1 <= t <= s/32 and R^2 <= t, then (e^{t Delta_4} m^r_s)(R) >= 1/(16 t): indeed m^r_s >= w_inv/2 on {1 <= |y'| <= (3 s)^{1/2}}; by (ii) of Remark (7) and since (1 - e^{-x})/x decreases, (e^{t Delta_4} w_inv)(R) >= (1 - e^{-1/4})/t >= 1/(5 t); the part of w_inv on {|y'| < 1} contributes at most (4 pi t)^{-2} int_{|y'| < 1} |y'|^{-2} dy' = 1/(16 t^2) <= 1/(16 t), the part on {|y'| > (3 s)^{1/2}} at most 1/(3 s) <= 1/(96 t), and (1/2)(1/5 - 1/16 - 1/96) = 61/960 > 1/16. (2) G_{t,u+1}(Z) <= 0 for all u >= 0 if Z^2 <= t, and -G_{t,u+1}(Z) >= 1/(24 t) if moreover t >= 2 and t/2 <= u <= t: then v := u + 1 >= t/2 and 3t/2 <= t + v <= 5t/2, so the three factors of -G_{t,v}(Z) are at least (5 5^{1/2} t)^{-1}, 2/3 and e^{-1/6} >= 5/6, with product (9 5^{1/2} t)^{-1} > (24 t)^{-1}. (3) |G_{t,v}(Z)| <= (t + v)^{-1} e^{-Z^2/(8(t + v))} for all Z, by (1 + 2x) e^{-x/2} <= 2 for x >= 0 (maximum 4 e^{-3/4} at x = 3/2).
The bound at a point. Let |Z - k Lambda_s| <= R for some integer k and t_R := max{2, R^2} <= t_max := s/32. Split a_eta(R, Z, -s) into (I) the term k of a_n over t_R <= t <= t_max, (II) the terms j different from k of a_n over the same times, (III) the part of a_n with t < t_R, (IV) the part of a_n with t > t_max, and (V) the contribution of the later windows; the earlier windows have beta < s and do not enter. (I): the term k is nonpositive for every u by (2), since (Z - k Lambda_s)^2 <= R^2 <= t, and on t/2 <= u <= t one has chi^t_s(u) = 1 (as 1 <= t/2 and t <= s/2) and (s + u)^{-1} >= (2 s)^{-1}; by (1) and (2), (I) <= -(1/2) int_{t_R}^{t_max} (16 t)^{-1} (t/2) (2 s)^{-1} (24 t)^{-1} dt = -(3072 s)^{-1} log(t_max/t_R). (II): |Z - j Lambda_s| >= 15 |j - k| s^{1/2} since R <= (s/32)^{1/2}, and t <= t + u + 1 <= 5t/2, so by (3) sum_{j != k} |G_{t,u+1}(Z - j Lambda_s)| <= (2/t) sum_{l >= 1} e^{-(45/4) l^2 s/t} <= (4/t) e^{-s/t} (here (45/4) s/t >= 360); with e^{t Delta_4} m^r_s <= 1/(4t), |(II)| <= (2 s)^{-1} int_{t_R}^{t_max} e^{-s/t} t^{-1} dt <= (2 s)^{-1} int_{32}^infinity e^{-x} x^{-1} dx < (64 s)^{-1}. (III): by (i) of Remark (7) applied to the nonnegative source of the window with m := m^r_s/s, |(III)| <= (k_e/s) int_0^{t_R} (e^{t Delta_4} m^r_s)(R) dt <= (k_e/s) t_R min{1, R^{-2}} <= 2 k_e/s. (IV): likewise, with e^{t Delta_4} m^r_s <= 1/(4t) and int_0^{min(t, s)} du/(s + u) <= log(1 + t/s), |(IV)| <= (k_e/4) int_{t_max}^infinity t^{-2} log(1 + t/s) dt <= (k_e/(4 s))(log 32 + 2 log 2). (V): the later windows have source times beta >= s_{n+1} = e^{32} s; by (i) and (ii) of Remark (7) with m := w_inv/(s + u), |(V)| <= (k_e/4) int_{s_{n+1} - s}^infinity du/(u (s + u)) <= k_e/(4 (s_{n+1} - s)) <= (16 s)^{-1}. Since k_e < 1/4 and log 2 < 3/4, (II) to (V) are together less than (1/2 + 1/64 + 21/64 + 1/16)/s = 29/(32 s), and
 a_eta^-(R, Z, -s) >= s^{-1} ((1/3072) log(s/(32 t_R)) - 1).
The set. Let N_s := 2 floor(s^{1/2}/16) + 1, r_s^3 := 3 s^{3/2}/(4 pi A_h N_s) and calS_s := the union over |k| <= floor(s^{1/2}/16) of {R < r_s, |Z - k Lambda_s| < R} (full azimuth). Then N_s >= s^{1/2}/16 and r_s^3 <= 12 s/(pi A_h) = 24 (2 pi)^{1/2} s < 64 s, so r_s < 4 s^{1/3}, and since s >= e^{32} > 2^{27}, max{2, r_s^2} <= 16 s^{2/3} <= s/32. The components of calS_s are disjoint (r_s < Lambda_s/2), their centres satisfy |k Lambda_s| <= s, calS_s lies in {|Z| < s + r_s} and in C^0_2(-s) (s + r_s < 2 s and R < r_s < 2 s), and |calS_s| = N_s (4 pi/3) r_s^3 = s^{3/2}/A_h. On calS_s the bound at a point applies with t_R <= 16 s^{2/3}, so a_eta^-(., -s) >= s^{-1} ((log s)/9216 - (log 512)/3072 - 1) there, and the bathtub form of B^mass gives (b). At s_n the bound equals n/288 - 1 - (3 log 2)/1024, which increases with n, is below 1/2 at n = 432 and above 1/2 at n = 433.
(c) (What would suffice.) By the envelope of Remark (7), for every finite nonnegative measure mu on the meridian half-plane (any law, drifted or not), int s |a_eta(., -s)| d mu <= (k_e C^2/4)((1 + 2 log 2) mu(total) + int log_+(4 s/R^2) d mu), with log_+(4 s/R^2) read as +infinity at R = 0. Hence, for the auxiliary strain, an inequality of the form of Remark (2) holds with c = (k_e C^2/4)(1 + 2 log 2 + L) and e(s) = 0 for every law at the age s of mass at most p(s/2) whose logarithmic moment at the axis satisfies int log_+(4 s/R^2) d mu_s <= L p(s/2). For the driftless killed law of Remark (7) the density of Y'_s is at most (4 pi s)^{-2}, so this moment is at most (4 pi s)^{-2} 2 pi^2 int_0^{2 s^{1/2}} R log(4 s/R^2) dR = 1/(4 s); since p(s/2) >= (1 - e^{-1/2})/s for s >= 1, L := 1/(4 (1 - e^{-1/2})) = 0.6354 is admissible, and c = (k_e C^2/4)(1 + 2 log 2 + 1/(4 (1 - e^{-1/2}))) = 0.18279 C^2 < 0.183 C^2 (weaker than Remark (7), by an argument that uses only the mass and this moment). The same values hold for the killed law of any drift with U^R = 0 and arbitrary U^Z: the radial component then solves the driftless equation, so its law, the killing, the moment and the mass are those of the driftless law (an observation of the parallel line of work, checked by the author); in fact the proof of Remark (7) applies unchanged to these drifts, since its pointwise majorant depends on R only and its expectation uses only the radial killed law, so the coefficient 0.0925 C^2 of Remark (7) holds for them as well. The density bound (40.5) and the mass give for the part of this moment on C^0_E(-s) the bound p(s/2)(1 + log(8 pi E A_h s^{1/2})) (the layer-cake estimate in the proof of (a)); when 2 pi E^3 A_h s^{3/2} >= 1, in particular for E = 2 and every s >= 1, this bound is attained by the density A_h s^{-3/2} p(s/2) on the thin tube {R < r_0, |Z| < E s}, r_0^2 := s^{1/2}/(2 pi E A_h), which then lies in C^0_E(-s). The set calS_s of (b) shows that the strain itself can exploit configurations near the axis: it lies within 4 s^{1/3} of the axis, below the parabolic scale s^{1/2}, and extends along it over |Z| < s + r_s, whereas the driftless law gives {R < r} mass at most r^2/(16 s^2) for every r > 0. So a cone estimate with e(s) = 0, uniform in s and over the auxiliary sources and all densities satisfying (40.5) and the mass bound, cannot follow from these restrictions alone, and by (d), for prescribed masses with 0 < p_0 <= p(s) <= p(s/2) <= 1, there is no such uniform estimate with an integrable remainder and a coefficient whose logarithmic time averages are bounded; additional information on the law, the source or their compatibility is required, and a bound int log_+(4 s/R^2) d mu_s <= L p(s/2) uniform in s is one sufficient option. No failure of the averaged criterion for a drifted circulation diffusion or for the limits is established here, no drift realizing the maximizing densities is constructed, and this remark does not change the hypotheses of the proposition.
(d) (All large ages; the logarithmic averages.) For E = 2 there is a source as in Remark (7) with C = 1, |R U^theta| <= 2 and U^theta = 0 for beta <= 2^384 such that B^mass(s) >= 2^{-18} log s - 21/16 - 25 (log 2)/2^17 >= 2^{-18} log s - 2 for every s >= s_* := 2^385. Consequently, for this source multiplied by any C > 0, any p_0 > 0 and any function p with p_0 <= p(s) <= p(s/2) <= 1 for s >= s_*: if c and e are measurable functions on [s_*, infinity), e integrable, such that int_{C^0_2(-s)} a_eta^-(., -s) rho dx_3 <= c(s) p(s/2)/s + e(s) for every s >= s_* and every rho with 0 <= rho <= A_h s^{-3/2} p(s/2) and int rho dx_3 = p(s), then (1/log t) int_{s_*}^t c(s) ds/s >= C^2 p_0 2^{-19} log t - 2 C^2 - (C^2 p_0 2^{-19} (log s_*)^2 + p_0^{-1} int_{s_*}^infinity |e| ds)/log t, which tends to infinity. An estimate with nonnegative coefficients c_1(s) of p(s)/s and c_2(s) of p(s/2)/s is of this form with c := c_1 + c_2. For the record start p >= 1/A (Proposition 26(l)); so, for the auxiliary strain of this source, the density bound (40.5) and the mass do not by themselves give, uniformly over the densities that satisfy them, the cone part of (40.2) in the averaged form used in Step 8, even with an integrable remainder. The constants are not optimized; the weaker bound 2^{-18} log s - 2 is positive exactly when log s > 2^19. Separate numerical illustrations, with a different rough source for each target age s, show the growth at moderate ages: with u := beta - s, the source q^2(R, Z, -s - u) := (1 - sum_{k in Z} 1_{|Z - 6 k s^{1/2}| < 2 u^{1/2}})/((s + u) R^2) for R > 0 and 0 < u < 9 s/4, and zero at the other source times (the intervals are disjoint, since 2 u^{1/2} < 3 s^{1/2}), has, for C = 1, E = 2 and the cap A_h s^{-3/2} p(s/2), the estimated values B^mass = 0.200, 0.280 and 0.362 at s = 10^4, 10^6 and 10^8 (computations in the parallel line of work: quadrature on a period cell followed by a discrete bathtub optimization), and the choice with spacing 8 s^{1/2}, half-width (2 u)^{1/2} and 0 < u < s gave 0.172, 0.246 and 0.324 (the author's computation, reproduced to within 1 percent by an independent implementation in the parallel line of work). These profiles have an unregularized factor R^{-2} and sharp edges, the finite cone is replaced by its period average, the computations have no certified error bounds, and they do not evaluate the source of (d), for which the estimate of the far source times in the proof below, applied to all source times, gives B^mass(s) <= (k_e/4) log(2^384/(2^384 - s)) for 0 < s < 2^384; a crossing of 1/2 at an age of order 10^{11}, suggested by a fit affine in log s, is an extrapolation of these values, not a result.
Proof of (d). The notation st, G_{t,v}, w_inv, k_e and the kernel facts (1) to (3) are those of the proof of (b) and of Remark (7); all logarithms are natural. For integers n >= 384 put ell_n := 2^n, tau_n := ell_n^{11/16}, F_n := ceil(ell_n^{1/16}) (so F_n >= 2^24), D_n := 64 ell_n^{7/16} and V_n := 3 ell_n^{3/4}; then ell_n^{3/4} <= F_n tau_n <= 2 ell_n^{3/4}, F_n tau_n + 1 <= V_n, 64 ell_n^{1/2} <= F_n D_n <= 128 ell_n^{1/2}, and D_n/(16 V_n^{1/2}) = (4/3^{1/2}) ell_n^{1/16} > 1. Put W_n(beta) := st(beta/ell_n - 1) st(6 - beta/ell_n) (zero outside (ell_n, 6 ell_n), equal to 1 on [2 ell_n, 5 ell_n]), Xi := sum_{n >= 384} W_n sum_{j in Z} phi_{n,j} Xi_{n,j}, chi_*(beta) := st(beta/2^384 - 1), m^r_beta(R) := st(4 - R^2/beta)^2/(1 + R^2), and
 U^theta(R, Z, -beta) := R chi_*(beta) st(4 - R^2/beta) (beta (1 + R^2))^{-1/2} (1 - Xi(Z, beta)/8)^{1/2}.
Hypotheses. Fix beta and n. The indices j of the active families (0 < beta - j tau_n < F_n tau_n) lie in an open interval of length F_n, so they have distinct residues modulo F_n, and each point of D_n Z is a centre of at most one active family, whose width parameter w + 1 is at most V_n. As in the proof of (b), since D_n^2/(4 V_n) >= 64 and (h - 1/2)^2 >= h/4 for h >= 1, sum_j phi_{n,j} Xi_{n,j} <= 1 + 2 sum_{h >= 1} e^{-64 (h - 1/2)^2} < 3/2. At most three W_n are nonzero at one beta (the dyadic numbers ell_n in (beta/6, beta)), so 0 <= Xi < 9/2 and 1 - Xi/8 > 7/16. A slab of times meets finitely many n and j, phi_{n,j} is flat at the ends of its interval, and on a period cell the lattice series converge uniformly with all their derivatives, uniformly for w + 1 in [1, V_n] (as in (b)); so q = U^theta/R is a smooth function of R^2, Z and beta with bounded derivatives on every slab, and U^theta e_theta is smooth across the axis. As in (b), |U^theta| <= beta^{-1/2}, |R U^theta| <= R^2 (beta (1 + R^2))^{-1/2} <= R beta^{-1/2} <= 2 (the radial factor vanishes for R^2 >= 4 beta), U^theta = 0 for beta <= 2^384, and f^sw_beta = q^2 = chi_*(beta)^2 m^r_beta (1 - Xi/8)/beta <= beta^{-1} min{1, R^{-2}}.
Kernel facts. (1') Fact (1) of the proof of (b) holds, with the same proof, with s replaced by beta and m^r_s by m^r_beta: (e^{t Delta_4} m^r_beta)(R) >= 1/(16 t) if 1 <= t <= beta/32 and R^2 <= t; also e^{t Delta_4} m^r_beta <= min{1, 1/(4 t)}. (3') |G_{t,v}(z)| <= v^{1/2} (t + v)^{-3/2} e^{-z^2/(8 (t + v))} (the proof of fact (3) before v <= t + v is used). (4) For z != 0 the positive part of G_{t,v}(z) vanishes for t >= z^2/2 and is at most 4/z^2 (in the formula for G_{t,v} drop the factor (v/(t + v))^{1/2} <= 1 and the term -1, and use 4 x^2 e^{-x} <= 16 e^{-2} with x := z^2/(4 (t + v))); at z = 0 it is 0; hence int_0^infinity sup_{v > 0} (G_{t,v}(z))^+ dt <= 2 for every z. The negative term. Let n be the integer with 2 ell_n <= s < 4 ell_n (so n >= 384), j := floor(s/tau_n), sigma_s := s - j tau_n in [0, tau_n), c a centre of the family (n, j), and |Z - c| <= R with R^2 <= tau_n. The set. Let N^V_s be the number of centres c of the family (n, j) with |c| <= s, (r^V_s)^3 := 3 s^{3/2}/(4 pi A_h N^V_s), and calV_s the union over these centres of {R < r^V_s, |Z - c| < R} (full azimuth). The consequence. Multiplying the source by C multiplies a_eta by C^2 (and the circulation bound 2 by C). For s >= s_* the density rho_s := p(s) A_h s^{-3/2} 1_{calV_s} has mass p(s), satisfies 0 <= rho_s <= A_h s^{-3/2} p(s/2), is supported in C^0_2(-s), and int a_eta^-(., -s) rho_s dx_3 >= C^2 p(s) (2^{-18} log s - 2)/s by the pointwise bound on calV_s. Since p_0 <= p(s) <= p(s)/p(s/2) <= 1 (as p(s/2) <= 1), treating the two terms separately gives C^2 (p(s)/p(s/2)) (2^{-18} log s - 2) >= C^2 (p_0 2^{-18} log s - 2), and the assumed inequality, divided by p(s/2) >= p_0, gives c(s) >= C^2 (p_0 2^{-18} log s - 2) - s |e(s)|/p_0; integration against ds/s over [s_*, t] gives the stated lower bound (after dropping the positive term 2 C^2 (log s_*)/log t). So (d) concerns estimates uniform over all densities with these marginal properties: the densities rho_s are test densities, no law of a diffusion, no drift and no path realizing them is constructed, and nothing is asserted for the laws of Proposition 40 or for the limits; Steps 6 to 8, which use the source budget through the envelope, and Remark (2) are not contradicted.
(e) (Incompressibility bounds the axis moment in logarithmic average.) Let nu = 1 and let X be the killed diffusion of the proposition started at (1, 0), driven by a prescribed meridional field U_mer = U^R e_R + U^Z e_Z in place of the field of a limit, smooth, axisymmetric and divergence-free, with |U_mer| <= K and bounded derivatives of every order, time dependence allowed; write U_s := U_mer(., -s), and assume that p_infinity := lim_s p(s) is positive. Put N_ax(s) := E[log_+(4 s/R_s^2); zeta > s] and lambda_ax(s) := N_ax(s)/p(s/2). Then
 limsup_T (1/log T) int_1^T lambda_ax(s)^2 ds/s <= 12/e,
so by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality limsup_T (1/log T) int_1^T lambda_ax(s) ds/s <= (12/e)^{1/2} < 2.1011. Consequently, for the auxiliary strain of Remark (7) of every Type I swirl, evaluated along the paths of every such X, the coefficient c_eta(s) := s E[a_eta^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s]/p(s/2) is at most (k_e C^2/4)(1 + 2 log 2 + lambda_ax(s)) by (c) (the mass p(s) is at most p(s/2)), hence
 limsup_T (1/log T) int_1^T c_eta(s) ds/s <= (k_e C^2/4)(1 + 2 log 2 + (12/e)^{1/2}) <= 0.2715 C^2,
and limsup_t (1/log t) int_1^t E[a_eta^-(X_u, -u); zeta > u] du <= 0.2715 C^2 p_infinity (write p(u/2) = p_infinity + (p(u/2) - p_infinity) and apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to the second part, whose square has logarithmic average tending to 0). This is the form in which Step 8 uses (40.2); it is below p_infinity/2 for C^2 < 1.84. A complete proof follows. The constant 12/e does not depend on K, on the time dependence or on the derivatives of U_mer.
Proof of (e). Write dx_3 = 2 pi R dR dZ, r := (R^2 + Z^2)^{1/2}, and A_ent := 2^{3/2} C_N, so that by Step 5 (with nu = 1) the law of X_s on {zeta > s} has a density rho_s with respect to dx_3 with rho_s <= A_ent s^{-3/2} p(s/2) <= A_ent s^{-3/2}. (i) (Forward equation and the axis.) The generator of X at the age s is L^ent_s = d_RR - R^{-1} d_R + d_ZZ - U_s.grad, and its formal adjoint with respect to dx_3 is calA_s := d_RR + 3 R^{-1} d_R + d_ZZ + U_s.grad (the adjoint of R^{-1}(R f')' - 2 f'/R in the weight R is f'' + 3 f'/R, and the zeroth-order term of the adjoint of -U_s.grad is div U_s = 0). Testing with smooth functions with compact support in {R > 0} gives d_s rho_s = calA_s rho_s in {R > 0}. In the lift rhotilde(y', Z) := rho_s(|y'|, Z) to R^4 x R this reads d_s rhotilde = Delta_5 rhotilde + b_5.grad_5 rhotilde away from y' = 0, where the lifted field b_5 is smooth across y' = 0 (a smooth axisymmetric field has U^R = R alpha(R^2, Z) and U^Z = beta(R^2, Z) with smooth alpha, beta); since rhotilde is bounded on compact sets of positive times, testing against functions that vanish on {|y'| < delta}, with first and second derivatives O(delta^{-1}) and O(delta^{-2}) on {delta < |y'| < 2 delta}, a region of volume O(delta^4), gives errors O(delta^2), so the equation holds across y' = 0 in the sense of distributions and parabolic regularity makes rho_s smooth up to the axis and even in R. For a smooth axisymmetric F and a smooth axisymmetric psi with compact support, two integrations by parts in R with the weight 2 pi R give
 int psi calA_s F dx_3 = int F L^ent_s psi dx_3 - 4 pi int psi(0, Z) F(0, Z) dZ,   (*)
the axis term coming from [psi R F' - (R psi' - 2 psi) F]_{R = 0} = 2 psi(0, Z) F(0, Z) (the drift term has no boundary term, div U_s = 0); the trace rho_s(0, Z) need not vanish: it determines the absorption flux into the axis, whose density with respect to dZ is 4 pi rho_s(0, Z) (with psi = 1, (*) gives p'(s) = -4 pi int rho_s(0, Z) dZ after exhaustion). (ii) (Second moment.) L^ent_s r^2 = 2 - 2 U_s.(R, Z) <= 2 + 2 K r. For n >= 2 let tau_n be the first exit from {1/n < R < n, |Z| < n}, and kill the path additionally at tau_n. Put M^ent_n(s) := E[r_s^2; s < zeta wedge tau_n]. Ito's formula for this additionally killed observable has nonpositive jumps at the killing and gives M^ent_n(s) <= 1 + int_0^s (2 + 2 K M^ent_n(u)^{1/2}) du (by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, since the remaining mass is at most one). The function Mbar_ent(s) := ((1 + 2 s)^{1/2} + K s)^2 satisfies Mbar_ent(0) = 1 and Mbar_ent' = 2 + 2 K Mbar_ent^{1/2} + 2 K s (1 + 2 s)^{-1/2}, so scalar comparison gives M^ent_n <= Mbar_ent. The bounded field excludes explosion to infinity, and on every surviving compact time interval the path stays at a positive distance from the axis, so the survival indicators of these increasing domains increase to 1_{zeta > s}; monotone convergence gives M_ent(s) := int r^2 rho_s dx_3 <= Mbar_ent(s), and passing to the limit in the integral inequality gives M_ent(s) <= 1 + int_0^s (2 + 2 K M_ent(u)^{1/2}) du; in particular M_ent(1) <= (3^{1/2} + K)^2. (iii) (Relative entropy.) Here d_s log g^ent_s = -3/s + 4 r^2/(s (l^2 + r^2)) >= -3/s, |grad log g^ent_s| = 4 r/(l^2 + r^2) <= 2/l, and (Delta_3 + 2 R^{-1} d_R) g^ent_s/g^ent_s = Delta_5 g^ent_s/g^ent_s = 4 (r^2 - 5 l^2)/(l^2 + r^2)^2 <= 1/(6 l^2) (the maximum of 4 (y - 5)/(1 + y)^2 over y >= 0 is 1/6, at y = 11), so -(d_s g^ent_s - calA_s g^ent_s)/g^ent_s <= (3 + 2 K/c_ent)/s + 1/(6 c_ent^2 s^2).
