for the same strain and the cone of slope 2, the best coefficient of the cone estimate that the density bound of the surviving law and its mass alone give at the age s >= 1 is at most C^2 (0.2751 + 0.0303 log s) for every swirl, at least (log s)/9216 - 1.003 along a sequence of ages for one swirl with C = 1, and at least 2^{-18} log s - 2 at every age s >= 2^385 for another swirl with C = 1 (Remark (8)); by the last bound, no estimate uniform over all densities with that bound and with prescribed masses bounded below, as at the record start, has an integrable remainder and a coefficient with bounded logarithmic time averages, the form in which Step 8 uses (40.2), while a bound on the logarithmic moment of the law at the axis would suffice for the auxiliary strain; this concerns an auxiliary strain under the fixed driftless law or against separately prescribed densities, not the strain and the paths of one velocity field, so the example bears on the derivation of (E_M) and is neither a counterexample to nor a proof of the averaged criterion. Remark (8)(e) adds information that the density cap and mass alone do not contain: for an actual killed diffusion with nu = 1, started at (1, 0) and driven by a smooth bounded axisymmetric incompressible meridional field with bounded derivatives of every order, with positive eternal survival, the normalized logarithmic axis moment has logarithmic mean square at most 12/e (for prescribed fields of this kind it need not be bounded at every large age, Proposition 40, Remark (9)(c)). This yields the bound 0.2715 C^2 p_infinity for the logarithmic average of the time-integrated expectation of the auxiliary compression along that law. Remark (9)(d) also proves absorption from a pathwise bound for the actual strain by u^{-1} f_pr(R_u^2/(nu u)), up to a deterministic nonnegative integrable remainder, when f_pr is nonincreasing, integrable at zero and has limit below 1/2 at infinity. The auxiliary profile k_e C^2 g_eta has these properties for every finite C. These conclusions do not identify the auxiliary strain with the actual strain of a limit, and hence do not supply the missing compression estimate. By the circulation martingale of Remark (9)(f), the pathwise bound is needed only on {Gamma_U > ell} for some 0 <= ell < 1, or eventually on an event of positive probability inside {calC_infinity > ell}. On the Type I swirl branch, for 0 < ell < 1, this superlevel set lies beyond a positive multiple of the parabolic radius. An admissible profile can then be replaced by a Type I profile, with enlarged constants, on the same set and at the same ages, retaining the deterministic integrable remainder; conversely a Type I profile is admissible. This is an equivalence between existence of bounds in the two profile classes on the same set and event. Proposition 38(c) instead concerns the absolute superlevel set and a bound with no remainder at all sufficiently large ages; the positive-superlevel or event-restricted bound of (f) is not identified with that hypothesis. Since a = -R^{-2} int_0^R r d_Z U^Z dr, a one-sided bound (d_Z U^Z)^+ <= D_+/u with D_+ < 1 on the radial segments below the paths gives (40.6), at the ages where that bound holds, with f_pr := D_+/2 and e_path := 0. The same axial stretching bound on an Euler cone of slope larger than K gives this profile bound eventually on almost every eternally surviving path, which suffices for exclusion by the restarted comparison (Remark (9)(g)); the axial stretching bound has not been derived for the limits. For a limit, the global axial stretching bound would follow from C_ax + d_ZZ P >= -alpha/tau^2 on R^3 x (-infinity, -1] with alpha < 2, where C_ax := d_Z U^R d_R U^Z and P is the pressure (Remark (9)(h)); with alpha = 2 the same argument gives the endpoint D_+ = 1, which is excluded as well. The bounded kinematic example there shows that this stretching bound does not follow for prescribed fields from the listed velocity, gradient and circulation bounds and the circulation equation, even with a Type I swirl bound; it makes no sharpness claim for Navier-Stokes limits.

## 4. Limitations and open questions

1. The decisive open step is an exclusion of the swirl-record limit in each alternative of Proposition 33 (as in the Overview), or an exclusion of both branches of Theorem 13. On the Type I swirl branch the first missing implications are (39.21), or (CW_loc) together with the source bound (39.19), which are incompatible by Proposition 39(f)(xiii) (a route from a source budget to (CW_loc), and the transport estimate it lacks, are described in Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(6)(e)), or (39.19_H) together with the small-budget inequality of Proposition 40, or directly an averaged compression bound along the record paths with a coefficient c <= 1/2 and an integrable error (Proposition 40, Remark (2)). For c < 1/2 it suffices to have this bound on a positive circulation superlevel set {Gamma_U > ell}, 0 <= ell < 1, with c q_ell(s)/s in place of c p(s/2)/s, where q_ell(s) is the probability that the path is alive at the age s with circulation above ell, provided that the terminal killed circulation has no atom at ell (Remark (9)(f)). At c = 1/2 this form excludes the limit under an additional uniform bound for the expected negative part of the localized functional of Remark (9)(f), which follows from a bound for the compression at the alive ages outside the superlevel set; neither bound was derived, and an abstract example in Remark (9)(f), in which the killed circulation is replaced by a bounded continuous martingale that vanishes after killing, shows that the hypothesis, the radial equation, the clock bounds and the divergence of the compression on eternal survival do not imply either bound. Another sufficient alternative is the following eventual bound for the actual strain. There are a fixed nonnegative nonincreasing profile f_pr, with int_0^1 f_pr(x) dx < infinity and lim_{x -> infinity} f_pr(x) < 1/2, a fixed deterministic nonnegative e_path with int_1^infinity e_path(u) du < infinity, and an event of positive probability contained in {zeta = infinity}, such that, almost surely on that event, for some finite age N and Lebesgue-almost every u >= N, a^-(X_u, -u) <= u^{-1} f_pr(R_u^2/(nu u)) + e_path(u). Remark (9)(f), using the comparison constructed in (d), excludes such an event. Remark (9)(f) obtains it if this bound holds almost surely at every age u >= 1 before killing where Gamma_U(X_u, -u) > ell, for some 0 <= ell < 1; it is also enough to obtain the eventual bound on a positive-probability subset of {calC_infinity > ell}, where calC_infinity is the terminal killed circulation. On the Type I swirl branch, for 0 < ell < 1, existence of an admissible profile bound is equivalent to existence of a Type I profile bound on the same chosen superlevel set, age range and event, retaining the deterministic integrable remainder and allowing the constants to change (Remark (9)(f)). Proposition 38(c) uses the absolute superlevel set and no remainder; its eventual bound implies the positive-superlevel hypothesis after adjustment of the finite initial age interval, but the converse is not supplied. Remark (9)(g) gives this eventual bound from (d_Z U^Z)^+(r, Z_u, -u) <= D_+/u for 0 < r < R_u with D_+ < 1, in particular from the same bound on an Euler cone of slope larger than K. For a limit, Remark (9)(h) gives the global axial stretching bound from C_ax + d_ZZ P >= -alpha/tau^2 on R^3 x (-infinity, -1] with alpha < 2, where C_ax := d_Z U^R d_R U^Z and P is the pressure, and with alpha = 2 the endpoint D_+ = 1, which is excluded as well. Its bounded kinematic example shows that the thresholds 1/2 and 1 cannot be raised among prescribed bounded smooth fields; no sharpness assertion for Navier-Stokes limits follows. None of these estimates has been derived for the actual strain of the limits. For the auxiliary strain induced by an arbitrary Type I swirl in the driftless linear model, the exact driftless law gives the averaged bound of Remark (2) for s >= 1 with c = 0.0925 C^2 and e = 0, a coefficient below 1/2 when C <= 2 (Proposition 40, Remark (7), in the normalization nu = 1 with the start (1, 0)); but the density bound (40.5) and the mass of the surviving law alone do not give it with e = 0 uniformly in time, sources and admissible densities, and, for prescribed masses with 0 < p_0 <= p(s) <= p(s/2) <= 1 as at the record start, not even uniformly with an integrable remainder and a coefficient whose logarithmic time averages are bounded, which is the form used in the proof (Remark (8)(b), (d)); this concerns the information supplied by these marginal restrictions, not a failure along an actual circulation diffusion. Remark (8)(e) now supplies additional information on the actual record law: after normalization to viscosity one, E[log_+(4 s/R_s^2); zeta > s]/p(s/2) has logarithmic mean square at most 12/e; for prescribed incompressible fields with p_infinity > 0 it need not be bounded at every large age (Remark (9)(c)). For the auxiliary strain of Remark (7), evaluated along that law, it gives a logarithmic-average compression bound of 0.2715 C^2 p_infinity, below p_infinity/2 when C^2 < 1.84 in this normalization. It does not bound the actual strain U^R/R. Remark (9)(d) gives another sufficient route: a pathwise estimate (40.6) for the actual strain with a nonincreasing profile integrable at zero and with limit below 1/2 at infinity, together with a deterministic nonnegative integrable remainder. The profile k_e C^2 g_eta obtained for the auxiliary strain meets these conditions for every finite C, but its bound has not been established for the actual strain. Neither this pathwise estimate, its superlevel-set form in Remark (9)(f), the split criterion of Remark (9)(e), nor a sufficient averaged bound for the actual compression has been derived for the limits. The missing implication therefore still concerns control of that compression through the source or its compatibility with the law. Possible sufficient approaches in branch (I) of Theorem 13 include a property of the Case-1 limits not shared by every member of LL (or a Liouville theorem for LL with Q <= C_*; a Liouville theorem for eternal members would exclude an eternal limit selected by Proposition 15 if its viscosity is positive, not an arbitrary prescribed viscous subsequence); in branch (II) they include a backward-decay estimate for the inviscid gradient-scale limits as in Proposition 12, a critical bound N(s_n) = o(1/kappa_n) as in Proposition 14, or another rigidity mechanism for ancient swirl-free Euler flows with |V|, |grad V| <= 1, |grad^2 V| <= C_*. None of these was obtained. A literature search up to 18 October 2026 (theorem statements read in the primary sources by a research consultation; proofs not re-derived), followed on 19 October 2026 by a search of recent arXiv abstracts, found no theorem that classifies LL: the closest results assume |u| <= C/r for the whole velocity [KNSS, Theorem 5.3], a uniform BMO bound for the vector potential [LZ], Gamma in L^infty_t L^p_x with p < infinity or uniform radial decay of Gamma [LZZ], a fixed axial period [LRZ1], or a quantitative approach of Gamma^2 to its limit superior at radial infinity [LRZ2]; the continuation criteria of [Sh], [QZ], [CSTY2] and [CFZ] concern finite-time solutions, and every member of LL is regular on every finite time interval, so their stated regularity conclusions do not provide the required Liouville classification. Nothing was found that gives a Liouville theorem under the additional hypotheses Gamma >= 0, U^R <= 0, ||q(tau)||_infty <= C/|tau| or ||eta(tau)||_infty <= C |tau|^{-3/2} with bounded meridional velocity alone. This is a search result, not a proof that no such theorem exists.
2. (A) involves global historical suprema whose maximizers need not lie near the swirl records. Theorem 13 shows that in branch (I) the normalized numbers m_n, d_n, h_n are bounded, and in branch (II) the gradient maximizers leave every swirl-record observation cylinder; in neither case was (A) localized to the record cylinders, and passing (A) with its constant to the swirl-record limit U was not justified.
3. Theorem 9 is about the global gradient; it does not place large gradients at the swirl records and does not use (K) or (TAIL). It rules out only one growth regime.
4. In branch (I) the swirl of the gradient-record limit has a uniform but nonexplicit lower bound on a fixed spacetime ball (from compactness and [KNSS, Theorem 5.2]); the amplitude and location of the original swirl record are not retained, because the historical swirl maximum may be attained far from the gradient record.
5. The cited results [CIV], [CIV2], [CSTY2], [ESS] (Lemma 2.2), [KNSS], [LZ] (Theorems 1.1 and 1.4), [LZ2], [LZZ], [LRZ1], [LRZ2], [LP], [QZ], [Se20] (Theorem 2.1, Proposition 1.4, sec. 3) were used as stated in the sources (statements checked in the arXiv texts where available); their proofs were not re-derived. The epsilon-regularity lemma is used in the form [ESS, Lemma 2.2] (absolute constants eps_0 and c_{0k}: a suitable weak solution of viscosity one on B(1) x (-1, 0) with int (|U|^3 + |P|^{3/2}) < eps_0 has |grad^{k-1} U| < c_{0k} on B(1/2) x (-1/4, 0)), whose statement was checked in the text; it is also [SS, Lemma 1.2] as quoted in [CIV], and [SS] was not retrieved. [Pan] and [ZZ] were not retrieved (for [Pan] the publisher's abstract was seen) and are used only as remarks. Proposition 20(c) uses [Se11, Proposition 1.1] only as it is quoted in [Se20, sec. 3]; that note was not retrieved, and the use is qualitative (its bound must involve pressure information, so only finiteness for one rescaled solution is used). [Se20, Lemma 2.2] is not used directly; an earlier proof of Proposition 20(d) relied on it, and a review reported printing errors in its statement (a sign and the position of an axis condition), which are not reproduced or verified here. Proposition 20(d) uses [LZ, Theorem 1.1]; [Se20, Theorem 2.1] remains an external dependency elsewhere. Propositions 30 and 31 use Kolmogorov's integral test as stated in [Erd] and [IM] (the exact locations were not checked against the sources), the weighted Hardy inequality of [Mu] (rederived with its constant in the proof of Proposition 31) and [Sh] (checked in the arXiv text) for the comparison idea; Propositions 31(f) and 36(f) and Proposition 32(d) use [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], as in step (a) of the proof of Theorem 1; Proposition 32(d) also uses, for 5/2 < kappa < 3, [Wei, Corollary 1.1]; the statements of both criteria were checked against the sources, their proofs were not re-verified, and the case 5/2 < kappa < 3 is stated as conditional on [Wei]. Feller's classification [Fel] is used only for the interpretation in Proposition 32, Remark (2). Proposition 35 uses the continuation lemma [CFZ, Lemma 2.5], whose hypotheses were checked against the arXiv text and whose proof was not re-verified, so Proposition 35 depends on it; the energy identities of [CFZ, Section 3], the identity in the proof of [CFZ, Lemma 3.1] and [Wei, Lemma 2.1] are rederived in its proof. Proposition 36 uses the weighted Hardy inequality of [Mu] (rederived in its proof), the comparison idea of [Sh] and [QZ], and, in (f) only, [LZ2, Corollary 1.3]. Proposition 37 uses [KNSS, Theorem 5.2 and Remark 6.1] in Remark (2) only. The statements of [AB, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 3.2] and [Se20, Theorem 2.1] described in Proposition 37, Remark (4), were checked in the arXiv texts; the comparison made in that remark is not used to prove parts (a) to (d) of Proposition 37, while [Se20, Theorem 2.1] is used elsewhere, in Proposition 20(a). [Se20, Lemma 2.2] is described in that remark only to locate the obstruction. [NU] was not retrieved and is cited as in [Se20]. [FB] was not retrieved and is cited only for the classical existence of steady vortex rings with Hoelder continuous compactly supported vorticity; the comparison of Proposition 37, Remark (2) with the Euler limits is conditional on rings with bounded second derivatives, which this citation does not verify. Proposition 40, Remark (4) uses the sharp Nash constant of [CLo] through the description of its optimizers in [CLi] (secs. 2 and 4 read; [CLo] not retrieved), with the Nash quotient of the optimizer checked by quadrature. Proposition 40, Remark (5) uses Gross's Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality [Gr] as stated (not retrieved), derives from it in the text the Euclidean form, which is also in [LL] (not retrieved; its location there was not checked), and follows the method of [Da] (not retrieved), whose steps are written out in the text.

Let U be the exact short evolution, with viscosity kappa, of N disjoint compression cells of the type above carrying swirl of relative size kappa = N^{-1/2}; then u(x, t) = kappa^{-5} U(x/kappa^4, t/kappa^9) has viscosity one, since u_t + u.grad u = kappa^{-14} (U_t + U.grad U) and Delta u = kappa^{-13} Delta U. If the uniform short-time bounds for this family hold (they were not checked), then u has bounded energy and circulation, D/M^2 of order kappa, S/M = O(kappa), time-integrated dissipation O(kappa) and time-integrated inflow of order M D, and no bound of the inflow by (D M/B) F(D/M^2, S/M, int ||grad u||_2^2 dt) with F -> 0 holds for all solutions with these bounds; this obstruction is conditional on those bounds. (xx) The regularity criterion (SD) of Proposition 29: does historical swirl domination, limsup_{t -> T} M(t)/S(t) < infinity, exclude a finite-time singularity of a smooth finite-energy axisymmetric solution with bounded circulation? Under it a singularity must be of Type II in the swirl, and an exclusion of Case 1 would prove (SD). (xxi) The inflow envelopes of Propositions 30 and 31: whether, for nonzero envelopes with C(t) -> infinity as t -> -infinity, the divergence of (KP_0) is also necessary for the radial comparison function to vanish at the axis (the converse half of the test; for F = 0 it fails, Remark (1) after Proposition 31); the endpoint beta = 3/2 in Proposition 31(f); and whether the cumulative inward radial displacements that Proposition 31 forces on a Case-1 trajectory, above any given dimension-zero envelope on arbitrarily short terminal windows, are compatible with (A), the energy bound and the records. Two elementary facts locate the difficulty. If at some time eta = 0 on {r > h} and (u^r/r)^- <= K, then (u^r)^- <= K h^2/r on {r >= h}: there u^r/r is Delta_5-harmonic, -K h^2/r^2 is Delta_5-harmonic, and the exterior minimum principle applies (u^r/r tends to 0 at infinity); with K = C_a/(T_* - t) and h = (T_* - t)^{1/2} this would give (T_* - t)^{1/2} g(t) <= C_a, so the required inflow needs meridional vorticity at radii beyond the parabolic radius. And for every rho > 0 and t, the improper integral lim_{L_-, L_+ -> infinity} int_{-L_-}^{L_+} u^r(rho, z, t) dz equals 0 (absolute integrability in z is not claimed), since the axial flux through the disc of radius rho has z-derivative -2 pi rho u^r(rho, z, t) and tends to 0 as |z| -> infinity; so no cylinder carries inflow only, and a localized estimate for eta with a radial cutoff meets an outflow term of unknown sign. The question is whether the exterior meridional vorticity, transported from earlier times, can be controlled well enough to give (T_* - t) g(t)^2 <= kappa L_2(T_* - t) eventually for some kappa < 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1), which would exclude the branch; at one time the strain bound alone does not suffice, since the smooth compactly supported field with stream function A z chi((r^2 + z^2)/R^2), chi a nonincreasing cutoff equal to 1 on [0, 1], has u^r/r >= -A everywhere and is irrotational, with inflow A r, on the ball of radius R. Three further facts (a research consultation, rechecked by the author; Review 20 in sec. 5) show that the strain, circulation, energy and dissipation bounds used above do not give the missing estimate; they do not show that a particular equation or region is indispensable to a proof. (1) The radial momentum equation gives (d_t + b.grad - Delta_5)(u^r/r) = -(u^r/r)^2 + q^2 - p_r/r (using (Delta - r^{-2})(r f) = r Delta_5 f); since u^r/r is recovered from eta by Delta_5 (u^r/r) = d_z eta, this equation is the equation for eta composed with that elliptic relation and carries no sign of its own. Nor has the pressure a sign at a minimum of u^r/r: for a smooth compactly supported pure swirl f(r, z) e_theta vanishing near the axis, the pressure on the axis is p(0, z_0) = -(1/(4 pi)) int f^2 |y - (0, 0, z_0)|^{-3} dy (since u(y) is orthogonal to y - (0, 0, z_0)), so p_rr = -(3/(8 pi)) int f^2 (r^2 - 4 z^2)(r^2 + z^2)^{-7/2} dy at the origin, which is negative for a thin torus near the plane z = 0 and positive for one inside the cone 4 z^2 > r^2; adding a small field of the type just described with disjoint support makes the minimum of u^r/r negative, attained at the origin, without changing either sign. (2) The one-time field extends to a family in time with the strain, circulation, energy and dissipation properties verified below; it solves the circulation equation but not the equation for eta. Let chi also vanish on [4, infinity), 0 < alpha <= C_a and R(t)^2 = (T_* - t) L_2(T_* - t); take the stream function (alpha/(T_* - t)) z chi((r^2 + z^2)/R(t)^2), and let the swirl solve its exact equation with this meridional velocity from a fixed smooth compactly supported datum with |Gamma| <= G. Then u^r/r >= -alpha/(T_* - t), |Gamma| <= G and the barrier (33.1) hold; the meridional kinetic energy is C alpha^2 (T_* - t)^{1/2} L_2^{5/2}, which tends to 0, and the squared L^2 norm of its gradient, C' alpha^2 (T_* - t)^{-1/2} L_2^{3/2}, is integrable in time; the swirl energy stays bounded, since its production, the integral of (u^r/r)^- (u^theta)^2, is at most C G^2 (T_* - t)^{-1/2} L_2^{1/2} (1 + log L_2) by the barrier; the cylinder identity holds; (T_* - t)^{1/2} g(t) >= alpha L_2^{1/2}/2 (at r = R/2, z = 0); and with H the Delta_5-harmonic function on {r > (T_* - t)^{1/2}} that has the values of u^r/r on r = (T_* - t)^{1/2} and limit 0 at infinity, the part of the inflow not explained by the core, (T_* - t)^{1/2} sup over r >= (T_* - t)^{1/2} of r (u^r/r - H)^-, is at least alpha (L_2^{1/2}/2 - 2 L_2^{-1/2}) (H >= -alpha/r^2 by the minimum principle). The family violates the equation for eta for every swirl with |Gamma| <= G: integrated in z over a suitable segment of length of order R(t) at a radius of order R(t), the transport part (d_t + b.grad - Delta_5) eta is of order (T_* - t)^{-2}, while the source d_z(q^2) integrates to a difference of two values of q^2, at most G^2 R(t)^{-4}, of order (T_* - t)^{-2} L_2^{-2}. (3) A sufficient form of the missing estimate is a bound for the outward pressure excess over the centrifugal term. The function (u^r)^- satisfies (d_t + b.grad - Delta + r^{-2}) (u^r)^- <= (p_r - (u^theta)^2/r)^+ in the Kato sense, and (S) gives (u^r)^- <= C_a (T_* - t)^{-1/2} on r <= (T_* - t)^{1/2}; so if (T_* - t)^{3/2} (p_r - (u^theta)^2/r)^+ <= C on {r >= (T_* - t)^{1/2}} for t near T_*, comparison on that moving exterior region with K (T_* - t)^{-1/2}, K >= max{2 C, C_a} and large enough at the starting time, bounds (T_* - t)^{1/2} g(t), contradicting Proposition 36(e). (xxvii) Strain records and Type I swirl limits (Proposition 37). On the Type II strain branch, under (A), a bound D(sigma_j) <= C_k K_j at the strain records (the strain controls the whole gradient there) would give compactness of the normalized solutions in the Euler regime; it was not derived. No exclusion of that regime from these hypotheses is proved here. Steady vortex rings share the bounded-gradient and compression normalizations, but a comparison with the full class of Euler limits is conditional on the additional regularity required in Proposition 37, Remark (2); the cited existence result with Hoelder continuous vorticity does not give bounded second derivatives. In the viscous regime the question is a Liouville theorem for the members W of LL with nonzero swirl, a_W >= -1 on (-infinity, 0] and a_W = -1 at a point (with Gamma_W bounded as in Proposition 37, Remark (2)). On the Type I swirl branch two estimates would advance Proposition 37(d): a proof that A_* < infinity, or only its time-integrated form (CW) of Proposition 37(e), for the limits of Proposition 33(e)(i) (for example, through bounded integrals of the physical strain k over the dyadic windows [T_* - 2h, T_* - h], Proposition 39(f)(xii)), which gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty = O(1/|tau|); and a barrier radius L(sigma), nondecreasing in |sigma|, with L(tau)/|tau|^{3/4} -> infinity as tau -> -infinity and a_U(., sigma) >= -A/L(sigma)^2 on {R < L(sigma)} for all sufficiently negative sigma with some finite A, which by the bound with the circulation in (37.3) gives ||q_U(tau)||_infty = o(|tau|^{-3/2}), and then, by the derivative estimate (D) of Remark (3) after Proposition 37 and (34.5), s^2 ||eta_U(-s)||_infty -> 0, contradicting Proposition 34(d)(ii) (the implication is proved there; the compression bound is not). By Proposition 39(f)(vi), (xiii) it would also suffice, when A_* < infinity, (CW_loc) or (H3) holds, that |tau| |omega^theta_U| decay outside the cylinders at a rate w(R/|tau|^{1/2}) with w -> 0 and int^infinity w(xi) dxi/xi < infinity; the kinematic family of Remark (7) after Proposition 39 has |tau| |omega^theta| of order 1 on |tau|^{1/2} << R <= |tau| and satisfies the bounds, the elliptic relation and the unsigned budgets used there, so such a decay, if true, needs further information, for instance from the evolution equations of eta and Gamma. If (CW_loc) fails, Proposition 37, Remark (5)(c)(8) shows that limsup_t int_t^{2t} [(K E'(s))^{1/2} + s^{1/2} E'(s)] ds = infinity for every larger cone C_{A'}, A' > A_c, E'(s) the supremum of |eta_U(-s)| over C_{A'}(-s); the axis identities, the reduction of the cone compression to the axis and the width bound for compressed axis intervals do not prove (CW_loc).
7. Information that the limit forgets was tested in quantitative form. In the normalized units of the swirl records (length r_n, velocity gamma_n/r_n, viscosity 1/gamma_n) the energy is at most E_0/(gamma_n^2 r_n) and the dissipation integral of the normalized field over the whole history (the time integral of the squared L^2 norm of its gradient, without the viscosity factor) at most E_0/(2 gamma_n r_n). Writing calE_n for the supremum of the normalized energy over the normalized past [-calL_n, 0], calL_n = t_n/T_n, and calD_n for the normalized dissipation over that interval, the energy inequality gives calE_n calD_n/(calL_n nu_n^4) <= E_0^2/(2 t_n) for the product that controls small critical data; this bound does not tend to zero with r_n, and it is neither an equality nor a lower bound on the actual product. At normalized distance delta/r_n from the rescaled singular set the normalized velocity is at most C_delta r_n/gamma_n (local energy, interpolation and epsilon-regularity), but the exterior circulation is not small. Tested quantitative versions of the Liouville arguments of [KNSS], [LZZ], [LRZ1], [LRZ2], [LZ] and of a forced potential-vorticity argument give deteriorating input bounds, sometimes only a nonvanishing bound independent of r_n; no uniform quantitative version of every cited Liouville argument is established here. Along a branch-(I) subsequence, with P_kappa a fixed smooth real radial low-pass Fourier multiplier and Q_kappa = I - P_kappa, for a sufficiently small fixed c > 0 the high-pass part at the record frequency satisfies ||Q_{c/r_n} u(t_n)||_2^2 >= c gamma_n^2 r_n (the low-pass swirl at the record is at most C r_n kappa M(t_n) <= S_n/2 with kappa = c/r_n, and D(t_n) <= C S_n/r_n spreads the remaining amplitude over a ball of radius comparable to r_n), while the commutator bound for the energy transfer into these frequencies gives only o(1) over the history; the missing factor r_n is the supercriticality of the energy. The commutator estimate is not specific to axisymmetry; the stated lower bound uses the swirl record and branch (I). For a kinematic history satisfying the numerical constraints, (A), finite energy and integrable dissipation, put l_n = r_n^{3/4}; at the record tops the scaled meridional quantities A_b and E_b are of order (rho/r_n)^2 for r_n << rho <= l_n, and for l_n <~ rho -> 0 the reported construction gives lower bounds of order rho^{-2/3} (the rho^{-2/3} asymptotics at all small radii is a statement at the terminal top), so, if that construction is correct, pigeonholing the numerical bounds does not produce good scales. A scalar history with M = 2S, D = 2S^2, H = 4S^3 satisfies (A) with waiting times between levels that are unbounded after division by the record time T_n, so forward growth gives no contradiction at the scalar level. The kinematic history is not constructed here and the statements about it are reported, not proved here (the scalar history is checked directly: 2S 4S^3 = 8 S^4 <= C_* (2 S^2)^2 for C_* >= 2). Verification: the statements of this item were supplied by a research consultation and checked by the author by hand and with a computer calculation for the exponents; the model histories are kinematic or scalar, not Navier-Stokes solutions. Two further kinds of fixed-trajectory information were tested in branch (I) (from a research consultation, checked by the author by hand, except the uniform Sobolev bounds for the family of data in the second obstruction below, for which a scaling argument is given there). First, let X_s be the backward diffusion of the circulation equation started at a record point x_n at time t_n (radial drift -u^r - 1/R, axial drift -u^z, noise sqrt2 in each coordinate, killed at the axis), and Y_s = sigma Gamma(X_s, t_n - s) with sigma = sgn Gamma(x_n, t_n) and Y = 0 after killing. Y is a bounded martingale with quadratic variation 2 |grad Gamma|^2 ds, so 2 E int_0^{(t_n - t_0) ^ zeta} |grad Gamma(X_s, t_n - s)|^2 ds <= G^2 - gamma_n^2 (zeta the killing time), additively over disjoint backward windows under the same terminal record, and by optional stopping the path keeps Y > g/2 on the whole backward interval with probability at least g/(2G - g) whenever gamma_n >= g. In the uniformly viscous scenario of sec. 3.7 with M <= C_0 S and D <= C_1 S^2 one may take g = 1/C_0; for geometric records S_k = S_0 lambda^k the ancestor radius R at time t_k satisfies R S_k >= (g/(2 C_1))^{1/2} on that event, and the expected number of k with R <= L/S_k at time t_k (alive) is at most 1/p, p = Phi(-(L + C_0 theta)/(2 theta)^{1/2}), theta = (lambda^2 - 1)/(4 C_1), Phi the standard normal distribution function. An exclusion would follow from divergence, along the terminal records n, of the cumulative mixing E_n sum_k int_{I_k} |grad Gamma(X_s, t_n - s)|^2 ds over the disjoint backward windows I_k = [t_n - t_k, t_n - t_k + theta/S_k^2], or if, for some fixed L < infinity, limsup_{n -> infinity} sum_k P_n{zeta > t_n - t_k, R_{t_n - t_k} <= L/S_k} = infinity, where the sum runs over the earlier geometric records and, for each n, all probabilities use the diffusion started at the same terminal record (x_n, t_n); a uniform positive lower bound on an increasing number of these probabilities would suffice. Neither was proved. Second, two obstructions. On r > a the exact steady field u^r = -beta/r, u^z = 0, Gamma = G_e (1 - (a/r)^{beta - 2}), beta > 2 (the field of Proposition 23(b)) has outward dyadic survival losses (a/r_j)^{beta-2} (1 - 2^{2-beta})/(1 - (a/r_{j+1})^{beta-2}) and circulation-variance charges G_e^2 (1 - (a/r_j)^{beta-2}) (a/r_j)^{beta-2} (1 - 2^{2-beta}), r_j = 2^j r_0, both summable although -r u^r = beta > 2. And a smooth decaying finite-energy datum, consisting of a compact core (u^theta = r e^{(1 - r^2 - z^2)/2} near the origin, meridional field (-8r, 16z) there, so that u^theta has its maximum 1 at (1, 0) with d_t u^theta = 4 there) and disjoint pure-swirl tori with circulation 4 f((r - R_j)/w_j) f(z/w_j), R_j = 2^{4j+8}, w_j = 2^j, f a smooth cutoff equal to 1 on [-1/2, 1/2] (energies O(2^{-2j})), has sup_x Gamma(x, t) = 4 at every time of its smooth existence interval, by the backward representation on the plateaus of the tori. The exterior example blocks a uniform per-annulus charge under the stated exterior hypotheses. The datum blocks a strictly positive decrement of the global circulation supremum at every genuine small swirl first crossing under finite energy and the short-time norm bounds; it supplies no singular time, no unbounded record chain and no Case-1 witnesses, so a decrement estimate that uses this additional singular history remains open.
8. Steady members of LL were tested separately. For a bounded smooth steady member the total head Phi = P + |U|^2/2 (the pressure is Lipschitz, since its gradient nu Delta U - U.grad U is bounded) satisfies nu Delta Phi - U.grad Phi = nu |omega|^2, where in axisymmetric form |omega|^2 = (d_Z U^theta)^2 + (omega^theta)^2 + (d_R U^theta + U^theta/R)^2, and for a steady Case-1 normalized limit the record conditions give |omega(e_1)|^2 >= 1. Hence a steady member whose head attains its supremum on R^3, for instance one with limsup_{|x| -> infinity} Phi <= Phi(e_1), is constant (strong maximum principle for nu Delta - U.grad, then omega = 0 and U is a bounded harmonic field), which contradicts the record. The attainment is not known: the swirl maximum gives no extremum of P + |b|^2/2, a bounded subharmonic function may approach its supremum only at infinity, and unbounded superlevel components carry an outer flux of unknown sign. The circulation equation with the scalar Case-1 facts does not exclude steady members: with a = 1 + R^2 and D = a^2 + 4Z^2, the smooth divergence-free field with Stokes stream function Psi = 6 nu R^2 Z a/D (U^R = -Psi_Z/R, U^Z = Psi_R/R; the coefficient of the angular vector potential of Proposition 19 is Psi/R) and U^theta = 2R/D^{1/2} solves b.grad Gamma = nu L Gamma exactly, has U^theta <= 1 with equality exactly on the circle {R = 1, Z = 0} (the point e_1 of the meridional half-plane), Gamma = 2R^2/D^{1/2} < 2 with d_R Gamma > 0 and Gamma(R, 0) -> 2, -U^R(e_1) = 3 nu and -R U^R(R, 0) -> 6 nu, but its meridional vorticity residual R_eta = b.grad eta - nu Delta_5 eta - d_Z(q^2) satisfies d_Z R_eta(e_1) = 648 nu^2 + 2, so it is not a Navier-Stokes field. Integration of the steady eta equation over Z in [-H, H] gives an exact identity whose limit H -> infinity needs an integrability that bounded U, grad U and Gamma do not give, and whose transport term int U^R eta dZ has no sign. Case-1 limits are not known to be steady or time periodic: a steady limit would follow, for example, from r_n S_n^{-2} sup |d_t u| -> 0 on compact rescaled sets, which is not established, and no strict Lyapunov functional on LL is known that would make the supports of invariant measures steady. Among the steady Liouville theorems, [LZZ, Theorem 1.3 and Remark 1.4] (Gamma in L^infinity_t L^p_x for some finite p, or Gamma -> 0 uniformly, also in the ancient case), [CW] (steady solutions with the decay assumptions stated there, under Gamma -> 0 at infinity, Gamma in L^q for some 2 <= q < infinity, or the one-sided bound u^r >= -1/r at viscosity one) and the slab, periodic and D-solution results [BGWX], [WY] do not cover bounded steady solutions with bounded circulation alone. Verification: supplied by a research consultation, checked by the author by hand and with a computer calculation (independent code); literature statements checked at abstract level, [LZZ] in the full text.
9. Mechanisms of other types were tested at their first step (supplied by a research consultation, checked by the author by hand, the Gaussian integrals with a computer calculation). (a) Topology of the meridional flow. A swirl record is not a meridional stagnation point (u^r < 0 there), and the axial Galilean transformation U_c(r, z, t) = U(r, z - ct, t) + c e_z, which preserves the Navier-Stokes equations, axisymmetry, the circulation bound, the swirl maxima and the record inequality, removes every meridional stagnation point of a bounded ancient solution when c > sup |U^z| (it does not preserve finite energy). The listed properties alone, allowing their finite constants to change, therefore cannot force meridional stagnation in the chosen frame. A stagnation-based argument for the fixed physical solution could instead use additional information selecting its distinguished frame. (b) Backward Gaussian monotonicity. At viscosity one, for F in C^2 with F(0) = 0, an axis point x_*, s = t_* - t, X = x - x_* and the three-dimensional backward heat kernel G_3 = (4 pi s)^{-3/2} e^{-|X|^2/(4s)}, the quantity E_F = int F(Gamma) G_3 dx satisfies E_F' = -int F''(Gamma) |grad Gamma|^2 G_3 dx - (2s)^{-1} int F(Gamma)(2 + X.b) G_3 dx, because the dx-adjoint of L is Delta_5 (the axis term vanishes since F(0) = 0) and d_t G_3 + Delta_5 G_3 = -G_3/s. The compression term X.b has no sign: for the finite-energy datum Gamma = r^2 e^{(1 - r^2 - z^2)/2}, b^r = -Psi_z/r, b^z = Psi_r/r with Psi = 80 sqrt2 r^2 z e^{-5(r^2 + z^2)/4}, x_* = 0, s = 1 and F(Gamma) = Gamma^2 one has E_F'/E_F = 2/5 > 0 at the initial time, while the swirl maximum (equal to 1, at (1, 0)) increases. (c) Comparison. The order Gamma_1 <= Gamma_2, eta_1 <= eta_2 is not preserved: for smooth finite-energy data with equal circulations, b_1 = 0, eta_1 = 0 and eta_2 = h, where h is nonzero, smooth, compactly supported, axisymmetric and nonnegative, with support strictly below a point p with Gamma_r(p) > 0 and Gamma_z(p) = 0, the Biot-Savart law gives u_2^r(p) > 0, so d_t(Gamma_2 - Gamma_1)(p) = -u_2^r(p) Gamma_r(p) < 0 at the initial time. (d) Renormalization dynamics. Uniformly over all finite constants and positive viscosities, terminal historical swirl-maximum attainment gives no additional Liouville hypothesis: every member of LL has a translation-closure representative attaining its swirl supremum, which can then be normalized as in Theorem 3. This does not preserve prescribed constants or establish realization by the fixed physical trajectory. In abstract compact dynamics attainment does not give a nontrivial invariant measure (the hull of t -> sech^2(t + s), s real, together with 0 has delta_0 as its only invariant probability measure), so this route needs a nontrivial recurrence theorem specific to Navier-Stokes; none is established here. (e) Lyapunov functionals for the Euler limits of branch (II). Since V(t) -> -V(-t) maps Euler solutions to Euler solutions, no autonomous functional invariant under V -> -V can be strictly decreasing along all Euler flows; a time-directed quantity would be needed. None of (a) to (e) excludes either branch.

## 5. Verification

The report combines author derivations and results supplied in research answers. Computer calculations check the specified identities, constants and examples; compactness, comparison, exhaustion, removability and subsequent extensions require separate analytic verification. The computer calculations check symbolic identities and illustrative examples with sympy, and some elementary lemmas numerically; the numerical checks are sanity checks only. Independent verification consists of adversarial audit rounds and research consultations conducted with a second model (GPT-6, run through Codex). Results supplied by an audit or a research consultation were checked by the author as stated below before inclusion. The Status line of each numbered item names its rounds. Research answers are numbered 1, 2, and so on, in the order in which they were obtained; the audit records, the research answers and the computer code are not part of this report. Forty-six adversarial audit rounds (rounds 1 to 19, round 21 with two parts, rounds 22 to 47; forty-seven audit reports) and one research consultation (round 20) are described below, followed by the reviews and consultations of the later work, numbered from 1 on: Reviews 1 to 20 concern Propositions 27 to 36 and the open questions of sec. 4, and the later reviews concern Propositions 37 to 40 and the summaries.

- Rounds 1 to 3. Round 1 covered the extraction, the reduction, the barrier and Route B; round 2 covered Route A, the pressure Hessian and Proposition 8; round 3 covered Theorem 9. The main named results were retained after repairs; incorrect auxiliary claims were repaired: the compactness order in the extraction, the scope of the reduction, the envelope in Route B, a Fourier sign and a running-maximum step in Theorem 7, the scope of Proposition 8, the running-minimum selection, notation and the far-field citation in Theorem 9, and the numerical excursion check.
- Round 4 covered the Type II analysis (Proposition 11 and the window discussion), the 5D identities and the literature notes. It found a wrong spatial normalization of the Gaussian example (now b = sqrt(e/2), valid for C_* >= sqrt2 e); a wrong claim that ||q||_{L^4(dx)} is supercritical and unbounded under (A) (it is subcritical, and the audit supplied ||q||_{L^4(dx)}^4 <= 4 E_0 H^2); a proof of window rigidity that needed an unproved comparison of M (replaced by the volume argument of Proposition 12, proposed by the audit); an incorrect description of the mechanism of [QZ]; and overstatements (equivalence of windows with decay, eternal rather than ancient limits, a missing planar alternative, overly broad literature and reduction statements). All were corrected.
- Round 5 covered Theorem 13 and the corrected Propositions 11 and 12. It found that the restart delays in the uniform local regularity step of Theorem 2 did not fit the step intervals (repaired with delays 2^{-j-2}), that the constant C_c of Theorem 13(b) had been shown to exist only for the fixed solution (a class version was supplied), a wrong quantifier in the statement relating branch (I) to the Liouville problem, a false sentence about single-profile solutions and an unproved conclusion in the heuristic jet discussion. It supplied the stronger bound on m_n in branch (II) and the uniform swirl witness. All were corrected or withdrawn. Research answers supplied the M-comparison in Theorem 13(e), Proposition 14 and its balance remarks, the Duhamel and q^2 bounds of sec. 3.6, the power-law histories of sec. 3.12 and the swirl-level eternal limits of Proposition 15; the gradient-level version of Proposition 15 is the author's adaptation.
- Round 6 covered Theorem 13(e) and Propositions 14 and 15. It found no wrong constant, one dropped hypothesis (the finiteness of N at an initial time in the mass balance, which finite energy does not imply) and several statements of scope that were too broad (the selection in Proposition 15 is existential; the regularity-criterion remark concerns global hypotheses only; several remarks now say "would suffice" instead of "would need"). All were corrected. Research answers supplied the o(D^{1/2}) bound for N, the backward adjoint identity, and the frozen-field and log-slow obstructions of Proposition 18. Propositions 16, 17 and 18(a) are the author's.
- Round 7 covered Propositions 16 to 18. It found the identities and constants correct and one gap: the unconditional finiteness of Y_p holds only for p >= 2 (a counterexample for 3/2 < p < 2 uses disjoint translates with slowly decaying amplitudes; the statement was restricted). It improved the stream-function threshold of Proposition 16 from 0.4748 to the values P_p, which increase to (8/3)^{1/2} = 1.632993..., by keeping the axial dissipation; it removed the hypothesis that N be finite at the initial time from Proposition 18(c), restricted the scalar-history obstruction to windows of normalized length O(1/kappa) and corrected one sufficiency statement worded as a necessity. Research answers supplied the pointwise inflow bound and the source-sign identity of Proposition 18(e), and the exact form of the coupled meridional energy identity, which agrees with a computer calculation
- Round 8 covered Proposition 19. It found the main statements correct (with an added identification argument at the initial time) and several defects in the remarks: ambiguous window quantifiers in the proposed closures; an unjustified necessity of signed cancellation in the balance of N (a stationary scalar counterexample was supplied and the statement withdrawn); a stale numerical threshold; and the global statement limsup N = infinity presented as new although it follows from [LZ, Theorem 1.4]. All were corrected. It supplied the divergence of the integrated absolute source of N (Proposition 19(d)) and the kinematic obstruction of sec. 3.11. Proposition 19 and Proposition 20(a)-(c) are otherwise the author's.
- Round 9 covered Proposition 20. It found (a)-(c) correct, made the constant in (b) explicit (152), repaired a ball-versus-cylinder step in (c) and two time-domain details in the existence of singular points, found that the first proof of (d) relied on [Se20, Lemma 2.2], which it reported to be misprinted as stated, and supplied the present proof of (d) through [LZ, Theorem 1.1], which also strengthens it; it corrected overstatements about the pressure quantity and the swirl energy in the remarks. The many-scale statement (e) is from research answer 6; its version at the singular top was not accepted. Propositions 21 and 22 are the author's, with identities checked by computer calculations; parts of Proposition 22(a), (b) were also derived independently in research answer 7.
- Round 10 covered Proposition 21. It found the Harnack chain, the barrier bound and the weighted-record argument correct, and supplied the strict inequality in (a), the extended range Gamma_0 < G_0 and the quantitative compression criterion in (c), and the exclusion of meridional bounds on cylinders reaching the axis in (b) (given in this report in outline only). It corrected several interpretations: the two hypotheses of the gain lemma fail jointly, not separately; the ancient-limit escape does not locate large meridional speeds at circulation maxima; the fixed-radius flux bound gives continuity in time (the defect is only at shrinking radii); the weight obstruction holds for fixed radial weights only; the averaging statement for nonlinear transforms needs Phi' > 0 on the range. The repairs were checked with a computer calculation
- Round 11 covered Proposition 22. It found the pressure source, the axis formula, the record inequalities, the Riccati equations and the Burgers formulas correct, and one error: the principal-value formula for the axial curvature of the swirl pressure omitted a local term 2c^2/5 (an explicit Gaussian example has curvature 2/5 while every spherical shell integral vanishes; a research answer derived the same term independently). The no-sign conclusion is unaffected. It corrected overstatements in the reading of the Burgers model (which also fails finite energy, the tail and a bounded canonical pressure, and for which no universal distance from the record follows), restricted the averaged pressure statements to trajectory averages, added the endpoint restriction t > 0 in the swirl-pressure lemma, and supplied the bound d_n^2 >= 2 + 6 beta_n^2/gamma_n^2 and further signed identities at the record.
- Round 12 covered Proposition 23 (the author's, with a computer calculation). It found the deficit comparison, the far-field theorem (including the comparison on the irregular near-maximal set and the order of the two limits) and the physical corollary correct, and noted that the Liouville consequence is the case b = 2 nu/R of Theorem 5. It found that the sample constants used an inadmissible value of A; that whole-space sharpness of 2 nu is not established (the line sink is singular on the axis); that a claim that Case-1 limits violate near-axis circulation moduli was false; that several literature entries were misdescribed (which theorem of [LZ] uses the drift decomposition, the swirl-potential form of [LZ2], the extra hypotheses of [LZZ], of Pan and Li [PL] and of [CIV], and the scaling of the quantity of [Se22]); that a sufficient condition was called an equivalence; and that the discussion of the near-maximal set drew causal conclusions about the origin of the inflow and a vorticity-smallness implication that do not follow (it supplied the zero-vorticity counterexample of sec. 3.16). All were corrected. The Feller form of Proposition 23(b) was added later and checked symbolically and by the author.
- Proposition 24 is from research answer 8; the author checked each part, and selected identities and one-sample examples symbolically; the small-dissipation target proposed there was shown false by the author (Proposition 24(e)). Round 13 audited the whole report for overclaims and consistency, and Proposition 24 in detail. It found the principal formulas of Proposition 24 and the dissipation lower bound correct, and found omitted hypotheses (Propositions 10, 16, 18(b), 20(e), 21(b), and the sign convention in Theorem 2), an invalid rounded stream-function threshold (1.633 exceeds the limit (8/3)^{1/2}), a slightly too large Burgers cylinder constant, and statements stronger than the evidence (that every critical functional has one unsigned term, that the total inflow could not be restricted, that different targets are the same missing implication, that exclusions must use particular listed information, and sufficiency statements worded as equivalences or necessities). All were corrected; the audit's common status paragraph is used at the top.
- Proposition 25 is from research answer 9; its identities were rechecked by the author and symbolically; the existence of the exhaustion limit in 25(d) was read, not rewritten. Round 14 covered it. It found the comparison arguments, the refinement (a), the flux and Biot-Savart bounds, the Morrey example (with constants rechecked by the audit), both models and the failure of the vorticity equation correct. It found a normalization constant in the Feller scale function that is exact only for base point e, an inapplicable citation of Theorem 5 for the prescribed drift (replaced by Proposition 23(b)), a reliance on sampled signs for the barriers (replaced by an analytic proof), missing quantifiers and a wrong symmetry argument in the limit-level equivalence (the reflection W^# replaces the negation of Gamma), a claim that a proof must use information that does not pass to the limit, a claim that the meridional field is close to a swirl-free solution in the near-maximal set (replaced by a small-residual statement), and sufficiency statements worded as reductions. All were corrected. Proposition 25(f) is from research answer 10; the exact slender residual and the Landau flow with potential swirl were rechecked symbolically, and the profile classification was read and partly rechecked.
- Proposition 26(a)-(d) are the author's. Round 15 covered Proposition 25(f) and Proposition 26(a)-(d). It found the identities, the exterior solution and the representation formula correct. The profile classification needed its class (odd, nonzero vorticity, finite slope at k = 0) and global formulas for the explicit profile. The comparison with [LRZ2] was misstated: the averaged hypothesis is weaker, so the result is a stronger necessary condition. A claim about the deficit in every large box was wrong, because a Banach limit is not a liminf, and was replaced. The audit supplied the stronger lower bounds for the averaged deficit now in 26(d), rechecked by the author.
- Round 16 covered Proposition 26(e) and the repaired 26(d). It found the deficit bounds, the subsequence argument, the convex-weight identity and its representation correct, extended the threshold theorem to the endpoint 2 nu with vanishing at every radius, and supplied the gap statement and the weighted outflow statement of 26(e) (rechecked by the author). It found that incompressibility was missing from the inherited hypotheses and gave the counterexample quoted in the statement of Proposition 26; that a pointwise corollary was already covered by Proposition 23(b); that exchanging a Banach limit with an improper integral needs a finite-interval argument followed by Tonelli's theorem; that A^2 - Gamma^2 need not be nonnegative; and that the deficit bound is asymptotic at each fixed radius rather than exact in each finite box. All were corrected.
- Proposition 26(f) is from research answer 11; its explicit formulas were rechecked symbolically and numerically. The computer calculations check algebra and selected constants only; the barrier inequalities, the exhaustion and the removability of the axis for the first field rest on the analytic arguments of that answer and of round 17. Round 17 covered Proposition 26(e), (f). It found the gap statement, the weighted outflow statement and the scalar construction correct. It found false the claim that the second explicit field of 26(f) satisfies all averaged identities, since the convex identity for the square of the circulation fails, and found that the conclusion drawn from it, that further progress must use the unaveraged equations, did not follow. It also required a C^1 rather than smooth window weight, a sufficient rather than necessary reading of the window-size condition, centres fixed before each diagonal stage, an explicit vorticity-equation hypothesis for the averaged vorticity identity, and the restriction of a positivity remark to weights with f(A) > 0. All were corrected.
- Round 18 covered Proposition 26(g) and the level-set part of 26(h), which are the author's. It found the vanishing of localized means, the growth argument, the two-level moment identities (for every admissible weight) and the periodic estimate correct; it found the Z-integrated balance unproved as written (repaired by explicit trace hypotheses), the level measure in need of a construction (supplied by a thin-strip estimate), and the pointwise flux-ratio limit and the claimed necessity of a lower bound for the level-set energy not justified. These were corrected. Proposition 26(g) was reviewed in round 18; its integrated balance is conditional on the explicit trace hypotheses. The momentum part of 26(h) is from research answer 12: the averaged radial, angular and axial momentum identities, the vanishing axis value of the averaged meridional vorticity and the leading-order behaviour of the periodic field were rechecked by the author (with a computer calculation for the averaged balances and the Wirtinger bound); the pressure bounds of the periodic field were checked only by the computer calculation of that answer.
- Round 19 covered Proposition 26(i). The theorem is correct after an indexing repair (D(s_k) >= lambda^{k-1} D_1); the audit supplied the sharper inequality dD/ds >= D^2/(2 G'^2 (1 + C^2)), so the theorem holds whenever int^infinity dr/(r (1 + C(r)^2)) = infinity, with no monotonicity, while an arbitrary unbounded sequence of good radii does not suffice in the scalar class (explicit saturating scalar example). A remark needs theta >= 0; the fixed-data remark is correct with the signed time boundary (only the earlier time is adverse) and with errors compared in consistent viscosity units. For the first construction of 26(i) (from research answer 13, with a computer calculation whose error constants were read, not rechecked) the flux is exactly MM[Phi_R^2] = (nu^2/2) R^{9/4}, and exponents 0 < alpha < 1/2 give saturating scalar examples with flux of order nu R^{1+alpha}; the level inequality of that answer needs a supremum bound on Phi, which is stronger than the mean-square hypothesis.
- Round 20, the research consultation (checked by the author), confirmed the growth criterion with 1 + C^2, constructed an exact saturating scalar solution with C(rho) = log rho (main-term identity checked symbolically by computer; error bounds read), gave the dip example showing that C^2 alone is not enough, computed the meridional vorticity residual of that solution (of order nu^2/(R log^3 R), checked symbolically, the order of the axial damping), and wrote the box inequality with smooth axial weights. The available upper bounds for inventory and mean Dirichlet energy have the same order; these are not two-sided estimates of the actual terms. It derived no improvement of the flux bound from the coupled system.

It found the residual formulas, the linearization, the jump identity, the general-p construction for each fixed p in (1/2, 1], the dip example and the logarithmic residual correct, and repaired an unstated assumption on the axial derivative of the circulation in the scaling test, a flux size that holds only at marginal balance, a missing integrability hypothesis in the jump identity, and two interpretations stated more strongly than the estimates allow. It also proved, independently of research answer 15, that bounded half-line solutions of the long-pattern equation are constant; the author rechecked this proof, with a symbolic check by computer. The scaling calculation and long-pattern analysis were reviewed in round 21, with the scope restrictions stated above. The extension for each fixed p in (1/2, 1], including the required corrector estimates, was reviewed in round 21; no uniformity as p down 1/2 is asserted. It found incorrect formulas (among them the integrating factor attributed to [Sh]), missing hypotheses, incomplete proofs and contradictory verification statements. The formula, notation and scope corrections were incorporated, and the proofs and key estimates appended to the numbered items respond to its list of missing arguments; several requested standalone proofs remain incomplete, and the items concerned say so in their text.

It supplied the short arguments now included in Theorem 5, Theorem 9 case (P), Proposition 19(a) (positive times only; the initial-time identification was removed), Proposition 20(e) (the record-scale dissipation statement), Proposition 21(a), (b) and Proposition 22(a) (boundary terms). The author checked these arguments, and checked the formulas of the tanh example (divergence, circulation residual, the axial derivative of the meridional vorticity residual at (L, 0)) and the dissipation scaling of Proposition 20(e) symbolically by computer; all corrections were incorporated, but the change of variables then written in Proposition 20(e) combined a record-centred ball with an axis-centred integrand (the computer check covers the prefactor and the time interval only); round 23 found this, and it is corrected. Its verdicts INCOMPLETE as a whole for Propositions 16, 18, 25 and 26 (global justification of the weighted integrations, the adjoint construction, the profile classification, some scalar constructions and the model pressure claims) stand, and the Status lines of those items say so. It found Proposition 23(f) correct, with the derivative statement to be read for each fixed order at least one (now stated), and the enstrophy remark and every exponent relation of sec. 3.9 correct (it checked in the text of [Se20] that the Type I definition used there needs only one of three scaled quantities to be bounded). - Round 24 audited the changes made after round 23, compared range by range with the version reviewed there: Proposition 20(e), Proposition 23(f), (g), the new entries of sec. 3.12, sec. 3.9, sec. 4(6)(xiv), (xv) and sec. 5. It found the corrected Proposition 20(e) and the revised sec. 3.9 correct, and Proposition 23(f) and (g)(i)-(v) correct up to quantifiers (0 < m < A in (ii); tau < tau_0 and a generalized inverse in (iv); the sense in which Gamma_U does not tend to 0 in (f)), now stated. - Round 25 audited the changes made after round 24, compared range by range with the version reviewed there: the repairs of Proposition 23(f), (g), the rewritten entry of sec. 3.12 on the time remaining to the singularity, the helicity entry, the new entry on weighted energies of (J, eta), sec. 4(6)(xiv) and sec. 5. It found the repairs correct up to two conventions (the value 0 of the generalized inverse calR on an empty set, and the condition 0 <= chi <= 1 in the cutoff test of (g)(vi)); it confirmed the rescaling, the statement, units and hypotheses of [KMT, Corollary 1.2] (Definition 3.2 and the factor delta^{-1} in N_delta, checked in the text), the remote-bump estimates for instantaneous data, the restart bound, the helicity integration and the computation for the core V_0, and it rederived independently the (J, eta) system, the transport term and the four Gaussian integrals. - Round 37 was a consistency audit of the whole report as revised after round 36. It found the principal conclusions, the status and the counts of this section consistent, rederived the exponent 5/(5 - alpha) of the budget comparison (as an exponent comparison only), and found minor issues of wording, all corrected: the first sentence of sec. 3.7 (only the critical-mass lower bound of Proposition 14 is a single-time statement); the undefined label branch (II-a), replaced by the explicit condition M(s_n)^5/D(s_n)^3 >= epsilon_0 > 0; the hypotheses of the power-law comparison; the BMO quantity of Proposition 19(b) in the summaries (a bound for the meridional vector potential, uniform in tau); the absorption criteria of Proposition 16, which are conditional and whose proof is a sketch; the description of the local model of Proposition 22(d); the window quantifiers of the far-field form of Proposition 23(c); and the scope of the energy bound in the Status line of Proposition 14. After round 37 the author added the atom-radius statement of Proposition 11(vii), the endpoint remark of Proposition 14 (from research answer 34) and the corresponding sentences of sec. 3.7.
- Round 38 audited these additions and the round-37 repairs. The referee rederived the atom-radius bound (with a factor-two slack, and noted that one may take t_m = 0), the constant c(C_*) of the record ball, the distance of the budget point from the axis, the bound |d_z(q^2)| <= 2 sqrt6 S^{3/2} H^{1/2} r^{-2} and its consequence at r >= c M/D (coefficient 2 sqrt3 c^{-2} C_* G), the exponents 5/(5 - alpha) and 5/4, and the far-field quantifiers and counts, and found them correct. After that audit, sec. 3.7 was clarified to concern the backward-diffusion representation of eta, not deterministic particle paths, and to identify both missing estimates (an o(X(s_n)) bound for the inner-region contribution and the all-late-time bound on rho_m), the stale parenthesis in the Status line of Proposition 14 was removed, and the Sobolev constant in the atom-radius proof was renamed K_S to avoid a clash with (K). After round 38 the author added Proposition 18(f) (the truncated potential-vorticity balance, the removal of N(a) < infinity from kappa_n S(s_n) -> infinity, and the exterior localization of the source; from research answer 35, checked by hand) and the completion of the radius bound in Proposition 18(c) by Proposition 11(viii), with the corresponding sentences of the opening, of secs. 3.7 and 3.10 and of sec. 4(6)(xvii).
- Round 39 audited these additions. The referee rederived the truncated balance with its axis-loss coefficient 4 pi, the finiteness of Q_lambda at positive times, the source bound by Y_2(a) + 3 I_in(a, b), the lower bound pi^2 c_0 rho^2/(4 kappa_n) and the volume estimate, kappa_n S(s_n) -> infinity without N(a) < infinity, the constants c_eta and c_Q, the exterior estimate with X_n l_n^4 = epsilon_n kappa_n, the radius bound R_0 <= R_1 + C(C_*) E_0 D_n^3/M_n^5 of Proposition 18(c) and the answer 35 kinematic exponents, and found them correct. It found one gap, in the sufficient condition of sec. 4(6)(xvii): smallness of the inner integral for some sequence c_n -> 0 is automatic (dominated convergence for each fixed n), so the condition must refer to a sequence for which the exterior integral is small, or to a fixed c; and the adjoint pairing is bounded above by a negative constant, so its absolute value is what is bounded below. Both were repaired, together with the time-based diagonal of the key estimates of Proposition 18(f), the positive starting time a in Proposition 18(c), the wording of the round-38 bullet and the description of the answer 35 kinematic family. After round 39 the author added Proposition 18(g) (from research answer 36, checked by hand), the extension of Proposition 18(f) to B_n^2 epsilon_n >= epsilon_0, and sec. 4(6)(xviii).
- Round 40 audited the round-39 repairs and these additions. The referee found the round-39 repairs present and correct, rederived the bound R(X_1)/B_n >= 2 min{R_1, rho}/(4 R_1 + rho), the constant c'_Q, lambda'_n -> infinity and the exterior factor 256 K_0/(c_0^2 c^4 B_n^2 epsilon_n kappa_n), verified the parabolic gradient estimate of Proposition 18(g) independently (by a heat-kernel and Gronwall argument in the moving frame), the cylindrical splitting of grad u, the Lipschitz constant sqrt3 D of the lifted drift, the consequences of (g) and the conditional extraction into LL with its tightness implication, and checked the kinematic descriptions and the Burgers vortex. It required three wording precisions, all made: the bookkeeping of the two past intervals in the Key estimates of (g), the qualifiers 'for all sufficiently large n' and 'a < t <= s_n' in the statement, and 'need not hold for an arbitrary prescribed sequence' in (f). After round 40 the author added Proposition 18(h) (own derivation) and sec. 4(6)(xix) (with research answer 37, checked by hand).
- Round 41 audited the round-40 repairs and these additions. The referee found the round-40 repairs present and correct, rederived the level-band balance (with the exact completion of the square -|grad eta|^2 - q^2 d_z eta = -(d_r eta)^2 - (d_z eta + q^2/2)^2 + q^4/4), its cutoff justification, the terminal lower bound in all of branch (II), the definition and properties of a_n, the constant c_h = c_0 c'_Q/8, the dissipation and circulation consequences and the exterior bound with its quantifiers, confirmed that the sufficient condition of sec. 4(6)(xix) ties the sequence c_n to the exterior estimate, and checked the answer 37 cell, its cutoff and its scalings. The referee found the repairs in (c) and (d) reproduced exactly and correct, rederived the record inequality, the Biot-Savart sign, the bounds on the radii of near-maximizers and the hull statement, confirmed the counts through round 46 and found no other change. It found one deviation: in (a) the report had written that a stagnation-based argument would have to use additional information selecting the distinguished frame, a necessity claim beyond the established insufficiency of the listed properties, where the referee had proposed that it could instead use such information; the referee's wording was restored, which also makes the attribution of the round-46 bullet accurate. - Review 1, audited the finite-window realization of Proposition 27 in an earlier version. The referee rederived the Duhamel difference, the weight ratio, the kernel moment with the Beta function B(3 + a, 1 - a), the Gaussian tail with mass 2^{3/2}, the singular Gronwall step, the smoothing and interpolation bounds and the record inequality at an interior window maximum, and found them correct. It found that the continuity argument then used for the dichotomy (d) was wrong (a smoothly parametrized family can lose regularity at bounded parameters), that the version normalized both the swirl amplitude and the record radius at viscosity 1, which the scaling forbids, and that several consequences were stated too broadly. The normalization and the dichotomy were repaired: (d) is now proved by a direct choice of radii and the statement is made at the viscosity of the normalized member; the consequence was narrowed and the non-claims are listed. The author then checked the repaired version step by step. The proposition keeps its conditional scope: it gives approximation and the stated inequalities under its hypotheses, not a classification of exclusion arguments.
- Review 2, refereed two candidate routes of the author: control of the horizontal-disc flux of the meridional field (rejected: the L^2 bound of the stream function is the estimate already used for Proposition 26(i), its normalized form loses a factor r_n^{-1/3}, and the averaged conclusion of Proposition 26(i) does not give a pointwise one) and an axisymmetric Landau constant (kept as a partial problem, with the limitation recorded in Proposition 28). The referee supplied the initial axis estimate and Hessian identity now in Proposition 28(a), (e); the author checked it step by step, verified the Hessian identity symbolically and the constants numerically, and narrowed the consequence of Proposition 27 to a single record window as the referee requested.
- Review 3, audited the repaired Proposition 27, Proposition 28 at axis points with its cross-references, and a first version of Proposition 29 with a literature comparison. For Proposition 27 the referee rederived the cutoff, Duhamel, weight, kernel-majorant, heat, Gronwall, smoothing and record estimates and found them correct; it required explicit window restrictions L >= 2 and T >= L^2 + 1 for (b) and (c), the kernel-majorant wording, C^0 convergence on a slightly larger ball for the interpolation, the proved upper bound (320 pi/3) K^2 rho^3 for the initial energy in place of an order statement, a narrowed consequence (a conditional compatibility statement, with the strict-maximum hypothesis sufficient and no necessity asserted), the dichotomy wording "at or before T, for arbitrarily large cutoff radii" in sec. 3.20, and the exact constant B_ax in the summary in place of a downward-rounded one. It confirmed Proposition 28(a) and its historical consequence and found that an earlier explanation in sec. 3.21, that the two largest axis singular values coincide, was false (the axis gradient with rows (1, -1, 0), (1, 1, 0), (0, 0, -2) has singular values 2, 2^{1/2}, 2^{1/2}); the explanation and the ordering step of the proof were corrected. For Proposition 29 it rederived the three implications with their constants, the smoothing bounds and the record consequences, and required the choice of the short-time constant for the derivative orders used, a justification of D -> infinity, the finite-prefix qualification of the record statements, the bounds C_S >= (1 + G^{-2})^{1/2} and 1/G <= nu_n <= (C_S^2 - 1)^{1/2}, the present title, the formulation of the uniform condition at all late times (not along a single branch-(I) subsequence), and a qualified literature statement. All of these were made with the referee's wording where it was given. The global constant of Proposition 28(b), (c) was proposed by another referee, written out in an independent derivation and checked by the author step by step and by a high-precision scan; the consequences in Proposition 28(d) and their use in Propositions 11(viii) and 14 are the author's.
- Review 4, audited the integrated text of Propositions 27 to 29, the summaries, the cross-references and the verification notes. It found Propositions 27 and 29 correct as written, including the smoothing constants, the three implications, the record consequences, the literature comparison and the Type II conclusion (a limsup statement, not a uniform growth rate). For Proposition 28 it recomputed all constants and comparison values, confirmed the global bound 3.9184 and the consequences in Propositions 11(viii) and 14, and required: a choice of sign valid when the eigen-component alpha vanishes, with the positivity of k stated, in step (3) of (b); the decimal expansions of the comparison values in (c); the range 1/B_axi <= C_* < 1/B_ax for the shell and a numerical example at an admissible C_* (the earlier example used an excluded value of C_*); and the statement that the scan is numerical evidence for the optimum, not a proof. It also required the window quantifiers in sec. 3.20, a qualified literature sentence in sec. 3.22 and a precise attribution in the review-2 note. All of these were made with the referee's wording.
- Consultation 5, a research and literature consultation on the criterion (SD), found no published or preprint result implying (SD) and no proof of it. It supplied the strict form gamma_n < G of the record inequality in Proposition 29(c) (by the radial derivative of r u^theta at the record point) and a first iterated-logarithm sharpening in the remark after Proposition 29, through [Sh, Corollary 5.4] (since replaced there by the unconditional Proposition 30(d)). The author rechecked both: the strict inequality in full, and for the sharpening the monotonicity of the comparison function, the substitution, the tangent bound and the moments int_0^infinity e^{-s/2} ds = 2 and int_0^infinity s e^{-s/2} ds = 4, and read the proofs of Lemma 5.1, Theorem 4.2 and Corollaries 4.3, 5.2 and 5.4 of [Sh] (the moving-frame change of variables, the similarity variables, the energy identity, the form of the weighted Hardy constant and the pointwise step). The criterion [Wei] used there and the Hardy criterion of Muckenhoupt were not rechecked. Neither addition changes the status of (SD).
- Review 6, a hostile referee of a first version of Proposition 30, rederived the comparison function, its supersolution property and the barrier argument, the killed Brownian representation and the direction of the event inclusion, the small-time Kolmogorov test by time inversion with the conversion of its integral, and all inequalities of the iterated-logarithm envelope, and reran the high-precision check of those inequalities. It identified issues with the regularity assertion, the quantifiers on the blowup records, the extended-real limsup argument and the attribution of part (a), all addressed in the revised text: the comparison function is only C^{2,1} (g is only continuous), which suffices; it suffices to assume limsup gamma_n > 0, by passing to a subsequence; the iterated-logarithm argument starts from an eventual upper bound of the bracket, which covers a limsup equal to -infinity; and the qualitative content of part (a) is implicit in [Sh, Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 4.2], whose quantitative bound implies it, so (a) is credited there. It proposed the constant G in place of 2G, terminal windows (part (b)), the instantaneous speed g, the conclusion S/M -> 0 through first-attainment times, further iterated logarithms and a radial localization; the author checked each and wrote the localization out by a deterministic comparison on a moving strip. It found a localization to a bounded neighbourhood of an axis point unproved without axial control, and no swirl-only version available; neither is claimed. The author rechecked the choice of h_0 in parts (d) and (e) and the bounded case of the Kolmogorov test.
- Review 7, an independent referee of the final text of Proposition 30 and of the passages that report it, rederived every step: the regularity of the moving lateral boundary and the corner compatibility, the killed backward representation, the monotonicity in x, the barrier, the event inclusion, the time inversion and the strict crossings, the joint terminal limit, the first-attainment argument for S/M, the bounds for F with the coefficient 3/2 and further iterated logarithms, the strip localization with its Gaussian constant, and the reduction to [Sh, (5.6)] (with Shahmurov's normalization ell_{h_0}(h) = log(e + log(h_0/h)), which differs from L_2 by o(1)). It found no failing inequality and required five corrections of wording, all made: Theorem 1 gives a lower bound for liminf gamma_n, not for every large n; the envelope bounds the cumulative inward displacement, not the speed; the heat comparison function is bounded by G times a survival probability rather than equal to one; the drift g is outward in the backward comparison diffusion; and the record of review 6 above lists all issues that review raised. The classical sources [Erd], [IM] and [Pet] were not available to it.
- Review 8, three independent referees of Proposition 31. The first examined an earlier version of the comparison function for the exact radial operator, the integral test and parts (a), (c), (d). It confirmed the barrier, the coefficient 5/2 and every constant of the spectral bound, and required repairs: corner control in the construction of the comparison function, C^{2,1} regularity in place of smoothness, separate removal of the time mollification and of the spatial truncation, the Gaussian factor in the bound for the terminal norm, the case G = 0, an explicit contradiction hypothesis in (d), and a narrower sharpness statement. The second examined the extended version with (b) and (e). It showed that the corner-compatible smooth approximation proposed there cannot exist, that the horizon in (b) has to be shortened so that the envelope is evaluated inside its domain, that bounded self-similar inflow and the order of the limits in (b) need explicit treatment, and that the barrier constant on the strip in (e) has to be adjusted. These points are repaired in the printed proof: truncated initial data compatible at both corners with monotone limits, the horizon h_0/2, the reduction to the envelope 2 D_1 v^{1/2}, the order of choice M, then v, then delta and r, and the strip constants. The integral test itself was supplied by a research consultation and rederived step by step by the author. The third referee rederived Steps 1 to 8 of the final text and every displayed constant: the barrier, the monotone limits and the killed representation, the pathwise monotonicity, the Gronwall comparison, the cancellation in logarithmic time, the weighted Hardy constant 32, the backward energy estimate (31.4), the terminal bound, the pointwise bound (31.5), the shifted terminal windows, the classification of the envelopes L_2 + beta L_3 + B, the strip and the exponent arithmetic in (f). It found (a) to (e) correct and found two gaps in (f): for negative beta the reduction to beta = 0 proves only the exponent 5/2, and shrinking h_0 lost part of the stated time interval. Both are repaired by keeping beta, using a working horizon and the bound psi >= L_2/2. The same referee checked the statement of [Wei, Corollary 1.1] in the arXiv version against its use in (f), but not its proof. A numerical evaluation of the weighted Hardy product gave ratios near 2 to e^{C^2}/C^3 for C = 2, ..., 5, against the proved 32.
- Review 9, a hostile referee of Proposition 32. It rederived the scale function and the supersolution identity, the comparison on the superlevel set with its boundary pieces at r = 0, r = r_1 and t = t_0, the closed forms of (b) and the equivalence of (F_0) with kappa > 1, the record argument and the joint liminf; it checked the hypotheses of [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] and [Wei, Corollary 1.1] against their statements together with the constants of Step 5, and verified the exit-time estimates of Remark (2) and the identity of Remark (3). It required: an explicit assumption G < infinity (it gave a finite-energy example with unbounded circulation), a restart at a positive time before the continuation criteria are applied, a definition of the joint liminf, the boundary specification of the comparison diffusion, a weaker attribution in Remark (1), the correction that the generator at the critical inflow, not the raw operator, is the radial Laplacian of R^2, the restriction of Remark (4) to prescribed fields, and the wording of Remark (5). It proposed the extension of (d) to the superlevel-set hypothesis and to time-dependent eps with a common lower profile. - Review 10, a hostile referee of a first version of Proposition 33, parts (a) to (e).
