- Review 11, a hostile referee of part (f) of Proposition 33 and of its literature status. It rederived (f)(i) from (a), the constants and identities of (33.5), the transfer of the comparison to bounded mild ancient solutions with viscosity nu (the uniform derivative bounds of [KNSS, Section 4] that make k_V continuous, the matching at the axis, the Riccati equation with the coefficient 4 nu, the barrier on the unbounded domain, the order of the limits and the extension to earlier times), the use of [KNSS, Theorem 5.2 and Remark 6.1] (mildness is essential: V = sin(tau) e_3 is a bounded ancient classical solution without swirl that is not constant in time), the two sufficient conditions and the monotonicity argument giving the divergent excess int_{-v}^0 k_V - (1/2) log v -> infinity, and (f)(iv) with the Type I swirl and Type I strain rates; it noted that the threshold 1/2 is sharp for the scalar integral test but not shown to be sharp for Navier-Stokes. It found (f) correct and required: a correction of wording in the proof of (iii) (one of the two cases has liminf equal to -infinity), the statement in Remark (5) that sec. 3.12 also gives lower bounds for tau_n from mild restart estimates, the restriction of the rate statement in Remark (5) to a quantitative Type II limsup rate, and the literature qualification now in Remark (6): the qualitative criterion (f)(i) follows from the swirl maximum principle and [CFZ, Theorem 1.1(1)] or [LZ2, Corollary 1.3], and [Sh, Corollary 3.9] contains it; it did not find (33.1) or (f)(iii) in the references it checked, which does not establish novelty. It proposed the stronger lower bound (1/2) log(4 v l_*/gamma_*) in (33.6) and the gap bound G - gamma_* >= G exp(-gamma_* ||grad U||_infty/2), both now in (iv), and warned that the comparison does not localize to a fixed neighbourhood of the axis. The first three passes examined the comparison lemma, the two clocks, the spectral bounds, the block chaining and the energy estimate of (c), and required repairs that are incorporated: the inflow hypothesis on a doubled window, the uniform terminal bound with the normalized weight, the C^1 hypothesis (W2) in (c) in place of an approximation argument that compared eigenvalues in the wrong direction, the starting-state lemma, and the local boundedness of the weights in the Hardy inequality. The fourth pass verified the corrected text and required two wording corrections (the square root of the spectral factor in the proof of (c), and the H^2 regularity at the restart time in (f)). The fifth pass compared the condensed text printed here with the full derivation, rederived the barrier inequality, the clock inequalities, the martingale of Step 3, the constants of (a) including both shift constants, the Jensen bound of Step 5, the level bookkeeping and the exponents of Step 6, the coefficients 81/16 and 3/2 of Step 7, the asymptotics of (d), the shrinking-window argument and the restart, and found no gap in the estimates; it found that (c) as first printed also asserted Cbar^2 = o(Lambda) and L_2 = o(Lambda), which do not follow from (W2) and (T''), that the last assertion of (f) needs the condition Lambda/L_2 -> infinity for the second envelope class, and that Remark (2) misdescribed the weight. These three corrections are incorporated, and the same pass verified the extension (35.1') of Proposition 35 and the derivation of (35.2'). The author rechecked the clock inequalities, the bound lambda_1 <= 1, the starting-state lemma, the Case-1 corollary and the restart.
- Review 16, an independent referee of the second term of c_G in (35.3). It verified the limit of the comparison integral of Proposition 33(a) with a fixed starting time (limsup (T_* - t) w <= (2 C_a - 1)/4), the bounds |u^theta/r| <= G w and ||u^theta||_infty^2 <= mu_0 G^2 w, the bound of the term -2 int (u^theta/r) J Omega dx with no derivative and no radial weight, the largest value of the quadratic form, the optimal lambda with the minimum 2 (C Q)^{2/3}, the threshold 3 mu_0^{-1/3} = 4.0472..., and that the continuation needs only the time integrability of ||Omega||_2^{4/3}; it noted that a rounded threshold must not be rounded upward. The author rederived the argument.
- Review 17, an independent referee of the model statement in Remark (6) after Proposition 34 (exactly self-similar Euler-scale profiles). It verified the backward confinement of the flow of y + V by variation of constants, the invariance of the axis, the exponential identity along trajectories and the harmonic-function conclusion, required the boundedness hypothesis on F near the axis (with the shear counterexample for C^1 fields), corrected an earlier description of the mechanism (the frame flow has fixed points, so no forward escape is claimed), and supplied the comparison with [CIV3].
- Review 18, a research consultation on constant-weight energy arguments under the bounds of Proposition 33(a), (b) (Remark (3) after Proposition 35). It constructed the two families, derived the exact periodic quotient, gave rational enclosures of the constants and treated the axial truncation with both axis terms; its optimization over the parameters is numerical and no sharp supremum is claimed. The author rederived the quotient formula and checked it, the constants and the scaling to C_a = 3/4 by symbolic differentiation and direct quadrature of the original functionals.
- Review 19, two independent consistency checks of the whole report. The first compared each statement with its proof and with the summaries. It found that parts (c) and (e) of Theorem 13 use (A) through parts (a) and (b) and must assume it; a wrong part label for Proposition 29; two remarks after Propositions 33 and 35 that did not match the proofs; a question in sec. 4 that the zero envelope answers trivially; a condition (T') described as necessary that is not; a missing viscosity factor in a cell rescaling, and an obstruction stated without the condition on which it rests; a missing horizontal translation for the gradient-record limits of Theorem 13(d)(I); an asymptotic statement inferred from an upper bound; and a scaling statement that holds only for swirl-free profiles. It also showed that Propositions 31(f) and 36(f) can use [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] in place of a criterion whose proof had not been checked. The second re-derived the key inequalities of Theorems 1, 7, 9 and 13(a), of Propositions 6, 8, 10, 14, 16, 18, 22, 23, 24 and 28 and of the setting of sec. 1.1, checked every internal cross-reference, equation label and citation key mechanically, and compared the cited statements of [KNSS] with the source. It found no mathematical defect in these; it found a proof step of Theorem 1 cited as a part 'Theorem 1(a)' (at nine places), a missing qualification 'for large n' in Proposition 22(b), an imprecise description of a dissipation integral in sec. 4 item 7, and references to unpublished identifiers inside statements. A further referee of the second check confirmed the constants of Propositions 14, 22 and 23 and of sec. 4 items 7 and 8. The author checked every finding against the text and made the repairs; they do not change the conclusions for Case 1, in which (A) is assumed.
- Review 20, a research consultation on the radial strain equation and the exterior part of the inflow on the Type I strain branch (sec. 4 item 6 (xxvi)). It derived the equation for u^r/r and its equivalence with the equation for eta, tested contraction and weighted-norm estimates for the exterior part of the inflow (none closes), constructed the time-dependent kinematic family and the pure-swirl pressure examples recorded there, and gave transport and parcel counts that rest on unproved amplitude assumptions and are not used. The author rederived the strain equation, the vorticity of the family, the bounds for its strain, kinetic energy, gradient, swirl energy production and inflow, the argument that it violates the equation for eta, the axis pressure formula and its second derivative, and the comparison argument for the pressure excess; a symbolic computer calculation checked the differential identities.
- Review 21, an independent referee of the strain-record statements (Proposition 37(a), (b) and Remark (2)), which were derived twice, independently. It confirmed the decay of u^r/r at spatial infinity and the sign of Delta_5 a - d_t a at the record point, required the convention for kbar(sigma) = 0 in (37.2), supplied the present proof of the bound for S(sigma_j), and repaired three compactness statements of Remark (2): the position of the record relative to the axis (rho_j in [0, 1]), compactness without a gradient bound when nu_* > 0 from the smoothing estimate for bounded mild solutions, and the use of the pressure-free weak formulation of [KNSS] for the limit. It also noted that the Burgers vortex, of infinite energy, gives equality for a local model only. The author checked every finding.
- Review 22, a research consultation on the Type I swirl branch (Proposition 37(c), (d), Remark (3)). It supplied the cylinder barrier with the quadratic profile 2 - R^2/L^2 (the factor 2 in place of F(beta) in (37.3), under A < 2 nu) and its consequence for m(tau), showed that the budget (34.5) for the potential vorticity gives no improvement by itself, and reported a counterexample to a particular localized Biot-Savart proposal for the compression on the parabolic cylinder (the Dirichlet Green formula on a ball leaves a harmonic term larger than the needed compression); its precise formulation and field are not reproduced or used here. Its heuristic scale discussions are not used. The author rederived the computation of calL phi, the comparison argument, the conditional rate and the gap analysis.
- Review 23, an independent referee of the quadratic cylinder barrier and of the conditional rate for it. It confirmed both, specified the comparison argument (the lifted domain in R^5 with the axis interior, the penalization in the axial direction and its constant, the exponential weight for the sign-indefinite zero-order term and the order of the limits), showed that the threshold 2 nu belongs to the quadratic profile, and supplied the Burgers profile f, which gives (37.3) and the rate of Proposition 37(d) for every finite A_*. The author rederived the identities for f and h and the comparison, checked the identity for calL phi by a symbolic computer calculation, and added the optimization over beta (beta = xi_0) in the consequence of Proposition 37(c) and the boundary values given by the bounded circulation (the bound with Gbar_U in (37.3)).
- Review 24, a hostile referee of Proposition 37 as a whole, of its summaries in secs. 1 to 4 and of reviews 21 to 23. It confirmed (a) to (d), including the record sign, the axis identity, the comparison on the lifted domain with its order of limits, the optimized constant (2 mu_0)^{-1/2} = 1.1080179... and both rates in (d), and found the following defects, all corrected: the Burgers example needs a z-independent swirl (otherwise the two meridional pressure equations are incompatible); the convention at kbar(sigma) = 0 was ambiguous by a factor 2; the comparison in Remark (1) is a leading-order criterion, and the Burgers vortex shows sharpness only of the local pressure inequality; the Euler compactness of Remark (2) needs (A) as an additional hypothesis, and one equality there was an inequality; the comparison with vortex rings needs rings of more than Hoelder regularity; in Remark (3) an integrand o(1/s) was said to have a divergent integral, (d) was called the first quantitative bound although the proof of (34.6) gives O(|tau|^{-1/2}), and the bound with Gbar_U needs the limits in the order A -> 2 nu beta, then beta -> infinity; the expanding radius must be nondecreasing in |tau|; Remark (4) described the zoom-out of [AB] in the reverse direction, read [AB, Remark 3.2] as a negative result, and derived logarithmic energy growth from a saturation that does not give it; review 22 was described as showing a counterexample that is not reproduced. It supplied the derivative estimate (D) with its proof, which makes the exclusion of the Type I swirl branch under an expanding-radius compression bound a proved implication. The author checked every finding, rederived (D) and the pressure compatibility in the Burgers example, and confirmed the reading of [AB] in the arXiv text.
- Review 25, a research consultation on Liouville theorems for bounded mild ancient axisymmetric solutions with a Type I bound and bounded circulation (Proposition 38). It checked in the primary texts the statements of [KNSS] (Theorems 5.2, 5.3, 6.1, 6.2), [SS09] (Theorems 1.1, 1.2, Lemma 3.5, Proposition 3.7), [AB] (Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 3.1 and Remark 3.2), [LZ], [LRZ1], [CSTY2] and [Se20], and found no published statement for this class; it showed that the constant of [SS09, Proposition 3.7] depends on local energy and pressure norms, so that the local estimate gives a bound C/|x'| only in a parabolic region; and it supplied the comparison argument of Proposition 38(a) for lambda = theta = 0 under a two-sided Type I bound on the meridional velocity, together with the deduction (b). The author rederived every step, added the one-sided, superlevel-set and theta forms, the quantitative bound (38.2) and part (c), and checked the change of variables, the equation for F' and the axial bound by a symbolic computation and the asymptotics of F' numerically. An independent referee followed (review 26).
- Review 26, an independent referee of Proposition 38 and its summaries. It rederived the change of variables, the equation and the asymptotics of F' at 0 and at infinity, the inequality calM F <= -1 (which uses only the lower bound for B^R), the axial barrier, the maximum principle on the truncated non-cylindrical domain (any positive maximum of g - H lies where g > lambda, so no regularity of the level set is needed) and the order of limits (eps, delta -> 0 for fixed S, then S -> infinity); it confirmed (a), (38.2), (b) (with a check that [KNSS, Theorem 5.2] needs no decay, and the example U = e^tau e_Z with pressure -e^tau Z, which shows that mildness is needed for constancy) and the constants of (c). It found the kinematic passage of (c) literally false off the ball where the cutoff equals 1 (repaired by restricting to Z = 0 and (1 + |tau|)^{1/2} << R <= (1 + |tau|)^{3/4}), the comparison with the Burgers criterion in Remark (1) imprecise (repaired), and the absorption rate in Remark (3) wrong (its order is C^3 e^{-C^2/nu}, not C e^{-C^2/nu}; the remark was replaced by the frozen-envelope consequence of (38.2) and the endpoint theta = 1/2 for C = 0, both supplied by the review; the author checked the asymptotics of F_{C, theta} numerically and the endpoint by hand). The spectral rate itself was not checked by the author and is not used.
- Review 27, an independent referee of Proposition 38(d) and its summaries. It confirmed the lower semicontinuity of k (strict superlevel sets are open, including at times where k is infinite) and the scaling identity a ((U^R)^- - C a^{-1/2})^+/R = ((B^R)^- - C)^+/rho, the finiteness of M_{C,theta} from the asymptotics of rho F' at 0 and at infinity, the closed form M_{0,theta} = 2/(1 - 2 theta) (through x e^x E_1(x) = int_0^infinity e^{-t} x/(x + t) dt, increasing from 0 to 1), the numerical values of M_{C,theta} by independent quadrature (as numerical checks, not certified bounds), the first-contact argument (strict inequality on the parabolic boundary, the continuous local minorant kappa_*, the backward difference quotient, which needs no Lebesgue point), the time conversion in (38.3), the rearrangement (38.4) and both logarithmic coefficients of the comparison with (34.3). It found four imprecisions, all repaired: the barrier is absolutely continuous, not Lipschitz, in sigma (the argument needs no more); (38.4) is a positive lower average in logarithmic time, not a positive density of times (spikes of unit area with summable widths have the first property and not the second); the comparison with (34.3) gives logarithmic lower bounds of the same form, not (38.4) with its constants; and the kinematic family of Proposition 37, Remark (3), satisfies (38.4) for large T (its k tends to alpha > 1/2), not for every T, while the statement that an exclusion needs the inflow bound was narrowed to exclusions through Proposition 38(a).
- Review 28, a research consultation on the Type I strain sub-branch of Proposition 33(e)(ii). It found no published criterion for a one-sided bound on U^R/R with an arbitrary constant and no exclusion; it supplied the counterexample to a Gaussian-localized positivity of the swirl-weighted frozen strain, the axial Galilean invariance of the hypotheses, the weighted energy identities with their unsigned transport fluxes, the blow-down scalings and the cut-off fields of Proposition 38, Remark (4). The author checked the kernel value, the divergence, the formula for U^R/R and the circulation residual of the cut-off fields (the latter three by a symbolic computation), and re-read [QZ, Theorem 1.1] and its proof in the arXiv text: its hypothesis is a bound on (u^r)^- uniform in space, used through a drift depending only on time, so it does not apply to the linear bound theta R/(tau_* - tau) of the sub-branch.
- Review 29, an independent referee of Proposition 38, Remark (4). It confirmed the pressure of the collapsing Burgers vortex, the reduction of the circulation equation, the swirl bound with the explicit maximizer x_0 (e^{x_0} = 1 + 2 x_0) and mu_0 = 4 x_0/(1 + 2 x_0)^2, the threshold statement for (38.1), the identification with (33.4), the maximum-principle bound of the first fact (with a growing barrier, so that no spatial decay is needed), the multiplier and the off-origin kernel of the second fact with c = 1/(8 pi^2), the Galilean transformation, and the identities, the bounds and the circulation residual of the cut-off fields. It found: the point normalization Gamma(e_1, 0) = 1 does not give the full normalization of the Case-1 limits (an example with d_R U^theta(e_1, 0) > 0), which holds for the specific parameters now stated; the blow-down limit is the Burgers formula with a = -tau, and the convergence of eta to zero holds on tau <= -delta only; the conclusions that a proof must use the bound |U| <= K, or information away from the parabolic region, or a particular far-field estimate, were necessity claims beyond what the examples show; the coincidence with the family of Proposition 37, Remark (3) needs its profile replaced; the linear response needs a stated convergence and choice of potential, and the divergence remark was incompletely justified. It supplied the explicit two-bump example for the negative Gaussian-weighted pairing and the verification of (38.4) for every T. All findings were applied; the author checked the normalization constants and the counterexample numerically, the formula for eta of the cut-off fields by a symbolic computation, and the remaining items by hand.
- Review 30, an independent referee of Proposition 39 in its first form (parts (a) to (e) with (d)(i), (d)(ii) and the exclusion under (H2), (H3) and (H4)). It confirmed the dependence of C_loc and every cutoff and Young constant of (a) and the source bounds; the Feynman-Kac representation of (b) with a true martingale on finite horizons, the vanishing terminal term through the uniform decay of Proposition 34(d)(iii), and the radial equation; the sign and normalization of the localized Biot-Savart formula, the axial maximum (3 pi/8)/L of the harmonic part, the Stieltjes form (39.7) and the coefficients 2/3 and C_1(delta) of (c); the hitting bound, the supermartingale, the occupation estimate and (39.5) of (d)(i), and C_eta, the inner and exterior coefficients and A' of (d)(ii); and the choices of parameters, the order in which they are fixed (no circularity), the inner-point mass bound, C_* and the contradiction with Proposition 38(c) in (e), with the Case-1 normalization as the only place where nonvanishing circulation enters. It found one false comparison in the proof of (c): for L < R_x/2 the exterior contribution is at most sigma_4 A_s (R_x/2)^{-delta}, not (sigma_4/2) A_s (R_x/2)^{-delta}; (39.4) is unchanged since C_2(delta) > sigma_4. It asked that the envelope of Remark (2) be stated for fixed a, that the domain of the Type I consequence of (39.5) be stated, that the logarithmic loss of Remark (3) be stated as a worst case at R_x of order s^{1/2}, and that the occupation statement of Remark (4) be made quantitative and compared with the envelope budget rather than with the budget of the source; it supplied the bounded kinematic fields of Remark (1) and the quantitative form of Remark (4). All findings were applied, and the author checked them by hand. Part (d)(iii), the second statement of (e) and Remark (5) were added afterwards and were not covered by this review.
- Review 31, a second independent referee of Proposition 39, of (d)(iii), the exclusion under (H2) and (H3) in (e), Remark (5) and the sentences of Remark (2) on the circulation-energy identity. It rederived the backward generator identities for Gamma and Gamma^2, the bounds for the martingale integrands, the combined boundary and weight term (the initial term has the favorable sign), the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on the product measure, the hitting bound, every constant of (39.8), and the steady front of Remark (5) with a stream function for its cutoff. It observed that the Type I swirl bound |U^theta|^2 <= C_I/(gamma_* |tau|) replaces the bound obtained from A_* < infinity, so that (H2) and (H3) alone are incompatible; it corrected Remark (4) (an entrance time rather than a hitting time, and the comparison with the tail of the budget is a lower bound only) and asked for f with bounded derivatives in Remark (1) and for the uniform bounds on q in place of smoothness at radii below 3. All were adopted after checking.
- Review 32, a third independent referee of Proposition 39, of (f), the general form of the proof of (e), Remark (6), Remarks (1), (2) and (4), and the literature on the physical corollary. It rederived the rescaling of the strain bound (A_* <= C_a), the energy of q under the Type I strain bound with both weight terms of favorable sign, the first-stretch and layer-cake constants of A''', and in (f)(iv) the generator of R^{-beta} (a + u)^gamma, the boundary equality at arrival, the parameter ranges, the exponent identities and both coefficients of A_kappa, with (39.10) applied at T wedge N; and it checked the hitting bound of Remark (6) with the factor 4 nu, the flux bound and the coupling of Remark (4). It found a reversed inequality in the general form of the proof of (e) (s^{-(3 - p)/2} <= r^{p - 3} for r >= s^{1/2} is false for p < 3) and supplied the corrected inner mass bound B_p s^{-(3 - p)/2} r^{5 - p} with the coefficient 1 + 4/(p - 1), which restores (f)(v); it asked that Remark (1) state that A_* <= C_a on the Type I strain branch, and that the comparison of weights be justified for random stopping times (the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the moments). It found no existing theorem with the hypotheses of the physical corollary, which does not establish novelty. All findings were applied after checking.
- Review 33, a fourth independent referee of Proposition 39, of the joined energy and its uses. It confirmed the interface relations, the Tanaka formula with the coefficient q^2/s of the local time, both drift bounds (the compression is used only inside the unit parabolic cylinders), the expectation step with bounded stopping times and monotone convergence, the exterior conversion and the constants E_q and C_eta'', and the uses in (f)(iii) and (iv) and the reduction of the bound C_d |tau|^{-1/2}. It found the same reversed inequality as Review 32, with the same repair; a stale sentence in the summary of Proposition 39 in sec. 1.3; and in sec. 3 a reversed direction (the joined energy has a lower drift bound) and wording to be qualified (probabilistic arrival, compression bounded by the Biot-Savart terms, the radius 3 of the exterior source bound). It asked for an explicit finite-horizon integrability sentence (moments of R and of the local time). All findings were applied after checking.
- Review 34, a fifth independent referee of Proposition 39, of (f)(vi), Remark (7) and the corresponding sentences of secs. 1.3, 3 and 4. It confirmed the scaling of the Biot-Savart integral, the axial integral pi/(2 d^3), the three-region bound for J with every constant, the choice of theta_0, M'' and C_J, the contradiction with Proposition 38(c), the reductions of (v) and of the (H3) form, and the absence of circularity; and in Remark (7) the divergence and vorticity conventions, the swirl, gradient and compression bounds, the vorticity on the central cylinder, both residuals, the flux identity, the survival and arrival bounds for c = 0 and the similarity equation. It found one error, the exact Gaussian law asserted for the path of the member c = 0 (only the linear comparison process is Gaussian, and the arrival conclusion follows by coupling), and overstatements: that a derivation must use both evolution equations (the example shows only that the listed bounds and budgets are insufficient), the attribution of the central vorticity to the axial part of the stream function, the missing restriction |tau| >= 1 for the central formula in sec. 1.3, the omission of the (H3) form in the summaries, and the conditional character of the tail computation. It asked for the value J(0). All findings were applied after checking.
- Review 35, a sixth independent referee of Proposition 39, of the additions to Remark (7) (the comparison with an Euler solution, the relative residuals, the self-similar circulation model and the homogeneous fields of degree 1). It confirmed the Euler solution and its pressure, the exact transport of its eta, both residuals with their expansions, the reduced transport equation, the ray rule, the constant-rate identity and the integral formula for the forced polar vorticity. It found an error in the normalization of the stream function of the homogeneous fields, a gap in the circulation statement (boundedness on the exterior gives only a constant circulation; zero follows from the equation on all R > 0 by continuation), two missing conditions (G + theta_c > 0, and smoothness of the Euler field only off the axis), the singularity at the axis of a vortical polar sector, and an overstatement on the global character of the failure. It supplied the coefficient recursion at all orders, the argument that bounded vorticity at the plane forces the Burgers profile without analyticity, and the indicial polynomial. All findings were checked by the author and applied.
- Review 36, a seventh independent referee of Proposition 39, of parts (f)(vii) and (f)(viii) and the corresponding summaries. It confirmed the closed form of the angular kernel, its monotonicity in R and (39.17) (with the axis case written separately), every constant of the outer, core and inner-point estimates, the layer-cake corollary, the reduction of (vi), the duality direction and the subinvariance argument behind the mass bound (39.18), and all constants of (viii). It found that the reduction of (vi) gives finite constants only for M' large, that the dyadic annuli have area at most 3 pi d_k^2, and that the statement of (viii) overstated the absence of hypotheses on the meridional field; it supplied the explicit approximation of the source from below and an example showing that bounds of the forms (H3) and (H4) give no axial integrability. All findings were checked by the author and applied.
- Review 37, an independent referee of Proposition 38(e), of the consequence (38.6), of Proposition 39(f)(ix) and of the corresponding summaries. It confirmed the similarity-variable identity, the identities for the three exponential barriers and for the barriers of the backward localization, the parabolic boundary of the comparison domain and the first-contact argument (including contact at the terminal time), the treatment of the complement of the cone, the backward localization with m := max{0, sup Gamma_U}, the error 9 e G'^2 eps^{-1} e^{-K' T_0}, the asymptotics of F and the threshold p_* (and that no Type I swirl estimate enters (38.6)), the harmonic term 1/(8 s), the inner-point reduction, the localized mass bound (39.20) with its Gaussian tail and every constant, and the bounds of the periodic example. It found that the proof of (38.6) asserted a limit where only an upper bound for the limsup is proved, and that the summaries in sec. 1 and 3.32 and the last sentence of (ix) overstated what the example shows (it gives sufficient conditions for failure for fixed-amplitude periodic profiles, and the exact condition there is a bound on int_s^{2s} dbeta/l(beta)); it observed that dyadic windows suffice in (39.19). All findings were checked by the author and applied.
- Review 38, an independent referee of Proposition 39(f)(x), Remark (8) after Proposition 39 and the corresponding summaries. It confirmed the identity (39.22) and the sign of its forcing, the cylinder identity and the constant kappa (no factor 2 is lost in the oscillation bound), the pointwise bounds for J and the constant C_J, the event version of the energy bound (the event must be determined by the path up to the stopping time, which holds for F_1), (39.23) with the factor P(F), the integrating factor and the sign of the source in the representation, the supermartingale and P(F_1) <= L^{-1/2}, the three forced contributions and delta, the averaged inherited part, the exit bound through the five coordinates, and the final budget (it noted that eps < 1 is used there); in Remark (8) it rederived the kinematic scaling, the linearized equations, the transported mode, the operator inequalities and gamma, the axis identity, both profile families and the coefficient 48 nu q_4/Q. It found a parenthetical overstatement on R-independent strains, an imprecise attribution of the derivative bound in the exit part, a clash between the compression constant of (f) and the cone width of (x), that the wavelength condition of Remark (8)(b) is sufficient and not necessary (it supplied a short-wavelength bound), the missing integrability proviso in (8)(c) (with an example of infinite total variation), and the missing hypothesis A_* < infinity in the summaries of secs. 1, 3.32 and 4. All findings were checked by the author and applied.
- Review 39, an independent referee of Proposition 37(e), Remark (5) after Proposition 37, the edited Remark (3) there, Proposition 39(f)(xi), the edits in (v) and in the proof of (x), and the corresponding summaries. It confirmed the identity for calL(w phi) and the comparison with the integrating factor, the lower semicontinuity and measurability of m_P, the inequality W_* <= A_* log 2, the dyadic recursion and the constant in (37.5) (which needs only (CW) and the boundedness of q), the excess form and the growing-envelope bound, the record and concentration bound of Remark (5)(c), the construction of Remark (5)(d) and the failure of both evolution equations there, the dyadic bound for the compression term of the joined energy with the constant D_W, the list of all uses of the compression hypothesis in the proofs of (iii) to (x), and the two edits in the proof of (x) (the factor 2 in C_4 and the event version through a stopping time equal to a large constant off the event). It found that the iteration behind the rate in Remark (5)(a) had to be written out, that the test field of Remark (5)(d) does not satisfy the normalization -gamma_* U^R(e_1, 0) >= 1 and so does not show compatibility of the failure of (CW) with all properties of the limits, nor that a proof of (CW) must use a particular evolution equation, that the sentence of (v) on A_* and (CW) was ambiguous, that the replacement of D_1 by D_W must include its explicit occurrence in the forced part of the proof of (x) and that (ix) needs only boundedness of q, that sec. 3.32 retained a pointwise compression bound under (CW), and that sec. 1.3 called the core source bound necessary. All findings were checked by the author and applied.
- Review 40, a hostile independent referee of Proposition 39(f)(xii), the energy paragraph of Remark (8)(b) after Proposition 39 with its summary in sec. 3.32, and the repairs of review 39. It confirmed (xii) with its constants (the application of Proposition 33(a) up to sigma = T_*/2, the scaling of a_U, the Fatou step with the lower semicontinuity of k_U, the window inclusion, the use of (xi) and the spike example) and its summaries, without repair. It confirmed the energy identity term by term (including the time derivative of z^2 K), the square completion, the coupling bounds and the Hardy bound with c_2, and required the restriction to nonzero axial modes, the sign condition z z' <= 0, a regularity class and a semigroup construction of the mild evolution, the withdrawal of an inference from the decay of the coupled evolution to the norm of the feedback iteration and of an unsupported reference to numerical transients, the degeneration of the energy at high radial frequencies, and the distinction between the homogeneous and forced problems; it supplied a forcing bound with an additional factor |z| under a weighted bound on the tail. It confirmed the repairs of review 39, and required the case eps >= 1 of Remark (5)(a) after Proposition 37 and the withdrawal of a necessity claim in Remark (3) there, whose kinematic field also violates the circulation equation. - Review 41, an independent referee of the observation in Proposition 37, Remark (2), that the viscous alternative at the strain records needs Type II swirl, and of the four overview paragraphs of sec. 1.2 on near-axis strain, the Type I swirl branch, strain records and Type I inflow against Propositions 33 to 39. It confirmed the observation, with the historical swirl bound, the past interval covered by the rescaling, the compactness at positive viscosity and the axis case of the normalization, and asked for the viscosity-normalized field in the statement on LL and for the separation of vanishing viscosity from Euler compactness in the summaries. It matched every assertion of the four paragraphs to its source and confirmed their constants (mu_0, the crossover G = 1.6584..., the coefficient 2 C_a/(2 C_a - 1) and its upper bound, the pressure constants at the records, C_I = G^2 exp(2 W_k)/4). It asked for four repairs, all applied: a precise description of the optimizers in the entry [CLi] (it is the shifted eigenfunction that vanishes on the boundary); the explicit replacements in (40.2) and the remainder e_c(s) when c > 1, with the remark that (40.1) is not evaluated with the new constants; the check needed in (xiv)(7)(b) if the later estimates are recomputed; and a precise form of the closing comparison with the heat semigroup, with a short proof of the drift-free constant. The identification of the sharp constant rests on the optimizer theorem of [CLo] as described in [CLi]; numerical agreement alone would not justify it.

- Review 69, a second consistency audit of the summary layer (the Overview, sec. 1.3, secs. 3.30, 3.32 and 3.33, sec. 4 and Reviews 64 to 68) against Proposition 37, Remark (5)(c), item (10)(h), (i), and Proposition 40 with Remarks (1) to (6). - Review 90, an independent referee of the passages changed after Review 87 (the repairs of Reviews 88 and 89, the new sec. 2 item for Proposition 40, the qualifications in sec. 3.10 and sec. 3.12, and the entries for Reviews 88 and 89), against the body. It found consistent with the body the sentence after the status label, the lists of results with sketch, conditional and key-estimate status, the restored restrictions of (39.29) and qualifications of Propositions 33(a) and 35, the sufficient alternatives of Proposition 40 and their independence from (39.19_H), and the repairs in sec. 3 and sec. 4. It found eight defects: the new sec. 2 item said that the bounded kinematic example attains the thresholds, whereas it shows only that they cannot be raised and the constant-profile endpoint is excluded (corrected); the opening and sec. 1.3 extended the conclusion of that example to the pressure condition, which the example does not test (restricted to the compression and axial stretching bounds); the opening stated the pathwise criterion without the conditions on the profile and the error (added); the verification paragraph said that every Status line of the proofs with key estimates specifies omissions, which one does not (reworded); and the Review 88 entry misdescribed two repairs and gave an unsupported reason for keeping the label (corrected).
- Review 91, an independent referee of the repairs of Review 90 as applied and of the thirty-seven items of sec. 2, against the body. It found the repairs consistent with the body except the reason given for the pressure qualification: a prescribed field can satisfy the momentum equation (a constant field does), and the point is that the construction of the example does not impose it (corrected in the opening, in sec. 1.3 and in the entry for Review 90). It found thirty-three method items consistent with the cited proofs and four defective: item 6 omitted the clipped inner radius min{D/H, M/D} and the empty annulus of Theorem 7; item 13 asserted the lower bound c_0/2 on a whole disc and gave kappa N instead of kappa N/pi for the meridional L^1 norm, whereas Proposition 14 obtains a/2 on a disc of radius a/(2 L_f); item 20 attributed the survey of published hypotheses, the literature search and the computer checks to the proof of Proposition 23; and item 34 did not locate the Bernstein estimate in Remark (3) of Proposition 37 (all corrected). Further audits of the same revision found that the pointwise majorizations behind the bounds for the sparse parts in Remark (6) of Proposition 40 need s >= 1, and the resulting bounds for S(s) and T(s) fail for small positive s (the range s >= 1, which covers their use, was added, as recorded under Review 72), that sec. 3.29 stated the extension of Proposition 36(f) without its hypothesis on the near-axis strain on a terminal interval (added), and that the opening stated the Euler cone form of the axial stretching criterion as giving the pathwise bound at every age, whereas it gives that bound eventually, which suffices by Remark (9)(f) (corrected).
- Review 92, an independent referee of secs. 3.1 to 3.20 against the printed results. It found that several summaries stated proof-sketch or unreproduced content as established (the whole-space scalar models of Propositions 25(d)(ii) and 26(f), the profile classification of Proposition 25(f), the scalar sharpness construction and the wavelength example of Proposition 26(i), the pressure bounds of the periodic field of Proposition 26(h), the adjoint construction of Proposition 18(c) and the kinematic family of sec. 3.11); that the hypotheses of Theorem 5 and of Propositions 10 and 21(c), the quantifiers of Proposition 18(f) and the dependence of Proposition 26(e) on the box family were not stated; that sec. 3.16 counted the conditional rate packages among the ancient Liouville theorems and did not say on which domain the first two classes need their bounds; that sec. 3.17 cited a derivative estimate that is not displayed; that the balance in sec. 3.12(e) was called exact although it is an inequality; and that the scope of the kinematic family of Proposition 37, Remark (3) in sec. 3.12(e) and the localization hypothesis of Proposition 26(g) were not stated. The author checked each finding against the printed results and applied qualified versions, keeping as proved the statements that are proved (the main theorem and the long-pattern rigidity of Proposition 26(i)). Further audits of the same revision corrected the description of [LZZ] (finite p, with the decay condition as a separate hypothesis), the windows in the source statement of sec. 3.17 (windows ending at the record time, Proposition 24(e)) and the description of the vanishing averages of the first model of Proposition 26(f), extended the qualifications listed in the overview to sec. 3, and corrected three further passages: the growth hypothesis of Proposition 26(g) in sec. 3.19 (an upper bound), the retention of the denominator of (A) in the limit in sec. 3.3 (it need not be retained), and the size of the swirl source on the near-maximal set in sec. 3.16 (now stated with the square-root deficit estimate of Proposition 23(e); a later audit noted that on the near-maximal set of Proposition 23(b), where the deficit is at most (A/2) e^{-lambda_{R_0}}, this estimate is exponentially small in lambda_{R_0}, as the earlier text had said without giving the estimate).
- Review 93, an independent referee of the repairs recorded under Review 91 (the ranges and constants in Remark (6) of Proposition 40 and their downstream uses, the hypothesis added in sec. 3.29, the Euler cone, endpoint and pressure sentences of the opening and of sec. 1.3, and items 6, 13, 20 and 34 of sec. 2). It confirmed all of them and found that the entries for Reviews 72 and 91 misdescribed the range of the sparse bounds (the bound for T(s) had been stated for every s > 0, and s >= 1 suffices for the pointwise majorizations behind the sparse bounds, the bounds fail for small positive s, and no sharp threshold was determined); both entries were corrected.
- Review 94, an independent referee of the repairs recorded under Reviews 92 and 93, as applied. It confirmed most of them and found four defects in sec. 3: an inference in sec. 3.19 from vanishing weighted mass to zero density of the superlevel sets (what follows is zero mean of the separated superlevel sets for the chosen Banach limit); a description in sec. 3.12 of the kinematic family of Remark (3) after Proposition 37 as having its circulation placed in the core and as showing that, for prescribed fields, no time-slice information on eta inside the superlevel set suffices (its circulation does not depend on Z, it violates both evolution equations, and it shows only that the listed kinematic bounds do not give the compression bound); a statement in sec. 3.16 that a critical meridional bound on the physical solution is required for the first two classes of Liouville theorems (it is one sufficient route; the localization of the inflow hypothesis of Theorem 5 by Proposition 23(b) was added); and the hypotheses of the long-pattern rigidity in sec. 3.19 (bounded C^4 profiles solving the leading-order equation). It also asked for the restriction m < A/2 and the locality of the derivative bounds in the sec. 3.16 source estimate, and for narrower wording of two clauses in the entries for Reviews 92 and 93. The text was revised accordingly.
- Review 95, an independent referee of the summary layer (the opening through the Summary, sec. 1.3, sec. 4, the items of sec. 2 on Propositions 11(v) and 36 to 40, and the entries for Reviews 88 to 93) against the body. It traced the cited claims, the status qualifications, the statements of the first missing implication and the literature statements, and found them consistent with the body, except: the Summary called the necessary conditions of Propositions 19 to 26 compatible, although their joint consistency is not established (reworded); item 33 of sec. 2 described (W2) as a square-integrable logarithmic derivative (now stated as in Proposition 36); the opening called the swirl source on the near-maximal set exponentially small without the estimate and with an unclear referent for the bound not derived (the estimate of Proposition 23(e) with the deficit of Proposition 23(b), and the bound -r u^r <= 2 on the windows, are now named; sec. 3.16 and the entry for Review 92 were adjusted, since the earlier description in sec. 3.16 as exponentially small was right on that set); and the entry for Review 88 gave a reason for keeping the status label (removed). Its proposal to replace the status label by prose was not adopted.
- Review 96, an independent referee of the repairs recorded under Review 94, as applied, and of the whole of secs. 3.12, 3.16 and 3.19 against the body. It found the repairs consistent with the body except the weighted-mass sentence of sec. 3.19, which omitted the admissible weights and the range 0 < theta < A of the cubic level (restored, with the definitions of a_f and F_f through the common Banach limit), and found the entry for Review 94 incomplete (completed). In the full sections it found, besides many claims traced as consistent: in sec. 3.12, the record dissipation count needs pairwise disjoint record cylinders; the description of the coupled critical meridional energy went beyond Proposition 16, a proof sketch (now stated as there); the backward adjoint reduction is part of a proof sketch (Proposition 18(c)); the list of published Liouville hypotheses was incomplete (the velocity and vorticity criteria, periodicity, the near-axis modulus of the physical circulation and the conditional rate packages were added); the self-similar growth of the five-dimensional mass concerns the full-space mass, not a fixed cutoff; the multiplier psi must be C^2 and the cutoff smooth, nonnegative and compactly supported; and the Gaussian swirl example needs C > 0. In sec. 3.16, the comparison with Proposition 21(c) omitted the range of Gamma_0 and the condition beta_0 > 0, and the vector-potential example shows a limitation for prescribed fields only. All these passages were reworded as stated.
- Review 97, an independent referee of the repairs recorded under Review 96, as applied, together with a parallel reading of sec. 3.19 and a check of the far-field source bound of sec. 3.16. It found the repairs consistent with the body, with these exceptions, all revised: in sec. 3.12 the near-axis modulus of the physical circulation fails along the trajectory, not for the limit; in sec. 3.13 the cutoff of the local mass balance was not specified; in sec. 3.14 the two targets drawn from Proposition 21 omitted their quantifiers (beta_0 > 0 and the range of Gamma_0 for the compression bound; for the Harnack alternative, that both hypotheses of Proposition 21(b) must hold infinitely often for fixed delta and B); in sec. 3.15 the statement that the axial pressure target would not suffice alone was stronger than what was shown; in sec. 3.20 and in Proposition 27, the statement that nothing is obtained after time T contradicted part (a), which gives T_rho > T under its hypothesis; in sec. 3.19 the saturating example in logarithmic means consists of explicit two-level data, not of a field; the entry for Review 96 understated the additions to the Liouville list and the conditions on the cutoff; and the wording of the Gaussian constant was clarified. It also confirmed that the exponential smallness of the far-field source in sec. 3.16 rests on the uniform derivative bounds for a Case-1 limit given by the smoothing estimate, which is now stated there.
- Review 98, an independent referee of the whole of secs. 3.1 to 3.11 against the body. Besides many claims traced as consistent, it found: in sec. 3.9, the statement that the interval-integral consequence of the Type I inflow envelope had not been shown to suffice contradicted Proposition 31(f), which covers it (corrected); the summaries did not consistently carry the proof status of the results they cite (a common status paragraph was added at the head of section 3, and the status of the first power-law consequence in sec. 3.9 is now stated); in sec. 3.2 the outer comparison of Theorem 5 needs R_1 >= R_0; in sec. 3.6 the backward Gaussian continuation needs its time interval, and its gradient factor equals 1 at the terminal time; in sec. 3.7 the circulation structure of eternal limits also uses Proposition 23(g); in sec. 3.10 the threshold 2 - 3/p lies between 4/5 and 2 only for p >= 5/2; and four statements were stronger than what was shown (that an exclusion for one fixed shape constant would not suffice, that scale-dependent stream-function bounds would not suffice, that the larger source rate is reached near the axis, and that the open limit statement for eternal limits requires an interchange of limits). All were reworded as stated.
- Review 99, an independent referee of the repairs recorded under Reviews 97 and 98, as applied, and of the whole of secs. 3.13, 3.14, 3.15, 3.17, 3.18 and 3.20 against the body. It confirmed the repairs (including the new status paragraph, checked against every Status line it names, and the reduction to Proposition 31(f) in sec. 3.9, where the late interval is met by taking h_0 small), except the narrowed statement on what Proposition 27 gives after time T, which was still too strong: under the hypothesis of (a) the local existence theory for bounded data gives a continuation with a bound uniform in rho on a short interval beyond T (revised in the proposition and in sec. 3.20). In the full sections it found, besides many claims traced as consistent (with the Burgers constants, the nonlinear weight identity, the Landau ray value 20 nu/9 and the two-level data recomputed): in sec. 3.14 the threshold of Theorem 5 was described as needed, while the opposite inequality is only a sufficient instance of its hypothesis; in sec. 3.18 the Biot-Savart condition omitted that it applies to the physical field, and the equivalence with the Liouville problem did not state which bound and with which quantifiers (the radius R_0(W) is chosen for each member). All were reworded as stated. A parallel hostile check of Proposition 40 (a) to (c) and Remarks (2) and (7) recomputed every constant and found no error; the threshold for the coefficient of Remark (7) is now stated as C <= 2, as in sec. 4.
- Review 100, an independent referee of the whole of secs. 3.21 to 3.33 and sec. 4 against the body (a second full pass), with the constants, the thresholds and the statements that a question is open checked against the results they cite. It confirmed the constants (0.2751 and 0.2715 belong to different estimates, the density-only bound of Remark (8)(a) and the moment bound of Remark (8)(e)) and asked for nine qualifications, all applied: the driftless bounds with c = 0.16 C^2 and c = 0.0925 C^2 and the density-only upper bound are proved for ages s >= 1 (secs. 3.33 and 4, item 1); the description of arbitrary swirls in sec. 3.33 omitted the smoothness across the axis and the slabwise derivative bounds assumed in Remark (7); the fixed model law starts at (1, 0); the moment bound of Remark (8)(e) is stated with its hypotheses (nu = 1, start (1, 0), an axisymmetric incompressible field with bounded derivatives, positive eternal survival); in sec. 3.32 the absence of the logarithm without radial velocity uses the global dyadic source budget of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(5)(e); and in sec. 4, item 6(xxvi), the axial flux argument gives an improper integral of u^r in z, not absolute integrability.
- Review 101, an independent referee of the repairs recorded under Review 99, as applied, and of the whole of sec. 2 against the body. It confirmed the repairs (the uniform continuation in Proposition 27 and sec. 3.20, with the time c nu/K_1^2 from the contraction estimate for the bilinear term, the sufficient instance of Theorem 5, the physical-field qualification and the memberwise radius in sec. 3.18, and C <= 2 in Remark (7)) and the qualifications of Review 100. In sec. 2 it traced every method item to the body and asked for six repairs, all applied: the description of the long-pattern part of Proposition 26 named circulation equations and linearizations that the body does not print (it prints the leading-order steady vorticity equation); the qualifications of the overview did not name sec. 2; the weighted swirl energies need p > 3/2 and Y_p finite; the energy inequality of Proposition 35 is an upper bound after normalization to nu = 1, not a growth rate; the historical smoothing bounds of Proposition 29(a) hold at sufficiently late times; and the cylinder barrier of Proposition 37 needs beta > 0 and 0 <= A < 2 nu beta.
- Review 102, an independent referee of the qualifications recorded under Review 100, as applied, of sec. 1.1 and its uses, and of a second pass through the opening, the Summary and sec. 1.3 against the body. It confirmed the qualifications (with the axial flux argument written out: the disk flux is uniformly Lipschitz in z and square integrable, hence tends to 0 at both ends) and every definition of sec. 1.1 and its uses, and asked for five repairs, all applied: in the opening, the zero-radial-velocity bound was attributed to the cone-local source budget, while it uses the global dyadic budget; the first missing implication named only the branches of Theorem 13, while sec. 4, item 1 also states the exclusion of the swirl-record limit in each alternative of Proposition 33 as sufficient; and the reduction of Theorem 3 was said to show that an exclusion for one fixed C_* would not settle the Liouville problem, which it does not show. In sec. 1.3 the hypothesis of Proposition 32 was said to fail on every Case-1 trajectory and, in the same sentence, not to be shown to fail; it fails by Proposition 32(c) and Theorem 1, and the sentence now says so; and the converse to (KP_0) was said not to have been examined, while Remark (1) of Proposition 31 settles it for F = 0 and leaves it open for nonzero envelopes.
- Review 103, two further independent referees, of Propositions 37(a) to (d) and 38(a) to (c), and of Proposition 34 and Proposition 40, Remark (8)(a), (b) and (d), against their proofs. They recomputed the constants (mu_0, (2 mu_0)^{-1/2}, F(1), the Burgers constants of Proposition 38, Remark (4), the heat-splitting coefficients, the constants of Remark (8)(a) and (b) and the crossing index there) and reproduced the numerical illustrations of Remark (8)(d) by an independent quadrature, within the stated accuracy of about one percent. They found no error and asked for three wording repairs, all applied: in Proposition 38(c) the radius rho_lambda is defined only for lambda in (0, 1) (for lambda = 0 the bound is trivial), and the proof of (c) now states C >= 0 and theta in [0, 1/2), as in the statement; in the proofs of the Bernstein estimate and of (34.6) the maximum principle on unbounded domains uses a positive barrier growing at spatial infinity whose coefficient is sent to zero, not a vanishing barrier.
- Review 104, two further independent referees, of Proposition 39(f)(xiv) items (1), (5) and (6) with their uses in Proposition 40, Steps 1, 2 and 5, and of Proposition 33(e) and (f), against their proofs, together with an own check of (xiv)(6)(a) and (b). They recomputed the constants (N_3, C_N = 2 6^{1/2}/pi^2, the constants of (6)(a), (b) and (d)(ii), the constant c(C_a) and the constants of (33.4) to (33.6)) and found no error. Four wording repairs were applied: in (5)(a) the logarithm of (3) is attributed to the integration over the observation times (the pointwise sum over dyadic lags is bounded); in (5)(d) the time bump is nonnegative with unit integral, as the mass count uses; in (5)(f) the solution class is stated, and the Gronwall step is stated for finite initial weighted mass and finite source mass (otherwise the inequality is trivial); in (6)(a) the summary of the cylinder mass bound keeps the proviso B > 0 and names the exponentially small term. A further independent referee of the sharp swirl-free inequality of Proposition 11(v) and of the changes of Reviews 101 and 102 found no error and recomputed all rational certificates; no change was needed.
- Review 105, an independent referee of Theorems 1, 2 and 3, Proposition 8(c) and Theorem 13 against their proofs, with the cited statements of [KNSS, Theorems 5.1, 5.2 and Remark 6.1] and [LZ2, Corollary 1.3] checked in the source texts. It confirmed the arguments and asked for precision in the statements, all applied: the record identity of Theorem 1 is stated for records with S_n > S(0), so that t_n > 0 and the one-sided time derivative exists (this excludes at most finitely many records); the converse of Theorem 3 names the topology and the operations of the closure (axial translations, time translations into the past, parabolic scalings, the reflection) and claims only the stated properties of the limit field in Theorem 2; Proposition 8(c) states the thresholds s >= max(t_A, t_P), the interval of definition of the rescaled fields, the passage to subsequences along records s_n -> T_*, the horizontal translation needed to put the viscous limits with bounded axis distance into LL, and the choice of the maximizer in the closed half-plane x_2 = 0, x_1 >= 0 used by the planar formula; Theorem 13(a) states that its consequences of (A) hold for t >= t_A.
- Review 106, an independent referee of Propositions 6, 10, 12, 14, 15, 17 and 22 against their proofs. It confirmed the arguments and found five defects of statement, all checked by hand and applied: Proposition 22 now fixes the sign at each record by the reflection P, since the records of sec. 1.1 use |u^theta| while the proof uses u^theta(r_n, z_n, t_n) = S_n; the swirl-level statement of Proposition 15 now carries the uniform lower bound kappa(s) >= c at all late gradient records that its proof uses; in Proposition 22(d) the Burgers vortex has alpha = 4 k nu, so the cylinder radius is (K^2 - 1)^{1/2}/(2 sqrt5 k nu); Proposition 11(vii) now states the decay o(sigma_n^{-1/2}) along a sequence that Proposition 12 requires, rather than an exponent; and Proposition 18(g) cites the Landau envelope S^{1/2} H^{3/2} as item (ii) of the L^infty budget of Proposition 14, where it is derived.
- Review 107, an independent referee of Theorems 4, 5 and 7 against their proofs, of their later citations, and of the changes recorded in Reviews 104 and 105, with [KNSS, Theorems 5.2, 5.3] and [LP, Corollary 1.1] checked in the source texts. It confirmed the three theorems and the changes of Reviews 104 and 105, and found two defects of description, both applied: the summary of Route A in sec. 3.2 now states the scope of the obstruction proved in Theorem 4 (the condition -R V^R >= nu fails on vertical segments longer than K R^2/nu), and Review 105 now describes the maximizer of Proposition 8(c) as lying in the closed half-plane x_2 = 0, x_1 >= 0, since the maximizer may lie on the axis.
- Review 108, a reading pass over the sharp swirl-free inequality of Proposition 11(v) as entered, with every constant and the three rational comparisons recomputed in exact arithmetic (no gap found), and two further independent referees of Proposition 39(a) to (e) (all constants recomputed, no error) and of Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(7)(a), (b), (e), (f) and (8)(b) to (d). Applied after checking by hand: the Overview now says that for C_* < sqrt7/8 there is no planar or swirl-free axisymmetric field with the bounds of Proposition 8(c), since the inviscid limits have no swirl (a field with swirl and quotient 0.313019 exists); in (8)(d)(i) a displayed intermediate expression carried an extra factor nu (the result 2 pi h nu was right) and the mass statement now holds for 0 <= t <= t_r, where the cutoffs equal 1; the two counting statements of (7)(a), (b) carry their quantifiers over delta > 0 and d > 0; in (8)(d)(ii) the cylinder mass and the averaged flux identities are stated for a <= l <= L_n (respectively a <= r <= L_n) during T_n <= s <= 2 T_n, which the radii used there satisfy.
- Review 109, an independent referee of Propositions 11, 16 and 18 against their proofs and of the changes recorded in Reviews 106 to 108. It confirmed the arguments at the level of their Status lines (Propositions 16 and 18 remain proof sketches with the stated omissions) and the changes of Reviews 106 to 108, and found three defects of statement, all checked by hand and applied: Proposition 11(vi) is stated for gradient records s >= max(t_A, t_P), since its local mass bound uses (A) and the normalization of Proposition 8(c) at s (the upper bound on epsilon(s) needs no restriction); Proposition 18(g) defines M_n, H_n and S_n at s_n, so that its final normalization does not mix the swirl records of sec. 1.1 with the gradient records; and the record statements of Proposition 22 assume S_n > S(0), as Theorem 1 does. It also supplied the absorption factor theta(p) of Proposition 18(a), now displayed after a check by hand.
- Review 110, an independent referee of Propositions 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 25 and 26 against their proofs and their later citations. It confirmed the BMO normalization, the physical cylinder sizes, the inflow thresholds and the cylinder and flux identities, and found the following, all checked by hand or by a symbolic computation and applied: in Proposition 26(f) the value -(5/2) beta^2 of R^3 b.grad eta at (R, R) is a limit as R -> infinity, not an equality at finite R (the exact rational expression is now given); in Proposition 26(g) the bump example satisfies only the first bulk condition; the proof of Proposition 26(d) states a liminf; Proposition 19(d) holds for n >= n_0(A); Proposition 21(c) names its test functions and says that only an upper bound for the flux diverges; the sequence example of Proposition 26(i) and the periodic field of Proposition 26(h) carry their review status locally. It also supplied a proof that no odd steady slender profile with bounded axial velocity and nonzero vorticity satisfies the flux bound of Proposition 25(b), through the identity C_4 = 8 nu beta k E_1(g) and the long-pattern rigidity of Proposition 26(i); the identity was checked by a symbolic computation, and Proposition 25(f) and sec. 3 now rest the exclusion on it, while the finer classification is marked as unproved and unused.
- Review 111, a second independent reading of Theorems 4, 5 and 7 and Propositions 28 to 32, 35, 36, 37 and 39 against their proofs, with the constants recomputed. It found no error of substance and ten imprecise passages, all checked against the proofs (and, for the cited Harnack lemma, against the source) and repaired: the quantifier on R_0 in Theorem 5; the attribution of the full integral test to Petrovskii in Proposition 30, now marked as not checked against that source; the reason why the restarted datum lies in H^2 in Proposition 31(f); the endpoint c = 3/2 for the criterion of Wei in Proposition 31; the time-dependent form of Proposition 32(a), now stated with the barrier built from the lower bound eps_*; the description of Proposition 31 in the opening; the scope of the optimality of beta = 1/2 in Proposition 39(f); the dependence of the constant of the cited Harnack lemma on the ratio M as well as on N_R in Proposition 37 Remark (4); and the passage to the limit on truncations in Steps 6 and 7 of the proof of Proposition 36, now done on the integrated inequalities.
- Review 112, a second independent reading of Proposition 27, Proposition 37 Remarks (1), (3), (5)(a), (b) and Proposition 39(f)(xii), (xiii), (xiv)(7)(c), (d) against their proofs, with the constants recomputed. It found one overstatement and seven imprecise passages, all checked against the proofs and repaired: the kinematic field of Proposition 37 Remark (3) is now said to satisfy the listed constraints, not every constraint that does not involve the equations (it violates (34.5)); the choice of K after the other parameters in that Remark; the reference to Proposition 39(f)(xi) in the Status line of Proposition 37; in Proposition 27 the normalization remark (the resulting viscosity is 1/gamma'), the time ranges of the window bounds in (b), and two items of the list of what is not claimed; and the scope of the ring example in Proposition 39(f)(xiv)(7)(c).
- Review 113, an independent reading of Propositions 27, 33, 34 and 38 against their proofs, with the constants of (38.3) recomputed. It found two gaps in proofs and several overstatements, all checked and repaired: the proof of Proposition 33(f)(ii) now treats a record at the initial time; the comparison with (34.3) in Proposition 38(d) now separates the parameter tau_* of (38.4) from that of Proposition 34(d)(iii) and integrates the allowance term explicitly; the record range in Proposition 33(e)(ii) is that of Theorem 1; and the statements on the circulation superlevel sets in Proposition 34 Remark (2), Proposition 38(d) and Remark (4), and in Sections 1.3, 2 (item 31), 3.30 and 3.31 now carry the restriction 0 < lambda < 1 and the correct scope of the unbounded example.
- Review 114, an independent audit of the summary layer (the overview, sec. 1.3, sec. 2, sec. 3 and sec. 4) against the numbered results, their Status lines and Reviews 104 to 111. It confirmed the statements of the first missing implication and the treatment of the cited literature apart from the items below, found no correction of Reviews 104 to 111 that had been undone, and found overstatements and omitted thresholds, all checked against the body and repaired: the verification status of Proposition 25, whose profile exclusion in (f) is proved (also in its Status line, and in sec. 1.3); the qualification of the first construction of Proposition 26(i), of the periodic field of Proposition 26(h) and of the whole-space model of Proposition 25(d) where the summaries use them; the finite-record and limiting inflow bounds in sec. 3.10; the thresholds S_n > S(0) and t >= t_A in the summaries of Theorem 13, Propositions 14, 15 and 22 (secs. 2 and 3.6, 3.7, 3.15); the restriction to sequences tending to T_* in the opening; the hypotheses of the periodic model profiles in sec. 3.32; the description of the Liouville consequence of [AB] and [Se20] in secs. 3.30 and 4; the unchecked attribution to [Pet] in sec. 2 and sec. 3.23; and an undefined formula in the opening. It also proposed replacing the status label; that label is retained, because the case remains unresolved.
- Review 115, an independent reading of the changes recorded under Reviews 113 and 114 against the body, with the comparison in Proposition 38(d) and the record at the initial time in Proposition 33(f)(ii) rechecked. It confirmed both proof repairs and found three overstatements, all checked and repaired: without the Type I swirl hypothesis the comparison in Proposition 38(d) still gives a lower bound, with a negative term of order T^{1/2} coming from the bound R > lambda/||U||_infty on the superlevel set, but no positive logarithmic coefficient; the parabolic radius in Proposition 34, Remark (2) is comparable to |tau|^{1/2} only as tau -> -infinity; and the summary of Proposition 34 in sec. 1.3 now says that no bound on the meridional field strong enough for exclusion was derived (the velocity bound gives (U^R)^-/R <= K/rho_lambda). It also proposed rewriting several list entries as complete sentences; these entries keep the list form used throughout.
- Review 116, an independent referee of a proposed addition to Proposition 40, Remark (2): the exclusion of the endpoint c = 1/2 when p(s/2) is replaced by p_infinity = P(zeta = infinity). It found every step correct (the lower bound from the clock of Step 7, the integrability of log^+ T_infinity, Fatou's lemma and the Tonelli upper bound) and showed that the qualification proposed for the original form with p(s/2) is unnecessary: comparing the time-integrated compression with (1/2) log of the stopped age t wedge zeta on the whole probability space excludes that form as well. The author checked this argument by hand and entered it, with c <= 1/2 in the statements of the averaged criterion in the overview, secs. 1.3, 3.33 and 4, and the corresponding sentence of Remark (9)(h)(i). A second independent referee checked the text as applied line by line (the clock bound off the eternal event, the moment of log^+ T_infinity, the lower bound for D_t, Fatou's lemma, both Tonelli identities, the cancellation bound log 2, the eternal-event variant and the closing sentence on c > 1/2) and found it correct.
- Review 117, an independent check of a one-paragraph addition to Proposition 40, Remark (2), made after Review 116: the necessary condition that int_0^t E[a^-(X_s, -s); zeta > s] ds - (1/2) int_1^t p(s) ds/s tends to infinity for every limit, which is the lower half of the endpoint argument, extended from the integers to the reals by monotonicity. It found the identity, the hypotheses used (only (b), Proposition 26(l) and the clock bound, not the bound with c = 1/2) and the extension to the reals correct, with no change required.
- Review 118, an independent referee of the averaged criterion on circulation superlevel sets in Proposition 40, Remark (9)(f), before its inclusion here. It confirmed the measure-theoretic steps (the convergence of P(F_{ell,n}) under the condition that the terminal killed circulation has no atom at ell, and the reverse Fatou bound for q_ell along sequences), the Fatou and Tonelli steps, the choice of delta, the variant without the condition on the atom and the countability of the atoms. It found two explanatory sentences inaccurate: the comparison with Remark (2) asserted that neither averaged hypothesis implies the other, which the two comparisons do not show, and the reason given for the restriction c < 1/2 was wrong, since the cancellation in Remark (2) does not use the monotonicity of p. Both were rewritten as it proposed, after checking. A second reading of the paragraph as included, with the sentences that cite it, confirmed the proof and asked that the overview, sec. 1.3 and sec. 3.33 state the condition on the atom, as sec. 4 does; this was done. A third independent check found every step correct; the convergence of q_ell, used in the sentence on c = 1/2, is now stated in the proof.
- Review 119, an independent referee of the conditional endpoint c = 1/2 of the averaged criterion on circulation superlevel sets in Proposition 40, Remark (9)(f), before its inclusion here. It confirmed the divergence of the accumulated error when P(F_{ell,n}) < P(F), the Tonelli identity and the upper bound for E[Psi_t], the decomposition Psi_t = D_t - (H'_t - (1/2) L'_t), the divergence of Psi_t on F, the Fatou step under a uniform bound for E[Psi_t^-], and the reduction of that bound, through the clock, to the compression at the alive ages outside the superlevel set. It found the representation log^+(t wedge zeta) = int_1^{t wedge zeta} ds/s false when t wedge zeta < 1, so the complementary terms are now defined by explicit indicators; it asked that the accumulated error be said to tend to infinity rather than to be infinite and that the missing estimate for the complementary term be stated as the absence of a direct estimate; and it noted that the forms of the hypothesis of Remark (2) with p(s) and with p(s/2) are equivalent once the integrable error may change. All were adopted after checking. A second reading of the text as included confirmed every step and asked that the summary in sec. 4 not suggest that the additional condition is necessary; this was done.
- Review 120, an independent referee of the abstract example at the endpoint c = 1/2 in Proposition 40, Remark (9)(f), before its inclusion here. It confirmed the parameters, the clock bounds (each total clock is below 1/256 plus an exponentially small term), the survival bound, the bounds for A, the factorization of the martingale and its terminal law, the threshold probability, the exact expression for E[a^-(s); calC_s > 1/2] - q_{1/2}(s)/(2s) at every age s >= 4 and the divergence (b). It found the bound calC_s <= A/16 before the lottery false at the ages s < 1, where the type is not yet known (calC_0 = 1), and asked that it be restricted to 1 <= s <= U_n; that the strain itself, not only its negative part, be specified; that the filtration be the augmented natural filtration of two independent Brownian motions, so that calC has a continuous version; that the survival probability be conditioned on the type; that the stopped clock be distinguished from the unstopped deterministic clock; and that the scope sentences not claim more than the construction shows. All were adopted after checking. A second reading of the text as included confirmed every mathematical step, including the clock bounds, the survival constant and the strict form of the final inequality, and asked for a more precise first sentence and a scope sentence that does not assert that the type cannot be encoded in a spatial state; this was done. An independent check in the parallel line of work found the same incorrect sentence and confirmed the rest, with the clocks also evaluated numerically.

An audit is evidence, not a proof of correctness.
